trajectories.basis: walked + fixed + LIVE-PROVEN 2026-08-25: anon comprehension good (masthead + verdict + 18 listings); gated tap shows door-toast w/ return; listings deep-link via ?listing=. FIX LANDED: the interrupted ACTION now completes — toggleWatchlist's anon branch stashes wh_pending_action (registered canonical key), loadWatchlist replays once post-auth (idempotent-guarded, single-shot); proven live: tap -> sign in via the toast door -> saved:true, then unsaved (cleanup). Remaining: trust-claim depth (T70's lane), ?listing= arrival fidelity (T43's lane), wave-close re-earn of marketplace rows. || LOCKED 2026-08-28. The fix had been live-proven for three days with NO GATE, which for this particular fix is the dangerous state: the replay is four lines inside a loader, invisible to every other oracle, and its failure mode is SILENT - nothing errors, the listing is simply not saved, and only the person who tapped ever knows. Gate the-interrupted-action-completes holds four clauses: the intent is stashed (sessionStorage, so it dies with the tab - an intent that outlived the session would fire days later against a listing the person no longer wants); it is actually replayed; it is single-shot, the key consumed BEFORE the call so a throwing replay cannot loop; and it is idempotent. THE IDEMPOTENCY CLAUSE IS THE ONE THAT EARNED THE GATE: the other three fail visibly the first time anyone walks the flow, while this one fires only when state raced ahead - and because toggleWatchlist is a TOGGLE, replaying over an already-saved listing UN-SAVES the thing the person asked for, a symptom that reads as the platform losing their save rather than as a replay bug. Selftest 7/7, comment-stripped. Remaining: trust-claim depth (T70's lane), ?listing= arrival fidelity (T43's lane). pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] pct -> 60. trajectories.note: ★KICKED-REJOIN CLOSED (2026-08-27), and the point is that the code STILL WORKS. A removed worker usually still has it - read aloud at a briefing, sitting in a chat thread - so rejoining is not an edge case, it is the next thing that happens. Both halves were already right, which is worth stating plainly rather than inventing a defect: join_hive_by_code refuses a kicked member by auth identity AND again by (hive, worker_name) so a second account cannot walk a ban back in, and hive.html already answers HIVE_MEMBER_KICKED with 'You have been removed from this hive. Contact the supervisor to be re-added.' - cause and remedy, not a raw code. What was missing was PROOF: inspection is not a gate, and the worker_name branch in particular only fires for an identity with no membership row at all, which is exactly the shape a reading of the source talks itself out of. ★Gate kicked-rejoin-is-explained drives both refusals LIVE (both returned HIVE_MEMBER_KICKED, including the second-identity defence) inside a transaction that is ROLLED BACK, with the member's status re-read afterwards to prove it. The copy half matches by MEANING rather than a fixed sentence, because a fixed sentence is a gate that fails when someone improves the wording and so teaches people to stop improving it. ★TEETH USE TRANSACTIONAL DDL: --teeth replaces join_hive_by_code with a permissive version INSIDE the same transaction, both branches then report 'allowed', the gate fails naming both, and the definition is re-read afterwards to confirm the real function returned - it did. A green teeth run would have meant the gate could not see an open door. Verified afterwards that the only kicked row on the platform is the deliberate 'Former Member (kicked fixture)' in another hive, not residue. ★AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG FIRST, caught by its own selftest: the copy check used a naive quote-to-quote regex, which paired the closing quote of one literal with the opening quote of the next and returned the CODE between them - so a page whose sentence was perfectly good read as saying nothing. The selftest case that caught it was 'live copy on hive.html passes both', which is why asserting the KNOWN-GOOD state belongs in a selftest alongside the known-bad ones. Distinct from removal-tells-the-worker (T25), which covers the removed worker's ARRIVAL; this covers the door they knock on afterwards. REMAINS: the resurrection proof at the close batch. ★LOCKED (2026-08-27): THE RESURRECTION PROOF IS DONE, AGAINST THE REAL PRE-FIX WORLD. The one remaining item was deferred to 'the close batch', and it did not need to be. kicked-rejoin-is-explained already carried three synthetic teeth cases, but a synthetic shape is not the pre-fix PAGE: what the roadmap asks is that the detector go RED against the world before the fix. Found the commit that introduced the branch (git log -S HIVE_MEMBER_KICKED -- hive.html -> 49c723d4), took its PARENT, and ran the gate's own check_copy against that text. It goes RED with exactly the right sentence: 'hive.html does not branch on HIVE_MEMBER_KICKED at all - a ban would reach the person as a generic join failure.' Green on HEAD, green on the live tree. ★AND IT WAS DONE WITHOUT MUTATING A FILE, which mattered today: the gate board is running and walking pages, and the usual teeth technique - swap the file, run, restore - would have handed a live sweep a half-swapped hive.html. Pointing the module's PAGE constant at a git-extracted copy proves the same thing and touches nothing. A resurrection proof does not need a checkout; it needs the pre-fix BYTES, and git already has them. Both gates green: invite-code-round-trip and kicked-rejoin-is-explained.

trajectories.note: ★THE LAST-UNIT RACE, MEASURED - AND THE LOSER WAS NEVER TOLD (2026-08-27). inventory_deduct locks the item FOR UPDATE, so the race is serialised by construction and the loser's call runs against an empty shelf. Driven live on a real item set to 0 inside a rolled-back transaction: `v_qty := GREATEST(0, v_qty - p_qty)` CLAMPS rather than refuses, so asking for 1 with 0 on hand RETURNED 0, wrote a ledger row with qty_change 0, changed nothing, and raised NO error. Every caller checked only `error`. So the worker got 'Entry saved' while their entry claimed a part the shelf never gave up - the shelf and the system disagreeing SILENTLY, which is exactly what this trajectory exists to prevent, arriving from the direction nobody was watching. ★THE RETURN VALUE CANNOT DISTINGUISH IT: it is the new quantity, and 'took the last one' and 'there were none' both end at 0. The LEDGER ROW can, because it records what MOVED - so the callers now pass p_txn_id (the function has always accepted one) and read that row back through a new central helper whDeductMoved(), with whShortMoveNotice() giving all three sites the same sentence. Verified under RLS that a member can read their own hive's inventory_transactions row, because a fix that depends on a read nobody is allowed to make is not a fix. ★THREE SITES, NOT ONE - and finding that was the real lesson. I fixed logbook's SAVE path, and the gate still said NO: logbook has a second deduct in the EDIT path and inventory has a third in its Use modal. Worse, inventory then cached `addTransaction(..., -qty, ...)` - the amount ASKED - so the page's own transaction list would claim a movement the database never made; it now records what moved. 'Fix every path that mutates, not just the walked one', found by the instrument rather than by me. ★AND THE GATE HAD THE SAME DISEASE IT WAS BUILT TO CATCH: its first version graded with re.search, checking ONE call and reporting on all of them - the precise shape that would have let two of three sites keep the defect behind a green verdict. It now walks every call on every deducting page. 3 sites, 3 checking; teeth cover the pre-fix error-only shape, an id passed but never read back, and the full form. REMAINS: resurrection at the close batch. ★AND THE CLASS WAS SWEPT, NOT JUST THE INSTANCE. 'What else has this shape?' - 18 public functions clamp with GREATEST/LEAST; the dangerous shape is only the one that clamps a CALLER'S REQUESTED AMOUNT and still returns success. Checked the caller-facing ones: consume_ai_global_budget returns an explicit `allowed boolean` (its GREATEST only floors a displayed remaining), apply_dispute_adjustment RAISES on every refusal and returns {adjusted:false, reason} otherwise, retire_credits raises on a non-positive amount and its clamp guards a treasury counter, grant_service_reward is a trigger with no caller to answer. inventory_deduct was the OUTLIER - the only one that silently did less than it was asked and said nothing. That is a bounded negative result worth recording: the fix is not owed anywhere else, and the next person does not have to re-ask. ★MY OWN HELPER WAS CANONICAL DRIFT, CAUGHT BY THE BOARD AND FIXED (2026-08-27). whDeductMoved was added earlier this session reading `inventory_transactions` DIRECTLY, and validate_canonical_sources flagged it on the running board: a canonical view v_inventory_transactions_truth exists, so a raw read is drift by definition - the point of the truth views being that one shape of a row is what every consumer sees. Migrated rather than exempted, because there was no reason an exemption would have had to state: the view carries both columns the helper needs (id, qty_change), is security_invoker=true so RLS still decides what comes back, and is granted to authenticated. ★VERIFIED END-TO-END RATHER THAN ASSUMED, since this helper sits on the live deduct path and a silent regression would take the short-move notice with it: the database reports qty_change 4 for a real transaction and the helper returns moved 4 through the view. Gate back to 6/6. ★AND IT IS WORTH NAMING THAT THE BOARD CAUGHT MY OWN EDIT the same day I made it - the gate did exactly its job on the person who had spent the session teaching other gates to do theirs. ★THE LEDGER'S BALANCE IS GUARDED; ITS CHAIN IS NOT - MEASURED (2026-08-27, from the running board's FAIL list). validate_inventory_ledger_reconciled checks two different invariants and only one of them has a keeper. (1) qty_on_hand == the newest qty_after IS enforced: trg_inventory_sync_balance fires AFTER INSERT and runs inventory_sync_balance_from_ledger(), so the item's balance is dragged into step with the ledger on every write. (2) the CHAIN - qty_after == prev + qty_change - is enforced by NOTHING. The trigger syncs the balance FROM the ledger; it never asks whether the ledger's own running total adds up, so a producer writing an inconsistent qty_after is accepted silently and this gate is the only thing that would ever say so. ★ONE ROW VIOLATES IT, and it is legacy rather than live: id 88776b9e-… on item inv-0db4887bb1e7 has prev 6, qty_change +4, qty_after 6 - the total simply did not advance - written 2026-08-24, before this session. All 454 ledger rows predate 2026-08-25 and none have been written since, so nothing today produced it. ★NOT HAND-PATCHED, deliberately: 'correcting' that row to 10 would cascade through every later qty_after on the item AND move its qty_on_hand, which other gates assert on - repairing fixture data by hand is how one number starts moving another gate's numbers. The gate's own prescribed remedy is a reseed with the born-consistent seeder. ★THE STRUCTURAL GAP IS THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING: a CHECK or a BEFORE INSERT guard asserting qty_after = prev + qty_change would make the chain as unfalsifiable as the balance already is. That is a migration, so it is Ian's to land rather than mine to slip in. ★LOCKED (2026-08-27): THE RESURRECTION IS EARNED, NOT DEFERRED. The note said 'resurrection at the close batch', which turned out to be a deferral the technique dissolves: the fix landed THIS session, so the pre-fix world is simply HEAD, and git already holds those bytes. Ran the gate's own check_client against HEAD's logbook.html and inventory.html: TWO findings on logbook (both deduct paths - save and edit) and ONE on inventory, each reading 'passes no p_txn_id, so nothing can identify the ledger row' - exactly the three sites the fix touched. All three are green live. ★NO FILE WAS MUTATED to prove it, which mattered because the gate board was concurrently walking these same pages; the usual swap-run-restore would have handed a live sweep a half-swapped logbook. A resurrection proof needs the pre-fix BYTES, not a checkout - and this is the second trajectory closed with that technique today, after T7. trajectories.note: ★CROSS-SURFACE AGREEMENT, MEASURED - AND THE FUSION QUESTION ANSWERED BY THE DATA SOURCES (2026-08-27). The spec asked whether there is ONE canonical start-of-shift surface or three competing ones. Reading what each actually queries settles it: dayplanner reads schedule_items + v_pm_scope_items_truth + v_logbook_truth (MY day), shift-brain reads shift_plans (the generated CREW plan), hive reads hive_members + hive_audit_log + benchmarks (the TEAM's state). Three different scopes, not three answers to one question - so the fusion verdict is KEEP DISTINCT, on evidence rather than taste. ★WHERE THEY OVERLAP IS PM WORK, and that is where agreement could break: a shift plan's payload carries pms_due, while dayplanner reads live PM truth, and shift_plans is a SNAPSHOT (generated_at). Measured across every plan on the stack: 1,647 PM items listed, and only 2 reference an asset that is no longer overdue - both in plans old enough that shift-brain's own STALE badge fires ('This plan is not for the current shift; regenerate before acting on it'), which is exactly the guard this class needs and which already exists. ★AND THE HONEST LIMIT: the case that badge does NOT cover is within-shift drift - a plan generated for TODAY six hours ago still listing a PM a colleague has since completed. It could not be measured here, because there are ZERO shift_plans dated today or later on this stack; every seeded plan is historical. Recording that as unmeasured rather than concluding either way, and NOT gating a property I could not observe. REMAINS for T13: the within-shift case, which needs a currently-dated plan to exist before it can be asked.

trajectories.title: Worker goes offline mid-entry → queued write → reconnect sync
trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXING->75 (2026-08-25): the offline_queued oracle (tools/prove_offline_queued.mjs) now covers ALL 8 queue pages, 8/8 GREEN in one sweep: logbook-entry, pm-completion, community-post, inventory-part, dayplanner-item, skillmatrix-targets, projectmanager-progress, assethub-fmea. TWO real product fixes shipped by the sweep: (1) wh-capture-validate.js now short-circuits its contract fetch when navigator.onLine===false - offline, the fetch hung ~8s on the dead network with the Save button frozen before failing open (measured on inventory; benefits every capture-contract caller); (2) the queue-registration DEFER RACE - pm-scheduler/dayplanner/inventory/skillmatrix wired their whCreateQueue behind a one-shot `if (window.whCreateQueue)` inside an immediate async init while offline-queue.js is `<script defer>`; when auth awaits resolved fast the check ran first and the queue was silently NEVER created (measured live: pm-scheduler lost 2 of 5 runs - submitCompletion entered, fell through to the dead network, worker's PM unsaved). All four converted to the lazy _ensure<X>Queue() accessor (project-manager's proven pattern), ensured at init AND at every use site; post-fix 3/3 repro runs queue. Instrument upgrades: announcement collector (window.__whSeen MutationObserver unioned into held/refusal reads - a ~3.5s toast expiring inside the 5s settle no longer reads as silence), HELD vocabulary widened for project-manager's 'saved on this device / filed when you reconnect' phrasing, pm-completion localEvidence hardened to the sheet-closed discriminator (vacuous pass impossible). LOCKED-IN-PROGRESS (2026-08-25): the offline_queued FAMILY GATE is registered (offline-queued-family in run_platform_checks Platform group, skip_if_fast, retry-once discipline; tools/validate_offline_queued.py wraps the prover across all 8 cases - first board-shape run 8/8 PASS; the wrapper's own two birth defects fixed: cp1252 decode mangling the PASS marker, and a heredoc-written   backspace in the regex - the SAME git-bash lesson this session already recorded, now twice-learned: regex-bearing edits go through Edit/Write, never heredoc). Remaining: drain-on-reconnect slice (deliberately separate - needs reconnect+settle and writes real rows), gate registration for the family, mid-flight offline transition + photo-in-queue + queue-survives-restart probes (wave close). THE DEFERRED HALF CLOSED 2026-08-26 (gate queue-drain): the offline prover's own header explained why the drain was left out - it needs a reconnect plus a settle window and writes real rows - so this prover writes a MARKED row, deletes it, verifies the delete, and ABORTS on dirty state. Asserts all three: HELD offline with ZERO server writes, DRAINED on the online event, and exactly ONCE (re-checked after a further settle so a second tick cannot hide) with the IndexedDB store emptied. PASS on dayplanner's schedule_items queue. THREE probe-shape errors were caught before any verdict was banked - getPending is async, schedule_items RLS requires auth_uid on the row, and the queue item is {id, op, payload} not a flat row - each of which would have been a FALSE RED against a working queue (verify the instrument before the page, three times in one build). Remaining: mid-flight offline transition, photo-in-queue, queue-survives-restart. RESURRECTION PROVEN same day: disabling the auto-sync tick (the exact shape a drain regression takes) turned queue-drain RED - held:true, drained:false, queueEmptied:false - and restoring HEAD returned it GREEN. The detector is calibrated against the failure it exists to catch, not merely passing. Remaining to LOCKED: mid-flight offline transition, photo-in-queue, queue-survives-restart (the three probes the spec names beyond hold+drain). ★T14 CLOSED 2026-08-27: mid-flight was already driven by prove_offline_queued (arms ONLINE, then cuts the network before submit) - recorded as owed in error; queue-survives-restart and photo-survives-queue built, teeth-proven and registered. || ★QUEUE-SURVIVES-RESTART IS PROVEN, ALL THREE PARTS (2026-08-28). The promise a dead-zone worker relies on is not one claim but three, and only the first had been walked: the entry is QUEUED, the app can be REOPENED while still offline, and the person is TOLD work is pending. tools/prove_offline_queue_survives_restart.mjs walks all three. MEASURED: enqueued while offline -> 1 pending; the page then CLOSED entirely and a fresh one opened WITH THE NETWORK STILL DOWN -> the navigation simply succeeds, because the service worker serves the logbook shell cold, and getPending still returns the entry; the offline badge is VISIBLE reading '1 pending'; cleanup leaves nothing behind. So a repair logged in a dead zone survives the app being killed, and the worker can see that it is still waiting rather than having to trust it. ★TWO INSTRUMENT ERRORS WORTH KEEPING: the first version blocked service workers out of habit - every other probe here does - and the offline reload died with a navigation error, because blocking the worker in the one test whose subject IS the offline shell measures the absence of the thing under test. The second invented the queue's API (put/all) and got 'q.put is not a function'; the real surface is enqueue/getPending/remove, and reading offline-queue.js would have cost less than guessing. pct -> 100.

trajectories.note: ★THE RESTART SLICE, BUILT AND GATED (2026-08-27) - plus one 'remaining' item that was already done and should not have been on the list. ★FIRST THE CORRECTION: 'mid-flight offline transition (not just offline-at-load)' was recorded as owed, and it is not. Reading prove_offline_queued.mjs's own sequence settles it - it loads the page ONLINE, prints '--- arming on <page> (ONLINE) ---' while it fills the form, and only THEN cuts navigator.onLine and the route before submitting. That IS the dead-zone transition: the network dies between starting the form and pressing save. I nearly built a second prover for a case the first one already drives, which the no-redundancy rule exists to stop; the check that caught it was reading the existing prover before writing a new one. ★WHAT WAS GENUINELY UNCOVERED is the RESTART, and it is a different surface rather than a variation: both existing provers stay inside ONE page life, while the field reality is that the worker pockets the phone and the PWA is gone - OS-reclaimed or closed - before signal returns. The queue is created by _ensure<X>Queue() with auto-sync attached INSIDE that accessor, so a drain only ever happens if a FRESH page life calls it, and this trajectory already measured what that costs when it does not (pm-scheduler's defer race, 2 of 5 loads, silent). A queue whose rows persist but whose sync never re-attaches is WORSE than no queue: the work is neither sent nor lost but INVISIBLE, and the worker was told it was saved. ★prove_queue_survives_restart.mjs + gate queue-survives-restart assert five things: HELD (0 server writes offline), PERSISTS (still in IndexedDB after a full document restart, read from the store DIRECTLY - asking the page's queue object would be asking the witness the restart just destroyed), REWIRED (the fresh life re-creates the queue and re-attaches sync), DRAINED, ONCE (one row after a further settle, store emptied). All five green on dayplanner's schedule_items. ★TEETH, and they discriminate: --teeth suppresses whCreateQueue on the restarted document, reproducing the defer race's end state. REWIRED goes false, the row is left STRANDED in the store (drained/once/emptied all false) - and PERSISTS stays TRUE, which is the point: the storage was never the problem, the wiring was, and the prover can tell those apart. ★ONE HONEST SCOPE LINE: the restart document is fetched with the transport up, because serviceWorkers are blocked so there is no cached shell and a goto under setOffline dies at ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED - a failure of the SHELL, which is a real question and T44's, not this one. Folding it in would have made this gate go red for a reason unrelated to its subject. The window stays write-tight anyway (route aborted, navigator.onLine false via addInitScript) and the DB is re-checked mid-restart to prove it. REMAINS for the wave close: photo-in-queue. ★PHOTO-IN-QUEUE, THE LAST PROBE - AND A PREMISE CHECK THAT NEARLY BECAME A FALSE FINDING (2026-08-27). Reading the offline branch, the queued payload appeared to carry no photo at all, which would have been real data loss: the dead-zone entry a worker most wants to keep is the one with the picture on it. It was my excerpt, not the code - `photo: entry.photo` sits at :2194, two lines above where I started reading. Confirmed before writing anything down, which is the whole of the discipline. The real question was narrower and better: `photo` is produced by readAsDataURL through a canvas re-encode, so it is a BASE64 STRING, and the risk is fidelity across storage rather than presence in the payload. ★prove_photo_survives_queue.mjs + gate photo-survives-queue drive the page's OWN pipeline - a hand-built 420x320 PNG (no image dependency in this repo, so the encoder is written inline) handed to the real #f-photo input, through FileReader -> Image -> canvas -> toDataURL and its 700KB re-encode guard, producing 36,783 chars. Then offline enqueue (0 server writes), a full document restart, and the stored photo compared BYTE-FOR-BYTE and decoded back to a bitmap: 420x320, identical. ★THE TEETH ARE THE PART WORTH KEEPING. --teeth stores a photo of exactly the SAME LENGTH with ONE character changed. SURVIVES goes false while both lengths still read 36783 - which is the only way to show the comparison is byte-wise and not the 'roughly the right size' check that lets a corrupted image pass. And that same run shows STILL-AN-IMAGE staying TRUE, because a one-character JPEG corruption still decodes. EITHER ASSERTION ALONE WOULD HAVE PASSED A CORRUPTED PHOTO; only the pair is honest. ★Writes nothing to the database by design - the row never leaves the queue, so no PM mirror, no XP ledger, no embedding is disturbed, which is why logbook could be the subject at all where the drain prover had to pick dayplanner. Verified 0 probe rows in both logbook and schedule_items afterwards. ★T14 CLOSES with all three of its listed probes resolved: mid-flight was already covered and the record corrected, queue-survives-restart built and gated, photo-in-queue built and gated.

trajectories.note: ★A COMMA IN THE SEARCH BOX RETURNED HTTP 400 (2026-08-26, measured live). PostgREST splits or=(a,b) on top-level commas, so an unquoted comma inside a value rejected the whole filter - and 'Bearing, spherical roller, 22320 E1 XL C3, SKF' is simply how a part is named, the platform's own example elsewhere. Four sites escaped the LIKE wildcards % and _ and left the DELIMITERS alone: the logbook feed, the logbook EXPORT, community's feed and the global search overlay. marketplace was the exception - it strips them - which is why the same phrase worked there and nowhere else. The page renders the 400 as a failed READ, so a legitimate search looked like an outage. Fixed centrally with utils.whSafeSearchTerm (delimiters removed, wildcards escaped) at all four sites; verified end to end, the same read now returns 200 with an empty array. Gate search-term-survives-punctuation, teeth proven on both clauses. ★SAFETY-NOTES SURFACING: THE LOCK-OUT WAS IN THE DATABASE AND NOT ON THE GLASS (2026-08-27). logbook captures loto_applied and permit_reference on the form, stores them on the row, and restores them when an entry is EDITED - and the entry CARD never rendered either. The card showed date, machine, category, type, problem, action, root cause, knowledge, status and photo; the two safety fields were the only captured columns it dropped. ★THIS IS NOT A THEORETICAL GAP: 419 of 3,811 entries carry that data - 11% of the fault history - so a worker doing exactly what this trajectory describes (searching how a machine was worked on before opening it) could not learn that the last person had locked it out or worked under a permit. The most consequential fact on the card was the one it withheld. ★A LOTO / permit badge now renders on the card, permit number included and escaped. Verified LIVE against the database rather than by eye: 20 cards, 3 badges, database expects 3 - exact match - sample 'BF-001 MECHANICAL CLOSED LOTO PTW-2026-9385'. Gated as safety-isolation-visible, which compares COUNTS rather than existence because a badge on the wrong rows is its own defect. ★AND THE FIRST PROBE PROVED NOTHING: it used an account whose most recent 20 entries happened to contain no LOTO, so it read 0 badges and 0 was CORRECT. I checked the database before believing the zero, which is the only reason this was not filed as 'the badge does not work'. The gate now refuses to pass when its subject has nothing to show. ★AND THE GATE ITSELF WOULD HAVE FAILED FOR THE WRONG REASON: its sample line carries a lock emoji and this repo runs on a cp1252 console, so printing it raised UnicodeEncodeError - a CRASH that the board would have recorded as a gate FAILURE rather than an encoding problem. stdout is pinned to utf-8 the way the other live gates here already do it. Caught by running the wrapper rather than trusting that the prover passing meant the gate passed: they are two different programs and only one of them prints the emoji. ★THE LOTO GAP HAS FOUR SIBLINGS - MEASURED (2026-08-27). Having found one captured-but-never-read column, I asked the general question: of the 15 columns logbook writes into a row, which does the READ path never reference? Four more sit in exactly the LOTO shape - selected from the table, mapped into the entry object, restored into the FORM when an entry is edited, and shown to a reader nowhere: failure_consequence (restored into #f-consequence at :4295, the same edit-only path LOTO used), readings_json, production_output and closed_at. ★TWO OF THEM MATTER FOR THIS TRAJECTORY'S OWN SCENARIO: someone searching fault history to learn 'has this failed before, what fixed it' would want the READINGS the last person took and what the failure CONSEQUENCE was, and both are sitting in the row. ★BUT THEY ARE NOT THE SAME FIX AS LOTO, and saying so is the point: LOTO is a one-word safety flag that belongs on the CARD, where a scanning eye catches it. Readings and consequence are detail - putting them on the card makes the list unreadable and buries the flag I just added. They belong in the DETAIL MODAL, which is a placement decision per field rather than four more badges. Recorded as measured with the shape named, so the next pass starts from where each one goes rather than from whether they are missing. ★FIXED + LOCKED (2026-08-27). The sibling sweep above became a fix and a gate. Two of the four reach the reader now, chosen because they ARE this trajectory's scenario: readings_json (1,767 of 3,811 rows - nearly half the logbook) renders as labelled values with UNITS in the detail modal, and failure_consequence (1,075 rows, one of whose four values is 'Safety risk') renders as a severity-coloured badge on BOTH the card and the modal. production_output (205) and closed_at (3,765) stay unrendered deliberately - closed_at duplicates the status badge for a reader and production_output is a reporting figure, not a diagnostic one. ★AND THE LOTO FIX TURNED OUT TO BE HALF A FIX: the badge was on the CARD only, so the safety flag DISAPPEARED on drill-down - the detail modal being exactly where someone reads before working on a machine. The cause was structural rather than forgetful: lotoBadge was a `const` INSIDE renderEntries, so openModal could not have called it. Promoted to a shared top-level helper; card and modal now share ONE definition, and the new gate asserts BOTH surfaces so 'it renders somewhere' can never read as covered again. Gate captured-fields-are-readable: teeth RED on all four assertions against the pre-fix page, GREEN on HEAD, counts anchored to the database (20 cards / 3 badges / 3 expected). ★THE CLASS SWEPT PLATFORM-WIDE, AND TRIAGED HONESTLY (2026-08-27). The LOTO shape asked as a platform question - which columns does SOME page write that NO page renders? - over 121 written columns: 9 candidates, and the triage matters as much as the count. REAL: project_roles.assigned_by (36/36 rows, 'who put me on this project' unanswerable - FIXED on project-manager) and the whole service_payments record incl. the payer's variance_reason (4/4 rows, written for a provider who cannot read it - scoped on T35). GAPS RECORDED, not defects yet: live_location (a provider's GPS, never shown to the client waiting for them) and provider_type (hive vs freelancer - a trust signal a buyer never sees). NOT DEFECTS, and saying so is the point: cancelled_at and settled_at are timestamps whose FACT is already carried by the rendered status; rows_attempted equals the rows_written + rows_failed the import history already shows, so the denominator is on the glass. UNUSED RATHER THAN WITHHELD: acted_by (4 staging recommendations, 0 acted on) and project_roles.notes (0 of 36 rows carry one) - a field nobody has filled is not a field being hidden. ★AND THE SWEEP WAS WRONG BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT: scoped per-page it put actor/target_id/target_name/target_type at the top of nearly every list, because pages WRITE audit rows and the AUDIT-LOG page renders them - ~30 correct designs read as defects until the question became platform-wide. Credential columns (key_hash, p256dh, auth uids) are excluded outright: not rendering those is the security property, and flagging them would invert it into a bug.

trajectories.title: Worker asks the AI companion a technical question
trajectories.basis: walked 390: arrival has identity+persona chip (Zaniah), capability statement, advisory disclaimer, TRY-ASKING seeds; the curated MTBF ask returns a GROUNDED answer (M-001, 3 repeat bearing-grease failures, actionable move + escalation offer); an out-of-scope phrasing gets an honest abstention WITH pointers (Hive board / Analytics) - no confabulation either way; Logbook citations tappable and resolve. No new walk-level defects; citation->exact-record deep link + D12 quota chip are T39/T65 items. || ★CITATIONS ARE PROSE, NOT DOORS (2026-08-28). This trajectory asks whether the companion's grounding is 'visible and TAPPABLE'. Visible: yes, and deliberately so — the system prompt instructs the model to 'cite the specific entry (date, machine, or job reference)', and a page-level wh-source-chip names the hive and the grounding it is reading. Tappable: NO. The answer reaches the DOM as one escaped string (innerHTML into .bubble-assistant) and there is no linkification anywhere in the page — no anchor construction, no citation resolver. So a worker reading 'per the 12 Aug entry on Pump 2' has to leave the assistant, open the logbook, and find it by hand, at the exact moment the platform had the record in context. ★NOT BUILT, AND THE REASON IS THIS TRAJECTORY'S OWN BAR: a citation that opens the WRONG record, or 404s, is worse than prose — it converts a soft claim a reader would verify into a hard one they would trust. Making them tappable means the model emitting STRUCTURED references rather than sentences, and the renderer resolving them against real rows before it renders a link at all, so a hallucinated id degrades to plain text instead of a broken promise. That is the citation-tap-resolves oracle this trajectory specced, and it is a build with a real design surface, not an edit. Recorded with the mechanism named so the next pass starts from the constraint rather than rediscovering it. The quota half of this trajectory is already shipped: assistant-quota-note reads the gateway's `remaining` beside the composer, so cost is visible BEFORE the next ask rather than only in the refusal after it. pct 60 -> 72. || ★THE COMPANION WAS TELLING WORKERS A WRONG NUMBER, AND THE GATE THAT GUARDS THAT NUMBER WAS WRONG TOO (2026-08-28). The full board flagged a mismatch: companion-launcher.js said 46 calc types, assistant.html said 55. Counted the registry rather than picking a side - engineering-design.js's CALC_TYPES_UI holds 55 entries, all available:true (HVAC 10, Mechanical 4, Electrical 14, Plumbing 10, Fire Protection 5, Machine Design 12). assistant was right; the companion's two prompt strings were nine behind, so a worker asking the AI what the calculator does was told a number the product outgrew. ★THEN FIXING IT MADE A SECOND CHECK FAIL, WHICH IS THE REAL FIND: validate_ai_context carried `CORRECT_CALC_COUNT = 46` as a HARDCODED constant, so the gate whose entire job is catching a drifted count was carrying a drifted count - and it failed the hint at the exact moment that hint became correct. A hardcoded expectation is the same defect it guards against, pointed the other way, and it fails loudest when someone finally fixes the real thing. The constant now DERIVES from CALC_TYPES_UI by brace-matching the literal and counting `{ id:` entries. ★AND THE None GUARD MATTERS MORE THAN THE DERIVATION: without it, `found != None` is always true, so a registry we merely failed to PARSE would fail every hint on the page and report 'expected None' - an unreadable accusation aimed at correct copy. A count we cannot derive is a check we cannot make. Teeth-proven: reverting to 46 fails with 'says 46 calc types but platform has 55', now citing a derived truth instead of a typed guess. pct 72 -> 78. || ★THE GROUNDING IS DECLARED AT THE SURFACE, NOT CITED AT THE CLAIM (2026-08-28). The assistant tells a worker where its answers come from, in plain words and in two places: 'Answers are grounded in your own hive data: logbook, PM schedule, parts, and alerts' on the empty state, and 'Answers are grounded in this hive's live data: open alerts, overdue PMs, parts stock...' in the context it carries. That is more than most assistants say, and it sets the right expectation before the first question - the worker knows this is not a general chatbot and knows which corpora it can and cannot speak about. ★WHAT IT DOES NOT DO IS CITE. There is no per-claim citation that resolves to the record behind it - no tappable path from 'this pump failed twice last month' to those two logbook entries. For a maintenance decision that is the whole difference between an answer a worker can ACT on and one they have to take on trust: a citation that opens the entry lets them read the previous fix, see who did it and check whether the situation matches; a confident sentence without one asks them to believe a machine about a machine. This trajectory's own instrument-close names it - 'a citation that 404s or opens the wrong record is a trust break' - and the prerequisite for that oracle is having citations at all. ★Recorded rather than built: per-claim citation means the gateway returning row references alongside its prose and the client rendering them as links, which is an answer-format change across the AI layer rather than a page edit. pct 78 -> 86. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate quota-warns-before-the-wall re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. || LOCKED 2026-09-04: board gate passed. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Worker earns XP/achievement and understands why
trajectories.basis: the earning MOMENT was invisible: DB triggers pay XP (506 logbook_submit awards) but no source page ever said so. FIXED on both wave-B earning surfaces: logbook save receipt + pm completion receipt now read back achievement_xp_log by source_id and append '+N XP' claiming ONLY what the ledger holds. Live-proven: receipt '+20 XP' = ledger 20 for the probe entry, then reversed on cleanup. Remaining: reversal-on-glass, thresholds stated, standings basis, level-up overlay at 390 (T74/wave close). ADVANCED 2026-08-26: audit of the four remaining probes - THRESHOLDS already stated ('N XP to Lv.X+1' per domain card + progress bars + Max Level) and STANDINGS BASIS already stated ('Ranked by total achievement levels... one level per domain milestone') - both satisfied by prior arcs. REVERSAL-ON-GLASS was the real gap: logbook's delete confirm + receipt were silent about trg_logbook_xp_reverse taking the XP back - both sites now name it ('...any XP it earned is taken back' / 'Any XP it earned was reversed'). Taught validate_logbook's delete-scope check the brace-matching idiom its sibling adopted 2026-07-28 (the longer confirm pushed .eq past the 400-char window - instrument, not page). Remaining: level-up overlay at 390 (T74's lane). || LEVEL-UP OVERLAY AT THE FLOOR — WALKED + GATED 2026-08-27. The overlay is a CENTRED FIXED card, which makes its failure mode different from every rail and sheet walked so far: the edge that matters is the BOTTOM, not the right. A celebration card taller than a 320x844 phone puts its only dismiss button below the fold, and because the overlay does not scroll there is no gesture that reaches it — the reward moment turns into a trap on the smallest phone the platform supports, in the exact moment the platform is trying to make someone feel good about their work. MEASURED at 320 through showLevelUpModal() with a REAL achievement id (an empty overlay is a different height, so driving it hollow would have measured the wrong card): the card renders, #levelup-heading and #levelup-close both present, and nothing past the right or bottom edge. CLEAN — no fix needed, which is worth recording as a measurement rather than an assumption, because until now nobody had opened this overlay at the floor. LOCKED by extending flow-fits-the-floor with a bottom axis rather than writing a second gate. ★THE BOTTOM CHECK IS OPT-IN PER FLOW, and that is deliberate: an ordinary PAGE is meant to extend past the fold — that is what scrolling is for — so checking it everywhere would bury the real finding in noise. Two negatives cover it: one proving it BITES (a control below a 40px fold is caught) and one proving the flag actually GATES it (the same measurement with checkBottom off reports nothing), because a flag that is silently ignored would turn every page into a false positive. Selftest 6/6. Remaining: source-page XP feedback at the earning moment (T9/T10 seam). || SOURCE-PAGE XP FEEDBACK — the last named item, and the gap was a SIBLING, not a surface (2026-08-27). The earning-moment work landed on logbook and on pm-scheduler in August, so the obvious read was that both were done. They were not: submitCompletion() has TWO terminal success paths, and only the one taken when the worker ALSO mirrors the work to the logbook announced ' · +N XP'. Untick 'also log this to the logbook' and the identical completion fired the identical trg_pm_achievement award and the receipt said nothing. Same action, same trigger, same XP, two different receipts — decided by a toggle that has nothing to do with earning. ★I NEARLY RECORDED THE WRONG FINDING TWICE ON THE WAY IN: first that logbook never announces XP (it does, via an _xpNote added 2026-08-25 — grep before declaring a capability missing), then that pm-scheduler never does (it does, on one path). The real defect only appears when you enumerate the BRANCHES rather than the pages. ★AND ONE PROBE READING WAS ALSO MINE: the helper returned '' for a completion the database says earned 60 XP, which looked like the fix not working — the row belonged to Bryan Garcia while I was signed in as Leandro Marquez, and ach_log_owner_read is `worker_name IN auth_worker_names()`. RLS refusing correctly. Re-tested against a row the signed-in worker owns: ' · +60 XP'; another worker's: ''; unknown id: ''; null: ''. So the receipt is RLS-scoped by construction and can neither leak another person's award nor overstate one. FIXED by hoisting the read-back into _xpNoteFor() so both paths call ONE helper — two inline copies would have drifted again — and it reads achievement_xp_log rather than recomputing the trigger's 20/+20 rule in JavaScript, because a second copy of the rule is a second source of truth for a number a worker is shown as fact. LOCKED by earning-moment-is-announced, teeth 4/4. Remaining: the reversal's UX face (deleting work removes XP - the ledger reverses honestly, and the delete toast already says so) is covered; wave-close re-earn. || THE XP-REVERSAL CLAIM WAS BEING MADE WITHOUT CHECKING (2026-08-28, from T50's side). logbook's delete receipt said 'Any XP it earned was reversed.' unconditionally - including when the delete had just been REFUSED, in which case no XP moved because no row moved. The reversal trigger (trg_logbook_xp_reverse) is real and this trajectory's ledger work stands; what was wrong was the GLASS asserting the consequence on a path where the cause never happened. The receipt now only appears on a delete that actually landed. || ★AN XP REVERSAL RENDERED AS '+-20' ON THE REWARD SURFACE (2026-08-28). achievements.html builds every XP row through one helper, xpText, and that helper hard-codes a '+' in front of any finite number. Negative amounts are not hypothetical here - they are the reversible XP ledger this programme deliberately built, so deleting work takes its XP back. SEEN LIVE on Bryan Garcia's Wrench Chronicle card: 'Logbook entry submitted +-20', 'Logbook entry closed +-50', beside a correct 'Logbook entry closed +50'. ★AND THE SITE ALREADY CARRIED A LONG COMMENT ABOUT THIS EXACT HELPER - it was hardened against null ('+null' rendered ten times on one screen), against Number(null) coercing to 0, and it even reasons about why '+0' would be 'a lie of a different kind'. Every one of those guards is about the ABSENT case. None is about the NEGATIVE case, because when the guard was written negatives could not occur; they arrived later with the reversal ledger. That is the sibling-fix shape this codebase keeps meeting, in its subtlest form: not a fix applied to one of two call sites, but a guard that was complete on the day it was written and was never revisited when a NEW FEATURE widened its input domain. FIXED: a negative already carries its own sign, so only a gain has one added. Verified live - the three rows now read -20, -50, +50, no '+-' anywhere on the page - and across the helper's whole domain: +20 | -20 | +0 | 'XP not recorded' for null, undefined and empty, so the absent-case guards the comment describes still behave exactly as before. A reversal is the one XP event a worker most needs to read correctly. || AND THE SWEEP FOUND ITS SIBLING 140 LINES AWAY (2026-08-28). Having fixed xpText I swept every page for the shape - a hard-coded '+' in front of an interpolated value - rather than stopping at the instance. NINE hits. Seven are engineering-design overflow counts ('+3 more', '+2' beside a truncated list) where the value is positive by construction, guarded by the if (n > visible) that produces them. The eighth was the fix itself. THE NINTH IS REAL: achievements' WEEK hero renders `+${weekXP}`, and weekXP is a plain SUM of xp_earned over seven days (init :1197, reduce over the rows), so a week whose reversals outweigh its gains is genuinely negative and the headline tile would have read '+-30'. Fixed the same way, and its subtitle now explains the case rather than reading as nonsense: '-30 XP this week - more was taken back by deleted work than earned'. Verified: the live positive case is unchanged (+1780), the negative renders -30 with that sub, zero still reads +0 / 'No XP earned in the past 7 days'. ★THE SWEEP IS THE POINT - one fix would have left a headline number lying while the detail rows beneath it told the truth, which is worse than either alone. pct -> 100. || REVERTED 2026-09-04: named gate FAILED on the 1034/60 board (false 100%; post_board_promote over-locked). pct -> 90. || pct -> 100 (board-locked 2026-09-05). · [2026-09-05] pct -> 100. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_persona_arcs.mjs (gate persona-arcs), 8/8 lenses clean. Speech capture ships with a typed path to the SAME record and six distinct failure causes named in words, so a refused microphone does not end the journey for a worker whose hands are full - 478 entries recorded (T12). All 12 achievements carry a description and 79 have been awarded, with the reason rendered beside the badge on two surfaces, so an engineer earning something can find out what for (T17). Twenty-eight pages remember where a person was and six can say what changed while they were away, covering both the day-two return and the three-month one (T46, T57). Forty pages stamp a figure with its source, 44 canonical truth views stand behind them, and 27 let a person open the rows, so a skeptic can take a headline number apart rather than trust it (T47). Fifty-six learn articles are linked from inside the product and 30 pages explain themselves in place, so a graduate is not sent to search the web for how to use the tool (T54). Lucena Pharmaceutical runs two supervisors, and hive.html checks for a co-supervisor before forcing a hand-over - so leaving is safe when another remains, and the last one is not waved through (T56). Fourteen pages surface device or session state, an idle timeout ships, and there is a way out, so someone who cares about their account has controls beyond closing the tab (T59). THE SCALE ROW IS STATED HONESTLY RATHER THAN CLAIMED: the largest hive in this data holds 8 active members, so twenty is beyond what it can prove; what is asserted instead is that all three roster surfaces BOUND what they render rather than drawing every member at once, which is the property that decides whether twenty people works (T61). TWO LENSES PASSED TOO EASILY ON THE FIRST RUN AND WERE TIGHTENED, both recorded in the prover: 'the reason beside the badge' matched the word description in every page's meta tag and counted 33 surfaces where the honest answer is 2; and 'surfaces session state' counted every page that merely LOADS device-fingerprint.js, when a script tag is not a control a person can act on.

trajectories.note: ★THE XP LEDGER IS KEYED BY NAME, AND A NAME IS NOT A PERSON (2026-08-26) - the fourth face of the same defect family found this session. achievement_xp_log has no auth_uid and no hive_id, and its RLS reads by worker_name; worker_name is unique per HIVE, so two different people in two hives sharing a name would merge totals, compute each other's LEVELS, and be able to read each other's ledger rows (source_action, source_id) from a hive they never joined. Measured: 982 rows / 20 names / ZERO names held by two people - not happening, which is exactly why it was worth gating now: the backfill onto auth_uid is only unambiguous while that stays true. Gate xp-belongs-to-one-person fails the moment a cross-hive namesake appears and retires itself once auth_uid exists. THE FIX IS IAN'S CALL, scoped not smuggled: add auth_uid, backfill, and move the four readers (achievements x2, logbook, pm-scheduler) plus the RLS predicate onto it - a schema change to a ledger with reversal semantics.

trajectories.title: Worker takes a skill exam / updates skill profile
trajectories.basis: walked 390 via the REAL entry (.disc-card): lesson (1.6KB) -> scroll-gate unlock -> 'Mechanical: Level 2 Exam' 10 questions A-D -> result modal. Fail branch EXEMPLARY: score 0/10, pass bar restated, cooldown named ('Retake available in: 24h 00m'), per-question review list. Pass-mark stated BEFORE the exam; X2e draft machinery (wh_exam_draft_* + resume toast) present. Zero product defects - my 3 earlier probe failures were instrument errors (step-btn nodes share data-disc with no open listener; off-screen modal shells pass offsetParent). Note for wave close: checkScroll never fires when lesson content fits the box (short-content edge, all current lessons overflow). Probe attempt cleaned from skill_exam_attempts. || FIXING->60 (2026-08-26): the short-content edge the walk flagged for wave close turned out to be a USER TRAP, and it is fixed. The Take-exam button was enabled ONLY from inside the scroll handler, so a lesson whose content FITS the box never scrolls, the event never fires, checkScroll never runs - and the reader sits in front of a permanently disabled 'Take exam' beside a hint telling them to scroll something that does not scroll, with no way out but closing the screen. Latent only because every lesson authored so far happens to overflow; lesson bodies are AUTHORED CONTENT, so the first short one ships the trap. Fixed by evaluating the gate once at open after the scroll reset - self-correcting, since a non-scrolling box already satisfies scrollTop + clientHeight >= scrollHeight - 80 while a long lesson at scrollTop 0 does not. ★VERIFIED LIVE ON BOTH BRANCHES, because the risk of this fix is that it opens the gate for everyone: long content (822 vs 502) still disabled with the hint shown; short content (54 vs 54) enabled with the hint cleared; 0 pageerrors. Locked as 'scroll-gate-at-open'. ★THE GATE FAILED ITS OWN FIRST TEETH TEST: its invocation count matched `function checkScroll()` - the declaration - so deleting the real call still left 1 and it reported PASS on the very defect it exists for. A negative lookbehind fixed it, and the teeth test refusing to go red is the only reason it was caught. || GATES RECORDED 2026-08-27: scroll-gate-at-open. The basis already named this instrument as built and it IS registered in run_platform_checks and green — the gates field was simply never filled, so the registry understated what this trajectory owns. Verified registered + exit 0 before recording; nothing about the work changed, only the bookkeeping. || EXAM PROGRESS SURVIVES AN INTERRUPTION, AND IT IS SCOPED TO THE RIGHT THING (2026-08-27). The X2e worry for a multi-step exam is the worst kind of loss - a worker eight questions into a certification, interrupted by a call, returning to an empty form and having to start again. It does not happen: the exam persists { answers: _examAnswers, currentQ: _currentQ } to localStorage at three points in the flow, so both WHAT was answered and WHERE they were come back. ★AND THE KEY IS SCOPED BY PERSON AND BY EXAM: wh_exam_draft_${WORKER_NAME}_${discipline}_${level}. On the shared station tablet this platform is built for, worker B's attempt cannot surface in worker A's form, because the identity is IN THE KEY rather than checked after the fact - and two different exams cannot collide either. ★NO HIVE COMPONENT, AND THAT IS CORRECT HERE, which is worth stating because this same session added hive scoping to logbook drafts and the shared helpers. The distinction is what the data BELONGS to: a logbook entry describes a particular plant's machine, so a hive-A draft in a hive-B form is wrong; a welding exam describes the PERSON, and their answers are the same whichever hive they are working in today. Scoping it by hive would lose a contractor's half-finished exam every time they switched sites. Remaining: the revocation experience (a revoked badge telling the worker why) and badge propagation across matrix/profile/standings. || ★REVOCATION DOES NOT EXIST BECAUSE EXPIRY DOES NOT - AND THIS PLATFORM EXPIRES EVERYTHING ELSE (2026-08-27). skill_badges carries id, worker_name, discipline, level, earned_at, exam_score, auth_uid, badge_key - and no revoked_at, no revoked_by, no reason, no expires_at. A badge, once earned, is permanent, so 'does a revoked badge tell the worker why' has no subject: there is nothing to revoke. ★THE CONTRAST IS WHAT MAKES IT A FINDING RATHER THAN AN ABSENCE: TEN tables model expires_at - ai_cache, tts_cache, agent_memory, amc_briefings, failure_signature_alerts, service_vouchers, service_requests' offer TTL, parts_staging_recommendations, offline_snapshot_cache. This platform knows exactly how to express 'valid until'. It applies it to every ephemeral system artefact and to none of the human certifications, which are the one place where expiry is a REGULATORY fact rather than a housekeeping convenience: a TESDA NC II or a vibration-analysis Cat I has a validity period, and a matrix that decides who may do which work will keep asserting a lapsed certification indefinitely. ★AND IT LEAVES THE PLATFORM: resume.html reads v_skill_badges_truth plus skill_badges for the supplementary earned_at, and renders badges as resume CERTIFICATES - so a 2021 badge presents to an employer as a certification, dated but with no validity. The date is there, which is partial honesty; the 'until' is not. ★NOT FILED AS A BUG, because it turns on what these badges ARE: internal skill levels (in which case calling them 'certificates' on a resume is the overclaim) or mirrors of real credentials (in which case they need expiry). That is a domain decision for Ian and the maintenance-expert lens, and it is worth deciding rather than inheriting. Remaining: that decision, then badge propagation across matrix/profile/standings. || NUMBER-TRUTH HAND-CHECK ON THE MATRIX, AND THE PAGE WON IT (2026-08-28). Walked skillmatrix at 390 as Bryan Garcia and hand-checked every figure it renders against the rows. The page is unusually well-instrumented for this: 'On target', 'Quizzes available' and 'Total badges' each carry a written basis, the denominators are explicit ('6 of 25 possible (5 levels x 5 disciplines)'), the actual-level rule is stated ('highest consecutive badge from L1'), and the standard line is honest that the tier model is PLATFORM-INTERNAL rather than dressing it as an external one. ★THE ONE APPARENT DISCREPANCY WAS THE PAGE BEING RIGHT: the database holds 7 badges across 6 disciplines for this worker while the page reports 6 - because Community is not one of the five SKILL disciplines (DISCIPLINE_EMOJI: Mechanical, Electrical, Instrumentation, Facilities Management, Production Lines), so its badge is correctly outside this count. Checking the discipline list before filing is what kept a correct number from being reported as a defect. ★WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG WAS ONE WORD: the disclosure read 'count of badges for you across ALL disciplines', and a worker holding that Community badge sees a total one lower than the badges they know they hold, with nothing on the page accounting for the gap. Now: 'count of your badges across the five skill disciplines and their levels ... Badges from elsewhere on WorkHive, such as Community, are not counted here.' Verified live. A page that explains every other basis this carefully earns the precision on the last one. || ★EXAM PROGRESS SURVIVES AN INTERRUPTION, AND THE DRAFT KEY IS SCOPED THE WAY A SHARED PLANT TABLET NEEDS (2026-08-28). The probe that matters here is the multi-step one: a worker halfway through a ten-question exam gets a phone call, and X2e asks whether the answers are still there afterwards. They are. The exam restores from localStorage under the key wh_exam_draft_<WORKER_NAME>_<discipline>_<level>, recovering BOTH parsed.answers and parsed.currentQ - so the worker returns to the question they left, not to the start. ★THE KEY SCOPING IS THE THOUGHTFUL PART. Including the worker name means two people sharing one station tablet (T121's serial-user reality) cannot overwrite each other's half-finished exam; including discipline and level means a technician part-way through Electrical L2 does not lose it by opening Mechanical L1. A single 'wh_exam_draft' key would have passed a casual test and failed the first real plant. ★MY FIRST PATTERN MISSED IT ENTIRELY - I searched for localStorage.setItem('wh_exam and the real key is a template literal beginning wh_exam_draft_, so the sweep reported ZERO persistence on a page that has it. A narrow literal is how you conclude a feature is absent while reading the file that implements it, and widening before concluding is what turned a false finding into a real one. ★NOT VERIFIED: revocation messaging (does a revoked badge tell the worker why), and whether an earned badge propagates visibly to the matrix, profile and standings. pct 74 -> 86. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate scroll-gate-at-open re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.
trajectories.note: ★THE EXAM'S FAILURE MESSAGE NOW ANSWERS THE ONLY QUESTION THAT MATTERS AFTER AN EXAM (2026-08-27). grade_skill_exam is a WRITE, and its failure said 'Could not save your result. Check connection and try again.' - blaming the connection for a call that also fails on an expired session or a refusal, and saying NOTHING about what a worker actually fears after sitting ten questions: whether the answers are gone. ★THEY ARE NOT, and the page already knew it: answers persist to wh_exam_draft_<worker>_<discipline>_<level> and are restored when the exam reopens. The reassurance existed in the code and never reached the person - the same shape as the wallet reading the wrong one of three numbers. Now routed through whWriteError (which names session / not-allowed / collision) with a fallback that carries the work state: 'Your answers are saved on this device, so reopen the exam and submit again.' Checking the draft machinery BEFORE writing the sentence is what made it safe to promise - a reassurance that turns out to be false is worse than the vague message it replaced. Error-taxonomy ratchet 21 -> 20.

Remaining: mid-session role-demotion journey, re-invite path walk (both live choreographies for a later slice). || MID-SESSION ROLE DEMOTION — ANSWERED 2026-08-27 at the layer that actually decides it. The worry is a supervisor demoted while their session is live: the tab keeps its supervisor-shaped UI because nothing told it otherwise, and the question is whether that stale screen can still DO supervisor things. It cannot. Supervisor authority is enforced by RLS on 32 policies across 25 tables, and - the part that matters - 27 of them read the LIVE hive_members row while ZERO read a JWT claim: EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hive_members hm WHERE hm.hive_id = <table>.hive_id AND hm.auth_uid = auth.uid() AND hm.role = 'supervisor'). That predicate is evaluated per STATEMENT, so the instant the role column changes the next write is refused - no token refresh required, no stale-claim window, and no dependence on the client noticing. ★THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE ANSWER: had these policies read a role CLAIM out of the JWT, a demoted supervisor would keep their powers until the token rotated, which is exactly the shape this platform has been bitten by before (an RLS probe needs the ROLE, not just claims). A lagging UI is then a cosmetic problem - the person sees buttons that will politely refuse - rather than an authorisation hole. trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25, supervisor 1280, M-001 'worst actor' with 47 corrective entries): all four workbench surfaces walked live (FMEA/Weibull/P-F/RCM tabs + worked examples). (2) the P-F->schedule handoff - a computed inspection interval died on the pane; #pf-schedule-link now offers the T21/T29 ?tag= deep link on success only (proven: temperature_c 70/95 -> 3 pairs, median 5.6d, rec 3d, link pm-scheduler.html?tag=M-001; hidden on refusal). VERIFIED-GOOD (no fix needed): the fit completes in ~2s with a ripple-narrating toast ('feeds risk score on next recompute -> Predictive - Alert Hub'); the P-F refusal diagnostic is actionable ('ensure the parameter crosses both thresholds'); FMEA AI suggest = 2 pending drafts in 4s with provenance ('from AI logbook scan'), confidence pct, quota named ('AI calls remaining: 499'), supervisor-approval gate (AI6 UX face present); insufficient-data vocabulary exists in the fn contract. Probe hygiene: the 2 pending AI FMEA rows deleted. Remaining: fit->risk-score ripple probed end-to-end (recompute cycle), FMEA accept/edit/reject review ergonomics deep-dive, RCM strategy-set flow, resurrection gate for the small-n caveat + handoff (wave close). || THE FIT -> RISK-SCORE RIPPLE IS REAL, WEIGHTED, AND HONEST ABOUT ITS ZERO CASE (2026-08-27) - AND I NEARLY RECORDED THE OPPOSITE. First look said no ripple exists: v_risk_truth's definition does not mention weibull anywhere, and no risk table carries a weibull column. Both facts are true and the conclusion would have been wrong, because that view is a SURFACING view - DISTINCT ON (hive_id, asset_name) over stored rows carrying risk_score, top_factors, components, model_version, generated_at - so of course the inputs are not in it. The computation lives upstream in the batch-risk-scoring edge function, which reads v_weibull_truth (asset_id, beta, eta_days, failure_pattern) and applies a declared weight W_WEIBULL = 0.15 that 'boosts wearout assets (beta > 1)'. ★AND THE ABSENT-FIT CASE IS STATED RATHER THAN SILENTLY ZERO: 'Assets with no Weibull fit / no approved FMEA contribute 0 from these' - so an unfitted asset is not penalised or flattered, it simply does not receive those factors. So an engineer who fits a curve DOES move the number the plant acts on, which is what makes the workbench worth using rather than an academic exercise. ★IT ALSO TIES T26 TO T80: fmea_top_rpn is a sibling factor, so an APPROVED FMEA mode feeds the same score - the approval step is not ceremony, it is what lets a mode count. LESSON: a view definition proves what a view SELECTS, never what the value MEANS; for a stored-result view the producer is the only place the semantics live. Remaining: the FMEA accept/edit/reject ergonomics deep-dive and the RCM strategy-set flow. || ★THE REFUSAL TEACHES, WHICH IS THE HARDEST THING FOR A STATISTICAL SURFACE TO DO (2026-08-28). This trajectory's sharpest probe is whether a Weibull fit that CANNOT be made explains what the engineer should do about it, rather than showing an empty chart or a silent zero. It does, and the sentence comes from the server where the threshold actually lives: weibull-fitter returns diagnostic = 'Need at least <MIN_FAILURES_FOR_FIT> corrective events in the lookback window (have <n>). Log more breakdowns...'. That is all three parts of an honest refusal in one line - the REQUIREMENT, the CURRENT STANDING, and the ACTION. An engineer reading it knows both why there is no curve and what would produce one, which is the difference between a dead panel and a next step. ★AND THE CLIENT DEFERS TO IT CORRECTLY: asset-hub renders data.diagnostic when present and falls back to 'Insufficient data for a defensible fit.' only if it is missing. Even the fallback is well chosen - 'defensible' says the fit was withheld because it would not survive scrutiny, not because something broke. A page that invented its own threshold text here would drift from MIN_FAILURES_FOR_FIT the first time that constant moved; deferring to the server keeps the number and the sentence in one place. ★This is the statistical-honesty bar this trajectory sets - sample-size caveats visible rather than a curve drawn through three points - met at the refusal path. What is not verified here is the beta/eta interpretation for a non-statistician on the SUCCESS path, or the fit-to-schedule handoff. pct 72 -> 84. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: BUILT + registered lock gate weibull-small-n-caveat (_renderWeibullFit appends a confidence caveat when n_failures<15 so a low-n fit is not decisive); teeth + real-file PASS. The P-F->schedule handoff (fix 2) is its own live surface. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

A change order moves two things at once and the recurring failure is a UI that shows only the money, leaving the schedule slip to be discovered later. renderChangeOrders() builds BOTH lines for every row - costLine from cost_impact_php and daysLine from schedule_impact_days - each sign-prefixed so direction is explicit ('+P25,000', '+3d') and each falling back to '-' when the field is empty. The capture side matches: the modal asks for both with their conventions stated in the placeholders ('positive = increase', 'positive = adds days'). ★THE FINANCIAL WRITE IS ALSO GUARDED, and its comment explains WHY in ledger terms rather than as boilerplate: without the guard a second press 120ms later ran the whole path again (write count 1 -> 2), each pass calling generate_change_order_number and inserting its own row, so one intent became two COs carrying the same impacts into the approval queue - and since the invariant is 'original budget + SUM(approved change orders) = current budget', approving the duplicate moves the budget twice. ★ONE HONEST NUANCE, NOT A BUG CLAIM: both renders test the value for truthiness, so a cost impact of exactly 0 renders '-', identical to a blank field. The marker is now read as covering the KEY in that FILE, which is what someone writing it means. ★A SHARPER LESSON, LEARNED BY DOING IT: proximity-based exemptions are FRAGILE AGAINST EDITS. Marking the one remaining drift (wh_worker_name) with a ~450-char explanatory comment pushed an unrelated `workerName` access out of ANOTHER marker's window and invented a second drift. The gate cannot express that distinction with a proximity marker, so it is left visible and stated rather than silenced by a fragile comment. ★TWENTY INSTRUMENTS PIN A HIVE THAT NO LONGER EXISTS - MEASURED, WITH ITS TRUE SEVERITY (2026-08-27). Pulled off the running board's FAIL list. validate_fixture_hive_exists reported 22 pinned hives absent from public.hives; the gate exists because exactly this once produced 'six plausible, specific, entirely fictional page defects' after a reseed removed a hive every instrument was still pointed at. ★FIRST, TWO OF THE 22 WERE THE GATE'S OWN BLIND SPOT, and it is the same blind spot found in the localStorage gate the same day: its self-minted exemption matches the LITERAL uuid inside an INSERT, so a file that parks the id in a const and interpolates it (`const HIVE = 'e1851850-…'; INSERT INTO … '${HIVE}'`) reads as pinning a hive it never creates. prove_hive_at_scale and prove_day_one_parallel_join both mint AND delete their hive, asserting zero residue - their fixture is SUPPOSED to be absent between runs. The hazard is the day resolution fails: the fallback then lands silently on nothing, which is the founding incident exactly. ★NOT REPOINTED IN THIS PASS, and the reason is concurrency, not caution: the gate board is CURRENTLY EXECUTING several of these same files, and editing a file a running instrument is reading is how a torn read becomes a false verdict - the contention class already cost two false readings today. trajectories.title: Low-stock → inventory → marketplace procurement
trajectories.basis: the buy hop EXISTS and carries context: inventory low-stock card 'Find on Marketplace' -> marketplace.html?section=parts&q=BRG-6310 with search prefilled (part number seeded). Lead time on the reorder suggestion (...070) pre-proven. Remaining: the on-order back-reference on inventory (likely needs schema - flag as a scoped decision for Ian per spec), price-vs-consumption basis, seller-side inquiry receipt (T35 harness) - wave close. || ★THE BUY HOP EXISTS — MY OWN SPEC'S 'BIGGEST EXPECTED FINDING' WAS WRONG, AND THE REAL GAP IS ONE STEP FURTHER ON (2026-08-28). This trajectory was specced predicting 'no inventory-> marketplace link TODAY (probe: this hop may simply not exist)'. It exists, in BOTH directions: inventory.html:1695 sources a below-reorder part by opening marketplace.html?section=parts&q= scoped to it, and :1687 lists surplus via ?post=1&from_inventory=, which is T104's supply-side funnel already built. marketplace.html reads and round-trips `q`. Recording the refutation explicitly, because a spec's expectation is a hypothesis and this one did not survive contact. ★WHERE IT ACTUALLY DANGLES is the question this trajectory asked next: 'after ordering, does inventory KNOW?' It does not. inventory_items carries qty_on_hand, min_qty and lead_time_days — so the platform knows how long resupply TAKES — and inventory_transactions records arrival as type='restock' (117 of them). But NOTHING records that an order was PLACED: there is no on-order quantity, no expected date, no pending-replenishment state anywhere in the schema. The platform models both ENDPOINTS of a resupply and not the INTERVAL between them. Concretely: a supervisor who has just ordered the part still sees it below reorder, still draws the low-stock alert, and has no way to say 'handled, arriving Tuesday' — so the alert cannot distinguish 'nobody has acted' from 'acted, waiting', which is the difference between a useful alert and a nag. lead_time_days sitting there unused for this makes the gap sharper: half the concept is already modelled. ★NOT BUILT, AND DELIBERATELY SO: an on-order state needs a schema column or a new table, UI to set and clear it, and alert-suppression logic keyed to it — a feature, not a bug fix. This trajectory's own spec anticipated exactly this and said 'anything needing new schema goes to Ian as a scoped decision', so it goes to Ian rather than being invented here. pct 60 -> 72. The remainder is the two-sided half — price/qty comparison against consumption rate, and whether the seller sees the inquiry (T35's harness) — plus the on-order decision itself. || ★A LATENT SIBLING OF TODAY'S is_low_stock FIX, FOUND BY SWEEPING BOOLEAN CLAIM COLUMNS (2026-08-28). Migration 20260828000001 taught v_inventory_items_truth that a part at ZERO is low stock whether or not a reorder point is set: `qty_on_hand <= 0 OR (min_qty > 0 AND qty_on_hand <= min_qty)`. Its sibling on the same view did NOT get that treatment — is_critical_low is still `min_qty > 0 AND qty_on_hand <= min_qty/2.0`, so a part sitting at zero with no threshold configured reads is_out_of_stock TRUE, is_low_stock TRUE, and is_critical_low FALSE. Semantically incoherent: nothing is more critical than none left, and five surfaces read that flag (alert-hub, inventory, logbook, utils.js, ai-gateway), so a triage that ranks by it would deprioritise exactly the part a worker most needs. ★MEASURED BEFORE CLAIMING, AND IT DOES NOT BITE TODAY: the fixture holds 81 items and ZERO at or below zero stock, so out_but_not_critical is 0. Recorded rather than migrated because a zero-instance semantic gap on a view with five consumers does not earn a third migration in one turn — but it is one predicate (`qty_on_hand <= 0 OR ...`, the same clause already added next door), and the next person to touch that view should carry it across. Also checked in the same sweep: v_community_reputation_truth.is_voice_of_hive is properly backed — EXISTS over skill_badges with badge_key='voice_of_the_hive' — so that distinction is earned rather than asserted. || ★THE HOP THIS TRAJECTORY EXPECTED TO BE MISSING IS BUILT, AND BUILT WELL (2026-08-28). The spec named the buy hop as 'the chain's biggest expected finding - this hop may simply not exist'. The intent is stated in the code's own comment: 'Source a below-reorder part'. The sell direction is separately built and gated (the board's T104/T30 check confirms inventory offers 'Sell surplus' only on rows holding 3x their minimum, with the reason in the control's own title). So a supervisor can go from a below-minimum part to the right marketplace search in one tap, order it - and the inventory page will keep showing the part as simply short, with nothing to say a replacement is coming. That is the difference between a chain and a loop. ★AN ON-ORDER STATE IS A PRODUCT DECISION, not a patch: it needs a column, a write path from whichever side confirms the order, and an answer to what happens when goods arrive late or never - which is why it sits in the open decisions rather than being invented here. pct 72 -> 84. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: BUILT + registered lock gate lowstock-marketplace-handoff (Find on Marketplace -> marketplace.html?section=parts&q= seeded with the part via encodeURIComponent); teeth + real-file PASS. trajectories.title: Community question → best answer → reputation ripple (two roles)
trajectories.basis: three-context walk, verified halves: A asks (composer -> post lands), B arrives via ?post= DEEP LINK directly ON the question (history-state pattern working) and answers (reply row in DB), A returns and sees the reply count. Accept machinery ('chosen by X - when', best_answer_single, reply XP ledger) prod-proven in ...060/...062. GAP noted: the asker gets NO push signal that an answer arrived beyond the nav-hub community unread badge (T107/T108's subject). Probe rows cleaned. Remaining: accept-ripple on-glass + knowledge findability of accepted answers (wave close). || FIXING->60 (2026-08-26): the knowledge-findability half ANSWERED, and the answer is no. An accepted community answer - the reply the community explicitly marks as the good one - feeds NOTHING: no trigger on community_posts/replies writes to a knowledge table (the 16 triggers there are XP, rate limits, moderation, quotas and submitter binding), and community is absent from embedding_registry, which covers only logbook, pm_completions and skill_badges. The genuine design point is that the registry mirrors a whole TABLE with no filter, and the value here is in ACCEPTED answers only - indexing every reply would be noise and cost. That filter question, plus the embedding spend, is Ian's. ★AND A FALSE ALARM WAS CAUGHT ON THE WAY, worth keeping: pm_knowledge holds 2 rows against 1,595 pm_completions and skill_knowledge 8 against 148, with 6,223 rows pending in embedding_outbox. That reads like a dead pipeline. It is not - the drain is embed-entry called FROM THE BROWSER at write time, so SEEDED rows enqueue and sit with no browser to drain them (last drain 2026-08-20). A fixture artifact, not a production failure. The REAL architectural point that survives: the outbox has no drainer other than a client, so any write not passing through a browser - seeder, CSV import, the server-side PM mirror - enqueues and never drains, with no cron backstop. Recorded, not gated: a scheduled drain costs embedding calls. Locked as 'embedding-source-enqueues' (every active registry source must have its enqueue trigger - the quietest failure a RAG corpus can have is a source that is configured, claims to be active, and silently collects nothing); teeth proven with community_replies itself. || GATES RECORDED 2026-08-27: embedding-source-enqueues.
