trajectories.note: ★THE LINEAGE IS ALREADY ON THE GLASS, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS - VERIFIED (2026-08-27). T32 asks whether a human can FOLLOW the number's movement between the logbook and PM compliance. They can, and the mechanism is not the one the spec assumed. PM -> LOGBOOK: an entry minted by the pm-scheduler mirror carries a 'pm-' id prefix and the entry renders a 'via PM Scheduler' badge, so a reader can tell a mirrored entry from a hand-typed one. LOGBOOK -> PM: submitting an entry with PM tasks ticked inserts pm_completions with notes 'Logged via Logbook: <machine>', and pm-scheduler RENDERS those notes italicised beside the completion - so the supervisor sees where it came from. Measured: 5 of 1,596 completions carry that origin today, so the path is live but lightly used in the fixture. ★AND I NEARLY RECORDED THE OPPOSITE. pm_completions has no source/origin COLUMN - id, asset_id, scope_item_id, hive_id, worker_name, status, notes, completed_at, auth_uid - and the obvious inference from a schema read is 'the row cannot say where it came from, so the glass cannot either'. The origin lives in NOTES, which is a weaker contract than a column (nothing stops a hand-typed note mimicking it) but is genuinely rendered and genuinely readable. Reading the render rather than stopping at the schema is what turned a false finding into a verified positive. ★THE FAILURE PATH IS HONEST TOO: when the completion insert fails the worker is told 'Entry saved. Its PM tasks did NOT record, so those PMs still count as due' - the entry and its mirror reported separately, which is exactly right when only one of them landed. REMAINS for T32: whether the compliance % delta names WHICH window moved.

trajectories.title: Resume: upload → extract → review → export
trajectories.basis: EXTRACT->REVIEW PROVEN with a real file: a .txt resume through the file-any input ran the extractor ('Reading file 1 of 1') and the review surface holds the file's ACTUAL content (employer/cert/skill strings verbatim) with keep/discard/merge vocabulary - the AI-draft-review shape works end-to-end. Upload formats broad, hive-grounded autofill runs, PDF/Word/Print exports present. Remaining: dedupe-against-hive-history visibility, export fidelity vs JSON Resume + ATS rules (skill-as-oracle), phone-side review ergonomics (wave close). || THE SKILL WAS THE ORACLE, AND IT NAMED AN ASSERTION THE SUITE DID NOT HAVE (2026-08-27). Retrieved resume-builder/SKILL.md rather than re-deriving ATS rules. Its grounded checklist item 6 asks THREE things of export - the preview opens and renders, ATS-plain shows NO EMPTY SECTION HEADERS, and the required ordering is present. journey-resume.spec.ts has 164 assertions covering all seven checklist items, and its export test covered only the first: preview opens, name renders, template toggle works. No test in the file mentioned empty section headers or ordering at all. ★THE BEHAVIOUR WAS ALREADY CORRECT - every section is emitted behind an `if (_present(...).length)` guard, so an empty section prints nothing - which makes this the verified-but-unguarded case: nothing stopped a later refactor from hoisting those headings out of their guards, and an ATS parses HEADINGS to segment a resume, so a bare 'EXPERIENCE' over nothing can make it read the next section's content as work history. Added both assertions; both pass. ★AND THE FIRST VERSION PASSED VACUOUSLY - TWICE, IN TWO DIFFERENT WAYS. (1) sec() emits 'Experience' but .r-sec-title is text-transform:uppercase, and Playwright's innerText APPLIES the transform, so the DOM text is 'EXPERIENCE' - .not.toContainText('Experience') could never match either way. (2) Fixing that with .not.toHaveText(/Experience/i) was vacuous AGAIN, because toHaveText matches the WHOLE text and a resume page is never just that word; the searching form is toContainText. A negative assertion whose subject cannot occur is not a test, it is a green light wired to nothing - and it is the SECOND-hardest kind of bug to see, because everything is green. The pair is now non-vacuous BY CONSTRUCTION: the ordering test is the positive control, asserting the same headings in the same template DO render (and in order) once sections have content. ★HONOURED THE FILE'S OWN MEMENTO LESSON: seeded via WHResume.set(), which renders and saves LOCALLY, rather than the upload path - a live Save writes a resume_documents row that a sibling journey loads on init and reddens the dedupe test. Remaining: dedupe-against-hive-history visibility and the phone export path. || THE PHONE EXPORT PATH WALKED AT 390 AND IT IS SOUND - AND MY FIRST PROBE OF IT WAS THE DEFECT (2026-08-28). Reading 1: one export control at rest, and exportJSON() returning no blob - which looked like a broken export. BOTH halves were the instrument. (1) The real controls do not exist at rest; they live behind 'Preview & Export' and had to be OPENED the way a person opens them. (2) exportJSON is PAGE-SCOPED, so `typeof exportJSON === 'function'` is false from the probe's world - the recorded page-scoped-symbols trap, and the hooks had to be installed with addInitScript so they live in the page's own scope before its scripts run. WHAT THE CORRECTED WALK SHOWS: four controls (#btn-export, #pv-pdf, #pv-print, #pv-json), every one >=44px on its MIN dimension and none past the right edge at 390; JSON emits an application/json blob with a real filename (Bryan_Garcia_jsonresume.json); PDF emits an application/pdf blob, and html2pdf loads in PROD too - it comes from cdn.jsdelivr.net, which _headers' script-src already allows, so this is NOT the prod-only-CSP class that killed mic+camera. ★THE INTERESTING ONE IS PRINT, because it is the only path that can be REFUSED BY THE DEVICE: it opens a popup, and phones block popups. Simulated that exact condition (window.open -> null) and the refusal SPEAKS - 'Allow pop-ups to print.' rendered visibly and was still readable ~3.9s later, so it names the problem AND the remedy and does not flash past at zero milliseconds. No page errors on any path. Remaining: dedupe-against-hive-history visibility. || ★THE REVIEW SHEET IS THE SHAPE THIS TRAJECTORY ASKED FOR (2026-08-28). The probe is whether a worker can accept, edit or reject each extracted item rather than being handed a finished CV to take or leave. Every row renders three things: a checkbox (aria-label 'Include this item') which is the accept/reject, an editable wh-input carrying the value with a per-item aria-label ('Edit <label>'), and srcChip(it.src) - a PROVENANCE chip naming where that line came from. That third element is the one most implementations omit and the one this trajectory specifically wants: it is how a worker sees WHY an item is there and whether it was merged from their hive history, rather than trusting a black box that assembled their work record. A live updateReviewCount() and escHtml() on every interpolated value complete it. ★AND THE A11Y IS DELIBERATE RATHER THAN ACCIDENTAL: the sheet explicitly does NOT call trapFocus(), with the reason written inline - it is a .sheet-overlay, so whModalA11y owns the trap and the focus restore. Two components both trapping focus is how a dialog becomes impossible to leave with a keyboard. ★The raw-survives-polish discipline is visible too, with 22 references to raw/original/revert paths. What is not verified here is the export artifact itself against the JSON Resume schema and the ATS rules in the resume-builder skill - the skill IS the oracle for that half and it is a separate check. pct 72 -> 84. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - the resume flow is a per-item review sheet (accept/edit/reject + checkboxes), not a take-or-leave CV; new teeth-tested gate resume-review-sheet (live PASS). pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Seller lists a part with credit reservation
trajectories.basis:
walked 390: composer opens via fab-post (requirePostAccount passed), AI-assist disclosed with review-before-posting, photo guidance, review-before-publish stated. FOUND+FIXED the cost-transparency break at the EXACT commit point: the composer said 'The marketplace is free... no platform fees' while guard_listing_requires_reservation holds 10% of price in credits at publish (measured live: P100 held on P1,000; hold returns on remove/redraft, funds the reward on sale). The sentence now states the whole truth. DB-proven guards (refusal names way out) pre-receipted. Remaining: the zero-credit refusal -> top-up -> draft-survives round trip (needs a broke-account choreography - wave close). || ★THE REFUSAL IS ALREADY GOOD — better than this trajectory assumed — AND THE GAP IS ONE STEP PAST IT (2026-08-28). Walked the credit-reservation refusal. It states the seller's REAL balance, the REAL floor, what the money is FOR ('it is not a fee - it is spent on your own commission when you get paid'), and names the remedy ('Top up via GCash'). Its sibling refusal does the same for badges: not_certified names WHICH trade, the level needed, and points at the Skill Matrix exam, with a comment stating the principle outright — 'a refusal with no route forward is just a wall'. The page's own history shows this was hard-won: a comment records that when the balance floor moved, the message did not, and a provider sitting at +150 was told their balance was NEGATIVE, 'which is both false and unactionable'. So the why_refused bar is met, and the cost-transparency question this trajectory asks is answered YES. ★WHAT REMAINS IS THE way-out-WALKABLE half: the remedy is PROSE. marketplace-seller's local showToast(msg, type) takes no action, so 'Top up via GCash' is a sentence, not a door — the seller must find the top-up flow themselves, though it does live on this same page. The platform already has the pattern and it is scoped too narrowly: whAuthRequiredToast() in utils.js renders a refusal whose remedy is CLICKABLE, but only for auth. Generalising it to any refusal-with-a-remedy is the move, and it is an enhancement rather than a defect — the path exists and the refusal names it, so nothing is broken or lying. Recorded with the existing helper named so the next pass extends it instead of writing a third toast. pct 60 -> 76. || ★THE COST IS NAMED AT THE COMMITMENT POINT, AND IT PREEMPTS THE OBJECTION (2026-08-28). This trajectory's first probe is whether the credit requirement is explained BEFORE a seller does the work of drafting, rather than sprung on them as a refusal. The copy sits in a

immediately above the publish button and reads: 'Publishing holds 10%% of the price in credits. It is not a fee: it comes back in full if the listing does not sell, and goes to your buyer as their reward if it does.' Three things right in one sentence - the AMOUNT, the explicit denial of the reading a seller would otherwise reach for ('it is not a fee'), and the outcome in BOTH branches. A hold whose fate is unstated is indistinguishable from a charge, and this states it. ★THE WAY OUT IS HEAVILY WIRED: 40 references to the top-up path across the seller surface, so the refusal names a remedy that exists rather than a dead end - the refusal-way-out-walkable oracle this trajectory specs. Combined with T103's finding that the displayed rate and the enforced amount both derive from service_knob_pct('reward_pct'), the number in that sentence cannot drift from the number charged. ★I NEARLY RECORDED THE OPPOSITE. The same claim also appears at line 311 as a SOURCE COMMENT ('CREDIT WALLET. A seller cannot publish without holding 10%%...'), and finding that first made it look as though the platform explained itself only to its own developers. Re-checking through a comment-strip - HTML comments, block comments and line comments removed the way this project's own gates do it - showed the user-facing

survives. A file that documents its own behaviour in comments will answer a careless grep with its rationale instead of its interface, in both directions: it can hide a real disclosure as easily as it can fake one. pct 76 -> 86. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: BUILT + registered lock gate listing-cost-transparency asserting the composer states the 10% credit hold AND its return-if-unsold, with a regression guard against a bare no-fees/free claim; teeth self-test PASSES + real file PASSES. The zero-credit->top-up->draft round trip remains a live wave-close item, but the cost-disclosure invariant (the seed fix) is now locked. Registered in run_platform_checks. Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Buyer hails a service → provider accepts (two-sided truth)
trajectories.basis: the buyer's COMPOSE half walked: the asset-hub hail chip's contract KEPT (svc-quote-scope prefilled '[GEN-001] Service call for Caterpillar 3516B' - my earlier 'not precomposed' was a body-text-only read); hail without a service = NAMED refusal ('Pick a service first'); presence honest ('7 providers online now - Manila (4), Angeles (1), Baguio (1)'); picking a certified trade surfaces the badge requirement + expiry + no-charge BEFORE commit. The hail needs the full compose (address/urgency/TTL) to insert - the two-sided accept lifecycle (davidvelasco's console, state agreement, windows) is the dedicated slice (wave close). || THE TWO SCREENS TELL ONE STORY, AND THEY DO IT THE RIGHT WAY (2026-08-27). The risk in a two-sided lifecycle is that each side invents its own words, so buyer and provider describe the same moment differently and neither can tell whether they are looking at the same job. That is not what happens here. ONE state machine - service_requests' CHECK enumerates requested, broadcasting, accepted, en_route, on_site, in_progress, completed, settled, plus the exits - and each surface maps it to language addressed to WHOEVER IS READING. marketplace-seller's SVC_STATUS_LABEL speaks to the provider ('Accepted: head over', 'On the way', 'On site', 'Marked done, waiting on the client'); marketplace's SVC_CHIP speaks to the client about the same rows ('Provider accepted', 'Provider on the way', 'Provider on site'), and in_progress renders as 'Work in progress' on BOTH because at that moment there is nothing perspectival left to say. ★THAT IS THE DISTINCTION WORTH RECORDING: 'same words on both screens' would actually be the wrong bar - telling a client 'head over' is nonsense, and telling a provider 'Provider on the way' is a sentence about themselves in the third person. What must agree is the STATE and the EVENT it names; the sentence should change with the reader. One vocabulary underneath, two viewpoints on top. ★AND THE BUYER GETS THE PRE-BROADCAST STATES TOO ('Draft', 'Finding a provider...'), so the waiting period before anyone accepts is narrated rather than blank - the same silence problem this session found on the goods side, already solved here. Remaining: the settle/dispute tail walked live with a seeded active request (the fixture T102 also needs). || ★ONE VOCABULARY, ENFORCED BY THE DATABASE, SO THE TWO SCREENS CANNOT DRIFT APART (2026-08-28). The property this trajectory turns on is that buyer and provider tell ONE story at every step. service_requests.status is CHECK-constrained to a single lifecycle - requested, broadcasting, accepted, en_route, on_site, in_progress, completed, settled - so neither surface can invent a state the other does not know, and a new one cannot be introduced quietly by a page. Comparing what each side actually renders: marketplace (the buyer) uses broadcasting, en_route, on_site, in_progress, settled; marketplace-seller (the provider) uses en_route, on_site, in_progress, settled. Identical on every state they SHARE, and the single difference is correct - 'broadcasting' is the window where the request is being offered TO providers, which is a state the buyer waits in and the provider experiences as an incoming offer rather than a status of their own. ★AND CANCELLATION NAMES ITS AUTHOR: the allowed set includes cancelled_by_client AND cancelled_by_provider as distinct values rather than one 'cancelled'. That is the two-sided honesty this trajectory asks for, encoded where it cannot be lost - neither party can be shown a vague 'this was cancelled' that hides who walked away, and a dispute later (T97) can read the answer off the row. ★WHAT REMAINS is timing rather than vocabulary: whether the acceptance WINDOW is visible to both sides while it is running, and whether completion-to-settlement is legible as it happens. Those need the two-context walk with a live request. pct 78 -> 88. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - buyer & provider tell ONE story: service_requests.status is CHECK-constrained to a single lifecycle and every state is reachable - the two screens cannot drift. Gates [service-state-machine, lifecycle-state-reachability] registered + PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; both named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

fixes: marketplace.html: svcHailNow + svcAskQuotes busy-guarded (shared with T41 - a manual hail carries no unique)
marketplace-seller.html: the finished-job card reports amount, method, ref and the payer's variance reason

trajectories.note: ★STATE AGREEMENT MEASURED ACROSS BOTH SIDES AND FOUND SOUND - and it is better than the probe asked for. The spec wanted 'the same words on both screens'; what ships is the same STATE described from each party's position, which is the right answer. service_requests has a 12-value status CHECK, and every shared one carries a label on each side: cancelled_by_client reads 'You cancelled' to the buyer and 'The client cancelled' to the provider; cancelled_by_provider reads 'Provider cancelled' / 'You cancelled this job'; en_route reads 'Provider on the way' / 'On the way'; completed reads 'Completed' / 'Marked done, waiting on the client', where the provider's is MORE informative because it tells them what happens next. No state where the two sides disagree about what occurred. requested and broadcasting have no provider label, correctly - a request still being broadcast has not reached a specific provider, so there is nothing for them to see. The dispute door exists as a first-class state ('In dispute' / 'The client reported a problem'). FIXED here under T41: a manual hail was not idempotent (the service_requests unique covers AUTO hails via pm_scope_item_id only), so a double press fanned a second request out to every provider; both svcHailNow and svcAskQuotes are now busy-guarded. REMAINS: the acceptance WINDOW's visibility on both sides, and settlement -> credit movement as a two-context walk. ★THE PAYER WRITES AN EXPLANATION NOBODY CAN READ - MEASURED (2026-08-27). From the same captured-but-never-rendered sweep: service_payments is INSERTED by marketplace.html:4734 and read by NOTHING - no page, no edge function, no view. The row is not useless (the guard_settle_requires_payment trigger consumes it server-side to gate settlement), but its human content is inert. variance_reason is what a payer TYPES to explain paying an amount other than the one agreed, and all 4 rows in the table carry one. The provider who receives an unexpected figure cannot read the reason the payer wrote for them - and the page takes variance seriously enough to guard it, quoting its own refusal verbatim ('This is 40% of the agreed ₱2,000…') before storing the answer where no one will look. ★THE DATABASE ALREADY EXPECTED A READER: policy service_payments_read grants SELECT to the client, the matched provider (matched_provider_id IN my_service_provider_ids()) and marketplace admins. The access was designed; the UI to use it was never built. amount_paid, method, gcash_ref and confirmed_by are equally unread. FIX SCOPED (needs the two-context walk, so it is built with the browser free, not guessed): read the payment on the provider's side of a settled request and render the amount, the method and the payer's reason. ★BUILT (2026-08-27): the provider's finished-job card now reports the payment. It showed the service, the status and the client and NO MONEY AT ALL - the one card that reports a provider's completed work never said what they were paid. It now renders the amount (via whFmtPeso, the shared formatter), the method, the GCash reference, and - in its own bordered note so it cannot be mistaken for the figure - 'Why this amount:' carrying the payer's variance_reason. The read mirrors the ratings fetch directly above it, including the degrade-quietly posture: a payment that cannot be read must never blank the finished-jobs list. No migration and no policy change were needed - service_payments_read already granted the matched provider SELECT. ★THE RATCHET GATE CONFIRMED ITS OWN FIX: captured-columns-reach-a-reader went 8 -> 7 and printed 'reached a reader since the baseline: variance_reason'. confirmed_by stays unrendered deliberately and its baseline reason was rewritten to say why - it is a raw auth uid, and printing a UID would trade this defect for the no-raw-internals one. STILL OWED on T35: the live two-context walk (client pays an off-amount with a reason, provider reads it), and live_location - a provider's GPS, written while en route and never shown to the client waiting for them. ★CORRECTION TO MY OWN RECORD (2026-08-27): I listed live_location as a GAP - 'a provider's GPS, written while en route and never shown to the client waiting for them'. MEASURED, it is 0 of 7 providers. The write path exists (marketplace-seller updates it from geolocation) and has never populated a single row, so nothing is being withheld from anyone - it is unused, the same verdict as acted_by, not a render defect. The gate's baseline reason now says so. Whether the geolocation flow is reachable at all is a separate question for the live walk; what is NOT true is that clients are being denied a location the system holds.

trajectories.title: Engineering calc → BOM/SOW → project import
trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25, supervisor 1280): the calc->BOM->SOW chain walked end-to-end on Cable Tray Sizing - the AI-assisted calc completes ~10s with standards-grade output (fill 2151mm2, required width 71.71mm -> selected 100mm per NEMA VE 1, NEC 392/PEC 2017 cited); the generated BOM is GROUNDED (33m = the 30m input + a NAMED 10% cutting allowance; computed 100x75mm carried into specs; unknowable quantities honestly labeled 'placeholder / per routing plan'); the checklist is editable (12 items, add/remove); the preview is a real document (doc no., preparer attribution, design basis, For Review status, CSV/PDF, AI-drafted disclosure note). THE CENTRAL FINDING, measured: bom_data + sow_text were WRITE-ONLY - no code on project-manager read them; the Contractor tile promised 'Extends Engineering Design BOM/SOW' with no implementation, so every computed BOM was re-typed by hand (the exact re-entry the done-definition forbids; also a claim-honesty defect). FIX BUILT: #modal-bom-import chooser on the Scope pane (both empty+populated branches) listing hive calcs with BOMs -> one tap imports each line as a project_item with qty+unit in the title and provenance in notes, then lands back on the Scope tab (refreshDetail resets to Overview and would hide the receipt). PROVEN live: 6->18 items, 'Anchor bolts M16 - 8 pcs' etc., zero pageerrors; probe rows cleaned. Remaining: SOW-text import (description/notes decision), wizard-level contractor integration matching the tile's claim, X2 calc-result survival across the auth wall, embedded-vs-app calc parity (T153 seam), double-import semantics note, resurrection gate (wave close). || ★THE CHAIN CARRIES ITS CONTEXT, AND THE ONE APPARENT LOSS IS THE SCHEMA BEING HONEST (2026-08-28). Walked calc -> BOM/SOW -> project import. THE HANDOFF IS COMPLETE: the engineering-bom-sow call sends discipline, calc_type, calc_inputs AND calc_results, so the generator sees everything the engineer entered and everything the calc produced - nothing is retyped, which is this trajectory's first and most important probe. The call is bounded by a client-side timeout, so a hung generation ends rather than hanging the engineer with it. ★THE IMPORT FLATTENS QUANTITY INTO THE TITLE - 'Copper pipe - 12 m' - and I checked whether that was a loss before calling it one. It is not: project_items has NO qty and NO unit column. Its shape is work-management (wbs_code, owner_name, status, pct_complete, planned/actual dates, estimated_hours, predecessors), because a project item is a piece of WORK, not a piece of MATERIAL. There is nowhere structured for a BOM quantity to live, so the title is the only carrier available and putting it there is adaptation rather than data loss. The honest statement of the probe's answer: the value SURVIVES and is visible, but it is text, so nothing downstream can sum or re-order by it. ★AND PROVENANCE TRAVELS, which the probe did not ask for: each imported row's notes carry the spec, the remarks, and 'Imported from Engineering Design: <calc_type>', so a scope item can be traced back to the calculation that produced it months later. ★ONE COSMETIC EDGE: a missing quantity renders literally as '?' in the title ('Copper pipe - ? m'), which is at least honest about being unknown rather than inventing a number. pct 60 -> 76. || ★THE CALC-TO-BOM HANDOFF CARRIES BOTH THE INPUTS AND THE RESULTS (2026-08-28). This trajectory's north star is that a computed design becomes an executable project 'without retyping a number', and the first hop delivers it: engineering-design invokes engineering-bom-sow with discipline, calc_type, calc_inputs (_lastInputs) AND calc_results (_lastResults). Sending BOTH halves is the part that matters. Inputs alone would force the generator to re-derive the answer and risk disagreeing with what the engineer just saw on screen; results alone would leave it unable to explain or adjust a quantity. Carrying both means the bill of materials is grounded in the exact calculation that produced it, which is also what makes the SOW text checkable rather than confabulated. ★AND THE CALL IS BOUNDED: invokeWithTimeout, annotated 'AI-4: bounded by a client-side timeout', so a slow or dead BOM function fails visibly instead of leaving an engineer watching a spinner - the T146 discipline applied at the point where an AI call is doing real design work. ★WHAT REMAINS unverified is the far end of the chain: whether the generated BOM arrives in project-manager as scope items with quantities intact (values_survive_the_write on the glass), and whether the standards citations travel all the way through. Those need the chain walked with a real calculation rather than read from the payload. pct 76 -> 86. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - calc -> BOM/SOW -> project carries inputs AND results without retyping: bom_sow_grounding + agent-handoff-contract prove the handoff contract holds. Gates [bom_sow_grounding, agent-handoff-contract, asset-pm-handoff-carries-context] registered + PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100. || REVERTED 2026-09-04: named gate FAILED on the 1034/60 board (false 100%; post_board_promote over-locked). pct -> 90. · [2026-09-05] pct -> 100. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_cross_page_chains.mjs (gate cross-page-chains), 4/4 lenses clean. These four rows are about lineage, which no single page can answer, and the discipline is that a chain is proven by the LINK rather than by both ends existing - two pages that each work with nothing joining them is exactly the failure they exist to catch. Twenty parts sit below their minimum, inventory flags them and offers a route onward to the marketplace, and the join that carries the thread (marketplace_listings.source_inventory_item_id) was TRAVERSED rather than merely found in the schema: zero rows had ever used it, so the walk created a listing from a real short part, read it back to confirm the link survived the write, and deleted it - the listing count is 28 before and after (T30). All 111 live community posts name their author, a good answer can be marked, and answering feeds eleven durable surfaces including worker_achievements, skill_profiles and v_community_reputation_truth, so contributing returns something that outlives the thread (T31). 3,820 logbook entries carry a maintenance type against 1,606 PM completions, joined through three shared asset columns, and compliance reads v_pm_compliance_truth from the same work - so doing the job is recording it rather than doing it twice (T32). The calculator produces a bill of materials and offers the hand-off, the project manager accepts one, and 90 project items exist across 12 projects, so a calculation becomes work instead of a number somebody retypes - which is where transcription errors live (T36). One honesty note kept in the prover: bom_knowledge is empty in this data, so K4's claim rests on the mechanism at both ends rather than on a traversal, and it says so.

trajectories.title: Slow-3G phone pass: skeleton honesty + perceived performance
trajectories.basis: the throttle-lane instrument BUILT (tools/prove_throttled_first_paint.mjs: CDP Slow-3G, first-content poll, skeletons@10s, SLOW-HONEST/STUCK-SKELETON/BLANK vocabulary, report JSON) and its FIRST RUN SELF-REFUTED: logbook (360KB) 'painted at 1.3s' under a 50KB/s profile - impossible, so the CDP throttle is NOT BINDING on this loopback setup and the 3 BLANK verdicts (hive/alert-hub/dayplanner) are equally unbankable (verify the instrument before the page). Calibration rails needed: a throttle-bind assertion (a timed known-size fetch) + page-aware content markers vs boot-gate chrome. NO findings banked from run 1 (five-faults discipline). Wave close: calibrate, then sweep. || FIXING->60 (2026-08-26): the PP1 first-paint half measured and locked. With every REST read throttled 1.5s, all 8 core signed-in pages paint their shell in 208-456ms against an 1800ms budget - so a slow connection never shows a blank screen. This pairs with 'waiting-is-spoken' from the same session, which proved the resulting GAP is filled with something honest (4 pages skeleton, 4 loading-text, zero silent): together they cover PP1's two halves - the gap starts fast and then says what it is. ★THE PROVER MANUFACTURED A FINDING FIRST, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE REUSABLE PART: reusing one browser context and walking pages in sequence, analytics.html - SIXTH in the run - reported 2220ms against 212-292ms for everything else. It looked exactly like a page whose paint waits on a slow read, and 2220 is suspiciously close to the injected 1500ms plus overhead. Measured ALONE it paints in 400ms unthrottled and 368ms THROTTLED: the 2220 was contention from the five pages before it, still holding delayed routes and competing for one renderer. The number described the HARNESS. The prover now closes each page before the next and RE-MEASURES anything over budget in a fresh context before reporting it, so only a page still slow BY ITSELF is a finding - a performance gate without that step will eventually accuse a healthy page, and someone then hunts a cause that is not there. Locked as 'first-paint-throttled'; teeth proven end to end at a 120ms budget (6 flagged, each confirmed alone). REMAINING: the LCP-is-the-right-element check and the premature-tap question across the roster (wave close). || GATES RECORDED 2026-08-27: first-paint-throttled. The basis already named this instrument as built and it IS registered in run_platform_checks and green — the gates field was simply never filled, so the registry understated what this trajectory owns. Verified registered + exit 0 before recording; nothing about the work changed, only the bookkeeping. || MEASURED BY AN ORPHANED PROVER NOBODY WAS RUNNING (2026-08-28). tools/prove_throttled_first_paint.mjs walks the Slow-3G lane (CDP emulateNetworkConditions, 500ms RTT / ~400kbps - the real shape, which context.route cannot produce) signed in as a worker against the correct /workhive/ base, and it is registered NOWHERE and invoked by NOTHING. Its reading: index 3.9s, logbook 1.6s, inventory 1.1s, community 1.4s to first meaningful content - and FOUR pages BLANK at the 10s mark, pm-scheduler, hive, alert-hub and dayplanner, meaning under 400 visible characters after ten seconds on plant wifi at its worst. ★RECORDED AS A MEASUREMENT, NOT YET A DEFECT CLAIM: BLANK here means 'did not cross the bar inside the window', not 'never paints', and the bar (400 chars / 10s) is this prover's own choice. What is certain is the SPLIT - four pages clear it comfortably and four do not clear it at all, on the same run, same account, same throttle - which is too clean to be noise and is exactly the lane this trajectory exists to walk. Next: confirm whether the four eventually paint and where the time goes (request waterfall), before any fix. It is a findings-RECORDER by construction, which is the honest reason it was never gated - but it should still be RUN, and it was not being. || ★MY ATTEMPT TO CONFIRM THE FOUR BLANK PAGES PRODUCED A VOID READING, AND I ALMOST BANKED IT AS A REFUTATION (2026-08-28). I re-walked pm-scheduler, hive, alert-hub and dayplanner with a longer 30s window and my own CDP throttle, and got first-content of 0.1-0.6s on all four - FASTER than the logbook control - which reads exactly like 'the prover was wrong, the pages are fine'. It is not. 0.1s first content is physically impossible at 500ms RTT: the first request alone costs half a second. Tested the instrument directly by running the same page throttled and UNTHROTTLED - both 0.1s, identical - so my emulateNetworkConditions never applied and every number that probe produced measures an unthrottled load. THE READING IS VOID AND REFUTES NOTHING; prove_throttled_first_paint's four BLANKs stand exactly as recorded, still a measurement awaiting confirmation rather than a defect claim. ★THE TELL WAS THE IMPOSSIBLY GOOD NUMBER, the same shape as an impossibly uniform one: 0.1s under Slow-3G should have been unbelievable before it was convenient. Next: confirm with a throttle proven to bite (assert an unthrottled/throttled DELTA before trusting any figure), then read the request waterfall on the four. || ★CONFIRMED WITH AN INSTRUMENT PROVEN TO BITE: FOUR CORE PAGES TAKE 14-20 SECONDS ON SLOW-3G (2026-08-28). The void reading above had ONE cause and it is worth keeping: the context lacked serviceWorkers:'block', so the SW served every page from CACHE and the throttle never touched the network - which is why throttled and unthrottled were byte-identical at 0.1s. The prover blocks SWs, which is why its numbers were real and mine were fiction. Re-walked with SWs blocked AND a control asserted first: logbook 0.535s unthrottled -> 1.564s throttled, a 3x delta, so the instrument demonstrably bites before any page figure is trusted. THE MEASUREMENT: alert-hub 14.3s, dayplanner 15.4s, pm-scheduler 16.9s, hive 20.0s to first meaningful content, against a 1.6s logbook control on the same run - roughly TEN TIMES the control, and 14-20 seconds is well past the point a worker on plant wifi decides the app is broken. prove_throttled_first_paint's four BLANKs were correct and precise; the only thing wrong was my attempt to refute them. ★AND THE COLD-CACHE SCENARIO IS THE HONEST ONE for this lane: a SW-cached repeat visit is fast for everyone, while the first visit on a bad connection is exactly the moment this trajectory is about. NEXT: read the request waterfall on those four to find where the 14-20s goes (they share chrome with logbook, which is fast, so the difference is in what each page FETCHES, not the shell). || THE WATERFALL NAMES ONE FILE, AND THE FIGURE HAS A BOUND I ALMOST OMITTED (2026-08-28). Recorded the request waterfall for the fast control and two slow pages under the proven throttle. logbook (1.6s): SEVEN requests, 3 stylesheets and 4 fonts, and NO SCRIPTS - it crosses the content bar from server-rendered markup before its JS matters. pm-scheduler (16.9s) and hive (20.2s): 24 requests each, 12-13 of them SCRIPTS, and in both the single slowest is utils.js at 14.4s and 15.9s. So the split is not mysterious: pages whose content is painted BY JavaScript wait on the shared bundle, and pages with server-rendered content do not. utils.js is 306.8 KB and - measured, not guessed - FIFTY PERCENT of it by bytes is comment prose, this codebase's own rich-comment discipline landing in the one file every page blocks on. ★AND THE BOUND: the local seeder does NOT compress - 314,129 bytes returned identically with and without Accept-Encoding - so 14-20s is an UNCOMPRESSED-transfer figure on the dev stack, and Netlify compresses text assets at the edge, where comment-heavy JS compresses especially well. Production is materially faster and these seconds must NOT be quoted as production numbers - the same prod-vs-local trap as _headers being prod-only behaviour. WHAT SURVIVES THE CAVEAT: the RELATIVE finding (JS-rendered pages block on one 307KB shared file while server-rendered ones do not) is compression-invariant, and utils.js remains the largest single blocking asset on the critical path either way. NEXT: measure utils.js compressed to size the real prod cost before proposing any split. || THE PROD-SIZED NUMBER, WHICH IS THE ONLY ONE WORTH ACTING ON (2026-08-28). utils.js compresses 306.8 KB -> 105.2 KB gzip (2.9x) -> 86.3 KB brotli (3.6x), and Netlify serves brotli. So the honest production estimate for the four slow pages is roughly 4.7-5.6s to first meaningful content on Slow-3G, not the 14-20s the uncompressed dev stack shows. That is SLOW but not broken, and it changes what the fix should be: this is not an emergency, it is a budget question. ★THE 50%-PROSE FIGURE ALSO SURVIVES COMPRESSION BETTER THAN IT LOOKS - comment-heavy JavaScript is exactly what brotli eats, so stripping comments from the shipped file would save far less than the raw 50% implies, and would cost the maintenance value the comments carry. The lever is NOT 'delete the prose'. THE REAL LEVER, if this is ever taken up: logbook proves the shape - it crosses the content bar from SERVER-RENDERED markup before any script matters, while pm-scheduler and hive paint nothing until a 12-13 script chain completes. Whether those pages can render a first meaningful frame without waiting on the shared bundle is the actual question, and it is a design change, not a minification pass. RECORDED with the numbers rather than acted on: the fix is a perf arc of its own and its priority is Ian's. || THE LCP-IS-THE-RIGHT-ELEMENT CHECK IS MEASURED (2026-08-28, tools/read_lcp_elements.mjs, 12 pages at 390px signed in). Every CWV instrument on this platform reports LCP as a NUMBER and none reports the ELEMENT - and the element is what decides whether the number means anything, because LCP exists as a proxy for 'the user can see the main content' and that proxy only holds if the largest early paint IS the content. RESULT: the LCP element is chrome on ALL TWELVE. A page subtitle (logbook 'Every job you log builds your skill profile'), a verdict CAPTION rather than the verdict (pm-scheduler #pm-verdict-sub, alert-hub #ah-verdict-sub), a bare H1 ('Analytics Engine'), an instructional line (hive 'Pick the one goal that matters most'), a greeting (index 'Good morning...'), and on THREE pages - asset-hub, marketplace, shift-brain - the wh-source-chip, which is metadata ABOUT the data rather than the data. This is structural, not sloppy: these pages render content after an async read, so at LCP time the largest painted thing is necessarily the shell. The consequence is the finding, and it is worth stating plainly - a CWV score for these pages grades how fast the FRAME arrives, not the answer, so every LCP figure previously banked for them measures the shell. ★AND THE PAGE WITH THE BEST NUMBER HAS THE LEAST CONTENT: dayplanner posts the platform's fastest LCP (76-100ms across runs) on DIV.aurora-bg - a position:fixed inset:0 pointer-events:none decorative gradient with NO TEXT IN IT. Not merely chrome-instead-of-content but a DECORATION counted as content, which makes the healthiest-looking score on the board the one standing for the least. The impossibly-good number is the instrument again. Left as a RECORDER and deliberately NOT registered as a gate: asserting 'LCP must be a content element' would redden all twelve for an architectural property no single fix changes - teaching the gate a state we do not have - and a prover that cannot fail has no business on the board either. What it buys is that the element is now visible beside the number, and a page regressing INTO a decorative LCP is noticeable. Remaining: the premature-tap question across the roster (wave close). || ★THE LOOPBACK LAB MISLEADS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and I nearly banked the second one (2026-08-28). T160's basis already records that the lab FLATTERS timing (no latency). It also PENALISES bytes, and that half was not written down: the local seeder serves UNCOMPRESSED while Netlify serves brotli. Measuring a page load over loopback gave 'index.html 2,366 KB, logbook.html 3,577 KB' - numbers that read like an emergency. Compressing the same files gives the shipped reality: utils.js 312K raw -> 107K gzip -> 88K brotli; index.html 328K -> 92K -> 71K; logbook.html 387K -> 110K -> 87K; nav-hub 96K -> 23K brotli; companion-launcher 94K -> 26K. The five together are ~295 KB brotli against 1,217 KB raw - a FOUR-FOLD difference between what the lab shows and what a visitor pays. Filing the loopback figure would have manufactured a crisis out of the instrument. ★AND IT SHARPENS THE utils.js QUESTION rather than answering it: at 88 KB brotli it is still the largest single script on the critical path, but the 'half of it is comment prose' observation buys less than it sounds - prose is exactly what compresses best, so stripping it saves a fraction of the raw 50%, not half the transfer. Any decision about splitting utils.js should be argued in BROTLI bytes, which is the only number a phone on 3G actually experiences. || ★WALKED UNDER A REAL SLOW-3G PROFILE, AND THE NUMBER IS 2,641ms (2026-08-28). Throttled to ~400kbps / 400ms RTT via CDP at 390px, signed in, and loaded logbook - the worker's core capture surface. FIRST MEANINGFUL PAINT: 2,641ms. Nothing at all is on screen before that: no skeleton, no shell, no chrome. ★AND A SKELETON CANNOT HELP HERE, which is the useful part of the finding. The platform HAS skeleton machinery (whListSkeleton) and it never appeared - not because it is missing, but because a skeleton is markup, and markup cannot paint before the document does. The 2.6 seconds are spent fetching the page itself. So this is a PAGE WEIGHT finding wearing a perceived-performance costume, and pointing more loading states at it would change nothing. MEASURED WEIGHT: logbook.html is 386 KB of HTML on its own; hive 394 KB, index 322 KB. The shared assets every one of them pulls add ~880 KB more - voice-handler.js 425 KB, utils.js 312 KB, nav-hub.js 97 KB, ~48 KB of CSS. Roughly 1.27 MB before a single row of data. On the link a worker actually has in a plant, that is the whole story. ★THE HONEST HALVES: the read itself behaves - no stuck skeleton at 3s, no false 'No entries yet' while the read was still in flight (the honest-empty work holds under throttle, which is exactly the condition it was built for), and no spurious retry state. What fails is getting the page there at all. The fix is code splitting or deferring the AI companion off the field pages' critical path, which is an architecture decision with real blast radius, not an edit - so it is measured and recorded rather than attempted at the tail of a session. pct 60 -> 72. || ★A SKELETON MUST RESOLVE OR ADMIT FAILURE - analytics could do neither if anything unexpected threw (2026-08-28). Measured skeleton/error pairing across all 27 pages that use whListSkeleton: 24 pair it with an error-taxonomy call. analytics.html appeared not to, and did not deserve the flag - it handles failure through whAiError and showToast, which my pattern simply did not include (the eighth incomplete instrument this stretch). Reading it properly also cleared my actual suspicion: its KNOWN read paths are defended, loadSnapshots setting _snapshotReadFailed and returning rather than throwing, fetchPhase catching. It is not a stuck-skeleton page. ★WHAT IT WAS is a page one unexpected throw away from becoming one. autoLoad() was invoked BARE at the boot site - an async function with no .catch() - while calling showSkeleton, applySavedFilters, renderPhase, renderRoleQuickView and _refreshSourceChip with no guard of their own. A throw from any of those becomes an unhandled rejection, and the state it leaves behind is the worst shape a wait can take: _loading stuck true, stopLoadingMessages never running, the spinner never hidden, and the skeleton never replaced - a page shimmering 'Loading analytics...' indefinitely while saying nothing. That is not hypothetical prose: the 22-page retry sweep graded this page's SIBLING analytics-report exactly that way, SILENT, sitting on its compiling message forever under a read outage. Same family, same failure, one file over. ★FIX: a catch that clears the loading state, hides the spinner and renders a retry - the admit-failure half of the contract, with a reload as the recovery since the boot path is what failed. ★AND I GOT THE HELPER WRONG FIRST: whListError's signature is (el, MESSAGE, onRetry) - a string and a function - and I passed an Error object plus a {retry} options bag, which would have escHtml'd the error into '[object Error]' and left the retry unwired. Checking the signature before trusting my own call is what caught it; replacing a silent wait with machine noise and a dead button would have been worse than the bug. Verified: the page parses and boots clean. ★NOT CLAIMED: agentic-rag-observability and ph-intelligence carry the same surface pattern and were NOT deep-read - so they were checked rather than left as an open insinuation: both carry real error handling (3 and 6 catch/toast/whAiError sites) and, decisively, ZERO bare async boot calls - neither has analytics' unguarded-invocation shape. Candidates cleared. Naming a suspect and not returning to it leaves a record that reads like a finding while resting on nothing. pct 72 -> 84. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED (fix+gate) - all assigned gates PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-06 with the grafana MCP + tools/prove_ops_liveness.mjs (gate ops-liveness): every panel's own SQL was pulled from Grafana, its macros expanded, and run against ITS OWN datasource - 53/53 panels across all six WorkHive dashboards now return a non-null value. Two instrument errors came first and both looked like a dead platform: psql -F '|' died on the Windows shell (0/53 'BROKEN'), then six GlitchTip panels read as broken because I asked Supabase for tables that live in a separate container under its own role. ONE REAL GAP remained and is now fixed: the SLO board's Latency p95/p50 panel had NO producer. _shared/envelope.ts has always computed latency_ms for every response and returned it to the caller, but nothing persisted it, and wh_traces' only writer (error-tracker.ts) fires on failures with a hard-coded latency_ms: null - so an SLO dashboard was missing the FIRST golden signal. ok()/fail() now record the trace they already measure (fire-and-forget, .then(noop,noop) because a bare Supabase builder never sends), ai-gateway feeds it the service client, and a live invoke banked the first row: ai-gateway status 200 latency 5587ms, agreeing with the envelope's own 5588ms. · [2026-09-05] pct -> 100. RE-WALKED 2026-09-07 with the instrument the lens names - the Chrome DevTools Protocol (Playwright CDP session, Network.emulateNetworkConditions: 500 ms RTT, ~400 kbps, the Slow-3G shape) via tools/prove_throttled_first_paint.mjs, gate first-paint-throttled PASS: every core page paints its shell fast with reads throttled; no blank screen, no stuck skeleton.

trajectories.title: Session expiry mid-WRITE on every committing surface
trajectories.basis: mid-write expiry walked on the flagship committing surface (logbook wizard, signOut between fill and submit): the refusal fired and the DRAFT KEPT the work (X2 held), but the message was raw internals ('new row violates row-level security policy'). FIXED: the insert error path routes whWriteError AND asks the session directly (a 42501 with no user behind it is a session event) -> proven: 'Your session expired, so nothing was saved. Your entry is kept in the draft - sign in again and press Save.' Remaining: the committing-surface roster sweep + resubmit-lands-once + the work_survives_reauth oracle (wave close). WORK_SURVIVES_REAUTH SLICE 2026-08-26: the flagship committing surface's half-typed entry now PROVEN to ride the full round trip (logbook-draft case in prove_g5d_reauth_restore.mjs, under the g5d-reauth-restore gate): fill f-problem -> whAutoSaveDraft writes the worker-scoped draft key -> session death -> ?signin=1&return= -> restoreDraft puts the note back verbatim. Remaining: resubmit-lands-once (needs a submit + dedup assertion), the roster sweep across the other committing surfaces. || THE COMMITTING-SURFACE ROSTER SWEEP DONE 2026-08-27, and it found exactly one hole. Census of every page that BOTH writes rows and offers a textarea: 12 surfaces, 11 on whAutoSaveDraft, logbook on its own DRAFT_KEY/saveDraft/restoreDraft trio, assistant exempt by reason (a chat turn is SENT immediately, so there is no compose-then-commit gap to lose) - and resume.html with NOTHING. Its #jd-input holds a job description the person PASTED in from somewhere else, which is precisely the work that is expensive to reproduce: a session dying between the paste and the Tailor call sent them back to go find the posting again. Fixed with the shared helper, which also stamps the draft with its OWNER (so a shared plant tablet never hands one worker's paste to the next) and its AGE, and restores only into an empty field so it can never clobber live typing. PROVEN LIVE: stored under wh_view_resume.html_draft_resume-jd, restored byte-for-byte after a full reload, no page errors. ★MY FIRST CENSUS WAS WRONG AND THE GATE IS SHAPED BY THAT: checking for whAutoSaveDraft alone reported LOGBOOK - the flagship committing surface of the whole platform - as unprotected. Absence of the shared HELPER is not absence of the GUARD. A gate that recognises one implementation measures a naming convention rather than the property, and would have sent someone to 'fix' a page that was already correct, so both forms count and only a page with NEITHER is a finding. Teeth 4/4, the load-bearing one being that a page-local mechanism must PASS. Remaining: resubmit-lands-once (needs a submit + dedup assertion). || RESUBMIT-LANDS-ONCE, MEASURED 2026-08-27 — mostly already guaranteed, with ONE asymmetry recorded rather than blind-fixed. The re-auth case is sound by construction: the first write is REFUSED by RLS while the session is dead, so nothing lands, and the resubmit lands exactly one row. The rapid double-tap case is guarded by saveBtn.disabled on submit (T41's domain). And pm_completions carries pm_completions_dedup_uidx - unique on (scope_item_id, worker_name, completed_at::date) - so a second completion of the same task by the same worker on the same day is refused at the DATABASE, with the 23505 handled in submitCompletion (it either upgrades a deferral or says 'Already recorded for this task today'). ★THE RESIDUAL, NAMED PRECISELY: logbook has NO idempotency key on the online path. The OFFLINE queue mints crypto.randomUUID() once and reuses it, so a queued entry replayed twice collides on the primary key and lands once; the online submit builds `id: Date.now().toString()` FRESH inside the handler, so if a write commits and its response is lost - a dropped connection after the row is already in - a second press creates a SECOND row for one piece of work. Two paths on the same page, opposite guarantees. NOT fixed here on purpose: making the id stable means holding it in form state and clearing it only on confirmed success, and getting that wrong on the platform's flagship write path trades a narrow duplicate for a stale id colliding against a legitimately new entry. It is a design decision about idempotency keys that should cover the queue and the online path together, so it is written down with its mechanism instead of guessed at. Remaining: that idempotency-key decision. pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_expiry_midwrite.mjs (gate expiry-midwrite): a session is destroyed for real between typing and saving - the stored token removed and every auth call answering 401 - and the surface must then SAY the session ended, KEEP what was typed, and offer a way back. 2/2 surfaces reached end to end now pass (inventory, marketplace-seller). ONE FIX: the copy already said the right thing, 'Your session has expired. Sign in again, then retry - your typed work is still on this page', and offered NOTHING to press, so reloading was the only exit and reloading is the one action that throws the work away; utils.js's shared notice now carries a Sign in control whose return path is the page the person was on. SCOPE STATED, not rounded up: 2 surfaces had no save this sweep could reach and 8 had no committing field on screen, all reported as unreached rather than as passes. THREE INSTRUMENT ERRORS came first, each accusing a working page: the committing field lives behind the Add button; the OPENER and the SAVE share a verb, so 'Add Part' was pressed instead of 'Save Part' and the form reset looked exactly like the page discarding the work; and a save blocked by client-side validation never meets the expiry at all.

fixes: resume.html: #jd-input (a pasted job description) now draft-protected via whAutoSaveDraft - the last committing surface on the platform with typed work and no mechanism at all

trajectories.note: ★THE DRAFT SURVIVES ON A THREE-LINK CHAIN NOBODY CAN SEE IN ONE PLACE (2026-08-27). whAutoSaveDraft saves the text; clearIdentityHard wipes only IDENTITY keys; and the restore is gated by an OWNER CHECK reading wh_last_worker - the key the expiry just deleted. It works solely because sign-in writes that key back. Re-key the check to anything sign-in does not restore and every draft is silently discarded after an expiry, with an empty form and no explanation. Gated by draft-survives-reauth, which asserts the chain resolves (at least one live link, since the check is a fallback chain whose alias is a documented dead read) and that expiry wipes no draft key. The owner check itself is the shared-tablet protection and must stay: removing it would 'fix' expiry by leaking one worker's typing to the next person on the device. ★THE ROSTER SWEEP, MEASURED: A COVERAGE GAP, NOT A BEHAVIOUR GAP (2026-08-27). prove_session_died drives 22 pages - the standard app set. Seven more pages carry write calls and are outside it: marketplace (25), integrations (22), marketplace-seller (18), founder-console (6), marketplace-admin (6), platform-actions (5), audit-log (2). ★BUT SIX OF THE SEVEN ALREADY HANDLE A DEAD SESSION, which is the part worth knowing before building anything: marketplace has 6 whWriteError + 4 whIsAuthFailure and 14 session sentences, marketplace-seller 18 whWriteError, integrations 9, marketplace-admin 3, founder-console 1+1, and platform-actions answers it explicitly with 4 whIsAuthFailure branches and 10 session sentences. whWriteError carries the session branch centrally, so adoption IS coverage of the behaviour. ★AND THE SEVENTH WAS MY REGEX, NOT A PAGE: audit-log's two 'write calls' are searchParams.delete() and Set.delete() - it commits nothing and is correctly a read-only surface. Checking what the matches actually were, rather than trusting the count, removed the only page that looked unprotected. ★SO WHAT IS OWED IS THE ROSTER, NOT THE PAGES: the prover does not ASK these six what they do when a session dies mid-write, so the claim 'every committing surface refuses honestly' rests on reading adoption rather than driving the case. Extending prove_session_died's roster to the six is the next unit - deliberately not started at the tail of a long turn, because adding pages to a live prover means running it and fixing whatever it finds, and doing that badly is worse than not doing it.

trajectories.title: AI quota exhausted: every AI surface refuses honestly with a way forward
trajectories.basis: THE ARCHITECTURE ITEM IS ALREADY LANDED: all 17 formerly global-cap-only fns now CALL checkRouteRateLimit (verified per-fn, 1 call each) - the 'D12 adoption 10.5%' receipt was stale prose; the code was right. Per-surface quota is observe-by-default, enforce on hive_route_quotas row (the T12 walk proved the deterministic cap=1 enforcement live). The flagship refusal UX proven in T12 (work survives, quota named). Remaining: the 429-storm roster sweep (refusal names quota + Retry-After surfaced + non-AI path offered per surface) - wave close. || ★NOTHING BYPASSES THE GATEWAY — the quota hole this trajectory worried about does not exist, and the real gap is granularity (2026-08-28). Measured every edge function that touches an AI: 25 route through ai-gateway, and ZERO call a provider endpoint directly (no api.openai.com, no generativelanguage.googleapis, no api.anthropic.com, no groq, no openrouter, in any of them, comments stripped before matching). So the global cap genuinely covers every AI call on the platform, and so does the gateway's cost logging — there is no unmetered path. ★MY FIRST READING SAID 32 FUNCTIONS HAD NO QUOTA CHECK AND WAS MEASURING THE WRONG THING: it counted functions lacking a LOCAL quota check, which is exactly what a centralised gateway is designed to make unnecessary. Counting the absence of a defence in the wrong layer produces an alarming number and no truth. The correct question is where the calls EXIT, and they all exit through one door. ★WHAT REMAINS IS D12's ACTUAL POINT — PER-SURFACE quota, so one runaway surface cannot drain a budget the whole platform shares, and so an owner can see which surface spent what. That is a granularity improvement on a sound architecture rather than a hole in a broken one, which changes both its urgency and its shape. pct 60 -> 72. || ★THE SERVER KNEW WHEN THE LIMIT CLEARED AND THE SENTENCE SAID 'A MOMENT' - closed (2026-08-28). Earlier this session the edge layer learned to be precise: every deny in _shared/rate-limit.ts gained retry_after_seconds plus a real Retry-After header, wired across 53 call sites. The marketplace surfaces consume it. The AI taxonomy did not - whAiError's 429 branch answered every quota refusal with 'You have hit the AI rate limit. Wait a moment and try again.' ★'A MOMENT' IS THE ONE THING A PERSON CANNOT ACT ON. A worker retries after ten seconds, is refused again, retries again, and concludes the assistant is broken rather than busy - on a shared free tier, on a Friday, which is exactly the condition this trajectory was written for. The information to say something better was already arriving in the response and being thrown away at the last layer. ★FIX: whAiError now reads a window off the error (retry_after_seconds or retryAfter, checked on the error and on a nested body/context/data) and says 'Try again in about 45 seconds' or 'about 10 minutes', bilingually - segundo/minuto in the FIL branch, matching the platform's Taglish register. Additive and defensive by construction: no window, a junk value or a zero all fall back to the original sentence, so this can only ever improve a message and never print 'in about null'. ★TESTED, 6 cases: absent window keeps the old copy, 45s renders seconds, 600s renders minutes, 'abc' and 0 fall back, and a 503 is untouched. utils.js loads on every page, so index, assistant, voice-journal, logbook and analytics were all booted in a real browser afterwards - 5 clean, 0 broken. ★What remains for this trajectory is the roster question rather than the message: whether every AI surface preserves the user's typed input across a 429 (T12's work_survives_quota), which is a per-surface walk. pct 72 -> 86. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED (fix+gate) - all assigned gates PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_refusal_kindness.mjs (gate refusal-kindness): the AI quota refusal answers 429 with 'AI call limit reached. Try again in about 52 minutes', names its scope so a person knows whose limit was spent, and the wait COUNTS DOWN across a retry rather than growing - a way forward, not a shrug. Scope stated: of 14 spending functions 1 refused and was measured, 1 took the burst without a limit, and 12 were not reached because their validation rejects the probe body before any quota is consulted.

fixes: utils.js whFnError: a 429's own words now reach the user instead of supabase-js's placeholder
utils.js whQuotaNotice + asset-hub + assistant: the quota warns BEFORE the wall, not only after
alert-hub.html: a live-upgraded brief no longer stamps itself as the stored one

trajectories.note: ★THE LOCK EXISTED AND WAS NEVER RECORDED (found 2026-08-26 by auditing 'locking' trajectories that name no gate). cb_retry_path asserts that a failure offers a retry which actually RE-ATTEMPTS and succeeds once the cause is gone, and cm_retry_views does it per (page, view) - a dialog whose reads fail must paint the failure AND offer a retry inside the view that recovers, with no-read and memory-rendered views measured not-applicable. That is precisely this trajectory's subject, and the retry_path family the roadmap's §6m finding named. The work was done; the registry just did not say so. ★THE STATUS PAGE IS ALREADY BUILT THE RIGHT WAY AND WAS UNGATED (2026-08-27). Both halves of this trajectory's sharpest probe hold: it is LINKED from failure states (whReadError's connection branch says 'Still failing on good internet? Open status.html'), and it SURVIVES the outage it reports - measured: zero Supabase client, zero getDb, zero table reads, so it renders with the database down. It is also not a static 'all good': it pings each edge function's public /health endpoint and renders a live card per service, ambering past the interactive SLO, with a Refresh. Nothing was broken; nothing protected it. Gate status-survives-the-outage asserts the DB-independence, the live checks, the absence of a hardcoded green, and the pointer in utils.js that sends people there at all. ★RESURRECTION ATTEMPTED, NOT YET EARNED - AND IT EXPOSED A REAL INSTRUMENT BUG (2026-08-27). The remaining item is the resurrection proof, so I tried the obvious subject: _fixtures/logbook.backup.html, which has ZERO retry affordances against the live page's 3 and is exactly the pre-fix world the fixtures were kept for. It came back UNGRADED - 'injection intercepted nothing'. The backup is old enough that its request shape no longer matches what the prover injects into, so the instrument cannot grade it at all. That is an honest negative and worth recording: a NEGATIVE FIXTURE ROTS. Kept to calibrate a detector, it silently stops being calibratable once the page's request shape moves on, and 'we have fixtures' is not the same as 'we have a resurrection subject'. A faithful red needs a pre-§6m COMMIT (HEAD is already post-fix - logbook carries no whListError in either HEAD or worktree, so its retry arrives by another route), which is wave-close work by the defer-ceremonies rule rather than something to pull forward mid-roadmap. ★THE BUG THE ATTEMPT FOUND, which is worth more than the attempt: prove_retry_path.mjs wrote retry_path_report.json on EVERY run, whether it had walked 22 pages or 1. My one-page fixture probe replaced the whole sweep's report with a single UNGRADED row - measured, not hypothesised, because I did it. prove_journey.mjs already carries this exact fix in its own header ('a fixed filename let a one-page test DESTROY a 66-persona run'); this prover never got it, and it matters MORE here, because tools/bank_prover_reports.py reads retry_path_report.json to bank cb_retry_path - so a spot-check could have fed truncated verdicts into the bank rather than merely losing a console log. A --page run now writes retry_path_report.partial.json. The full sweep was re-run to repair the damage: 22 pages, 21 PASS / 1 NO-RECOVER (analytics-report), report restored, and the banker was never run against the clobbered file. ★A LESSON THAT GENERALISES PAST THIS PROVER: any tool whose output feeds the bank must not let a narrowed run overwrite a full one, and the two provers that share this hazard were written months apart - the fix travelled with neither. ★THE SWEEP'S ONE SILENT PAGE, DIAGNOSED AND FIXED (2026-08-27). The 22-page retry sweep ended 21 PASS / 1 not-recovering, and reading the actual row showed something worse than a missing retry: analytics-report graded SILENT - 'the page renders no failure under a REST read outage'. It sat on 'Compiling analytics across all 4 phases' with a spinner, saysFailure false, retryControls []. Its catch block was fine and even carried an earlier T40 retry fix; the catch simply never ran. TWO CAUSES, both in fetchReport: (1) NOTHING BOUNDED THE RUN - a read that never answers is not an error but a promise that never settles, so no catch fires and the spinner turns forever; (2) `_arAbort` was created AFTER `db.auth.getSession()`, a REST call, so until that resolved _arAbort was null and the Cancel button's `if (_arAbort) _arAbort.abort()` was a NO-OP - the one control offered during the wait did nothing in exactly the outage where someone would press it. The controller is created before anything is awaited now, and a 90s budget (generous: the orchestrator has measurably taken 32.6s) aborts and throws. ★AND THE TIMEOUT MUST NOT WEAR THE CANCEL'S CLOTHES: both surface as AbortError, and reporting the cutoff as 'Generation cancelled' would tell someone they stopped something they were waiting on AND hide the outage the timeout exists to reveal. A flag separates them; the timeout falls through to the red failure state with the retry. ★THE SMOKE TOOL WAS WRONG ABOUT THIS PAGE TWICE while verifying it - once for an unseeded role, once for judging 'thin' by characters alone (371 chars, but 66 controls: a generate-on-demand page's resting state is a period picker, an audience picker and a button). It counts controls now, which keeps the stuck-skeleton catch and stops punishing terse pages. ★AND THE GATE THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT WAS THE REASON NOBODY DID (2026-08-27). long-fetch-bounded already existed and already covered analytics-orchestrator - it passed analytics-report on every run, because its BOUND pattern accepted a bare `AbortController` or a bare `signal:`. Those are a CANCEL BUTTON: somewhere for a person to press, not a clock that fires on its own. The page had both and hung forever anyway, which is the whole distinction. Rather than add a rival gate, the existing one was TAUGHT: a bound now requires a TIMER (fetchWithTimeout, AbortSignal.timeout, a setTimeout that calls abort, or a Promise.race against a timed promise), and the controller may sit beside those without standing in for them. A --selftest pins five cases, the first being the pre-fix analytics-report source, which must be RED; all 11 slow-endpoint fetches pass under the stricter rule. ★ONE MORE FELL OUT OF THE RE-SWEEP: voice-journal's tts-speak was the last raw unbounded call. speakAzure returns false on failure SO THAT the caller can fall back to the browser's own speech - but an unbounded fetch never returns false, it never returns at all, so a hung TTS left the fallback unreachable and the reader got silence instead of a different voice. Bounded at 15s, using the same wrapper the page already used in four other places. ★THE RESURRECTION PROOF, RESOLVED - AND IT NEEDED A DISTINCTION RATHER THAN A HARDER TRY (2026-08-27). The earlier attempt used _fixtures/logbook.backup.html and came back UNGRADED because the backup is old enough that the prover's injection no longer matches its request shape. The technique that works is cheaper and exact: take the pre-fix BYTES FROM GIT rather than from a checked-in stale copy. Proven on T7 the same day - git log -S found the commit that introduced the kicked branch, its PARENT went RED with precisely the right sentence, and no file was mutated, which mattered because the gate board was concurrently walking pages. ★APPLIED TO T40's status-survives-the-outage, IT REVEALED THERE IS NO PRE-FIX WORLD: status.html was BORN database-independent and health-pinging - its first-ever commit (cbac3136) passes every check. The gate locks nothing that was once broken; it is a PROACTIVE regression guard. Demanding a git-history resurrection from such a gate is how a good gate gets marked unfinishable. ★THE RIGHT TEETH FOR THAT SHAPE ARE SYNTHETIC NEGATIVES, and the gate had NONE - it read the live page, passed, and nothing ever demonstrated it could go red, which is the a-check-that-cannot-fail problem. Its four properties are now a pure function with a --selftest of six cases: a clean page passes, and each property is shown to catch its own violation (a Supabase client appearing, the /health ping removed, a hardcoded 'All systems operational', the utils.js pointer lost), with the live page asserted green alongside them. ★THE TRANSFERABLE RULE: a gate that locks a FIX owes a resurrection proof against the pre-fix bytes; a gate written PROACTIVELY owes synthetic negatives instead. They are different obligations and only one of them is satisfiable by git. ★THE ONE NON-PASS PAGE, RESOLVED - AND THE INSTRUMENT HAD ALREADY SAID SO (2026-08-27). The 22-page sweep's single non-PASS is analytics-report, and re-running it alone today still returns SILENT. It is NOT a defect, and prove_retry_path's own header says why in a note dated 2026-08-19: 'TWO SILENT VERDICTS ARE UNCONFIRMED - DO NOT BANK THEM AS DEFECTS ON THIS EVIDENCE … analytics-report catches and replaces the mount with whAiError("Could not generate report: …"). The collector saw only "Compiling analytics across all 4 phases".' ★AND TODAY EXPLAINS WHY THE COLLECTOR ONLY EVER SAW THAT: the generation was UNBOUNDED, so under a read outage it never left the Compiling state at all - there was no later frame in which the error path could paint. That is now fixed (90s budget, Cancel working from the first moment, timeout distinguished from a user cancel), so the failure state is reachable; the probe simply does not wait 90 seconds to see it. ★AND THE PAGE OWES NO LOAD-TIME FAILURE ANYWAY: its only own read is loadHiveName, called LAZILY from generateReport and explicitly non-fatal (it supplies a default Client field on the cover page). A generate-on-demand surface with nothing pending has nothing to report, and demanding a PASS there would mean inventing a failure the page does not have - bending the product to please a gate. ★KEPT AT 97 RATHER THAN LOCKED, deliberately: two of the four entries in this trajectory's gate list (cb_retry_path, cm_retry_views) are BANK-FAMILY oracles measured by the board's CB/CM sweeps, not registered gate ids, so a lock claim here would not be mechanically backed the way the registry validator backs the others.

trajectories.title: Rage-tap/double-submit on every committing control under latency
trajectories.basis: flagship proven under TRUE concurrency: five same-tick clicks on community's Post to Hive -> exactly 1 row. Third receipt of the class this sweep (T145's two-supervisor race decided cleanly; T10's defer/complete 23505 dedup+supersede). Remaining: the latency-injected roster sweep over the T50 registry's 52 committing controls + aria-busy communication check (wave close choreography). || 2026-08-26, the aria-busy COMMUNICATION half attempted, and the honest result is mostly an INSTRUMENT finding. Census: 87 in-flight `.disabled = true` sites across 26 pages. ★THREE STATIC APPROACHES, ALL UNRELIABLE, AND THE FAILURE MODE IS THE LESSON: (1) demanding aria-busy specifically would enforce ONE TECHNIQUE when a label change ('Saving…') communicates just as well - taste, not defect. (2) A proximity window slid the answer purely by size - 15 silent at 300 chars, 11 at 1200, 5 at 2500 - because this codebase comments heavily BY DESIGN and the explanatory prose between a disable and its feedback is what moved. analytics-report was flagged that way and is EXEMPLARY: role=status + aria-busy + aria-live + spinner + 'usually takes 5-15 seconds' + a Cancel button, all just outside the window. (3) Switching to the enclosing FUNCTION failed differently - brace-matching could not resolve the scope for 11 of 15, and those counted as silent BY DEFAULT, which is accusing on unknown: the wrong direction to be wrong in. CONCLUSION: this property is not reliably measurable statically; it needs the latency-injected LIVE probe this trajectory's spec already names - click the control under injected delay and observe whether anything changes. That is the correct instrument and it is the remaining build. ONE FIX LANDED, confirmed by reading the code rather than by heuristic: community's Reply button only went disabled during its insert - a greyed control is indistinguishable from one that ignored you, and a screen reader announces 'unavailable', not 'working', which on a plant connection is where a second tap comes from. It now says 'Posting…' and restores the label at the single exit both paths share, using the idiom the same file already uses at :2897. Page live-verified healthy, 0 pageerrors. No gate shipped: a gate built on any of the three failed oracles would encode the flaw. || THE SHARED DOUBLE-TAP HELPER HAD THE SAME DEFECT AS THE ONE BUTTON I FIXED, AND FIXING IT ONCE FIXES EVERY ADOPTER (2026-08-27). This trajectory had already found and fixed community's Reply button - disabled during the insert, so a screen reader heard 'unavailable', which is indistinguishable from a control that ignored the press. Measured the class platform-wide: 34 files set .disabled = true (111 sites) and only 19 use aria-busy anywhere. Rather than sweep 111 sites - most of which are validity-gating, where disabled ALONE is correct - I looked for the shared path, and it exists: button-lock.js's withButtonLock(btn, asyncFn), the platform's own single-flight guard. It set disabled and an is-loading CLASS and NO aria-busy. So a sighted user saw the press land and the work run; a blind user heard only 'unavailable', on exactly the controls a double-tap costs the most. ★FIXED IN THE CONTRACT: aria-busy set on lock, removed in the release beside disabled so an exception cannot strand a button announcing itself busy forever. ★AND IN BOTH PATHS - the file has TWO lock/release pairs, and fixing only the first would have made a shared helper that is right half the time, which is worse than one that is wrong consistently. VERIFIED LIVE through the real helper: during the work aria-busy='true', disabled=true, is-loading; after, aria-busy removed, disabled=false, return value preserved, 0 page errors. Three adopting pages (dayplanner, inventory, marketplace-seller) get it at once, and so does every future adopter. Remaining: the latency-injected concurrent-dispatch sweep over the T50 registry's 51 controls - whose denominator this session proved complete. || LOCKED 2026-08-28. The aria-busy contract was fixed in BOTH pairs and verified live, then left ungated - and this one is a SHARED helper, so a regression would reach every adopting page at once while looking like nothing on screen (the sighted path is unchanged; only the announced state breaks). Gate a-busy-button-says-working holds four things per pair: aria-busy set on lock, REMOVED on release, disabled set, disabled cleared. Selftest 6/6, and the negatives mutate each pair INDEPENDENTLY, because the failure this trajectory actually recorded was a fix landing in one path only - a helper right half the time is harder to trust than one consistently wrong. Remaining: the latency-injected concurrent-dispatch sweep over the T50 registry's 51 controls. pct -> 100.
