trajectories.note: ★THE FUNNEL IS THE FINDING: 118 -> 12 -> 4. A first pass flagged 118 write handlers with no busy guard, which would have been 118 false findings. Narrowing to handlers reachable STRAIGHT FROM AN ONCLICK that INSERT (the least idempotent operation) gave 13; one of those, generateApiKey, was already guarded and my matcher missed it because the pattern was CASE-SENSITIVE and the flag is _genKeyBusy - my instrument wrong, not the code. Then the DATABASE settled the rest: community_reactions (post+worker+emoji), service_vouchers (code), service_credit_topups (gcash_ref where not rejected), project_links (project+type+link) and marketplace_reviews (request+direction) all carry BUSINESS-KEY uniques, so a double press there yields one row and a refusal - protected, and deliberately left alone. ★FOUR WERE GENUINELY UNPROTECTED and are now guarded: svcHailNow and svcAskQuotes (the service_requests unique is on pm_scope_item_id, which covers AUTO hails - a manual hail carries none, so a second press fans a second request out to every provider); saveSyncConfig (integration_configs has nothing but a PK, so two live configs would both sync the same endpoint); and saveNewTask (pm_scope_items likewise, so the same maintenance obligation is created twice and the compliance denominator moves with it). Guards release in a finally so a throw cannot wedge the control shut; verified live - all three pages load with 0 page errors and a second concurrent entry returns in 1ms doing nothing. REMAINS: startImport (its insert target did not resolve statically), the same sweep over UPDATE-only handlers, and true concurrent dispatch under injected latency rather than a simulated in-flight flag. ★startImport GUARDED - THE LAST ONE, AND THE MOST EXPENSIVE TO PRESS TWICE (2026-08-27). The earlier sweep guarded svcHailNow, svcAskQuotes, saveSyncConfig and saveNewTask and left this one open because its insert target did not resolve statically. It is a BULK CSV import behind a bare `onclick="startImport()"` with no disabled state, so the only thing between a double-tap and a doubled plant register was how fast a finger moved. ★AND THE BATCH ID MAKES IT WORSE, not better: `_batchId = 'import-' + Date.now()` mints a NEW id for the second run rather than colliding with the first, so the duplicate rows land under a DIFFERENT batch and nothing downstream - including the rollback, which works by batch_id - can undo them together. Guarded with the same shape as saveSyncConfig, released in a finally; verified live, a second concurrent entry returns in 0ms having done nothing. ★AND A STALE TABLE NAME FELL OUT OF THE SAME READ: WH_TABLE mapped asset -> 'assets', and to_regclass('public.assets') is NULL - it was dropped in Phase 5c. The ROLLBACK map twelve hundred lines below carries the correction in its own comment ('rolling back assets silently no-op'd - C1 fix 2026-07-06'); the IMPORT map it mirrors never got it, so the fix did not reach its sibling. The value does not route the write (that is hard-coded to asset_nodes) but it is stored on external_sync and RENDERED to the user in plant-connections' sync table, so an asset import labelled its own ledger row with a table nobody can look in - and disagreed with the 16 rows already there, all of which say asset_nodes. REMAINS for T41: the UPDATE-only handler sweep, and true concurrent dispatch under injected latency. ★THE UPDATE-ONLY SWEEP IS CLOSED, AND THE ANSWER IS A CLEAN ZERO (2026-08-27). The question is narrower than 'do UPDATE handlers have guards', because most UPDATEs are IDEMPOTENT - setting status to 'done' twice leaves one 'done', so a double press costs nothing and a guard would be ceremony. The harmful subset is an update whose new value is DERIVED FROM THE OLD one: a balance plus an amount, a Number(x) + 1, an array spread that appends. Those double when pressed twice. Swept across every page: ZERO. Every increment on this platform happens server-side in an RPC or a trigger, which is why the XP and credit ledgers could be made reversible at all. ★THE DETECTOR WAS GIVEN TEETH BEFORE THE ZERO WAS BELIEVED - five cases, catching balance+amount, Number(x)+1 and an array spread while correctly ignoring a plain set and a timestamp - because a sweep that cannot find the thing it is looking for returns zero for the wrong reason. REMAINS for T41: true concurrent dispatch under injected latency, which needs the browser and an unawaited double-click rather than a simulated in-flight flag.

trajectories.title: Deep-link cold start for every `?param` page
trajectories.basis: the sweep's DENOMINATOR built: tools/build_param_route_registry.py generates substrate/reference/param_route_registry.json (18 served pages, 60 params, atomic write, --check staleness gate) from source enumeration of URLSearchParams reads - the complete param-route surface no one can shrink silently. T1/T8's return-contract lanes already cover ?signin/?signup/?return. --check WIRED into the board 2026-08-26 (gate param-route-registry, static/fast) after a regen moved the denominator 60->61 params (T19's logbook ?view=team - the exact drift class the gate exists for). Remaining: the cold-start x auth-state x foreign-id sweep across the 61 lanes (wave close). || ★WALKED LIVE: a deep link that cannot resolve says NOTHING - a third outcome neither branch of this trajectory's question anticipated (2026-08-28). Signed in as a Baguio worker and opened asset-hub.html?node_id=<an asset belonging to Lucena Pharmaceutical>. The probe asked whether the page names the ACCESS boundary or reads as an empty plant; the answer to both is NO. It renders the worker's OWN hive's asset list - BE-001 Beumer, BLR-001 Cleaver-Brooks, CT-002 Marley - exactly as if no deep link had been requested. Repeated with a well-formed but NONEXISTENT uuid: identical. So `?node_id=` is silently discarded whenever it does not resolve, for either reason. ★THE GOOD NEWS FIRST, because it is the part that matters most: nothing leaks. RLS holds, the foreign asset is not rendered, and there is no false 'no assets yet' claiming the worker's own plant is empty - which is the failure this trajectory most feared and the one that did not happen. ★THE GAP IS WAYFINDING: someone who follows a colleague's link to a specific machine lands on a generic list with no explanation, and cannot tell whether the link was wrong, the asset was deleted, or it belongs to another plant. `?node_id=` is the asset deep-link contract (T29's whole diagnostic chain rides on it), so a link that degrades silently degrades the chain with it. The honest shape is one line naming which of the three happened. Recorded, not built: the copy is a small decision about how much to say to someone who may not be entitled to know the asset exists at all - and 'not in your hive' versus 'not found' is exactly that trade. ★INSTRUMENT NOTE: the probe printed the full visible text rather than only its two booleans, which is the only reason the third outcome was visible at all - both flags read false, and a checker that trusted them would have reported 'no problem found'. pct 60 -> 74. || ★CORRECTION — THE CLAIM ABOVE IS WRONG, AND THE ERROR WAS MINE (2026-08-28). I recorded that an unresolvable ?node_id= 'says nothing'. It says: 'That asset link could not be resolved in this hive.' The page has had that branch since AH1/AH18 (2026-07-28), and its own comment even names the class it was fixing — the ?tag= arm had been given unresolved handling in JA1/JA2 and the ?node_id= arm had not, 'the fix every path, not just the walked one class'. It also distinguishes PENDING and REJECTED assets, scrolling to the Pending Approvals card and naming which of the two happened, because the fleet list is approved-only and ~18% of nodes are unresolvable for that reason alone. All of that was already right. ★WHY I MISSED IT: the message is a TOAST, and my probe took ONE reading at 6 seconds — after it had faded. Re-probed sampling every 500ms for 12s and caught it immediately. That is the platform's own recorded trap ('the toast FADES; the empty state is what stays') and my instrument walked straight into it: a single late sample cannot distinguish 'never said' from 'said and gone', and I banked the stronger claim. ★WHAT SURVIVES, narrower and real: the explanation is EPHEMERAL. The ?tag= arm leaves a PERSISTENT trace — it puts the requested tag in the search box so the list is scoped and its empty state truthful — while the ?node_id= arm leaves only a toast. So the two arms of that same if/else still differ, just far less than I claimed: one leaves evidence on the page, the other leaves a few seconds of it. A supervisor who follows a link and glances away has no way to learn what happened. That is a durability gap in a good fix, not the absence of one. pct 74 -> 80. || ★THE DENOMINATOR EXISTS, IS GENERATED, AND IS ALREADY DOING WORK (2026-08-28). This trajectory's instrument-close asks for 'a param-route registry (enumerated from source, gated complete)'. It is built: substrate/reference/param_route_registry.json holds 18 pages and 62 params, GENERATED by tools/build_param_route_registry.py from the actual URLSearchParams .get() calls each served page makes - so it cannot drift from what the pages really read, and it lives under substrate/ where the freshness gate keeps it current. Its own meta names this trajectory: 'T43's sweep denominator: cold-start x auth-state per (page, param)'. ★AND IT IS NOT WRITE-ONLY - validate_report_link_fidelity CONSUMES it to assert something sharper than 'links carry params': that every param a link carries is one the TARGET PAGE ACTUALLY READS. That is the check which catches a link decorated with ?window=90d pointing at a page that reads no params - more specific-looking than a bare link while delivering nothing, and worse for it, because it reads as context that was handed over. A registry that another gate depends on is a registry that stays honest. ★WHAT REMAINS IS THE SWEEP ITSELF: 62 params x cold-start x auth-state, walked for arrival fidelity - does the wall preserve the destination, does a foreign-hive id refuse by name rather than showing emptiness, does a malformed id say so. The denominator is built; the walk over it is the work, and it is a live-browser matrix rather than something readable from source. pct 80 -> 88. || CENSUSED 2026-08-31, and the diagnosis half of boundary_not_emptiness now has numbers. 34 bank rows carry that ONE oracle and no gate covered it (checked: empty-state-discrimination is search-0 vs first-run; failed-read-is-not-empty is a read that ERRORED; auth-boundary is whether the server refuses). This is the third thing - the read SUCCEEDED, the server lawfully returned nothing, and the question is whether the page says 'you cannot see this' or 'there is nothing here'. Measured across 42 root surfaces: 26 own an absence state, and 10 of those carry NO refusal copy (the figure first read 25 and the INSTRUMENT was wrong twice over - a vocabulary narrower than the product's, plus literal backspace bytes written where   word-boundaries were intended, so the join/create clause could never fire; 25 -> 24 -> 22 -> 10 with no page changing). It is hard for a structural reason - RLS refuses by FILTERING, so a foreign-hive read and an empty hive are byte-identical (200, zero rows) unless the page makes a separate membership read. The ordinary trigger is not exotic: a removed worker keeps wh_active_hive_id, their next read is filtered to zero, and pm-scheduler answers 'No completions recorded yet.' THE FIX PATTERN IS ALREADY HERE: marketplace.html:1222-1226 keeps _rateLimited, _authExpired and _accessDenied with the reasoning written beside them - but that covers only the LOUD 403; the silent filtered case needs the membership read. Refining the census showed the backlog is cheaper than the count: pm-scheduler and inventory already carry membership machinery, so they can ask the question and simply never say the answer. Instrument: tools/census_boundary_not_emptiness.py, held as the forward-only gate boundary-refusal-ratchet (baseline 25, may fall, never rise; teeth proven). PCT UNCHANGED - this is the diagnosis, the runtime half still needs the walk (member of hive A requesting hive B's object, and a removed member re-opening the app). || FIXED AND VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-31. The walk (member of hive A pointed at a hive they do not belong to = the removed-member state, no membership mutated) found FOUR surfaces answering a removed worker with emptiness: alert-hub 'All clear' (a SAFETY claim about a plant it could not see one row of), community 'No activity yet', pm-scheduler 'Nothing due', and inventory/dayplanner falling back silently to a populated personal view. Every page had already fixed the SIBLING case - the read that FAILED - and none modelled the read that was REFUSED, which arrives as an ordinary 200 with zero rows because RLS filters. Fixed with three helpers in utils.js (whHiveContextLost / whHiveMembershipLost / whHiveContextNotice - one sentence, one probe, one persistent region, so five surfaces cannot drift) wired into pm-scheduler, inventory, alert-hub, community and dayplanner's plant rail. RE-WALKED: 12 surfaces, 0 answer with emptiness (was 4). The harness went red against the pre-fix world and green on HEAD with no change to itself - the resurrection proof. PCT UNCHANGED: T43's own subject is deep-link arrival fidelity across param routes; this closes its boundary_not_emptiness dependency, not the trajectory. pct -> 88. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: FIXED the one boundary-refusal-ratchet failure — ph-intelligence.html owned an absence state (No intelligence data yet) but ZERO refusal copy, so a viewer with no hive saw "no data" not "join a hive" (the refused-read fourth-state). Added a no-HIVE_ID refusal branch to maturityGateCheck (Join or create a hive to see PH Intelligence; blocks loadReport). Gate now PASSES: 26 absence-owning surfaces, 0 with no refusal copy. pct -> 92. || LOCKED 2026-09-04: board gate passed. pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-06 via tools/cwv_probe.mjs + gate cwv (the existing two-tool CWV scorer, recalled rather than rebuilt): headless MOBILE Chromium measured 119 public surfaces for warm-median LCP, INP and CLS - 0 over threshold on all three - and tools/cwv_gate.py ratcheted PASS with no check over baseline.

trajectories.title: Installed-PWA mode: offline shell, stale-cache honesty, update flow
trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25): the install-reality walk found the trajectory's central hole BEFORE any two-version test was needed: the PWA installs from index (manifest + beforeinstallprompt button live there) but a repo-wide grep found exactly ONE root-scope serviceWorker.register - on report-sender.html, a supervisor page a field worker may never open. An installed app therefore had NO shell precache, NO offline-fallback navigation shell, and `serviceWorker.ready` hung forever on every other page (the documented marketplace-seller push-alerts hang was this same hole). SECOND finding: marketplace-seller's registration hardcoded '/workhive/sw.js' - the LOCAL tester prefix that PROD does not serve (feedback_workhive_url_prefix), so the push flow that fix built stayed 404-broken exactly where it ships. FIXES: nav-hub.js (SHELL) now registers the worker centrally with a DERIVED root (whSwRoot(): '/workhive/' local, '/' prod), guarded + catch-silent; marketplace-seller derives the same root; sw.js CACHE_NAME v238->v239 (nav-hub is precached). PROVEN live: logbook load -> registration activated, 30 shell files precached, then OFFLINE COLD START serves the logbook shell with the offline banner speaking, and a non-precached page renders its honest 'Saved snapshot, computed 1h ago' state. Remaining: the two-version SW transition test (deploy v_N+1 under a live v_N session - update nudge? mixed-version hazard?), install-prompt timing probes, queue-survives-restart (T14 seam), PWA integrity gate re-run (wave close). DEPLOY NOTE: sw v239 replaces the pending v238-only note at Ian's gate. || ★THE TWO-VERSION TRANSITION IS MEASURED, AND THE DESIGN TURNS OUT TO BE RIGHT (2026-08-28). Built tools/prove_sw_two_version_transition.mjs, which replaces sw.js ON DISK while a logbook page sits open and then calls registration.update() - the real shape of a deploy landing under a live installed session, and the one probe here that must run with serviceWorkers ENABLED. BEFORE: caches ['workhive-shell-v241'], worker controlling the page. AFTER: installing false, waiting FALSE, active true, caches ['workhive-shell-vT44TEST'] - one cache, the new one. No update nudge anywhere on the page. ★READ AGAINST THE HANDLERS RATHER THAN GUESSED, which changed my conclusion: my first instinct was that the old cache had been deleted out from under a live session. It has not. install does caches.open(NEW).then(c => c.addAll(SHELL_FILES)) INSIDE waitUntil, so the new cache is fully populated before install resolves; only then does activate delete every other key; and skipWaiting() + clients.claim() hand the live page straight to the new worker. So there is never a moment without a usable shell, an installed user runs the old build only until their next navigation rather than until every tab closes, and the MISSING UPDATE NUDGE IS CONSISTENT rather than absent - the nudge exists for designs that leave the new worker WAITING, which this one deliberately does not. ★THE RESIDUAL WINDOW, stated honestly: the page already rendered keeps its old HTML/JS until the next navigation while the cache holds the new files. Because this shell precaches whole PAGES rather than hashed chunks, an old page cannot fetch a mismatched fragment, so the classic chunk-mismatch failure does not apply. ★ALSO A NAMING CORRECTION ON MY OWN PROBE: it reported 'controllerIsOld: true' from a check that only tested whether a controller EXISTS - it proved nothing about WHICH worker held the page, and with clients.claim() the honest answer is the new one. Not registered as a board gate: it rewrites sw.js mid-run (restored in a finally, and the restore is asserted - verified back at v241). pct 70 -> 85. Remaining: install-prompt timing probes and queue-survives-restart (T14 seam). (STATUS CORRECTED the same minute: I set this to 'locking' and the registry validator refused it - 'locking' MEANS a registered gate exists, and what this trajectory gained is a HARNESS that rewrites sw.js mid-run and is deliberately NOT on the board. Back to 'fixing' at 85. The rule is right and the refusal is the registry doing exactly what it was built for: stopping me from spending a status I had not earned.) || ★QUEUE-SURVIVES-RESTART IS PROVEN, ALL THREE PARTS (2026-08-28). The promise a dead-zone worker relies on is not one claim but three, and only the first had been walked: the entry is QUEUED, the app can be REOPENED while still offline, and the person is TOLD work is pending. tools/prove_offline_queue_survives_restart.mjs walks all three. MEASURED: enqueued while offline -> 1 pending; the page then CLOSED entirely and a fresh one opened WITH THE NETWORK STILL DOWN -> the navigation simply succeeds, because the service worker serves the logbook shell cold, and getPending still returns the entry; the offline badge is VISIBLE reading '1 pending'; cleanup leaves nothing behind. So a repair logged in a dead zone survives the app being killed, and the worker can see that it is still waiting rather than having to trust it. ★TWO INSTRUMENT ERRORS WORTH KEEPING: the first version blocked service workers out of habit - every other probe here does - and the offline reload died with a navigation error, because blocking the worker in the one test whose subject IS the offline shell measures the absence of the thing under test. The second invented the queue's API (put/all) and got 'q.put is not a function'; the real surface is enqueue/getPending/remove, and reading offline-queue.js would have cost less than guessing. || ★★THE PWA SHELL WAS PRECACHING 4.2 MB OF IMAGES TO DRAW A 56px AVATAR (2026-08-28) - the largest single performance defect this programme has found. Chasing the funnel's image weight I checked what ELSE sits in sw.js SHELL_FILES and found brand_assets/hezekiah.png and zaniah.png: 1254x1254 masters at 2016 KB and 1997 KB, BOTH precached, so every installed PWA downloaded ~3.9 MB of portrait before it could work offline - on a platform built for Philippine plant workers on phones, whose own T37 arc is about Slow-3G. ★THE INTENT WAS ALWAYS RIGHT AND THE FILES WERE NEVER BUILT: wh-persona.js carries a comment reading 'PWA-conscious: 256x256 progressive JPEGs (12KB each) generated from the 2.2MB source PNGs'. Those derivatives never existed - a 2026-07-03 fix for the resulting 404 repointed at the MASTERS, which stopped the broken image and shipped 4 MB instead, leaving a comment that still promised 12 KB. They exist now: 9.6 KB and 9.8 KB, progressive JPEG, and the source carries no alpha (mode=RGB), so JPEG was the correct format all along. The masters stay in brand_assets for print and for explainer_studio; they are simply no longer shipped to every device. ALSO: the logo went 1024px/229 KB -> 640px/81 KB, sized from the LARGEST real render (260px on index, found by scanning every sized instance - the obvious 36px and 80px would have produced a 240px asset that was soft on the hero). NET: shell brand assets 4,242 KB -> 100 KB, about 4.14 MB off every PWA install. VERIFIED LIVE with service workers ENABLED: cache workhive-shell-v242, all 31 files precached, worker active, the page fetching zaniah-256.jpg at 9.8 KB, zero page errors - and every SHELL_FILES entry confirmed present on disk first, because a precached missing file fails the whole install. CACHE_NAME bumped v241 -> v242; without it an installed device keeps precaching the masters and never sees the derivatives. || ★SHELL BUMP v242 -> v243, DETERMINED BY PARSING SHELL_FILES RATHER THAN BY MEMORY (2026-08-28). Twelve files were edited this turn; exactly TWO are precached — nav-hub.js (the seller dashboard's new registry entry) and voice-handler.js (the companion's PM-skips grounding) — so without a bump an installed device would keep a nav that cannot reach the seller dashboard and a companion that cannot see a skipped PM. The check matters more than the bump: asset-hub.html and pm-scheduler.html BOTH appear elsewhere in sw.js and a loose grep listed them as shell files; parsing the actual 31-entry array showed neither is precached, and search-overlay.js is not either. This worker's own history records the opposite error twice (v234 and v236 both bumped for pages that turned out not to be in the shell, and said so afterwards) — over-bumping is harmless and under-bumping ships a stale build, but knowing which is which needs the array, not recall. validate_pwa green (7 PASS / 0 FAIL). || ★THE LANDING PAGE'S '5 MB' CLAIM, MEASURED - AND TODAY'S ASSET FIX IS WHAT MAKES IT TRUE (2026-08-28). index.html promises, twice, that 'the app installs as a PWA in under 5 MB'. Measured the actual precache: 31 SHELL_FILES, ALL 31 resolving, 2.37 MB total. The claim holds with room. ★AND IT WOULD NOT HAVE, YESTERDAY: the shell was carrying two 1254x1254 portrait masters (2016 KB + 1997 KB) and a 229 KB logo until this session's T160 fix replaced them with 9.6/9.8 KB derivatives and a 640px logo - about 4.05 MB. Add that back and the shell is roughly 6.4 MB, and the sentence on the front page becomes false. A marketing claim was quietly out of date because an ASSET regressed underneath it, which is a drift no copy review would ever catch. ★THE OTHER HALF OF THIS READING IS SHELL INTEGRITY: all 31 entries resolve to files that exist. That is not cosmetic - the SW install calls addAll, which REJECTS ATOMICALLY on a single 404, so one bad path means no precache at all and no offline shell for anyone. This worker's own history records exactly that failure, portraits pointed at names that 'never existed, which fails the SW install addAll'. Zero missing today. ★INSTRUMENT NOTE: the first extraction reported 8 'missing' files that were COMMENT FRAGMENTS - the shell array is heavily commented and a naive string-literal scan reads prose as paths. Stripping comments before extracting moved the count from a false 23-of-31 to a true 31-of-31. pct STAYS 92. (★I TYPED 78 AND THE PROGRAMME TOTAL CAUGHT IT: the overall moved 79.72 -> 79.65, exactly -14 points over 200 trajectories, which is the arithmetic signature of lowering ONE entry by 14. This edit only ADDED verification - a measured 2.37 MB against a 5 MB claim, and 31 of 31 shell files resolving - so the score could rise or hold and could not fall. Restored to 92. Same class as the invented pct earlier this session, caught the same way: a scoreboard that moves the wrong direction is the check on a number I asserted rather than derived.) || ★MY OWN FIXES WOULD HAVE SHIPPED INVISIBLY TO EVERY INSTALLED USER (2026-08-28). nav-hub.js is in sw.js SHELL_FILES - precached, served from the cache to installed users until CACHE_NAME changes. Today's v243 bump was made at 14:38 for an earlier nav-hub change; I then edited nav-hub.js THREE more times, finishing at 17:30, nearly three hours later. Without another bump, an installed worker would have kept serving the v243 copy and received NONE of it: not T149's flagged-post badge fix, not T144's cross-tab convergence, not T126's reconnect refresh. The fixes would have been live for browser users and absent for exactly the population the PWA exists to serve - the April stale-nav incident's shape, where a shell file sat cached for weeks. Bumped to v244 with the three changes named in the comment, following the file's own convention (130 prior bumps are preserved as commented history, each naming what changed and why). ★AND THE GATE DOES NOT CATCH THIS, which is the instrument finding. validate_sw_shell_membership asserts that all 8 shell HTML pages EXIST and that CACHE_NAME is SET - both true before my bump and both true after, so it passed while the cache was stale. What it does not compare is TIMES: whether any file in SHELL_FILES is newer than sw.js itself. That is a two-line check (max mtime over SHELL_FILES versus sw.js's) and it is the difference between a gate that confirms the mechanism exists and one that confirms it was USED. I found this by reading mtimes by hand because I happened to wonder; the next person will not - so the gate now does it. ★INSTRUMENT CLOSED: validate_sw_shell_membership gained _stale_shell_files, which compares every PRECACHED asset's mtime against sw.js's and fails when one is newer, naming the files and telling the reader to bump CACHE_NAME. Deliberately scoped to all shell entries (.html, .js, .css, .json) rather than only the HTML pages the old parser read, because the shared chrome is where silent staleness hurts most - nav-hub.js ships on 31 pages, so one stale copy is 31 stale pages. RESURRECTION PROVEN BOTH WAYS: green with the v244 bump in place, and RED naming nav-hub.js the moment that file is touched again. A gate that confirms a mechanism EXISTS is not the same as one that confirms it was USED, and this one now does the second. pct 92 -> 92. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: BUILT + registered lock gate pwa-sw-central-register (nav-hub.js shell registers the SW at the derived whSwRoot on every page; no hardcoded /workhive/ prod-404); teeth + real-file PASS. pct -> 92. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-06 via tools/cwv_probe.mjs + gate cwv (the existing two-tool CWV scorer, recalled rather than rebuilt): headless MOBILE Chromium measured 119 public surfaces for warm-median LCP, INP and CLS - 0 over threshold on all three - and tools/cwv_gate.py ratcheted PASS with no check over baseline.
trajectories.note: ★AND THE FIX WOULD HAVE BEEN INVISIBLE TO INSTALLED USERS WITHOUT A CACHE BUMP (2026-08-27). report-sender.html is one of only TWO html files in sw.js's SHELL_FILES (the other is offline-fallback), so an installed PWA serves the CACHED copy of it. Editing the chips without bumping CACHE_NAME would have left the people most likely to send a weekly pack - the ones who installed the app - still choosing between reports with no window shown, while every gate and every browser tab said the fix had shipped. That is the April stale-nav class: correct code, invisible to the users who matter most. ★FOUND BY CHECKING WHICH EDITED FILES ARE IN THE SHELL, not by remembering - a mechanical intersection of 'what I touched' against SHELL_FILES, which took one command and would have taken a production incident otherwise. v240 -> v241 with the reason named, following the bump history the file already keeps commented above the active line (each entry saying which shell file changed and why). sw.js parses, exactly one active CACHE_NAME, PWA gate 7 PASS / 0 FAIL. ★THE EXACT RULE FOR WHEN A SW BUMP IS REQUIRED, VERIFIED FROM THE FETCH HANDLER (2026-08-27) - so the next editor does not have to re-derive it or bump defensively. sw.js is CACHE-FIRST (`caches.match(request) || fetch(request)`) but it precaches ONLY the 27 SHELL_FILES and never calls cache.put at runtime. So: a file IN SHELL_FILES is served from cache until CACHE_NAME changes, and a file NOT in it is always fetched from the network. That makes the bump rule mechanical - intersect what you edited against SHELL_FILES, and bump if the intersection is non-empty. ★APPLIED TO THIS SESSION: of eleven edited pages plus utils.js, exactly ONE is in the shell - report-sender.html - so v241 was required and sufficient. utils.js is NOT precached despite being the most-edited shared file today, so its changes reach installed users on the next load without any bump; nav-hub.js IS precached but was only read, never edited. Supabase, Google Fonts and gstatic are explicitly network-only, so no API response is ever served stale. ★THE VALUE OF WRITING THIS DOWN is that 'did my edit reach installed users' is otherwise answered by memory, and the April stale-nav incident is what memory gets wrong.

Translating only the new ones would have left the region half-translated, which reads worse to a Filipino worker than a consistently English one and hides the real gap. Recorded here rather than fixed piecemeal: the unit is the whole join-error region, EN and FIL together, not the three newest lines. ★MEASURED: THE ENTIRE ERROR TAXONOMY IS ENGLISH-ONLY (2026-08-27). Counted _t() calls inside every central error helper in utils.js - whReadError, whWriteError, whAiError, whFnError and the new whVoiceError - and the answer is ZERO in all five. The pages are bilingual through _t(en, fil) and the taxonomy they delegate to is not, so a worker running the FIL toggle gets Filipino chrome and an English sentence at exactly the moment something has gone wrong and precision matters most: 'Your session has expired. Sign in again, then retry - your typed work is still on this page.' ★THIS CONFIRMS THE DEBT THIS TRAJECTORY ALREADY RECORDED (the error-taxonomy sweep added EN branches while FIL kept prior copy) and puts a number on it: it is not a handful of strings on a few pages, it is the SHARED LAYER, so every page that adopted the taxonomy inherited an English failure voice. Fixing it centrally is one edit per helper rather than per call site - the same leverage that made adoption worth doing. ★SELF-AUDIT NOTE: whVoiceError, added today, returns English like its four siblings. I checked whether I had introduced a FIL regression and I had not - the sites it replaced ('Voice error: ' + code, 'Mic error: ' + code) were English too - but 'consistent with the family' is only a defence while the family itself is the debt. ★THE SHARED FAILURE VOICE NOW SPEAKS FILIPINO (2026-08-27) - fixed centrally, where the debt actually lived. whAiError and whVoiceError now return through _t(en, fil): nine branches translated between them (session expired, AI rate limit, service busy, network, generic; and for the mic - browser blocking, no microphone, no internet, unsupported language, stopped early, generic). Verified LIVE in both languages rather than by reading the source: every branch returns a different string under WH_LANG='fil', and the caller-supplied fallback correctly stays untranslated because it is the PAGE's own English sentence to own. ★WHY CENTRAL WAS THE RIGHT PLACE: _t is defined in utils.js itself, forty lines above the helper that never used it, and it falls back to EN when a phrase has no FIL - so partial coverage can never blank a message and this was safe to do incrementally. Every page that adopted the taxonomy inherits the translation at once; the alternative was one edit per call site across the roster. ★REGISTER MATCHED TO THE PLATFORM'S EXISTING FIL COPY rather than invented: Taglish, technical nouns left in English ('Nag-expire na ang session mo', 'Naabot mo na ang AI rate limit', 'suriin ang koneksyon at subukan muli'), following the shape of lines already shipping like 'Hindi ma-load ang activity log. Suriin ang koneksyon at subukan muli.' REMAINS: whReadError, whWriteError and whFnError are still EN-only - the same one-edit-each fix, and the next slice of this trajectory. ★whReadError AND whWriteError NOW SPEAK FILIPINO TOO (2026-08-27) - the taxonomy is bilingual on all four high-traffic helpers, seventeen branches translated in total. Verified live in both languages on each, not read from source. ★TWO JUDGEMENTS WORTH RECORDING, both about what NOT to translate: (1) the caller-supplied `fallback` passes through untouched, because it is the PAGE's own English sentence and a page that wants a Filipino fallback passes one; (2) whWriteError's deliberate-guard passthrough (`return msg`) is left alone - that branch carries a policy refusal that took the trouble to explain itself ('Listing needs PHP50 credits held and you have 0 available'), and rewriting someone else's explanation in another language is not translation, it is replacement. Both verified as differ=false in the live probe, which is the CORRECT result rather than a miss. ★AND A COPY DEFECT I INTRODUCED AND CAUGHT IN THE SAME PASS: the FIL sentences interpolate the caller's noun, which arrives with its English article ('the activity log'), so the first version read 'ang THE activity log'. Filipino carries its own article. Stripping a leading 'the ' for the FIL half only gives 'Hindi ma-load ang activity log' - which is character-for-character the shape of a line already shipping elsewhere on the platform. Reading the OUTPUT rather than the diff is what caught it. REMAINS: whFnError (which mostly delegates to whAiError and so is already largely covered), and the FIL parity of the per-page copy this trajectory originally set out to true up. ★GATE BUILT BECAUSE THE REGISTER REFUSED THE CLAIM: moving T45 to 'locking' failed validation with 'status locking but names no gate - locking MEANS the gate is built, so either register it or drop back to fixing'. That is the registry doing exactly its job, and the honest answer was to build the lock rather than lower the status: taxonomy-speaks-filipino drives all 14 branches in-page under both WH_LANG values. It is worth noting how easily the other choice would have passed unnoticed - the work WAS done, the claim only outran its proof by one artefact. ★ALL FIVE HELPERS DONE, 15/15 BRANCHES GATED. whFnError's own fallback translated too - its other three paths return the edge function's OWN sentence or delegate to whAiError, so one string was all it owned. ★AND ADDING IT CAUGHT A FLAW IN MY OWN PROVER: whFnError is ASYNC (it reads the FunctionsHttpError body), so calling it synchronously stringified to '[object Promise]' - and crucially that made EN and FIL compare EQUAL, i.e. the case reported a real translation as missing. A probe that awaits nothing turns every async branch into a meaningless-but-equal comparison; the same shape would have silently passed a case that was supposed to stay the same. Awaiting fixes both directions, and non-promises are unaffected, so one shape covers every helper. ★THE MECHANICAL HALF OF FIL PARITY IS CLEAN - MEASURED (2026-08-27). All 46 _t(en, fil) call sites platform-wide were compared argument-for-argument; 5 pass the same string twice, and all 5 are defensible rather than missed: 'hives' is the product's OWN noun (translating it would rename the thing), and 'Shift', 'rows', 'Avg DT' and 'WORLD CLASS' are terms Philippine workplaces routinely code-switch in English - a Tagalog sentence carrying 'shift' reads more naturally to this audience than a translated coinage would. So an identical-args lint would have a baseline of 5 legitimate entries and catch nothing today; it is not built for that reason. ★WHAT REMAINS IS THE HARDER HALF AND IS NOT MECHANICAL: page copy that has no _t() wrapper at all. That needs the product's Filipino VOICE decided phrase by phrase, not a bulk pass - the same reason the taxonomy prover asserts that two things must NOT translate (the caller's own fallback, and a policy refusal that already explained itself). Recorded so the next pass starts from the copy inventory rather than re-deriving that the _t sites are fine.

trajectories.title: The first-week loop: day-2 return, remembered context, honest re-engagement
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, worker 390, two-session day-2 return): the return surfaces graded VERIFIED-GOOD - personal time-aware greeting ('Good afternoon, Bryan - Tuesday, Aug 25 - Afternoon Shift'), an action-first priority banner ('29 PM tasks are due - claim the next one') with honest denominators ('29 of 30 assets'), ZERO dark-pattern urgency vocabulary, streak copy guilt-free ('keep your streak going, your XP this week feeds your hive standing'), no notification beg at first paint. RECORDED GAP (scoped decision for Ian, not built unilaterally): no 'since your last visit / while you were away' surface exists (RE1-as-journey) - the priority banner answers 'what needs me NOW', which may be the better field answer; a changelog-style return brief would be a net-new surface. G5 filter restore NOT re-derived (PDDA holds it at 100%). Remaining: day-N clock-advanced harness (T57 shared), digest->deep-link fidelity (Resend secret = Ian-gated), empty-week honesty on a quiet-hive fixture, notification opt-in moment probes (T105 seam). || FIXING->60 (2026-08-26): the notification opt-in MOMENT probed, and the platform is doing this well. Two prompts exist and both are earned: marketplace-seller's svcEnablePush() runs from an onclick behind online/support/signed-in checks and refuses honestly ('Alerts stay off until you allow notifications'); voice-handler's _requestPushPerm() fires ONLY when the worker has VERBALLY opted in and only while the state is still 'default', inside the open gesture window, so a prior denial is never re-prompted. Neither begs at first paint. ★WHY THIS IS WORTH GATING WHEN IT ALREADY PASSES: a mistimed prompt is the one UX mistake with NO undo - the person says no because they have no reason yet, and the browser remembers forever with no in-app way back. Locked as 'permission-in-context' (guarded + not-at-load), teeth proven with an injected DOMContentLoaded prompt. ★AND THE GATE'S FIRST VERSION ACCUSED A CORRECT PROMPT: a 1200-char lookback could not see that svcEnablePush is bound to an onclick 350 lines earlier, because a gesture binding is a property of the enclosing FUNCTION, not of nearby text. It now resolves the function name and asks whether the file wires it to a click - the same structural-over-proximity correction that has come up repeatedly this session. REMAINING: the empty-week honesty walk on a quiet-hive fixture and digest deep-link fidelity (Resend secret = Ian-gated). || GATES RECORDED 2026-08-27: permission-in-context. The basis already named this instrument as built and it IS registered in run_platform_checks and green — the gates field was simply never filled, so the registry understated what this trajectory owns. Verified registered + exit 0 before recording; nothing about the work changed, only the bookkeeping. || ★THE PERMISSION ETHIC HOLDS, AND THE 'WHAT CHANGED' MECHANISM GOT FIXED THIS TURN (2026-08-28). Notification opt-in timing - the probe that catches most products - PASSES on both surfaces that ask, and passes for the right reasons. Notification.requestPermission is called in exactly two places platform-wide. marketplace-seller reaches it only through svcEnablePush(), wired to an explicit 'Enable job notifications' button, so the browser prompt follows a deliberate click. voice-handler reaches it only when _isPushOptInReply(transcript) is true - the worker has VERBALLY said yes mid-conversation - and the code comments that the user-gesture window is open. Neither fires at first paint, which is the anti-pattern this probe exists to catch. Better still, the voice path is guarded by pushState === 'default', so a worker who already DENIED is never asked again: denial is respected rather than re-nagged, which is the half of permission ethics most implementations skip. ★THE DAY-2 'WHAT CHANGED SINCE YOU LEFT' SURFACE turns out to be the nav-hub community badge - a since-last-seen count bounded by wh_community_last_seen:<hive>, excluding the reader's own posts, with a 3-day lookback so a returning worker sees recent activity without being flooded. That is a real re-engagement mechanism and it was materially WRONG until today: T149 found it counting moderated posts the reader's feed hides (badge said 3, feed opened to 2) and T144 found it computed once per page load and never again, so a worker who read the posts in one tab kept being told they were new in another. Both fixed this turn, which means this trajectory's central return-visit signal is now honest in a way it was not when the trajectory was written. ★HONEST LIMIT: the empty-week question - does a quiet hive resist faking urgency (DP1) - cannot be settled by reading code, because it is about what the surfaces SAY when there is nothing to report. It needs the multi-day clock-advanced walk this trajectory specs, over a hive seeded quiet, and is not claimed here. pct 60 -> 74. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED (fix+gate) - all assigned gates PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] pct -> 100. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_persona_arcs.mjs (gate persona-arcs), 8/8 lenses clean. Speech capture ships with a typed path to the SAME record and six distinct failure causes named in words, so a refused microphone does not end the journey for a worker whose hands are full - 478 entries recorded (T12). All 12 achievements carry a description and 79 have been awarded, with the reason rendered beside the badge on two surfaces, so an engineer earning something can find out what for (T17). Twenty-eight pages remember where a person was and six can say what changed while they were away, covering both the day-two return and the three-month one (T46, T57). Forty pages stamp a figure with its source, 44 canonical truth views stand behind them, and 27 let a person open the rows, so a skeptic can take a headline number apart rather than trust it (T47). Fifty-six learn articles are linked from inside the product and 30 pages explain themselves in place, so a graduate is not sent to search the web for how to use the tool (T54). Lucena Pharmaceutical runs two supervisors, and hive.html checks for a co-supervisor before forcing a hand-over - so leaving is safe when another remains, and the last one is not waved through (T56). Fourteen pages surface device or session state, an idle timeout ships, and there is a way out, so someone who cares about their account has controls beyond closing the tab (T59). THE SCALE ROW IS STATED HONESTLY RATHER THAN CLAIMED: the largest hive in this data holds 8 active members, so twenty is beyond what it can prove; what is asserted instead is that all three roster surfaces BOUND what they render rather than drawing every member at once, which is the property that decides whether twenty people works (T61). TWO LENSES PASSED TOO EASILY ON THE FIRST RUN AND WERE TIGHTENED, both recorded in the prover: 'the reason beside the badge' matched the word description in every page's meta tag and counted 33 surfaces where the honest answer is 2; and 'surfaces session state' counted every page that merely LOADS device-fingerprint.js, when a script tag is not a control a person can act on.

trajectories.title: A skeptical engineer verifies one KPI end-to-end
trajectories.basis: the skeptic's hand-check RAN and PASSED on worst-MTBF: the tile states value+asset+n+formula+standard ('0.6d - CT-001 between failures - from 2 failures - ISO 14224 calendar days'); psql recompute of CT-001's last failure pair = 14.1h = 0.59d = the glass's 0.6d. The tile's own 'from 2 failures' phrase corrected my wrong all-time span/(n-1) formula - the glass alone sufficed, which IS the oracle's bar. Remaining: OEE hand-check + headline-KPI cross-surface parity gate (wave close). || FIXING->60 (2026-08-26): the OEE hand-check RUN, and the glass passes its own bar. analytics renders 'OEE (AVG, PARTIAL) 88% · Avg across 20 assets · WORLD CLASS · ISO 22400-2:2014 · Availability x Quality only. Add each asset's cycle time to include Performance.' - the value, the denominator, the STANDARD, which factors are actually in the product, and what to do about the missing one. A skeptic can recompute from the glass alone and knows exactly what they are recomputing, which is this trajectory's whole test. ★WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: OEE is a three-factor product, so a two-factor figure is not approximately right, it is systematically HIGH - the omitted factor can only reduce it. A supervisor who takes 88% into a management meeting without knowing Performance was excluded is carrying a number they cannot defend under the first question. The card refuses to let that happen. Locked as 'partial-metric-declared' (a headline OEE must name its factor basis; teeth proven by stripping the clause). ★THE GATE ASSERTS THE DECLARATION, NOT THE VALUE, and does NOT demand full OEE: whether this hive has cycle times is a data question, and the honest answer to missing data is to say what is missing. This pairs with kpi-parity (PM compliance agreeing across analytics and pm-scheduler) - one gate for the number being the same everywhere, one for the number saying what it is. REMAINING: extending the cross-surface parity slice to MTBF/OEE once a second surface renders them with a figure (wave close). || GATES RECORDED 2026-08-27: partial-metric-declared. The basis already named this instrument as built and it IS registered in run_platform_checks and green — the gates field was simply never filled, so the registry understated what this trajectory owns. Verified registered + exit 0 before recording; nothing about the work changed, only the bookkeeping. || THE PARITY PRECONDITION IS MET FOR MTBF, NOT FOR OEE, AND ONLY SCOPE-MATCHED (checked 2026-08-27). Two surfaces bind an MTBF FIGURE to an element - analytics.html (an-mtbf-hero + sub + tag) and asset-hub.html (risk-mtbf, :1930) - while OEE binds on analytics ALONE, so that half is still genuinely waiting for a second renderer rather than being ready and unbuilt. ★BUT THE TWO MTBFs ARE NOT THE SAME NUMBER, and a tile-to-tile comparison would be the two-windows-one-name category error this trajectory exists to catch: analytics renders 'Worst MTBF (partial)' - a hive-level SELECTION over assets - and asset-hub renders the SELECTED ASSET's MTBF inside its risk panel. Comparing them directly would manufacture a disagreement out of two correct figures. THE PARITY THAT IS ACTUALLY BUILDABLE is scope-matched, and the worst-MTBF tile already carries what it needs: it NAMES its asset ('0.6d - CT-001 between failures - from 2 failures - ISO 14224 calendar days'), so the test is to read that asset and value, open asset-hub for THAT asset, and require the figures to agree - the drill-path shape, not a tile diff. Recorded as the spec for the slice rather than built, because the walk needs the live pair and the wave close is where the cross-surface instrument lands. || A FIELD WHOSE NAME IS A COMPLIANCE CLAIM AND WHOSE COMPUTATION IS AN ACTIVITY COUNT (2026-08-27). Searched the DB for functions that admit to being provisional and found two. rerank_kb_chunks is inert (nothing calls it). The other is inside compute_hive_readiness, the function behind the readiness score: `v_audit_compliant := (v_audit_writes_30d >= 10); -- placeholder; full compliance audit later`. A hive is 'audit compliant' if somebody wrote ten audit-log rows in thirty days. That measures ACTIVITY, and the field is named for COMPLIANCE. ★AND IT IS NOT PRIVATE: it is returned in the result payload as 'audit_compliant', and it gates a MATURITY TIER - one of four conditions in an ELSIF ladder that holds a hive back from the next stage. So the approximation both leaves the function under a name that overstates it and moves a stage a user sees. No page renders the field by that name today, so the exposure is the tier plus any future consumer who trusts the label - which is precisely how this class does its damage: the next person to read `audit_compliant` has no reason to suspect it counts writes. ★THE HONEST PART IS THAT THE CODE SAYS SO - the comment is right there, and this is a knowingly staged approximation rather than a mistake. The gap is that the HONESTY lives in the source while the CLAIM travels in the payload. Cheapest fix is a rename (audit_activity_ok) so the field says what it measures until the real audit lands; that costs nothing and removes the trap. Recorded rather than renamed unilaterally - it is a contract field with consumers. Remaining: that rename decision, plus the hand-check chain for the headline KPIs. || ★THE HAND-CHECK CHAIN WAS WALKED FOR MTBF, AND IT RECONCILES (2026-08-28) - the skeptic's test this trajectory exists for, run as the skeptic rather than described. WHAT THE GLASS ALONE OFFERS on analytics: the window ('Based on your logbook - last 90 days (rolling, ending now)'), the snapshot's age and how to refresh it ('Saved snapshot, computed 7h ago - Refresh to recompute'), the definition in words ('lowest MTBF in days across all assets with at least one corrective failure in the window'), the standard (ISO 14224:2016 SS9.3), the subject and value ('Worst MTBF CT-001 - 0.6d'), the INPUT COUNT ('CT-001 between failures - from 2 failures'), a per-machine table of failures-and-MTBF for every asset, the population total ('153 total failures'), a PARTIAL marker on both MTBF and OEE, and the verdict thresholds. That is enough to attempt a recomputation, which is the bar. ★AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT LOOKED LIKE A DEFECT: 2 failures in a 90-day window reads as ~45d, not 0.6d. Checking the source rows settles it - CT-001's two Breakdown/Corrective entries are 2026-06-14 10:05:02 and 2026-06-15 00:10:43, 14h06m apart = 0.587d, which rounds to the 0.6d displayed. So the page means the INTERVAL BETWEEN failures, exactly as its own label says ('average between failures'), not window/count - and a skeptic who reads the label rather than assuming the formula gets the right answer. The glass is hand-checkable and the number survives an independent recomputation from the rows. Worth noting the honest edge: with n=2 there is exactly ONE interval, so 'average' is generous - but '(PARTIAL)' and 'from 2 failures' both sit next to the figure, so the reader is told the sample is tiny rather than left to discover it. pct 78 -> 88. Remaining: the audit_compliant rename decision (a contract field with consumers - not renamed unilaterally), and the same hand-check for OEE. || AND OEE HAND-CHECKS TOO, ROW BY ROW (2026-08-28), so the chain is done for BOTH headline KPIs. The OEE presentation is the strongest on the platform for a skeptic: it declares itself '(AVG, PARTIAL)', cites ISO 22400-2:2014, states the full formula (Availability x Performance x Quality), states WHICH factor is missing and WHY in the same breath ('Availability x Quality only. Add each asset's cycle time to include Performance.'), names the population ('30 ASSET(S)'), and then publishes a PER-ASSET TABLE of Availability | Quality | OEE (partial) - which is what makes the arithmetic checkable rather than merely explained. VERIFIED by multiplying the published columns: CH-001 0.979 x 0.853 = 0.8351 -> 83.5% shown; BE-002 0.967 x 0.875 = 0.8461 -> 84.6% shown; BF-002 0.946 x 0.90 = 0.8514 -> 85.1% shown. Three of three reconcile to the displayed figure. ★THE 'PARTIAL' LABEL IS DOING REAL WORK HERE rather than hedging: an OEE that silently omitted Performance would read as a complete OEE and overstate the plant; this one says what it is, says what would complete it, and publishes the two factors it DID use so anyone can check them. Together with the MTBF walk above, both headline KPIs on this platform survive an independent recomputation from what the glass alone shows - which is this trajectory's whole question. STATUS locking/95: the hand-check chain is done and gated by partial-metric-declared; what remains is the audit_compliant rename, a contract field with consumers and therefore a decision rather than a fix. || ★PCT FIELD CORRECTED DOWN TO MATCH THIS BASIS (2026-08-31). The field read 95 while the basis's own last word was 88 - a later note revised the number and only the prose was updated. Every one of the six rows found this way was inflated, never deflated, which is the direction drift always takes when nothing checks it: the number a reader trusts drifts up while the narrative underneath it says otherwise. Now gated by pct-matches-basis. pct -> 88. pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] pct -> 100. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_persona_arcs.mjs (gate persona-arcs), 8/8 lenses clean. Speech capture ships with a typed path to the SAME record and six distinct failure causes named in words, so a refused microphone does not end the journey for a worker whose hands are full - 478 entries recorded (T12). All 12 achievements carry a description and 79 have been awarded, with the reason rendered beside the badge on two surfaces, so an engineer earning something can find out what for (T17). Twenty-eight pages remember where a person was and six can say what changed while they were away, covering both the day-two return and the three-month one (T46, T57). Forty pages stamp a figure with its source, 44 canonical truth views stand behind them, and 27 let a person open the rows, so a skeptic can take a headline number apart rather than trust it (T47). Fifty-six learn articles are linked from inside the product and 30 pages explain themselves in place, so a graduate is not sent to search the web for how to use the tool (T54). Lucena Pharmaceutical runs two supervisors, and hive.html checks for a co-supervisor before forcing a hand-over - so leaving is safe when another remains, and the last one is not waved through (T56). Fourteen pages surface device or session state, an idle timeout ships, and there is a way out, so someone who cares about their account has controls beyond closing the tab (T59). THE SCALE ROW IS STATED HONESTLY RATHER THAN CLAIMED: the largest hive in this data holds 8 active members, so twenty is beyond what it can prove; what is asserted instead is that all three roster surfaces BOUND what they render rather than drawing every member at once, which is the property that decides whether twenty people works (T61). TWO LENSES PASSED TOO EASILY ON THE FIRST RUN AND WERE TIGHTENED, both recorded in the prover: 'the reason beside the badge' matched the word description in every page's meta tag and counted 33 surfaces where the honest answer is 2; and 'surfaces session state' counted every page that merely LOADS device-fingerprint.js, when a script tag is not a control a person can act on.

trajectories.title: Keyboard-only + screen-reader user completes a core flow
trajectories.basis: keyboard-only journey COMPLETES end-to-end: ?signin=1 modal focuses si-username, typed sign-in works; asset-picker-btn reachable in 7 tabs, Enter opens with focus IN the search; FIXED the arrows gap (measured: ArrowDown+Enter selected nothing; options were Tab-only) - combobox wiring added (ArrowDown from search enters the list, arrows navigate, ArrowUp from first returns to search, Enter activates the native buttons); proven: AC-001 picked by keys, wizard completed, entry saved + visible. Remaining: NVDA announcement-coverage probe + the no-mouse-events harness + data tables (wave close). || ANNOUNCEMENT-COVERAGE SWEEP: 64 toast/error containers, ONE real gap (2026-08-28). Swept every toast and error surface for a live region. The shared machinery is sound - whListError renders role='alert', index's showToast creates its host with role='status' + aria-live='polite', and engineering-design's #toast carries role='alert' aria-live='polite' in markup, so the two separate toast implementations both announce. ★MOST OF THE 17 APPARENT GAPS WERE MY REGEX: toast-icon and toast-text are CHILDREN of a div that already announces (a child needs no role of its own), and alert-msg in alert-hub is a list row's message TEXT that matched on the substring 'alert' while being no kind of announcement surface. Judging containers by name rather than by their parent chain manufactures a11y defects out of correct markup. THE ONE REAL GAP: integrations' #import-error-section, revealed when a CMMS import SKIPS rows, had no role and no aria-live - a sighted user watched a red panel appear and a screen-reader user was told NOTHING, so they would believe the import landed whole. Fixed with role='alert' aria-live='assertive' (rows silently dropped from an equipment import is not something to mention at the next convenient pause), and the existing reveal order already suited a live region: the section is un-hidden BEFORE #error-detail's text is set, so the change fires inside a region already in the accessibility tree. Verified live: role and aria-live present, page clean, no errors. Remaining: the scripted keyboard-only journey and an NVDA pass. || ★KEYBOARD WALK OF THE WORKER'S CORE CAPTURE PAGE - CLEAN, MEASURED (2026-08-28). Tabbed through logbook 43 stops with no mouse. ZERO focused-but-invisible stops (the phantom-stop class Q2 exists for), ZERO stops without an accessible name, and 43 of 43 with a painted focus ring. The order opens with a real 'Skip to main content' link, then home, back, Voice Journal, the page-guide disclosure, and straight into the capture controls - Speak, Capture, the asset picker, Scan equipment tag, 'What happened?', Clear form, My Entries. That is the actual task order a worker would want, not DOM order that happens to be tabbable. ★RECORDED AS A POSITIVE BECAUSE THIS TRAJECTORY EXISTS TO DOUBT IT: it was specced against the axe-0-violations false-100 lesson, where a static scan passed while aria-label-only controls were invisible to sighted keyboard users. A live walk is the instrument that can tell those apart, and on this page it finds nothing to fault - every stop is visible, named, and ringed. The remaining half of this trajectory is the ANNOUNCEMENT axis (do state changes reach a live region) and the modal trap/restore cycle under a real screen reader, neither of which a tab walk can see. pct -> 78. || ★STATE CHANGES ARE ANNOUNCED, AND THE SHARED NOTICE LAYER IS THE BEST-BUILT PART (2026-08-28). This trajectory's sharpest a11y probe is whether a change of state reaches somebody who cannot see it. Broadly yes: 34 pages carry aria-live regions and 32 carry role="alert" containers, so the platform announces rather than merely paints. The canonical notice helper _whShowNotice creates its element with role="status" and aria-live="polite" - correct for session, permission and connection notices, which are informational rather than urgent. ★TWO DETAILS IN ITS COMMENTS SHOW THE THINKING: each notice owns a DIFFERENT bottom offset (88px session, 160px permission, 232px connection) because 'two boxes at an identical offset would cover each other exactly and the top one would read as the only message' - a sighted-and-screen-reader problem both. And self-expiry is declared non-optional, with the reason: 'a pinned notice makes a transient failure look permanent to a person, and it contaminated a later probe that read a stale Your session expired and scored four innocent pages as blaming the session'. A notice that outlives its truth misleads the user AND the instruments. ★THE UNEVEN LAYER IS TOASTS: showToast is not in utils.js as one canonical implementation - pages define their own (analytics and index both carry inline versions), so announcement quality varies by page rather than being guaranteed by a shared helper. Combined with T180's finding that only 2 pages use aria-describedby, the shape is: announcement is broadly present, ASSOCIATION and CANONICALITY are not. ★What this does not prove is the JOURNEY - completing T9's logging flow keyboard-only, under a real screen reader, in sane tab order. That needs the no-mouse harness this trajectory specs. pct 78 -> 86. pct -> 86. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: BUILT + registered lock gate picker-arrow-keys asserting the logbook asset-picker handles ArrowDown/ArrowUp + arrows move focus (the Tab-only gap T48 fixed); teeth + real-file PASS. Awaiting board earn. pct -> 92. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_a11y_path.mjs (gate a11y-path): 19/19 signed-in surfaces pass a real keyboard walk - every on-page interactive control reached by Tab, a visible focus ring at each stop, no trap - plus the landmark and heading ladder and the live-region-at-load check a screen reader depends on. Built because axe cannot press Tab and cannot know whether an aria-live region existed BEFORE the message that needed announcing. One product fix came out of it: four pages had no navigation landmark at all, fixed once in nav-hub.js.

fixes: voice-journal.html (erasure route added to the existing permanence disclosure)

trajectories.note: ★THE RIGHT-TO-ERASURE IS VOICE-ONLY, AND THE PAGE NEVER SAID WHERE TO GO (2026-08-27). Tracing what a worker can take back took FOUR corrections, and every intermediate answer would have shipped a false statement into the platform's most private surface: (1) 'there is no delete' - WRONG: voice-handler's _isErasureRequest detects "delete my voice history" / "burahin mo lahat", the agent asks for a yes because it cannot be undone, a scoped DELETE runs against that worker's rows and an audit row records it; (2) 'you can say OR TYPE it' - WRONG: the check sits in _converseInline, called only from _onStopRecording, so it is reached ONLY after a voice recording, and this page's typed box goes processTurn -> callJournalAgent -> ai-gateway without ever touching voice-handler; (3) there is no typed route anywhere - assistant.html has no erasure path and the companion panel has no text input; (4) a SINGLE note cannot be removed at all, because renderHistory offers only 'Speak again' and ai-gateway persists the row inside the same call that generates the reply. ★WHY VOICE-ONLY MATTERS MORE THAN IT SOUNDS: this page's typed fallback exists, in its own words, for 'a loud plant floor, a denied mic, or a worker who cannot speak' - precisely the people left with no way to invoke the right. ★AND THE FIX WAS ALMOST DUPLICATION: the permanence was ALREADY disclosed on the primary surface ('saved as soon as the assistant replies ... an entry cannot be edited or removed here afterwards'), and a first attempt added a SECOND copy of it inside a collapsed <details> nobody opens - a new element surfacing what already had a home. Reverted. What was genuinely missing was the other half: the copy said a note cannot be removed HERE and never said where it CAN be. One clause now completes that sentence, pointing at the documented Data Rights Request route which validate_erasure_path_intact already proves the database honours. The voice phrase is deliberately NOT advertised as the remedy, because for a worker who cannot speak it is not one. ★STILL OPEN (product decision, and small): wiring the typed path to the same check - both _isErasureRequest and _executeErasure are already exported, and _executeErasure needs only db + hive_id + worker_name, all available on this page - plus whether a per-entry delete should exist at all given the row is embedded for retrieval.

trajectories.title: Every export control produces a truthful, complete artifact
trajectories.basis: flagship audited GREEN by design: audit-log's Export CSV does a paginated FULL fetch (range-walked, never the display window), resolves the range filter the same way the screen does, falls back HONESTLY ('exports the N entries loaded' - named, never silent), and the artifact STATES ITS OWN SCOPE in embedded meta (hive, range) - the compliance-export row-cap class is extinct here. Remaining: the export-fidelity sweep across engineering-design BOM/SOW CSVs + resume + PDF exporter, psql row-count audits per artifact (wave close). (2026-08-26: one more capped export found and fixed by a different lens - logbook's TEAM branch exported the loaded window (~30) instead of the filtered whole (941). See T129.) EXPORT-FIDELITY SWEEP COMPLETED 2026-08-26 - every download path on the platform enumerated and each judged against the cap class: (1) logbook CSV - MINE branch already paged (earlier arc), TEAM branch FIXED today (was exporting ~30 of 941; now paginated with the same filters + honest shortfall toast, proven 941==941); (2) audit-log CSV - already hardened 2026-08-19 for this exact class, with the scope resolved the same way the screen resolves it; (3) resume exports (cover letter .txt, JSON Resume, .docx) - a single document per person, no cap by shape; (4) engineering-design BOM CSV + SVG diagram - written from the in-memory working set the user just generated, which IS the artifact, not a bounded DB read. So the capped-export class is closed on every path that has one. Remaining: basis/window STAMPED INSIDE the artifacts (a spreadsheet outliving its context), phone download reality, empty-set export honesty. BASIS-INSIDE-THE-ARTIFACT advanced same pass, including a claim MY OWN fix had just falsified: the logbook CSV's meta block said 'Scope: team view (current search results)' - true while that branch exported the loaded window, misleading the moment it started paging the whole filtered history. Rewritten to state what the file now contains AND the cut it was made with: 'Scope: whole team history for hive Baguio Textile Mills, filtered by from=2026-08-18 + to=2026-08-25' (verified by evaluating the export's own inputs in-page). A spreadsheet outlives the screen that made it, so it has to carry its own scope. Harness note: the download itself resisted capture (no download event, no blob interception under the probe), so the mechanics were proven by row count (941==941) and the copy at its source - stated rather than implied. Remaining: the same stamp audited on the other artifacts, phone download reality, empty-set export honesty. || THE STAMP AUDITED ON THE OTHER ARTIFACTS 2026-08-27 - every export surface on the platform, and each one already carries its scope in the form its FORMAT expects. logbook.html builds a meta block and prepends it to the CSV itself (:5985-5997): 'WorkHive logbook export', the worker, Scope - team-history-for-<hive> with the filters joined, or the literal 'no filters applied' so a reader is never left guessing - plus entry count, date range and export timestamp. resume.html's JSON export stamps through the JSON Resume spec's own meta field (cleanResume :1902: version, generator 'WorkHive Resume Builder', lastModified), which is the conformant place for it rather than a bolted-on comment. audit-log's CSV was the flagship and was already done. ★ONE ARTIFACT IS CORRECTLY UNSTAMPED: the cover-letter .txt download (resume.html :1882) is the user's own prose on its way to an employer - a scope line inside it would corrupt the document, not document it. That is a real covered-by-nature, reached by checking what the stamp would DO rather than by assuming. ★AND THE FIRST READING WAS WRONG: grepping for the CSV's 'Scope:' wording scored resume.html at zero and would have filed a missing stamp - the stamp was there in the format's own idiom. A cross-format audit has to ask what each format's provenance slot IS. Remaining: phone download reality, empty-set export honesty. || EMPTY-SET EXPORT HONESTY VERIFIED 2026-08-27. Both DATA exports refuse rather than hand over a file that could be read as loss: logbook.html :5947 and audit-log.html :839 carry the identical guard - if there are no entries, showToast('No entries to export.') and return, no file - so the two surfaces also speak with one voice. Each finishes with a receipt naming the count ('Exported N entries.'). The DEGRADED path is honest too: when the full read fails, logbook falls back to the loaded window and says so in the toast, so a shorter file never passes as a complete one. resume.html is correctly NOT guarded, and that is the interesting half: isEmptyResume() exists, but it requires work AND skills AND education AND projects AND awards AND references to all be empty, so guarding the export on it would refuse a fresh graduate with only their name and contact details a perfectly legitimate file. For a user-authored DOCUMENT, sparse is not the data-integrity ambiguity an empty CSV is. Remaining: phone download reality (needs a device-shaped run). || ★CORRECTION 2026-08-27: the audit above said 'every export surface on the platform' and that was WRONG - it grepped *.html only, so it saw three surfaces and missed the .js one. engineering-design.js carries a BOM CSV (downloadBomCsv :30994) and an SVG diagram export, and the BOM is precisely the case the stamp exists for: it writes _bomItems.filter(it => it.checked !== false) - a SUBSET - as bare header+rows with no provenance at all. A BOM with unchecked lines dropped reaches a supplier looking like the complete bill of materials, and an incomplete one was indistinguishable from a complete one on disk. A denominator that only looks at one file extension is how a surface stays unaudited while the audit reads as exhaustive. FIXED: the CSV now opens with a meta block naming the export, the project, the calculation, the export time, and - the load-bearing line - 'Items: N of M selected', with ' - unselected lines are NOT in this file' appended ONLY when N < M, so a complete export carries no false alarm. Verified by evaluating the builder on sample data (3 of 7 warns, 7 of 7 is quiet, an unnamed project falls back to '(unnamed)'); engineering-design.js parses and _calcType/_bomItems/_lastInputs are all in scope at the call site. The SVG diagram is deliberately left alone - it is a drawing, not a data slice. Remaining: phone download reality, and the PDF exporter's own row-count audit. || THE PDF/PRINT AUDIT DONE 2026-08-27, and it is a DIFFERENT AXIS from the one already locked. export-reads-its-own-set holds the ROW axis: an export must not inherit the render buffer's cap, so no row goes missing. The PDF surfaces fail differently. All three (resume.html, project-report.html, engineering-design.js) render the PDF from the DOM - html2pdf/jsPDF capture #report-panel or the print stylesheet - so the artifact is a picture of the screen, and the risk moves from the row to the CELL. FOUND: project-report.html rendered every daily-progress log through `.slice(0, 200)` with nothing appended. That page exists to be PRINTED and handed to a stakeholder, and on paper there is no hover, no expand, no scroll: a 350-character blocker arrived as a complete-looking 200-character sentence, usually cut mid-word, with no way for the reader to know anything had been removed - and Blockers is precisely the field that carries WHY a project is late. ★THE FIX IS NOT 'STOP TRUNCATING': the printed column is real and text has to fit. The cap stays; what changed is that it now SPEAKS - a conditional marker on the cell plus a one-line note under the table, appearing ONLY when the cap actually bites, so a complete report carries no false alarm. Both are print-safe (a disclosure hidden by @media print discloses nothing to the person holding the printout) and --muted #5B6878 on white paper is legible. VERIFIED LIVE on WO-2026-001: 6/6 rows render (matching the DB), zero marks and no note because no fixture value exceeds 200, while clip() on a synthetic 500-char value keeps exactly 200 and marks it and a 50-char value passes untouched; no page errors. ★TWO INSTRUMENT FAULTS CAUGHT EN ROUTE, both mine: I first probed a project in ANOTHER HIVE and read the empty section as my own regression - it was RLS refusing correctly - and then read a 7-second load as a broken page when it simply had more data than the previous one. Neither was a product defect. Gate printed-truncation-is-disclosed registered, 5/5 synthetic negatives (bare slice, unconditional helper, marker hidden in print, helper with no marker, real surface clean); one of those negatives initially replaced a string absent from the source and so tested the UNCHANGED file - a negative control that negated nothing - and was fixed to strip every marker token including the title attribute. Remaining: phone download reality (T44's installed-mode lane). || PHONE DOWNLOAD REALITY — CAPTURED 2026-08-27 at a 390 viewport, by intercepting the actual download event rather than asserting the button exists. An export control that produces nothing a worker can find is not an export, and the phone is where that fails. RESULT: the download fires, the file is named workhive-logbook-<worker>-<date>.csv - self-identifying on both axes, so it is findable in a downloads folder a week later - and the CSV OPENS WITH ITS OWN BASIS: 'Worker: ...', 'Scope: whole team history for hive Baguio Textile Mills, filtered by from=2026-08-20 + to=2026-08-27', 'Entries: 1', 'Date range: ...', 'Exported: ...'. That scope line is the property this trajectory exists for: the artifact states the FILTER that produced it, so a one-row export cannot be mistaken for the whole history - the compliance-export row-cap incident in reverse, where the file now argues its own limits. Verified end to end with no page errors. The only cosmetic note is a space in the filename ('Leandro Marquez'), which is legal everywhere the platform ships and is recorded rather than 'fixed' into a finding. Remaining: nothing owed beyond the wave-close re-earn - the row axis, the cell axis (printed truncation) and now the phone download are all measured. || ★EVERY CSV EXPORT WAS MOJIBAKING FILIPINO NAMES IN EXCEL - FIXED (2026-08-27). Neither CSV export on the platform emitted a byte-order-mark, so Excel opened them as the system codepage and an asset like 'Pena Line 2' (with the tilde n that this platform's own diacritic-folding code exists to handle) arrived mangled. On a product whose users are Filipino and whose machines and workers carry that character routinely, every exported logbook and audit trail was arriving wrong in the tool people actually open them with. ★AND audit-log LOOKED CORRECT: its blob already declared type 'text/csv;charset=utf-8'. Excel ignores the MIME charset and sniffs the bytes, so the declaration reads exactly like the fix while doing nothing - the most expensive kind of near-miss, because it stops anyone looking further. FIXED both blobs to lead with ﻿, VERIFIED AT RUNTIME by intercepting Blob construction on both pages: startsWithBOM true, type text/csv;charset=utf-8, zero page errors. ★MY OWN DETECTION LIED TWICE FIRST: a scan for 'BOM' reported logbook and engineering-design as compliant, because in THIS codebase 'BOM' means BILL OF MATERIALS ('asset-BOM prioritization', 'specify refrigerant type in the BOM') - domain vocabulary colliding with the thing I was searching for. Then searching the real character found ﻿ in logbook and ph-intelligence, which turned out to be at line 1 before <!DOCTYPE html> - the HTML FILES were saved with a BOM, nowhere near the export path. Two false greens before the true answer: no export had one. ★AND THERE WAS A THIRD CSV EXPORT, found only by auditing EVERY Blob rather than the two I had already fixed: engineering-design.js's BOM/SOW export, same missing byte-order-mark. Now fixed, so all three lead with ﻿ and declare charset=utf-8. Its runtime path needs a completed calculation to produce a blob, so it is source-verified rather than runtime-verified - the identical idiom is runtime-proven on the other two. ★THE OTHER DOWNLOADS WERE CHECKED AND CORRECTLY LEFT ALONE: resume's application/json must NOT carry a BOM (it breaks strict parsers) and the SVG export needs none. The mark belongs to the format Excel sniffs, not to every download - a sweep that added it everywhere would have broken the JSON export to fix the CSVs. ★ONE MORE SELF-INFLICTED DETAIL: my first patch wrote a LITERAL invisible U+FEFF character into the JavaScript source instead of the ﻿ escape. It works identically at runtime and is a maintenance trap - an invisible character someone will eventually delete or a tool will strip, with no visible diff. Replaced with the readable escape the other two already used. || ★LOCKED 2026-08-31: the wave-close re-earn landed and every gate this row names read PASS on a FULL board (export-reads-its-own-set,printed-truncation-is-disclosed). That was the only item its basis still owed. pct 99 -> 100. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_export_truthful.mjs (gate export-truthful): every export control the sweep could reach was PRESSED and the artifact opened and read - it arrives, it has real bytes, its filename says what it holds, and a CSV carries at least as many rows as the screen showed. An export is the one artifact that leaves the platform. One finding came out of it and was fixed: the audit-log export headed itself 'Hive: (unnamed)' when the name was absent from local storage, so an auditor received a file that could not say what it was a record OF.
