trajectories.note: ★THE EXPORT FIX WAS UNGATED (2026-08-26). The team-branch export had already been corrected - it used to hand over the feed's render buffer, producing a compliance file that looked whole - but nothing stopped that returning. Gate export-reads-its-own-set asserts every exporter pages its own set with a TOTAL order and never reuses the buffer, and checks the assertion is non-vacuous against real volume (largest hive 1,700 rows vs a 30-row page). Its own first version made TWO false accusations from a fixed character window that ran past the function into a comment and the handler's announced fallback; bodies are now brace-matched. Teeth proven on buffer reuse and on a paged read missing its tiebreak. ★EMPTY-SET EXPORT HONESTY: CHECKED, AND ALREADY SATISFIED (2026-08-27) - recorded as a bounded NEGATIVE result so the item closes instead of being re-investigated. Enumerated every export surface rather than sampling one: audit-log refuses with 'No entries to export.' and logbook with the same sentence, and logbook additionally warns when a fallback would hand over a SHORTER file ('Could not read the full history, so this exports the N entries currently loaded') - which is the sharper half of the same honesty and was already there. resume's downloads are GENERATED artifacts (cover letter, PDF) rather than row-set exports, so the empty-set question does not apply to them; integrations' !rows.length guard is on the IMPORT side. Nothing to fix here. The remaining T49 items are the basis stamp on the other artifacts and phone download reality, both of which need the artifact in hand rather than a source read. ★THE BASIS STAMP ON THE OTHER ARTIFACTS - CHECKED, AND THEY ALL CARRY IT (2026-08-27). logbook's CSV writes a meta block before the rows: Scope (team vs personal, and 'filtered by X' or the explicit 'no filters applied'), Entries, Date range, Exported timestamp. audit-log's does the same and handles the partial case honestly - when the full read fails it exports what it has and SAYS so - with its reasoning written in the source: 'an auditor holding the CSV has no page around it, so completeness must be legible from the artifact rather than inferred from where it came from.' resume's JSON export deliberately carries NO stamp, and that is correct: it emits standards-conformant JSON Resume, and non-schema meta risks breaking the ATS parsers the whole format exists to satisfy. A basis stamp belongs on an artifact DERIVED over a window, not on a document that is simply itself. ★AND THE PDF KEEPS ITS PROVENANCE - VERIFIED UNDER PRINT MEDIA, AFTER I REASONED MY WAY TO THE WRONG ANSWER. project-report has no class='page', so I inferred from a truncated line that the E3 source chip fell back to document.body and was therefore killed by `body > *:not(#ar-print-wrapper) { display: none }` - which would mean the client-facing PDF dropped the one element saying where its numbers came from. Emulating print showed the opposite: the chip's host resolves to main#wh-main-content INSIDE the wrapper, and under print media it computes display:block with its text intact ('Recomputed when this report is generated · Based on your project...'). The inference was wrong because it rested on a line I had only seen truncated - the partial-read trap aimed at myself. Checking cost one probe; recording it would have cost a false finding in the register.

trajectories.title: Destructive-action sweep: proportional confirm + undo everywhere
trajectories.basis: the DENOMINATOR instrument built: tools/build_destructive_control_registry.py generates substrate/reference/destructive_control_registry.json (20 files, 52 whConfirm/whPrompt call sites with message heads + lines, atomic, --check) - the platform's own are-you-sure vocabulary as an unshrinkable roster. Kick/reject/complete confirms consequence-audited in T25/T20/T10 walks. Remaining: the proportionality + undo + receipt sweep across all 52 entries + Z3 adjacency (wave close). || FIXING->60 (2026-08-26): audited all 52 registry entries for consequence-naming, and most are strong - 'Linked RCM strategies will cascade', 'They lose the verified badge until re-verified', 'kept for history', 'This cannot be undone'. ★ONE WAS NOT, AND IT WAS THE MOST EXPENSIVE: logbook's 'Remove this asset from the registry?' guarded a real asset_nodes delete while naming NO consequence. Read from pg_constraint, not guessed: that row CASCADES seven children (asset_edges, asset_embeddings, pf_intervals, rcm_fmea_modes, sensor_readings, sensor_topic_map, weibull_fits) and detaches five more (logbook, anomaly_signals, drone_inspections, pm_knowledge, child assets) - and a supervisor reaches it on an APPROVED asset, so months of reliability history could go behind a four-word question. Rewritten to name both halves, because 'what survives' is the half that decides whether someone proceeds. ★AND THE GATE THAT EXISTS FOR THIS CLASS WAS VACUOUS: cascade-confirm-parity's consequence pattern accepted `removes?`/`deletes?`, i.e. the ACTION VERB, so 'Remove this asset...' passed on the word 'Remove'. Nearly every destructive confirm is phrased that way, so it had been reporting 0 while asking nothing. Tightened to require a statement BEYOND the ask; proven by resurrection (old pattern 0, new pattern catches it) and it revealed no other site, so the close cost no backlog. Also regenerated the destructive_control_registry, whose line numbers had drifted. REMAINING: the undo/receipt half and Z3 adjacency across the 52 (wave close). || 51 OF 51 DESTRUCTIVE CONTROLS ARE CONFIRM-GATED, AND THE APPARENT SHORTFALL WAS A UNIT MISMATCH (2026-08-27). The registry - the denominator this trajectory exists to make un-shrinkable - holds 51 destructive controls across 20 files, while validate_destructive_safety reports 29 confirm-sites across 14 pages and passes. That gap reads like 22 unguarded controls until you notice the two are counting DIFFERENT THINGS: the gate counts distinct whConfirm CALL SITES, the registry counts CONTROLS, and several controls legitimately route through one shared handler. Walked every registry entry against its own handler body: 51 examined, ZERO without a whConfirm / confirm / whPrompt gate. ★WHICH IS WHY THE REGISTRY MATTERS MORE THAN THE GATE'S OWN NUMBER: a confirm-site count can look like coverage while saying nothing about how many controls exist, and a control that never entered the registry would be invisible to both. The registry is the denominator no one can silently shrink - that was this trajectory's whole design - and it now reconciles against the handlers rather than against another count. Remaining: proportionality (does each confirm NAME what dies and what survives) and the undo story for the reversible ones - both judgement passes over a set that is now provably complete rather than a sample. || ★A DESTRUCTIVE CONFIRM WAS SAYING 'OK' BECAUSE ITS LABEL OPTION WAS SILENTLY DROPPED (2026-08-27, found while measuring dialog contrast). The contrast probe rendered inventory's remove-a-part confirm and its button read 'OK'. Reading the call: whConfirm(..., { title: 'Remove part', confirmLabel: 'Remove', tone: 'danger' }) - and whConfirm reads okLabel and cancelLabel. All THREE keys were ignored, silently: passing an unsupported option throws nothing, it simply does not apply. So the author explicitly tried to name the consequence, this trajectory's whole property, and the platform quietly rendered a generic OK on a cannot-be-undone action. FIXED to okLabel:'Remove', cancelLabel:'Keep' and PROVEN side by side in one run: old options -> ['Cancel','OK'], fixed -> ['Keep','Remove']. 'Keep' is the better decline too - it names what happens if you say no, so both outcomes are stated. ★AND MY AUDIT MISSED IT: a platform-wide sweep of whConfirm option keys reported 33 okLabel / 33 cancelLabel and effectively no misuse - because the pattern excluded braces, and THIS call's message is a template literal full of ${...}. The one call that got the options wrong was the one shape my regex could not see. Remaining: proportionality wording across the other 50 registry entries, and the undo story for reversible cascades. || PROPORTIONALITY AUDITED ACROSS EVERY CONFIRM, WITH A PARSER THAT COULD ACTUALLY SEE THEM (2026-08-27). Re-ran the sweep using balanced-paren extraction instead of a brace-excluding regex - the exact flaw that had hidden inventory's broken call - and the result is trustworthy: 49 whConfirm calls platform-wide, and only TWO lack an okLabel. One is utils.js:3458, which is whConfirm's own DEFINITION (its parameters are literally `message, opts`) - a false positive. The other is design-system.html:154, 'Delete this demo row?', a component-showcase row that no user acts on, and which also passes { danger: true } - another option whConfirm does not read. So 47 of 48 real destructive confirms name their action rather than saying OK, and the one genuine production outlier was inventory's remove-a-part, fixed this pass. ★THE LESSON IS ABOUT THE PARSER, NOT THE PLATFORM: the first audit cleared the codebase and the second found the defect, using the same corpus - the difference was whether the pattern could read a call whose message is a template literal. A sweep that cannot parse the codebase's ordinary idiom does not report zero findings, it reports zero VISIBILITY, and the two look identical. Remaining: the undo story for reversible cascades. || A NEW CHECK FOR THIS REGISTRY'S SWEEP, found in T27 (2026-08-28): ★DOES THE CONFIRM'S NAMED WAY BACK EXIST UNDER THAT NAME? project-manager's completion confirm said 'Subsequent edits will need to reopen it' and the page has no Reopen control at all - the way back is Put on hold, which stays enabled on a completed project and which the sentence never mentions. The remedy was real and unfindable, which is the walkable-remedy class applied to a CONFIRM rather than a refusal. The sweep should therefore check three things per destructive control, not two: the consequence is named, the reversibility is stated, and any control the copy names ACTUALLY EXISTS with that label. The third is the one no oracle here covers today and the one a reader cannot detect - prose naming a plausible-sounding button reads as correct until someone goes looking for it. Second instance from the same walk: the branch fired by the RISKIER path (completing with open scope items) omitted the reversibility sentence that the safe branch carried, so the sweep should compare branches within one control, not just controls against each other. || ★A REFUSED DELETE ANNOUNCED SUCCESS - FOUND, FIXED, RESURRECTION-PROVEN (2026-08-28), and it is the sharpest instance this registry has. logbook's delete button called confirmDelete(), a wrapper around deleteEntry(). deleteEntry is careful: it confirms, deletes with .select('id'), and speaks honestly on BOTH failure paths - a refused write ('The delete did not go through. The entry is still there.') and an RLS-empty result ('you can only delete your own entries.'). The wrapper undid all of it. It asked THE SAME QUESTION AGAIN, then called deleteEntry, then announced 'Entry deleted. Any XP it earned was reversed.' unconditionally - so on a refusal the honest message appeared and was OVERWRITTEN a moment later by a claim that the entry was gone and its XP reversed. MEASURED against the pre-fix file with a bogus id (the RLS-empty path, no data touched): confirms=2, toasts=['Could not delete: you can only delete your own entries.', 'Entry deleted. Any XP it earned was reversed.'] - the truth first, the lie last, and the lie is what a person reads. After: confirms=1, one toast, the honest one. ★AND A THIRD DEFECT IN THE SAME CONTROL: the button ran document.getElementById('modal').classList.add('hidden') SYNCHRONOUSLY right after calling the async confirm, so the entry's modal vanished before the person had answered and CANCELLING still closed it. deleteEntry closes the modal itself, only once the delete has landed. Three defects in one destructive control, and the registry sweep should look for all three shapes: a wrapper that re-asks, a success message that does not check, and a state change that runs before the answer. || CLASS SWEPT immediately after (2026-08-28): searched every page for the same shape - an awaited call followed by a success toast ('deleted/removed/saved/updated/reversed/complete/sent/approved') with no check in between. THREE instances, all in logbook: the delete receipt inside deleteEntry (guarded - the error and empty-result checks return before it), the 'Entry updated.' receipt (guarded - a comment at the site records it was deliberately placed AFTER the 0-row guard, the same lesson learned on asset-manager: never write a receipt for an amendment the database refused), and the offline 'Edit saved offline' receipt (follows an awaited queue write). Only the confirmDelete wrapper was unguarded, and it is fixed. So the shape is common and the platform is mostly disciplined about it - which is exactly why the one exception was worth finding: it sat inside a page whose OTHER two receipts were carefully guarded, so nothing about the file looked careless. || ★THE LAST NATIVE confirm() IS GONE, AND IT WAS GUARDING THE MOST PUBLIC ACTION THE PLATFORM HAS (2026-08-28). 48 call sites already went through whConfirm; one did not, in founder-console, and it gated publishing a piece of feedback to the PUBLIC roadmap. Its REASONING was already excellent and written down - the comment names the irreversibility precisely ('once /feedback/ is indexed by Google the content can be cached even after un-publishing') and the guard is proportional, firing only on the newly-public transition while un-publishing and saving a private item pass through untouched. The message named what could leak: contact emails, worker names, internal notes. Only the MECHANISM was off-standard. ★WHY THAT MATTERED ANYWAY: a native dialog cannot be translated - the same reason dayplanner, platform-actions and resume each recorded when they migrated - and it renders as browser chrome at the exact moment somebody is about to make another person's words permanently public. Now an awaited whConfirm carrying the same content bilingually, with named buttons ('Publish publicly' / 'Cancel') rather than OK/Cancel, so the irreversible choice is the one that says what it does. saveDrawerChanges was already async, so nothing structural changed. ★VERIFIED: the page parses and boots clean, whConfirm sites 48 -> 49, and the only remaining match for a native confirm anywhere in the codebase is the comment I wrote explaining this migration. pct 96 -> 96. || ★AND THE MIGRATION I JUST MADE BROKE A DIFFERENT RULE, CAUGHT THE SAME DAY (2026-08-28). The bilingual confirm I wrote to replace the native dialog contained an EM DASH in both languages ('nothing private — contact emails, worker names, internal notes'). Arc P bans em dashes in DISPLAYED copy and holds a forward-only ratchet at 0; the gate went red naming founder-console with 2 prose instances, and they were both mine, written about an hour earlier. Replaced with colons, which carry the same 'here is the list' beat. Re-run: 0 displayed em dashes, back to baseline, page boots clean. ★THE PATTERN WORTH RECORDING: I improved one property (a translatable, consequence-naming confirm) and silently regressed another (displayed-copy typography) in the same edit, because I was thinking about dialogs rather than about the platform's copy rules. A gate board is what makes that survivable - the second rule was enforced by something that does not get tired at the end of a long session. Fifth self-inflicted regression caught by this platform's own instruments today, and the argument for every one of them. || 2026-09-01 LOCK INSTRUMENT BUILT: tools/validate_destructive_proportional_confirm.py (destructive-proportional-confirm) — wraps build_destructive_control_registry.py --check (roster current = no destructive action escapes a confirm) + HARD: no blank confirm message + forward-only floor on the roster count; REPORTS (never fails) consequence-light confirms (proportionality of prose is the hand-audit, not a lint - avoids the units_at_boundary over-reach). Self-test teeth-proven (blank/shrink redden, light counted-not-failed). REMAINING to lock: regenerate the roster post-board (build_destructive_control_registry.py - my session edits changed confirm sites, --check is STALE now; regen touches substrate so defer past board 3) + register the gate + board green. Then this row locks on its denominator + the already-done proportionality audit. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered the lock gate destructive-proportional-confirm (built earlier this session, self-test PASS + real-file PASS after regen); the destructive-confirm roster (52 controls) is current + forward-only; okLabel/cancelLabel proportionality fix. Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 96. || LOCKED 2026-09-03: post-board promote - every named gate PASS on the 2026-09-02 full board (1028 PASS run). pct -> 100. || AUTO-REVERTED by post_board_promote 2026-09-04: named gate FAILED on this board (stale-health false-100% guard). pct -> 90. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-06 via tools/prove_destructive_sweep.mjs (gate destructive-sweep): every destructive control the sweep could reach across 20 interactive surfaces was PRESSED - 28 of them - with every dialog answered CANCEL and the DB row counts compared before and after; 7/7 reached surfaces guard all of theirs, and no row count moved. SCOPE STATED HONESTLY: 13 surfaces are reported NOT REACHED, not clean - inventory's 'Remove from inventory' and logbook's 'Delete' live inside a role-gated item-detail modal this sweep does not open, and a 0 there would be the loudest kind of false green. Three calibrations, each of which first accused the platform of a defect it does not have: the guard renders as utils.js's OWN overlay (id=wh-modal-ov-*) rather than a [role=dialog], and counting role=dialog also mis-counts the six transform-CLOSED sheets this platform ships; a real mouse click is INTERCEPTED by whatever is already on screen and Playwright's refusal is caught and silent, so eleven guarded Reject controls on founder-console and marketplace-admin read as unguarded until the click was dispatched in page - probing one by hand proved the guard, which opens asking 'Tell the seller why'. · [2026-09-05] CORRECTED 2026-09-06 after the walk destroyed data and its own damage-check could not see it: 7/7 reached surfaces guard every destructive control, 7 controls pressed, no LIVE row count moved. THE PRODUCT WAS RIGHT AND MY INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG THREE TIMES ON ONE CONTROL. community.html's Delete post is proportionate - a SOFT delete with a 10-second undo toast that really restores - but (1) the guard check looked at 1.6s, before the toast rendered, and called it unguarded; (2) the damage check counted count(*), which CANNOT SEE A SOFT DELETE, so it reported 'no row count moved' while ten seeded posts left the feed - found only because a psql invariant (public-feed__only_public_appears) went red afterwards; (3) it pressed every identical Delete button in the feed, and since only one undo toast exists at a time, each extra press destroyed a row it could not put back. Fixed: the census counts LIVE rows on every table that has deleted_at, the sweep presses the undo it finds (which also tests the half of the guard that matters - an undo nobody can reach is not a guard), and it presses ONE control per distinct label, which is full coverage of the handlers. trajectories.title: Multi-hive worker switches hives mid-day
trajectories.basis: walked 390 as pabloaguilar (2 hives): a FRESH device learns both memberships (wh_hives rebuilt from server), 'Switch Hive (2)' visible on hive board, switch flips hive name AND ROLE (Lucena supervisor -> Manila worker - role re-scope correct), the next page (pm-scheduler) answers for the new hive, switch-back restores. The .maybeSingle multi-hive fix + hive-capture invariant holding. Remaining: mid-session switch injection on OPEN pages (stale-figure sweep), per-hive draft/filter scoping, chrome current-hive indicator on every page (wave close). CHROME INDICATOR SWEPT + FIXED 2026-08-26: census found 5 pages rendering hive-scoped data with NO current-hive indicator; 3 owed one and got the pm-scheduler chip pattern (dayplanner top-bar, skillmatrix header, achievements header - self-filling from wh_hive_name, live-proven all 3 render 'Baguio Textile Mills' signed-in at 390). Exclusions by design: marketplace (cross-hive surface), voice-journal (journal_private, personal). Probe lesson: the first null readings were the SIGN-IN WALL (signed-out context), not a missing element - auth state is part of the instrument. Remaining: mid-session switch injection on OPEN pages (stale-figure sweep), per-hive draft/filter scoping audit; chip is load-time - live re-scope on switch rides the injection walk. (2026-08-26: per-hive/per-user draft+filter scoping advanced from the T121 side - both are now owner-stamped, so state no longer crosses between people on one device.) || PER-HIVE DRAFT SCOPING: THE STAMP CARRIES WHO AND WHEN, BUT NOT WHERE (2026-08-27). whAutoSaveDraft stores `{ __owner: _draftOwner(), __savedAt: Date.now() }` and refuses to restore a draft belonging to somebody else (T121's shared-device fix) or to restore one silently once it is stale (T57's age stamp). Both guards are right and neither one covers THIS trajectory's axis: a multi-hive worker is the SAME OWNER in both hives, so the ownership check passes by design and a draft typed against hive A restores into the same form after a switch to hive B. The seeded data already has 2 members in more than one hive, so this is a real population, not a hypothetical. ★WHAT IT COSTS: the machine PICKER would not match after a switch, so the wrong-plant submission is not silent - but the TYPED fields are, and a symptom note describing hive A's bearing failure sitting in a hive B entry is the wrong-plant record this whole trajectory exists to prevent. Not a security hole (both hives belong to that person) but a correctness and confusion one, and precisely the T51 class. ★THE FIX IS THE PATTERN ALREADY THERE, ONE FIELD WIDER: stamp the active hive alongside the owner and refuse the restore on mismatch - the same shape as __owner, so the draft is preserved for the hive it belongs to rather than purged. SEQUENCED AFTER THE BOARD: utils.js is read by a large number of gates and editing it mid-run is exactly what voided this session's earlier board. Remaining: that hive stamp, plus the mid-session switch injection on OPEN pages (stale-figure sweep). ★AND IT IS TWO STORES, NOT ONE - FILTERS CARRY THE SAME GAP AND MAY BITE HARDER. whAutoRememberFilters has its OWN owner stamp (`{ __owner: _fOwner() }`) and its own restore guard (`if (!s || !s.__owner || s.__owner !== _fOwner()) return;`), independent of whAutoSaveDraft's _draftOwner - two separate implementations of the same T121 lesson, and neither knows about the hive. For a multi-hive worker the owner check passes in both, so filters cross the switch exactly as drafts do. ★THE FILTER CASE IS THE NASTIER SYMPTOM: a remembered filter pinned to a hive-A machine or asset, restored after switching to hive B, matches NOTHING - and the page renders an empty list, which this platform has spent a great deal of effort teaching to mean 'there is nothing here' rather than 'your filter is from another plant'. A worker would reasonably conclude the new hive has no records. That is the empty-vs-filtered confusion the E2 family exists to prevent, arriving through the back door of remembered state. So the fix is the same one field wider, applied to BOTH stamps - fix every path that remembers, not just the one I walked. Still sequenced after the board, since utils.js is read by a large number of gates. ★COMPLETENESS PASS BEFORE TOUCHING ANYTHING - EVERY REMEMBERED STORE ENUMERATED, AND THE FIX IS EXACTLY TWO POINTS. whRememberView is the base, so I walked all of its callers rather than fixing the two I happened to find. THREE in utils.js: whAutoRememberFilters (:2400, owner-stamped, needs the hive), whAutoSaveDraft (:2461, owner-stamped, needs the hive), and whAutoRememberTabs (:2419) which carries NO stamp at all - correctly, because it remembers only which tab is active, and the same tabs exist in every hive, so there is nothing to scope. THREE on pages: alert-hub's 'alert-filter' is a .restore() of state the helper stores (covered by the helper fix); marketplace's 'mkt-section' is again a tab selection; and marketplace-seller's 'draft_svcquote_' LOOKED like a page-local draft bypassing the owner stamp - a real leak if true - but reading it shows the call is a .clear() after a successful send, with `function () { return {}; }` as a dummy capture to satisfy the signature. The actual store is whAutoSaveDraft('svcquote_' + request_id, ...) at :1952, so a provider's typed quote goes through the shared owner-stamped path like every other draft. ★SO TWO EDITS IN utils.js COVER EVERY CONTENT-BEARING REMEMBERED STORE PLATFORM-WIDE, and the hive read is whHiveId() (:2591), the canonical accessor with the registered-alias fallback chain - not a fourth hand-rolled localStorage read. Declared but not yet applied, so this line is a plan, not a claim. || FIXED IN BOTH PLACES - AND MY FIRST 'PROOF' WAS AN ARTIFACT I HAD TO THROW OUT (2026-08-27). utils.js: added _stateHive() (reusing whHiveId(), the canonical accessor with the alias chain, returning '' rather than null so a blocked-storage save and restore compare equal) and stamped __hive into BOTH shared stores - whAutoRememberFilters and whAutoSaveDraft - with a matching guard in each restore. Legacy entries carry no __hive and are not restored, the same one-time cost the owner stamp chose. logbook.html: its draft store is PAGE-LOCAL ('wh_logbook_draft_' + WORKER_NAME, raw localStorage, never touching whAutoSaveDraft), so the shared fix could not reach it; keyed by hive AS WELL, which is better than stamp-and-refuse here - each hive keeps its OWN draft, so nothing is discarded and switching back finds the note where it was left. ★TWO MISTAKES OF MINE, BOTH CAUGHT BEFORE THEY SHIPPED AS CLAIMS. (1) My first utils.js edit put a // comment on a line that CONTINUED with live code, and the comment swallowed the rest of the statement including its closing brace - node --check caught it immediately; the repair moved the swallowed ids.forEach onto its own line and made the comment a BLOCK comment. That is the backtick-in-a-comment class exactly. (2) Worse, my live 'proof' was FALSE: I forced wh_active_hive_id to a hive the signed-in worker does not belong to (Leandro Marquez is a member of Baguio ONLY), saw the field come back empty, and read that as the guard working. It was an impossible state - the page could not resolve a foreign hive at all - and logbook's restoreDraft has NO hive check, so the draft would have restored. Verifying the MECHANISM instead of the symptom is what exposed it: the stored key is now 'wh_logbook_draft_<hiveId>_<worker>', which is the property, checked directly. ★AND MY EARLIER 'COMPLETENESS PASS' WAS INCOMPLETE FOR A NAMEABLE REASON: I enumerated callers of the shared helper and called that every store - but the gap lives precisely in the store that OPTED OUT of the helper. Enumerate the behaviour, not the abstraction's users. Remaining: the mid-session switch injection on OPEN pages (stale-figure sweep). || ★THE SWITCH IS CORRECT WHERE IT HAPPENS AND INVISIBLE EVERYWHERE ELSE - the THIRD instance of one pattern found today (2026-08-28). Switching hives updates localStorage (wh_active_hive_id, wh_hive_id, wh_hive_name) AND the in-page globals in the same breath, with a genuinely careful offline branch - when the membership check cannot reach the DB it fails OPEN and trusts the cached role 'so the worker stays in', rather than locking somebody out of their own hive because the network blinked. On the switching page, nothing is stale. ★BUT 15 FILES CACHE wh_active_hive_id AND ONLY 3 LISTEN FOR `storage` (companion-launcher, session-timeout, and nav-hub - the last of which only started listening today, for the community badge). There is no reload on switch, so a contractor with the logbook open in one tab and the hive board in another switches to hive B and the logbook keeps showing hive A's entries, silently, under a chrome that may or may not have updated. For a MULTI-HIVE worker - the entire persona of this trajectory - that is not a stale badge, it is looking at the wrong plant's data believing it is the right one. ★AND IT IS A CLASS, NOT AN INCIDENT: today produced three instances of the same shape - the community badge (T144), the hive NAME after a rename (T140), and now the ACTIVE HIVE. All three are identity written to localStorage by one tab and read at boot by others; localStorage already broadcasts every one of those writes to every other tab, and almost nothing listens. One shared listener in the chrome that every page loads would close all three at once, which is the argument for treating this as a platform fix rather than three page fixes. pct 78 -> 88. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate hive-seating-is-by-identity re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100. || REVERTED 2026-09-04: named gate FAILED on the 1034/60 board (false 100%; post_board_promote over-locked). pct -> 90. || pct -> 100 (board-locked 2026-09-05).

fixes: index.html (resolveActiveHiveContext seats by auth_uid, not by display name)

trajectories.note: ★THE TENANT SEAT WAS CHOSEN BY NAME (2026-08-26). resolveActiveHiveContext() picked which hive a session lands in via .eq('worker_name', displayName) against v_worker_truth, whose worker_name IS worker_profiles.display_name - so it leaned on profiles_read_own (auth_uid = auth.uid()) to mean 'mine'. No live defect (measured: 1 visible profile row; both filters return the same 2 memberships for a real multi-hive account), but the safety was the POLICY's, not the query's, and any widening of profile reads would have seated a person in a namesake's hive. Now keyed on auth_uid, passed explicitly from both call sites, with solo mode as the answer when identity is unknown. Gate hive-seating-is-by-identity asserts the page half AND that the RLS policy is still self-scoped. Third face of the same day's defect family with T185's namesake join and T1's records-linked notice: a name is not an identity. ★THE XP LEDGER IS KEYED BY NAME, AND A NAME IS NOT A PERSON (2026-08-26) - the fourth face of the same defect family found this session. achievement_xp_log has no auth_uid and no hive_id, and its RLS reads by worker_name; worker_name is unique per HIVE, so two different people in two hives sharing a name would merge totals, compute each other's LEVELS, and be able to read each other's ledger rows (source_action, source_id) from a hive they never joined. Measured: 982 rows / 20 names / ZERO names held by two people - not happening, which is exactly why it was worth gating now: the backfill onto auth_uid is only unambiguous while that stays true. Gate xp-belongs-to-one-person fails the moment a cross-hive namesake appears and retires itself once auth_uid exists. THE FIX IS IAN'S CALL, scoped not smuggled: add auth_uid, backfill, and move the four readers (achievements x2, logbook, pm-scheduler) plus the RLS predicate onto it - a schema change to a ledger with reversal semantics.

First-class engineer ROLE (authz, landing emphasis) = a schema+RLS product decision FLAGGED for Ian, not built. ★BASIS CORRECTED 2026-08-27: this line used to read 'Eng.Design (engineer-only)'. trajectories.note: ★PREMISE CORRECTED, THEN THE REAL DEFECTS FOUND. The spec calls the engineer 'the third persona'; there is no third role (hive_members.role is CHECK-constrained to worker | supervisor), so the probes as written - 'what does an engineer SEE that others do not', 'are they denied surfaces by role' - had no subject. The trajectory's real question is whether the two ENGINEER LENSES cohere, and they did not: the hub lens and the asset-hub toggle shared a word and no state, and the toggle did not even reflect its own stored value until an asset was opened. Both fixed and gated. REMAINS: whether the nav-hub 'engineer' tool filter actually selects the right tools for that work, which is a content question about the TOOLS registry rather than a state question. ★THE OPEN CONTENT QUESTION, ANSWERED AND GATED (2026-08-27). The note above left one thing open: 'whether the nav-hub engineer tool filter actually selects the right tools - a content question about the TOOLS registry rather than a state question.' Measured: 24 tools, 13 visible in the Engineer lens, and every member of the design-and-reliability lane present. ★THE FINDING IS THE SHAPE OF THE LENS, not a missing tool: EVERY engineer-tagged tool is also supervisor-tagged, so the Engineer lens is a strict SUBSET of the supervisor lens - a FOCUS filter that removes field tools, never a distinct capability set. That is coherent with the corrected premise (a lens, not a role) and is exactly why it needs holding: a future tool tagged roles:['engineer'] alone would sit in NO role's default spine, since no engineer ROLE exists to grant it - reachable only by someone who had already switched the lens by hand, and invisible to the supervisors who ARE the engineers here. That is the retired-page class (a live control behind a door most people never open), and nothing was holding it. New gate engineer-lens-covers-its-lane asserts both halves: no engineer-only orphan, and every lane member engineer-visible. 5 selftest cases, the two RED ones being an engineer-only tool and a lane member leaving the lens. ★AND WHAT I DID NOT DO: 'Reports' is engineer-visible while the lane does not name it, and I left it. The registry records that tagging with a reason, and a validator overturning a judgement call on my preference would be bending the code to the gate. The lane is gated as a FLOOR, not a ceiling. Sibling gate engineer-lens-is-one-lens is untouched - it holds STATE coherence between the two switches; this one holds lens CONTENT, so no redundancy. REMAINS for the wave close: the engineer-lens journeys on the core pages. ★THE LANE JOURNEY IS LIVE, AND THE LENS MECHANISM WAS MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS ASSERTED (2026-08-27). A probe first, because a journey written against guessed selectors measures its own assumptions: the hub renders its tiles EAGERLY (no FAB press needed - my first draft would have clicked a button it did not need), and the four modes give 11 / 13 / 20 / 20 tiles for engineer / field / supervisor / all. ENG1 then walks the lane signed in as the supervisor who IS the engineer here: lens declared ONCE on index, then engineering-design -> analytics -> asset-hub -> project-manager, asserting on EVERY page that the mode is still engineer, the lane tool is present and all three field-only tools are absent. R/J/T/X all green, LIVE. ★THE X ASSERTION IS THE POINT: logbook is hidden from this lens and must still open by direct URL, because a lens is not authorization - no role denies it. A display filter that quietly became a permission would be the retired-page class, a live control unreachable because a preference hid its only door. The journey restores the default mode at the end so later journeys are not walked through an engineer lens. ★A NEW FINDING, FLAGGED NOT FIXED: the Supervisor lens and the All lens render IDENTICAL tile sets - 20 each, set difference empty both ways, measured. So two of the four mode chips are indistinguishable for a supervisor: pressing Supervisor after All changes nothing, which is the click-that-changes-nothing class. The cause is taxonomy drift - every non-hidden tool is either universal or supervisor-tagged, so supervisor-narrowing is vacuous. MY VERDICT, for Ian to take or leave: either retire the Supervisor chip (All already IS it) or un-tag the field-only tools from supervisor so the chip means something. I did not pick one, because which tools are 'not a supervisor's' is a product judgement, and it cannot be gated green today in either direction - the invariant would fail on the current registry. Recorded as a measured finding, not a silent fix. ★AND ONE INSTRUMENT SELF-CATCH: the gate I wrote an hour earlier said 'every lane member is engineer-VISIBLE' while computing role TAGGING. They differ - isVisibleInMode drops every hidden:true tool from EVERY mode, and two of this lane's six are hidden Phase-B pages reached from a parent button - so the label claimed something the code never measured. Caught by reading isVisibleInMode while writing the journey, before it could go false-green; wording, docstring, board label and two new selftest cases all now say TAGGED. The oracle-does-not-match-the-claim class, in my own fresh work.

And asset-hub was not thin at all: a slightly longer wait shows 'Asset fleet mostly healthy, a couple of things to do - 4 pending - TOTAL ASSETS 25', which is precisely the verdict-at-a-glance this persona wants; my 562-char reading had caught it mid-render, so the low count was my timing, not the page's content. It also requires the reader got WORDS - visible text, not figures, since this trajectory's own walk twice misread a healthy surface as thin (once mid-render, once by counting figures on analytics-report, whose correct state is an instruction with none). 6/6 green at 1280; teeth 5/5, each clause injected on a real page and each checked NON-VACUOUS against a clean baseline, because a gate over already-correct behaviour has never been seen to go red. trajectories.note: ★PREMISE CORRECTED, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE FINDING. The spec assumes a read-mostly executive persona. The probe 'is there anything they can DESTROY by accident' has an answer, and it is: everything a supervisor can. The confirms added under T50/T67 reduce the blast radius but do not change who holds the trigger. It is a schema change (the CHECK constraint, the RLS predicates that branch on role, and every UI that tests for 'supervisor'), so it is a real piece of work rather than a toggle - and until then, the honest statement is that WorkHive has no way to let someone watch without also letting them act.

trajectories.title: New graduate onboarding (the learning lane)
trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25, worker 390, three-surface ladder walk): the grad growth ladder (quiz -> badge -> resume) EXISTS end-to-end - skillmatrix offers '5 quizzes available right now' with an Achievements link, achievements' locked badges show their HOW, and the Resume Builder's 'Auto-fill from my WorkHive data' consumes skills+badges+history - but the ladder was only discoverable TOP-DOWN from the resume; no lower rung pointed up. FIXED + VERIFIED: (1) skillmatrix now states the path under its verdict ('pass a quiz -> earn the skill badge -> it lands on your Resume automatically', linked); (2) achievements now carries the resume line ('Every badge you earn here lands on your Resume automatically - employers see certified skills, not claims'). Both proven rendering live. Remaining: a grad-facing 'start here' entry (learn-cluster <-> skillmatrix wayfinding - content decision), the learn->signup->skillmatrix continuity walk as a fresh grad account, mentorship/community entry points (wave close). || ★ONE DOOR, THEN FIFTY-TWO UNSORTED ROOMS (2026-08-28). This trajectory asks whether a fresh graduate finds a coherent 'start here'. Measured: the learn hub carries exactly one sequencing affordance - 'Start here if you are new', pointing at the overview of what the platform does and how one logbook entry makes the hive smarter. That is a real and well-written first step. ★BEYOND IT THERE IS NO PATH: 53 guides, and ZERO of them carry any difficulty or level marker - no data-level, no data-difficulty, no educationalLevel, no proficiencyLevel, nothing. No prerequisite chain, no beginner/intermediate/advanced grouping on the hub. A grad who takes the one recommended step is then facing 52 titles with no signal about which is next, which assumes knowledge they came here to acquire. The ladder this trajectory describes - lesson to exam to badge to resume - exists as MACHINERY (skillmatrix exams, achievements, the resume builder all work) but is not presented anywhere as a sequence a person can see and follow. ★THIS CONVERGES WITH T152's already-open item, reading-order guidance for the learn cluster, which is on Ian's list. Recording the measurement so that decision has a number under it: the cost of adding order is 53 guides' worth of metadata, and the cost of not adding it is that the platform's stated audience gets one step and a wall. pct 60 -> 70. || ★THE LADDER IS WIRED END TO END; IT IS JUST NEVER SHOWN AS A LADDER (2026-08-28). Measured the graduate's path rung by rung and every joint holds: 37 of the learn articles link into skillmatrix, skillmatrix links onward to resume, and resume genuinely CONSUMES what was earned - 14 references to worker skills, badges and certifications, so a badge won in the matrix actually becomes a line on the CV rather than a number in a game. That last link is the one that makes the promise real for this persona: the platform's pitch to a fresh graduate is employability, and employability means the credential leaves the platform with them. It does. ★WHAT IS MISSING IS THE PRESENTATION, not the plumbing. Nothing shows the sequence AS a progression. The only onboarding stepper on the platform (onboarding.js, hive.html) is role-specific and OPERATIONAL - signed in, joined a hive, logged an entry, uploaded a photo, completed a PM - which is the right ladder for a worker starting a job and the wrong one for a graduate building a career. A grad arriving with 'what do I do first, and where does it lead' meets 37 separate doors into skillmatrix and no map saying learn -> certify -> resume -> hired. The rungs exist; the ladder is not drawn. ★That framing matters for whoever builds it: this is not a wiring job, it is a single wayfinding surface over connections that already work - the cheapest kind of improvement to make and the easiest to mistake for a big one. pct 70 -> 82. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - the new-graduate learning lane is coherent: learn-graph (articles reachable) + skill-library-wiring (the quiz->badge->resume skillmatrix path is wired) + scroll-gate-at-open. Gates [learn-graph, skill-library-wiring, scroll-gate-at-open] registered + PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] pct -> 100. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_persona_arcs.mjs (gate persona-arcs), 8/8 lenses clean. Speech capture ships with a typed path to the SAME record and six distinct failure causes named in words, so a refused microphone does not end the journey for a worker whose hands are full - 478 entries recorded (T12). All 12 achievements carry a description and 79 have been awarded, with the reason rendered beside the badge on two surfaces, so an engineer earning something can find out what for (T17). Twenty-eight pages remember where a person was and six can say what changed while they were away, covering both the day-two return and the three-month one (T46, T57). Forty pages stamp a figure with its source, 44 canonical truth views stand behind them, and 27 let a person open the rows, so a skeptic can take a headline number apart rather than trust it (T47). Fifty-six learn articles are linked from inside the product and 30 pages explain themselves in place, so a graduate is not sent to search the web for how to use the tool (T54). Lucena Pharmaceutical runs two supervisors, and hive.html checks for a co-supervisor before forcing a hand-over - so leaving is safe when another remains, and the last one is not waved through (T56). Fourteen pages surface device or session state, an idle timeout ships, and there is a way out, so someone who cares about their account has controls beyond closing the tab (T59). THE SCALE ROW IS STATED HONESTLY RATHER THAN CLAIMED: the largest hive in this data holds 8 active members, so twenty is beyond what it can prove; what is asserted instead is that all three roster surfaces BOUND what they render rather than drawing every member at once, which is the property that decides whether twenty people works (T61). TWO LENSES PASSED TOO EASILY ON THE FIRST RUN AND WERE TIGHTENED, both recorded in the prover: 'the reason beside the badge' matched the word description in every page's meta tag and counted 33 surfaces where the honest answer is 2; and 'surfaces session state' counted every page that merely LOADS device-fingerprint.js, when a script tag is not a control a person can act on.

trajectories.title: Supplier/contractor persona enters via marketplace
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, davidvelasco 390, worker-seller lane): marketplace-seller dashboard graded GOOD - tier chip (Bronze) + ID Verified up top, stats first (3 Listings / 0 Sales / 0 New Inquiries), and the credit-hold economy explained inline in plain language ('10% of its price is HELD... comes back in full if it does not sell, goes to your buyer if it does; taking a listing down releases its hold immediately') - the T34 cost-transparency bar carried to the dashboard. Nav hub shows the full worker toolset, CORRECT for david (he IS a hive worker who also sells). OPEN for the true story: the PURE seller (no hive) - needs a signup-without-hive fixture to grade nav drowning (no 'Seller' lane exists in the hub's role filters), seller-only first-run, and the notification lane (inquiries reaching a hive-less account). Remaining: pure-seller fixture walk, earnings/fee-basis section at n>0 sales (aged-seller fixture), vendor community participation scope (wave close). || THE HIVE-LESS SELLER STATE IS REACHABLE - AND MY FIRST READING SAID THE OPPOSITE, TWICE OVER (2026-08-27). Question: can an account with marketplace access and no hive exist, or does the plant model swallow the supplier persona? Probe: sign in, delete wh_active_hive_id + wh_hive_name, reload marketplace. FIRST reading said the user was bounced to index.html showing 'Free Industrial Tools for Every Filipino Worker' - the signed-OUT marketing pitch served to a signed-in person, with no explanation. Both halves of that were my instrument. (1) I captured location.pathname and DISCARDED location.search, which is exactly where the explanation lives: the platform's one bounce helper is whSignInWall(), which sends index.html?signin=1&return=marketplace.html, so I deleted the query string and then reported that no explanation was given. (2) Worse, the bounce itself was a SINGLE SAMPLE. Re-run three times with the URL captured whole: marketplace.html every time, 18 listings rendered, no wall, no redirect. The first run had raced its own teardown - I removed the identity keys mid-initialisation and read the result as product behaviour. ★SO THE FINDING INVERTS: browsing the marketplace does NOT require a hive, and the pure-seller state is reachable today. One reading is an anecdote; the defect I nearly filed was the probe. WHAT REMAINS REAL: nav-hub carries a single universal 'Marketplace' entry under Connect and no seller lane, so a supplier who never joins a plant still gets the full field-tools nav (logbook, PM scheduler, inventory) they can never use - the nav-scope question stands, unaffected by the false bounce. Remaining: the seller-lane nav scope, the pure-seller fixture walk, earnings/fee-basis at n>0 sales (aged-seller fixture), and vendor community participation. || THE SUPPLIER PERSONA IS POSSIBLE IN THE DATA AND UNPAVED IN THE PRODUCT - MEASURED ON ALL FOUR LAYERS (2026-08-27). POPULATION: 17 auth users, 15 with a hive membership, and the 2 without are both PROBE accounts left by earlier walks (wh-t175-probe@, consumer.walk@) - so there is not one genuine pure-supplier account to walk, which is itself the answer to 'what does a seller-only account see'. SCHEMA: it would allow one. marketplace_listings.hive_id is NULLABLE, marketplace_sellers.hive_id is nullable, and ZERO RLS policies on marketplace_listings reference hive_members - listing visibility is not gated on belonging to a plant at all. All 27 listings carry a hive only because every seller happens to be a hive member. NAV: measured live as a real seller (Bryan Garcia) at 390 - the hub offers 17 items, of which Logbook, Inventory, PM Scheduler, Day Planner, Shift Brain and Hive Board are plant operations a supplier can never use; Marketplace is one entry among them, and no role-filter chips rendered. ONBOARDING: signup routes everyone through hive.html to create or join a hive, so a parts supplier must attach themselves to a plant to sell to plants. ★SO THE HONEST ANSWER IS NOT 'BROKEN' OR 'FINE' BUT 'UNPAVED': the data model would hold a hive-less supplier today without a migration, and nothing in the product offers, scopes or names that path. Whether the supplier is a first-class persona or deliberately out of scope for launch is a product call - and it is worth stating rather than leaving implied, because the marketplace's supply side depends on the answer. Remaining: that scoping call, then (if in scope) the seller-lane nav and a hive-less fixture; earnings/fee-basis at n>0 sales still needs an aged-seller fixture. || ★THE SELLER'S OWN DASHBOARD WAS NOT IN THE SPINE AT ALL — AND NOT FINDABLE BY SEARCH EITHER (2026-08-28). Walking the nav as this persona: nav-hub's TOOLS registry carried 24 entries and marketplace-seller.html was NOT one of them. Not `hidden: true` — ABSENT. That distinction is what made it worse than the T173 cases: `hidden` entries are still published on window.WHNavTools and merely filtered from the grid, whereas an absent page is unknown to the registry entirely. And because search-overlay.js:327 reads that same registry (`.filter(t => !t.hidden && ...)`), the page was unreachable from the global search too — no query for 'seller', 'listings' or 'my listings' returned anything, anywhere on the platform. The ONLY route was remembering to open Marketplace and spotting a 'My Listings' pill in its header at marketplace.html:762. For the supplier persona this trajectory is about, that page IS their platform, which is precisely the 'a daily tool is not an internal page' class T173 unhid Voice Journal and Shift Brain for. FIX: registered as 'My Listings' in the Connect section, universal like Marketplace itself because anyone may sell (T104's premise), reusing the pill's own label and ic-list icon so the two affordances read as one destination. ★TWO ORDERING TRAPS, BOTH AVOIDED BY READING getCurrentTool() RATHER THAN ASSUMING: it returns the FIRST match by `path.includes(m)`, so the entry MUST precede Marketplace or 'marketplace' would claim the page first — the same rule the registry already documents for Analytics Report before Analytics. And the match term carries '.html' deliberately, because bare 'marketplace-seller' is also a substring of marketplace-seller-profile.html — the PUBLIC profile a BUYER reads, a different page with a different job — which would have been mis-claimed. Verified by simulating the resolver over all four marketplace paths: seller->My Listings, and marketplace / seller-profile / admin all still resolve to Marketplace unchanged. nav-registry (no duplicate hrefs, match[] unique) and page-roster (nav_hub 24->25) both green. ★NOTED, NOT BUILT: `match` serves double duty — path detection AND search keywords — so 'sales' and 'earnings' still find nothing, and adding them would pollute path matching. A separate `keywords` field would separate the two concerns honestly; recorded here rather than built, since it touches search-overlay too. pct 25 -> 55. STILL OPEN and the larger half of this trajectory: there is no 'seller' MODE in the vocabulary (field | supervisor | engineer), so a pure supplier still sees Logbook, Inventory, PM Scheduler and the rest of the plant they cannot use — the 'drowning in plant tools' question is surfaced and unanswered. Seller onboarding, their notification lane, and vendor community scope are un-probed. || ★AND IT WAS PROVEN LIVE, because the fix was made statically and static cannot tell you a person can get there (2026-08-28). New prover, registered: it signs in, opens the real hub, and reads the LINKS a person could click — the seller dashboard now has a visible entry labelled 'My Listings' — then drives the global search with Ctrl+K (the documented shortcut, so the probe takes the path a person takes) and confirms 'seller' reaches marketplace-seller.html and 'audit log' reaches the audit trail. All five checks green. ★TEETH: with the registry entry removed AND the `!t.hidden` search filter restored, three of the five go red — '17 links, none to marketplace-seller.html' and 'no results' twice — so the prover fails for the right reason and reports the count that explains it. Asserting reachability rather than markup matters here: a check that the registry array contains a string would re-test what the static fix already guaranteed, and would pass just as happily if the grid never rendered. || ★AND THE FULL BOARD CAUGHT WHAT THE TARGETED GATES DID NOT: registering this entry as VISIBLE broke a budget I had not thought to check. validate_home_stack_coverage caps how many primary-nav tools each role sees, and both affected roles were deliberately AT their cap - so one universal entry pushed field to 14/13 and supervisor to 21/20 simultaneously. nav-registry and page-roster both stayed green throughout, because they check different properties; only the 53-minute full board found it. A change can satisfy every gate you thought to run and still break one you did not. ★THE FIX IS `hidden: true`, AND IT IS ONLY THE RIGHT ANSWER BECAUSE OF THE OTHER CHANGE THIS SESSION MADE. `hidden` used to mean UNFINDABLE - grid AND search - which is precisely the orphaning this trajectory set out to end, and would have been a retreat. Since T78 made search index hidden entries, `hidden` now means exactly what it should: not promoted, still reachable by name. The page costs nobody a nav slot, answers to 'seller' / 'listings' / 'my listings', keeps its current-page resolution, and marketplace's own pill remains the parent deep-link the home-stack gate asks for. The two fixes only work as a pair. ★AND THE LIVE PROVER WAS CORRECTED WITH IT: it asserted the entry is VISIBLE in the grid, which after this became an assertion that the cognitive-load cap is broken. It now asserts the opposite - that the dashboard takes no primary-nav slot - plus the two search reachability checks, and its PASS line no longer claims 'the grid shows it', because it deliberately does not. || ★REACHABLE, PROVEN LIVE - BUT THE SELLER HAS NO NAVIGATION IDENTITY (2026-08-28). The reachability half is settled with a live browser walk: prove_seller_dashboard_is_reachable passes all four assertions - the hub panel opens, the seller dashboard is deliberately NOT consuming a primary-nav slot (hidden by design, protecting the home-stack budget), searching 'seller' reaches it, and searching 'audit log' reaches that hidden page too, confirming the search lane genuinely serves the hidden set rather than the dashboard being a special case. Curated out of the nav and findable by name is the right answer for a page most users never need. ★THE PERSONA GAP IS THE REAL FINDING. nav-hub's role vocabulary is field, supervisor and engineer - every single role-tagged TOOLS entry draws from those three, and NOT ONE carries a seller or vendor role. So a supplier or contractor who joins WorkHive purely to sell - this trajectory's entire persona, whose world is the marketplace plus community - is bucketed into a plant-worker lane and shown a hub full of tools they will never open: logbook, PM scheduler, asset hub, shift brain. They do not drown because the nav is broken; they drown because the nav has no concept of them. ★THAT IS A PRODUCT DECISION, not a defect to patch: adding a fourth mode changes the mode switcher for everyone and only makes sense if WorkHive intends seller-only accounts as a first-class persona rather than as plant workers who happen to sell. The cheap intermediate - defaulting a seller-only account to a marketplace-first view without minting a whole mode - is available and is what the evidence here would support. Recorded for Ian with the measurement behind it: 19 role-tagged nav entries, zero of them reachable by a seller's identity. pct 68 -> 80. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: The account-security-conscious user
trajectories.basis: findability audit: password change exists ONLY via the recovery-link loop (forgot -> email -> PASSWORD_RECOVERY -> whPrompt with 8-char floor) + supervisor-reset for workers; there is NO in-app change-password for a signed-in user, no active-sessions view, no sign-out-everywhere, no 2FA statement. Per spec this is the SCOPED PRODUCT DECISION for Ian: an account-security surface (change password + sessions + revoke + honest 2FA absence note). Reset-loop injection tests remain (wave close). || ★THE ACCOUNT-SECURITY BASICS ARE LARGELY ABSENT, AND ONE OF THEM IS A ONE-ARGUMENT FIX (2026-08-28). Walked what a security-conscious user could actually do. THERE IS NO ACCOUNT OR SETTINGS SURFACE AT ALL - marketplace-seller-profile is a seller's public page, not account controls. Consequences, each checked rather than assumed: (1) PASSWORD CHANGE: the only updateUser({password}) on the platform sits inside index.html's RECOVERY flow, behind a reset link. So a signed-in worker who wants to change their password must SIGN OUT and email themselves a reset - the one action security advice tells people to do routinely is the one the product makes hardest. (2) SIGN-OUT-EVERYWHERE: every signOut() call on the platform - hive.html, four in index.html - is the bare form. Supabase revokes ALL sessions only with signOut({ scope: 'global' }); bare signOut() ends the local one, so a worker who loses a phone cannot sign it out, and on the SHARED plant device this platform explicitly serves (T121's persona) a previous user's session survives elsewhere. That is a one-argument change, though which calls should be global is a real decision - signing every device out on an ordinary sign-out would be its own hostility. (3) No active-session visibility, so nobody can see what to revoke. (4) No 2FA, and no statement that there isn't one - the honest-absence half this trajectory asks about is also missing. ★RECORDED, NOT BUILT: an account surface is a product decision about scope and placement, not an edit, and the scope='global' question needs Ian's call on which paths deserve it. pct 60 -> 72. || ★PASSWORD CHANGE IS BUILT AND GATED, AND ITS COPY UNDERSTANDS THIS PLATFORM'S WORKERS (2026-08-28). validate_password_change_reachable passes live: a signed-in worker finds Change Password beside Sign Out, it meets the 44px touch floor, and the prompt says what will happen. The sentence that makes it right for a plant is the second one - 'Enter the email on your account for a reset link. No email on file (most field workers)? Ask your hive supervisor to reset your password for you.' Most WorkHive accounts are username-only by design, so an email-reset flow alone would strand the majority of the workforce; naming the supervisor path turns a dead end into a procedure, and it matches the supervisor-reset-password function that actually exists. ★THE GAP IS REVOCATION, and for a plant it is the consequential one. All seven signOut() call sites use Supabase's DEFAULT scope, which is local - the current device only. There is no sign-out-everywhere and no active-session list, so a worker whose phone is lost, stolen or left in a jeepney cannot end that device's session from another one, and a supervisor cannot end it for them. On shared plant hardware (T121's serial-user reality) that is the difference between an account and an open door. ★2FA is scaffolded but not real: mfa_enrollments exists with auth_uid/worker_name/last_verified_at/notes and ZERO rows, and it holds no factor secrets (those would live in Supabase's own auth schema), so it reads as an audit table awaiting an enrollment flow that was never built. Honest position: absent, not broken. ★THE DECISION Ian owes: whether signOut should ever pass scope 'global'. The ONE surviving guest-era surface is the C2 'Secure account' upgrade banner (index:2669) + upgradeToAccount(): it fires ONLY for name-with-no-session (a legacy pre-auth-migration guest, or lost auth storage - the idle hard-clear also removes wh_last_worker so expiry cannot trigger it), opens the auth modal on the SIGNUP tab with display_name locked to keep records linked, and the T1 reciprocity link ('Already have an account? Sign in') gives the wrong-door user an exit - judged COHERENT for its audience, no fix needed. Remaining: the dead-feature-remnant detector (orphaned panels/functions with no entry path - generalizes feedback_declared_but_never_wired) as a wave-close instrument; a legacy-guest-population count on prod would confirm the banner's real audience size (Ian-gated, prod read). (2026-08-26: one dead-remnant found and removed by a different lens - logbook's caller-less saveAssets() with an unconfirmed cascading delete, caught by T139's FK-parity oracle. Evidence that the remnant detector this trajectory wants has real prey.) || 2026-08-26, the remnant DETECTOR attempted and its failure is the finding. Built the orphaned-function census this trajectory asks for (declared, never referenced, and still holding a write). It reported exactly one prey: logbook's saveEditAsset(), a 5KB function with a real asset UPDATE. ★IT WAS A FALSE POSITIVE, AND ACTING ON IT WOULD HAVE DELETED A LIVE, RECENTLY-HARDENED SAVE HANDLER - the function is wired by onclick at logbook.html:1390 and its modal is opened from the asset list. The census could not see the call site because its comment-stripping had blanked it: `accept="image/*"` at line 679 contains a literal /* , which the strip read as a comment OPENER and ran 58,551 characters to the next real */, erasing the whole modal region including that onclick. Proven exactly - the same reference count reads 1 with the naive strip and 2 with a `/\*(?!["'])` lookahead, while genuine inline /* xss-allow */ comments still strip correctly. A detector whose false positive means DELETE LIVE CODE must take its reference count from the RAW source, where a mention inside a comment makes code look USED - the safe direction to be wrong in. NO GATE SHIPPED: the detector is not trustworthy enough to point at deletions, and the honest outcome of this attempt is the root cause plus the five gates it silently corrupted, now all fixed. T60 stays WALKED. || SYSTEMIC SWEEP (same day): the flaw was not mine alone. trajectories.title: The hive at 20 members (social scale)
trajectories.basis: THE STANDING FIXTURE BUILT: tools/grow_hive_fixture.py grows one hive's roster to N with realistic named members (layout truth needs real name lengths), manifest-tracked + --revert removes exactly what was added (proven: 3->20->3). At 20 on 390: hive roster renders all 20, count chip '- 20', no h-overflow; community presence stays honest (live viewers only) + no h-scroll. DEEP PASS RUN at 20: the team-search worker picker holds all 21 options alphabetized (usable; the datalist-combobox threshold - pm-scheduler's own cat-filter lesson - applies at ~50, noted); achievements standings render clean, no h-scroll; community presence honest. Reverted to canonical 3. Remaining: notification fan-out at 20 + per-member drilldown latency (fixture on demand). FAN-OUT AT 20 MEASURED 2026-08-26: the notification lane does NOT multiply rows with audience size - fanout_broadcast_push collects the recipient ids into an ARRAY and enqueues ONE outbox row, and enqueue_user_push takes uuid[] the same way. Proven in a rolled-back txn: 20 recipients -> outbox rows 214 -> 215, delta 1, with all 20 uids in a single payload. So a 20-member hive costs one queued job per event, not twenty - the storm risk lives at DELIVERY (one push per person, correct by definition) and is now bounded on the other side by T110's identical-push dedupe window. Remaining: per-member drilldown latency on the grown fixture. || PER-MEMBER DRILLDOWN LATENCY MEASURED 2026-08-27, the last item this trajectory named. Grew Baguio 3->20 with grow_hive_fixture.py, walked hive.html as the signed-in supervisor, reverted to the canonical 3 (17 removed, re-counted). FIRST, THE SHAPE: there is no per-member modal - the roster ROW is the detail (avatar, tier badge, role tag, workload word), so the latency that matters is assembling all twenty of them. MEASURED: 20/20 rows built in 719ms, 21 REST calls for the whole page, and the busiest single endpoint hit 3 times - not 20. The per-member data is genuinely batched: loadWorkerTiers (utils.js:4060) takes the whole name list through one `.in('worker_name', names)` against v_worker_achievements_truth, and open-job counts are folded from one already-fetched set rather than queried per worker. So the N+1 this probe existed to find is not there. ★AND THE INSTRUMENT LIED FIRST: the initial probe read 0 members and would have been recorded as a scale failure - the roster is COLLAPSED by default, so a visibility-blind selector saw nothing while the DOM already held all 20 and the count chip already read ' - 20'. Diagnosed before banking, which is the only reason this says 719ms instead of 'the roster does not render at 20'. STATUS fixing->locking: every item the basis named is now walked; what remains for locked is the resurrection at close, same as its wave siblings. || ★LOCKED 2026-08-31: the wave-close re-earn landed and every gate this row names read PASS on a FULL board (hive-at-scale). That was the only item its basis still owed. pct 95 -> 100. · [2026-09-05] pct -> 100. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_persona_arcs.mjs (gate persona-arcs), 8/8 lenses clean. Speech capture ships with a typed path to the SAME record and six distinct failure causes named in words, so a refused microphone does not end the journey for a worker whose hands are full - 478 entries recorded (T12). All 12 achievements carry a description and 79 have been awarded, with the reason rendered beside the badge on two surfaces, so an engineer earning something can find out what for (T17). Twenty-eight pages remember where a person was and six can say what changed while they were away, covering both the day-two return and the three-month one (T46, T57). Forty pages stamp a figure with its source, 44 canonical truth views stand behind them, and 27 let a person open the rows, so a skeptic can take a headline number apart rather than trust it (T47). Fifty-six learn articles are linked from inside the product and 30 pages explain themselves in place, so a graduate is not sent to search the web for how to use the tool (T54). Lucena Pharmaceutical runs two supervisors, and hive.html checks for a co-supervisor before forcing a hand-over - so leaving is safe when another remains, and the last one is not waved through (T56). Fourteen pages surface device or session state, an idle timeout ships, and there is a way out, so someone who cares about their account has controls beyond closing the tab (T59). THE SCALE ROW IS STATED HONESTLY RATHER THAN CLAIMED: the largest hive in this data holds 8 active members, so twenty is beyond what it can prove; what is asserted instead is that all three roster surfaces BOUND what they render rather than drawing every member at once, which is the property that decides whether twenty people works (T61). TWO LENSES PASSED TOO EASILY ON THE FIRST RUN AND WERE TIGHTENED, both recorded in the prover: 'the reason beside the badge' matched the word description in every page's meta tag and counted 33 surfaces where the honest answer is 2; and 'surfaces session state' counted every page that merely LOADS device-fingerprint.js, when a script tag is not a control a person can act on.
trajectories.note: ★THE 20-MEMBER FIXTURE THIS TRAJECTORY ASKS FOR DID NOT EXIST (2026-08-26): the largest seeded hive holds 8, so every people surface had only been read at a size where nothing can go wrong. Built as an ON-DEMAND fixture rather than the standing one the spec imagined - a permanent 20-member hive would move the member counts, standings and rollups every other gate reads. prove_hive_at_scale grows a marked hive, asserts the roster returns every member (silent cap = a 20-person crew reading as a small team), that the count matches the list, that the ordering is TOTAL so members cannot swap between refreshes, and that no duplicate names survived the per-hive unique index - then removes it and re-counts 0. Names are Filipino and collide-prone on purpose; 'Worker 7' twenty times would sort perfectly and prove nothing. REMAINING: the live browser half - standings, presence and the assignee pickers walked at 20 - which this fixture now unblocks. ★THE LIVE HALF IS IN: rows agreeing was never the question - a roster fails by printing 20 beside a list of 10. The prover now tops a REAL hive to 20, signs in, expands the roster and compares rendered rows against both the printed count and the database (20 / '· 20' / 20, 0 pageerrors), then removes only the marked fixtures so the hive's own three members are untouched - verified back at 8/6/3 afterwards. Teeth: capping the render to 10 fires BOTH live assertions, the shortened list and the count that disagrees with it.

HIVE rename exists (H11, audited - T140's receipt). Per spec the deliverable is: document name-as-key as DOMAIN TRUTH + the rename-propagation recipe (count dangling attributions) as the future gate if identity-keyed migration ever lands. Remaining: the domain-truth statement + recipe (wave close docs). DELIVERABLE LANDED 2026-08-26: substrate/reference/identity_domain_truth.md - name-as-key declared as domain truth (rename does not exist and must not be added casually; hive rename safe by id-join contrast; the what-to-tell-a-user answer), plus the rename-propagation recipe (dangling-attribution count across logbook/pm_completions/inventory_transactions, DELTA-form because departures legitimately leave history). Remaining: none local - the statement is the spec's deliverable; an identity-keyed migration is a future product decision. pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_identity_lifecycle.mjs (gate identity-lifecycle), measured through PostgREST as the person rather than as the owner, because RLS is the only thing that can answer whether access followed. Membership was changed for real and restored: Wilfredo Malabanan reads 944 logbook rows as an active member, 0 once kicked, 0 once deactivated, and 944 again once restored - so access follows membership in BOTH directions and the walk left nobody worse off. Identity is reconcilable: worker_name is denormalised into 47 tables, and 21 triggers plus 3 views reconcile those copies against the profile, so a display-name change is not stranded in the rows that copied it. A member of two hives reads 1,170 and 1,700 rows under their own two hives and 0 under a third. The words for a lapsed membership are read from the CHECK constraint (active/kicked/deactivated) rather than guessed - the first run wrote 'removed', which the constraint rejects, so the membership never changed and the prover reported that unchanged world as a leak.

trajectories.note: ★MEASURED, AND A RENAME-WITH-HISTORY IS NOT IMPLEMENTABLE ON THIS DATA MODEL (2026-08-26) - found while hardening T185's namesake fix, which introduced the platform's FIRST reachable rename path and therefore made this trajectory's question urgent rather than theoretical. worker_name is a denormalised attribution label on 47 tables. 28 also carry auth_uid, so a rename can follow them precisely; 19 DO NOT, and for those the name is the only link. achievement_xp_log is the worst case: neither auth_uid NOR hive_id, so one person's rows cannot be located at all - matching on the old name alone would sweep up a namesake in another hive, the very collision this arc exists for. A trajectory parked on a product decision with its local deliverable done and gated belongs in locking, not fixing; leaving it low made the roadmap under-report itself. ★LOCKED (2026-08-27): THE DONE-DEFINITION'S SECOND BRANCH IS THE ONE THAT APPLIES. trajectories.title: Integrations page: the CMMS/ERP promise
trajectories.basis: walked 1280: honest state tiles (0 active / 0 stale / 12 disabled-kept), CSV-import path EXISTS ('drop a CSV from your CMMS - history on day one' - T135's does-import-exist answer is YES), Live Sync promises daily SAP pull + push-back. FOUND+FIXED an on-screen verdict contradiction: with 12 disabled/0 active the next-step else-chain said 'Everything is syncing.' under a hero saying 'No integrations syncing right now' - the all-off branch was missing; added + verified ('All 12 integrations are switched off, so nothing is syncing...'). Remaining: test-connection affordance (absent), claim-vs-fn capability alignment audit, mock-CMMS sync-lifecycle journey (wave close). || CLAIM-VS-CAPABILITY AUDIT DONE, AND THE PROMISE WAS KEPT WHILE ITS FAILURES WERE INVISIBLE (2026-08-28). The page's strongest claim is 'WorkHive pushes finished jobs back to SAP automatically, as each one is closed.' CHECKED THE PREMISE FIRST and it holds - logbook.html:2315 genuinely invokes cmms-push-completion when a job closes, so this is NOT the built-but-never-called class. The defect is what happens when that push FAILS. ★THE FAILURE MARKER WAS WRITTEN IN A WORD NOTHING READS. cmms-push-completion left the row at sync_status='failed'. The status CHECK permits five values ('active','deleted','error','failed','success') but v_external_sync_truth - the view whose entire job is classifying sync state - buckets only three: is_active, is_deleted, is_error. A row at 'failed' is NONE of them, so the durable marker F3 added specifically to stop a lost completion being silent landed in the one value that made it invisible to the truth view too. The seeder settles the intended vocabulary independently - it seeds 'error' because 'a sync that is FAILING is the state a dashboard should show'. And nothing anywhere SELECTS 'failed', so the retry its own comment promises ('so a retry (cron / next sync) can re-attempt it') does not exist. Fixed to write 'error'. ★AND NO SURFACE READ THE MARKER AT ALL. cmms-push-completion updates external_sync and automation_log and never touches integration_configs.last_sync_status - which is the ONLY status this page rendered (the red 'failed' badge at :1792 reads it, and only cmms-sync, the INBOUND pull, ever writes it). So a supervisor saw a green healthy integration while finished jobs silently never reached SAP; the worker meanwhile got a sync badge that shows unconditionally at logbook.html:2311, before the push result exists. The page now counts is_error records for the hive and leads its next-step with them, ranked ABOVE stale configs because a completion that never arrived outranks a config that has not run. LIVE-VERIFIED: Baguio shows '1 record failed to sync with your CMMS ... These are kept and can be re-synced' - correctly singular, and correctly 1 rather than the 5 that exist across all hives, so the tenant scoping holds. ZERO-CONTROL run too: with the error row flipped to active the notice disappears and the existing all-off branch returns, so it is a signal rather than furniture (row restored exactly - EQ-FL002 back to error, not merely the count). ★A CORRECTION TO THIS BASIS: it recorded 'test-connection affordance (absent)' and the markup DOES carry a Test Connection control - that line was stale. Remaining: whether Test Connection actually probes the endpoint, and the mock-CMMS sync-lifecycle journey (wave close). NOTE: the edge-function change is source-correct and needs a deploy to take effect in prod - Ian's gate, not applied here. || ★THE CLASS GATE GREW ITS MISSING HALF (2026-08-28). automation-log-status asserts every status literal is PERMITTED by its CHECK constraint. That answers 'may this value be stored' and never 'does anything downstream know what it means' - and the second question is where the real defect was hiding. cmms-push-completion wrote external_sync.sync_status='failed' as the durable marker for a completion that never reached the CMMS; the CHECK permits five values so a constraint-shaped gate passes it happily, but v_external_sync_truth buckets exactly three (is_active/is_deleted/is_error), so the marker built to make a lost completion VISIBLE landed in the one value that made it invisible to the truth view as well. New gate status-literals-are-classified asserts the other half: every status literal the code WRITES must be one the consuming view CLASSIFIES. It reads the LIVE view definition rather than a migration, so it measures what the database actually buckets. Resurrection-proven - restoring 'failed' names the orphan value and its exact line. ★AND ITS COLUMN PATTERN CARRIES A WORD BOUNDARY, which cost a wrong reading earlier the same day: without one, `sync_status` matches the tail of `last_sync_status` - a different column, on a different table, with its own vocabulary ('failed'/'success') and its own reader at integrations.html:1792. Two columns whose names overlap are not one column. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate no-eaten-escapes re-verified PASS standalone (exit 0; slow but green). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. || LOCKED 2026-09-03: post-board promote - every named gate PASS on the 2026-09-02 full board (1028 PASS run). pct -> 100.
