trajectories.note: Claim-vs-reality settled against cron.job: inbound sync has no scheduler, so three surfaces were promising a cadence nothing runs. Push-back IS real (logbook fires cmms-push-completion on close) and was kept. Also confirmed by disposition, not called a bug: data-fabric-normalizer is DECLARED scaffolding, which is why unified_events is empty. REMAINS: a setup walkthrough that can be completed, test-connection feedback, and sync-failure surfacing (who learns, where). ★A ROLLBACK THAT ANNOUNCED SUCCESS WITHOUT CHECKING - FOUND AND FIXED (2026-08-27). Sweeping for the MIRROR of the unconfirmed-write class (a false SUCCESS is worse than a false failure: the reader stops looking) found rollbackBatch. Its three steps - delete from external_sync, delete the imported rows from the target table, mark the audit entry rolled back - each did `await db.from(...)...` and DISCARDED the result, then it said 'Import rolled back successfully.' ★THE try/catch AROUND IT CANNOT HELP: supabase-js does not THROW when a write is refused, it RESOLVES with { error }. So an RLS refusal on any step sailed past the catch and the person was told their import had been undone while every imported row was still there. On a REVERSAL that is the worst available lie - they stop looking, and the bad data stays in the hive. Each step's error is captured now and any one of them takes the honest path the catch already had, naming that records may still be present. ★AND THE SMOKE THAT VERIFIED IT WAS ITSELF WRONG FIRST: integrations came back 'RENDERED ALMOST NOTHING' because tools/smoke_pages.mjs seeded the hive and the worker but not wh_hive_role, so a page whose gate reads that key showed 'Supervisor access only' to an account the DATABASE lists as a supervisor. A probe that jumps straight to a URL has to write what real navigation would; the tool seeds the role now and the page renders 1,950 chars. ★'SYNC-FAILURE SURFACING - WHO LEARNS, WHERE' IS ANSWERED, AND IT IS WELL BUILT (2026-08-27). The audience is the SUPERVISOR and the surface is plant-connections (HIVE_ROLE-gated), which carries a PRIORITISED ladder rather than a status dump - each rung naming the next action: no CMMS linked yet -> where to start and what most hives start with; a CMMS that has not synced in over a week -> 'Open Show details below, then click into the stale row'; API errors -> the COUNT over the last 7 days plus which panel holds the cause; no sensors mapped -> an honest degradation note that the Anomaly Engine still works on logbook and PM signals alone; SSO pending review -> the exact artefact to send and to whom. That is the shape a failure surface should have: one thing to read, and the thing to do about it. So T63's open question is closed as a verified positive rather than a fix. REMAINS for T63: a setup walkthrough that can be COMPLETED end-to-end, and test-connection feedback - the one control whose entire job is saying why an endpoint did not answer.

trajectories.title: Audit-log page as a destination (beyond T28's reachability)
trajectories.basis: accumulated-evidence ledger: the page's own bars verified across T28/T49 walks - ?q=/actor/action/target deep links + G5a filter restore + range windows resolved the same way for screen AND export, paginated FULL export with honest fallback + self-describing artifact, Load More pagination, supervisor gate. Remaining: roster/denominator membership decision (rubric Tier B), volume behavior at 1000s rows (T129 fixture), entry before->after comprehension (wave close). || ★THE TRAIL IS APPEND-ONLY TO CLIENTS, AND I PROVED IT BY ACCIDENT WHILE TRYING TO BREAK IT (2026-08-28). Walking audit-log I found my own gate's leftovers in it - 'delete asset node WH-PROBE-UNDOGATE-2' and siblings - because asset_nodes carries trg_asset_node_delete_audit and every probe row it removes is dutifully recorded. Correct by the trigger, residue by the probe, so I taught the gate to clean them and the delete DID NOTHING. Silently, which is the RLS-filtered delete shape this codebase knows: 0 rows, no error. The policies explain it and are exactly right - hive_audit_log carries ONE insert policy and TWO select policies and NO delete or update policy at all, so no client can erase or amend an entry. WITHDRAWN LISTING: trg_release_reservation flips the reservation to state='returned' with released_at stamped, on the removed and draft paths. SOLD LISTING: grant_listing_reward reads the still-HELD reservation and writes a TWO-LEGGED ledger entry - the seller debited 'funded the buyer reward', the buyer credited 'reward for buying' - then marks it released_to_buyer. So on a completed sale the seller DOES part with the 10%%; it goes to the BUYER, never to WorkHive. 'There are no fees' is therefore true of the platform and would have been a half-truth to the seller - except that the page says the rest of it, verbatim: the hold is 'returned if the listing does not sell, and GOES TO YOUR BUYER AS THEIR REWARD if it does'. The fate of the money is disclosed at the surface, matching the ledger exactly. That is what the what_does_it_cost oracle asks for and it is rare to find it this clean. ★TWO DETAILS THAT MAKE IT MORE THAN LUCKY: the rate is fetched from the server via svcRewardPct() and warmed before first paint, so the hold the seller SEES is the hold the database ENFORCES rather than a hardcoded 10 that could drift from the knob; and grant_listing_reward refuses to let the money evaporate when the buyer cannot be resolved - it returns the credits to the seller, with the reason written in the source ('A reward with nowhere to go must never become a silent deduction'). trajectories.title: Marketplace-admin moderation lane
trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25, leandro=platform-admin + christine=non-admin, 1280): the lane's ARCHITECTURE verified against the substrate memory - marketplace-admin.html is deliberately KEPT as a deep-browse behind a full-screen reversible RETIRED overlay (redirect-first: Grafana volumes + Platform Actions doors), with the LIVE moderation fused into founder-console#sec-mkt-mod on the same is_marketplace_admin authority. Gate proven: the non-admin supervisor is REFUSED the underlying queue (0 approve controls, refusal text). FIXED + shipped: the overlay printed 'Grafana login: admin - password in infra/mcp/.env.mcp' to ANY signed-in visitor - a credential-location pointer in page copy (T170 screen-share class, worse because the overlay is the one part everyone CAN see); replaced with 'see the infra operator notes'. INSTRUMENT NOTE: my first read graded the under-overlay queue as 'still operating' - getClientRects sees THROUGH a covering overlay; pointer-reachability, not rects, decides what a user can operate (the page-guide-chip-covered-Save lesson's twin). Remaining: the fused founder-console moderation walk (queue triage at volume, self-deal guard UX face, dispute three-party views via T35's harness), the localhost Grafana link's non-founder audience note (wave close). || THE SELF-DEAL GUARD IS EXCELLENT AND HAS NO DOOR (2026-08-27). Read apply_dispute_adjustment's definition: four distinct refusals, each naming its cause in language a person could act on - 'Only a platform admin may adjust a disputed job' (42501); 'Unknown request'; 'Only a disputed job can be adjusted (this one is %)', which INTERPOLATES the actual status rather than leaving the admin to guess; and the self-deal check, 'You are the client on this job; another admin must adjudicate it', which is the rare refusal that names the conflict AND the remedy in one sentence. That is exactly the UX face this trajectory was looking for, and it already exists at the layer that enforces it. ★BUT NOTHING CALLS IT. A search for a real rpc('apply_dispute_adjustment') invocation across every html/js/ts finds exactly three, all inside tests/marketplace-sim-aftermath.spec.ts. The only mentions in product files are COMMENTS in marketplace-seller.html and marketplace.html describing what the function would do. So the adjudication path is written, guarded, and covered by a test - and an admin cannot reach it through the glass; a real dispute would have to be settled by someone with direct database access. The guard's careful messages are, today, addressed to a test runner. ★THIS IS THE 'BUILT BUT NEVER CALLED' CLASS ONE STEP ON: not dead code, but LIVE code with no entrance - which reads as healthy on every static check because the function exists, is referenced in prose, and passes its test. Directly relevant to T97 (dispute resolution end-to-end), whose three-party walk cannot exist until this door does. Remaining: the adjudication UI in the admin lane, then queue triage at volume and the three-party dispute views via T35's harness. ★AND THE 'NO CALLER' FINDING SURVIVES THE OBVIOUS OBJECTION, WHICH I WENT AND CHECKED (2026-08-27): marketplace-admin is RETIRED behind an overlay, its moderation having moved to platform-actions.html, so the natural rebuttal is that the caller simply lives on the new page. It does not. platform-actions documents the history precisely - an 'Open disputes' card was retired 2026-08-03 because it read marketplace_disputes, a GHOST TABLE with 0 rows and no client writer, and offered a 'Refund buyer' button for money the platform never holds - and the same comment names the real mechanism: 'Real disputes are service jobs, adjudicated through apply_dispute_adjustment.' So the platform correctly removed a fake dispute UI, wrote down what the true path is, and has still never built a door to it. That is a stronger version of the finding, not a weaker one: the gap is not an oversight nobody noticed, it is a known mechanism with a documented name and no entrance. || WALKED 1280 SIGNED IN (2026-08-28): the page is RETIRED, and the retirement is the exemplary kind. A full-screen overlay states what moved and WHERE - volumes to Grafana panels, approve / verify / resolve actions to platform-actions.html - and links BOTH destinations rather than leaving the visitor to hunt. Its source comment records the design as 'redirect-first + REVERSIBLE: the original markup is preserved below (validators that scan this file still pass). To un-retire: delete this <div id="wh-retired-overlay"> block', which is how a retirement stays cheap to undo. There is also a T69 note that a Grafana CREDENTIAL POINTER was deliberately removed from the copy because 'this overlay renders for ANY signed-in visitor to the URL, not only the founder, and a credentials location baked into page copy is a screen-share/shoulder hazard' - the right instinct, and rare. ONE OBSERVATION rather than a defect: the underlying page still RUNS - my walk read live figures from behind the overlay (4 Pending Review, 20 Published, 13 Sellers, 9 Pending Verification), so a retired surface is still issuing its queries on every visit. That follows from the preserve-the-markup choice and is the price of reversibility; worth knowing rather than worth changing. || ★THE ADMIN LANE IS GENUINELY AUDITED - and the boundary where auditing STOPS is a schema fact, not an oversight (2026-08-28). marketplace-admin DEFINES writeAuditLog(action, targetType, targetId, targetName, meta) at :454 and calls it from five action paths, and the database agrees that it works: 32 admin-scope rows (listing / KYB / voucher actions) sit in hive_audit_log today. So every moderation action on this lane leaves a traceable record with an actor - the probe this trajectory cares about most, answered with rows rather than with code-reading. ★THE CONTRAST WITH ITS SIBLING IS THE FINDING. founder-console calls writeAuditLog three times and NEVER DEFINES IT; all three calls sit behind `if (typeof writeAuditLog === 'function')`, so the guard is permanently false and the owner's own actions - minting a voucher, deciding a top-up - are silently unaudited. A guard written to be defensive became the thing that hides the absence: no error, no row, no signal. ★AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL, which is why the earlier pass documented it rather than patching it: hive_audit_log.hive_id is NOT NULL. marketplace-admin can satisfy that because everything it acts on belongs to somebody's hive - a listing has a seller, a seller has a hive. founder-console acts at PLATFORM scope, where there is no hive to name, so the table has no valid row shape for its actions and the function was never written. Defining writeAuditLog there without first deciding WHERE platform-scope actions live would just move the failure from silent-skip to a NOT NULL violation on the owner's most consequential controls. ★THE DECISION Ian owes this: a nullable hive_id with a scope discriminator, or a separate platform_audit_log. Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.
trajectories.note: ★A FAILED READ RENDERED AS 'NOTHING TO MODERATE' (2026-08-27). marketplace-admin's three loaders each did `catch { _x = []; toast('...check your connection...') }` and re-rendered. The toast fades; the EMPTY STATE stays - so a refused read (and on an admin surface an RLS refusal is the likeliest failure of all) ended as 'No pending listings / All listings have been reviewed'. On a moderation queue that is the single most costly false sentence the product can show: it is the one that makes someone stop looking. All three now record the failure and render 'This is not an empty queue - the list could not be read', and the messages route through whReadError so a dead session stops being reported as bad wifi. ★THE PLATFORM HAD ALREADY LEARNED THIS TWICE. marketplace.html carries the diagnosis verbatim in its own source from a deepwalk - 'the toast alone was insufficient, it fades, leaving the GRID showing the first-run CTA on a full marketplace' - and seller-profile carries 'Only a read that ANSWERED may license a conclusion about this seller'. Both were fixed; the moderation queue never was. Second fix-that-did-not-travel in one session, so it is now gated: failed-read-is-not-empty. ★THE GATE FOUND A SECOND VICTIM I HAD NOT LOOKED FOR: dayplanner's plant-PM rail returned '' on a failed read and simply VANISHED - not a false claim, an invisible one, which a worker cannot tell from a quiet day. It now says why it is empty. ★AND THE GATE WAS WRONG TWICE BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT, both times too NARROW or too BROAD in vocabulary: it first flagged alert-hub's legacy JSON-parse fallback (correct code - scoped it to catches that wrap a QUERY), then failed the very page I had just fixed because marketplace-admin spells its flag as a property (_readFailed.listings) and the regex only accepted bare identifiers. An oracle's vocabulary is part of the oracle, for the sixth time today.

trajectories.title: Seller-profile as the buyer's trust page
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the full chip census done - each claim checked against its enforcing query). THE PROFILE IS IN GOOD ORDER and every trust pixel is computed from data rather than decoration: Top rated = ratingAvg >= 4.5 AND ratingCount >= 5; Quick reply = avgResponseHours < 4 AND replyCount >= 5; Tier carries its own thresholds (silver 11 sales, gold 51) and says 'set by WorkHive from completed sales, not self-assigned'; ID Verified is gated on kyb_verified; Certified routes through the central whCertBadgeEarned on ALL THREE surfaces that render it (seller profile, seller dashboard, listing sheet). ★ONE READING LOOKED LIKE THE ORIGINAL BUG AND WAS NOT: the certifications SECTION tests cert_verified on its own, which is the exact shape of the recorded incident - but the whole block sits inside `if (certSection && certs.length)`, so a non-empty list is guaranteed by construction. Read verbatim before accusing; that check would have been a false finding. Locked as 'trust-claim-backed', guarding the FIXED class: no buyer-facing surface may present a certification claim from cert_verified alone - it must call the central predicate or guard on the certifications list in the same breath. The incident it protects against is concrete: three sellers once carried a violet 'Certified' chip with certifications NULL and cert_verified_at NULL, the platform vouching to a buyer about to send money for credentials that did not exist. ★MODERATION SURFACES EXCLUDED BY NAME, not for convenience: marketplace-admin, founder-console and platform-actions are where verification is GRANTED and must see the raw flag - including the 'set but no certifications on file' state this gate keeps off a buyer's screen. Blinding the moderator to what they moderate would invert the goal. Teeth proven by reverting the profile badge to the flag alone, resurrecting the original incident's shape. REMAINING: the report-a-seller path walk (wave close). || ★THE ID-VERIFIED CHIP IS QUERY-BACKED, AND I NEARLY FILED IT AS INVERTED (2026-08-28). Walked two sellers side by side and the chip looked exactly wrong: Dennis Aquino, whose listings carry seller_verified TRUE, showed NO badge, while Pablo Aguilar, whose listings carry FALSE, showed 'ID Verified'. A trust badge on the wrong person is about the worst defect this page could have, so I read the render before writing it up: the chip is driven by _seller?.kyb_verified from marketplace_sellers, NOT by marketplace_listings.seller_verified. Checking THAT column settles it - Dennis kyb_verified f, Pablo kyb_verified t - so the chip agrees with its own source on both sellers and the claim is enforced. I had compared two similarly-named fields on two different tables and read the mismatch as a defect. ★AND THE CODE ALREADY CARRIES THE LESSON THIS TRAJECTORY EXISTS FOR, at the render site: 'a verification badge requires the thing it verifies. Central rule in utils.js so all three surfaces that render this chip cannot drift apart' - the ID-verified-chip-nothing-enforces memory, fixed centrally rather than per page. ★WORTH RECORDING AS A RISK RATHER THAN A DEFECT: seller_verified (listings) and kyb_verified (sellers) are two different booleans about the same human, one table apart, and I am not the last reader who will assume they mean the same thing. THE PARAMLESS CASE IS ALSO CLEAN: the page refuses with a remedy ('No seller specified. This page needs a seller name in the URL. Open it via marketplace.html.') and its source chip names the corpora it read. || ★AND THEN THE REAL DEFECT, ONE LAYER UNDER THE NEAR-MISS: THE ID-VERIFIED CHIP DISAGREED WITH ITSELF ACROSS FOUR SURFACES (2026-08-28). Having established the chip is query-backed on the profile, I checked who ELSE renders it, and found four sites with four different predicates - marketplace card `item.seller_verified`, marketplace detail `sp.kyb_verified || item.seller_verified`, seller profile `_seller.kyb_verified`, asset-hub mini-card `r.seller_verified`. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE on the fixture: Dennis Aquino carries kyb_verified FALSE on his seller record and seller_verified TRUE on his listings, so he read as VERIFIED on three surfaces and UNVERIFIED on his own profile page. A trust badge that contradicts itself is worse than none, because each surface looks authoritative alone. ★THE CENTRALISATION LESSON WAS ALREADY HERE AND HAD BEEN APPLIED TO THE WRONG CHIP: the comment 'a verification badge requires the thing it verifies. Central rule in utils.js so all three surfaces that render this chip cannot drift apart' sits directly above whCertBadgeEarned - it governs CERTIFIED. The ID-Verified chip standing beside it never got the treatment, and drifted. FIXED with whIdVerified() in utils.js, and the rule is the CONSERVATIVE one on purpose: identity belongs to the SELLER (marketplace_sellers.kyb_verified), not to a listing row whose seller_verified is a copy that can be stale - and reading the seller record is the direction that cannot OVER-claim, which is the failure that matters for a trust signal. No fallback to the drifted field: absent evidence is not evidence. The data was already there - v_marketplace_listings_truth exposes seller_kyb_verified - so the four card queries simply select it now. VERIFIED: the helper returns true/false correctly for a seller record, for the joined column, and crucially FALSE when only the drifted seller_verified is present; the view's column matches the DB join exactly (7 of 20 published); the profile shows the chip for Pablo (kyb true) and withholds it from Dennis (kyb false); zero page errors. ★A SYNTAX ERROR I INTRODUCED AND CAUGHT: my first edit left a stray docblock fragment outside a comment in utils.js - a file every page loads. `node --check` found it immediately. Running the parser is cheaper than discovering it on a page. pct 78 -> 90. || ★AND THE GATE'S OWN CENSUS IS WHERE THE DRIFT HID (2026-08-28). validate_trust_claim_backed carries a census listing every trust claim on this page, and one line reads 'ID Verified — gated on kyb_verified'. That was true of the PROFILE, examined alone, and stated as a platform fact - while three other surfaces granted the same badge from marketplace_listings.seller_verified. A census that examines one surface and generalises is the same too-narrow-scope failure as a gate scoped to one call site, one level up: it produced a WRITTEN RECORD saying the class was safe. The gate's assertion only ever guarded the CERTIFIED chip. Extended now to the identity chip too: a buyer-facing render may not grant the badge from the drifting per-listing copy. TEETH-PROVEN by putting `item.seller_verified` back on the marketplace card - FAIL naming marketplace.html:2183 - and green again on restore, with 8 identity-badge renders counted and 0 from the wrong column. pct 90 -> 95. Remaining: the response-time and sales-history claims still want the same treatment the identity and certification chips now have. || ★THE ROOT OF THE ID-BADGE DRIFT IS IN THE VIEW, AND IT IS LATENT RATHER THAN FIXED (2026-08-28). The client fix routed every identity badge through whIdVerified(), and trust-claim-backed now holds it there — 8 identity-badge renders, 0 reading the drifting copy. But the copy itself is still MANUFACTURED, one layer down: v_marketplace_listings_truth computes `COALESCE(ms.kyb_verified, false) OR COALESCE(ms.cert_verified, false) AS seller_verified`. That OR conflates two different verifications — an identity check (KYB) and a trade-credential check (certifications) — into one boolean whose NAME reads as identity. A seller with certifications on file and no identity check would therefore be seller_verified = true, and any surface that ever reads that column for an ID badge would vouch for an identity nobody confirmed. ★MEASURED, AND IT IS NOT MANIFESTING TODAY: the fixture holds 4 KYB-verified and 4 cert-verified sellers with ZERO divergence, so no seller currently sits in the gap. That is why this is recorded rather than migrated — the semantics are wrong but nothing renders wrongly, the badge decision no longer consults the column, and a gate fails any surface that starts consulting it again. The trigger case to watch for is the first seller granted cert_verified without kyb_verified; splitting the column (or renaming it to say what it means, e.g. seller_any_verification) is the real fix and touches every consumer of the listings view, so it goes to Ian rather than being done quietly under a badge fix. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: the fix is verified and the registered gate trust-claim-backed PASSES standalone (re-run this session). Awaiting the next full-board earn to promote to locked. pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_page_as_destination.mjs (gate page-as-destination): eight destination journeys walked as one family, each page opened COLD in a context that has never visited the app - what a bookmark or a link in a message actually does. 8/8 orient someone arriving from nothing: a heading that names the page, the page's own data on screen with no stuck skeleton, a source chip saying how fresh it is, and at least one internal link leading onward rather than a cul-de-sac the back button is the only exit from. Measured: audit-log 2,195 characters and 2 ways on, founder-console 13,701 and 10, platform-actions 4,096, the seller trust page 1,175 under the seller's own name, status 1,293, dayplanner 3,852, voice-journal 1,996. Recorded rather than claimed: that page tells you what is missing and cannot help you choose a project from there.

The empty branch now teaches from the definition: live-proven 'No activity yet. How to earn: Manage inventory and BOM - XP lands here automatically as you do that work.' Remaining: standings privacy posture, marketplace-tier vocabulary bridge. || THE TIER-VOCABULARY BRIDGE EXISTS AND IS CORRECT - THE TWO SYSTEMS ARE ONE (2026-08-27). The open worry was that achievements and the marketplace both say bronze/silver/gold for different things, which is the one_vocabulary failure: same word, two meanings, and a worker who earns 'Gold' somewhere cannot tell which ladder moved. Read the code and the worry is unfounded in the best possible way - achievements.html reads v_service_provider_truth, the SAME view the marketplace surfaces render from, and displays that row's own tier field. There is no second tier ladder to collide with; there is one ladder shown in two places. ★AND IT IS SHOWN WITH ITS NEXT STEP, which is the property T74 and T98 both want: not a bare badge but '10 more completed jobs reach Silver' / '25 more jobs and a 4.5-star average reach Gold' / 'Top tier - you get first look at new hails', so the ladder is predictable rather than mysterious. It is also correctly scoped: a member who is not a service provider gets the section rendered as NOTHING rather than an empty or zeroed tier ('not a provider: render nothing'), so a plant worker who never sells is not shown a Bronze badge for a ladder they are not on. ★THE MEASUREMENT NEEDED CARE: a raw grep for 'tier' in achievements returns mostly CSS COMMENTS about the type scale ('joined the 18px title tier', 'the text tier exists for exactly this') - typography prose, not the domain concept, and counting those would have manufactured a vocabulary problem out of a stylesheet. Remaining: standings PRIVACY posture - there is no opt-out, hide-me or anonymise control anywhere on the page, so every hive member appears in the standings by default. Whether that should be opt-out-able is a product call (a team leaderboard is normal; being unable to leave it is a different thing), so it rides as Ian's. || ★AN XP REVERSAL RENDERED AS '+-20' ON THE REWARD SURFACE (2026-08-28). achievements.html builds every XP row through one helper, xpText, and that helper hard-codes a '+' in front of any finite number. Negative amounts are not hypothetical here - they are the reversible XP ledger this programme deliberately built, so deleting work takes its XP back. SEEN LIVE on Bryan Garcia's Wrench Chronicle card: 'Logbook entry submitted +-20', 'Logbook entry closed +-50', beside a correct 'Logbook entry closed +50'. ★AND THE SITE ALREADY CARRIED A LONG COMMENT ABOUT THIS EXACT HELPER - it was hardened against null ('+null' rendered ten times on one screen), against Number(null) coercing to 0, and it even reasons about why '+0' would be 'a lie of a different kind'. Every one of those guards is about the ABSENT case. None is about the NEGATIVE case, because when the guard was written negatives could not occur; they arrived later with the reversal ledger. That is the sibling-fix shape this codebase keeps meeting, in its subtlest form: not a fix applied to one of two call sites, but a guard that was complete on the day it was written and was never revisited when a NEW FEATURE widened its input domain. FIXED: a negative already carries its own sign, so only a gain has one added. Verified live - the three rows now read -20, -50, +50, no '+-' anywhere on the page - and across the helper's whole domain: +20 | -20 | +0 | 'XP not recorded' for null, undefined and empty, so the absent-case guards the comment describes still behave exactly as before. A reversal is the one XP event a worker most needs to read correctly. || AND THE SWEEP FOUND ITS SIBLING 140 LINES AWAY (2026-08-28). Having fixed xpText I swept every page for the shape - a hard-coded '+' in front of an interpolated value - rather than stopping at the instance. NINE hits. Seven are engineering-design overflow counts ('+3 more', '+2' beside a truncated list) where the value is positive by construction, guarded by the if (n > visible) that produces them. The eighth was the fix itself. THE NINTH IS REAL: achievements' WEEK hero renders `+${weekXP}`, and weekXP is a plain SUM of xp_earned over seven days (init :1197, reduce over the rows), so a week whose reversals outweigh its gains is genuinely negative and the headline tile would have read '+-30'. Fixed the same way, and its subtitle now explains the case rather than reading as nonsense: '-30 XP this week - more was taken back by deleted work than earned'. Verified: the live positive case is unchanged (+1780), the negative renders -30 with that sub, zero still reads +0 / 'No XP earned in the past 7 days'. ★THE SWEEP IS THE POINT - one fix would have left a headline number lying while the detail rows beneath it told the truth, which is worse than either alone. || ★EVERY ACHIEVEMENT SAYS WHAT EARNS IT, AND THE CATALOGUE IS ORGANISED BY MOTIVATION RATHER THAN BY FEATURE (2026-08-28). The probe is whether a locked achievement teaches its own HOW. Each definition carries a desc that names the activity in plain language - 'Log and close maintenance jobs', 'Complete PM tasks on time', 'Identify root causes of breakdowns', 'Write detailed entries and handovers' - so a worker reading the catalogue learns what the platform wants from them without opening anything. ★AND THE GROUPING IS DELIBERATE PSYCHOLOGY, not a feature index: every achievement is tagged to one of three pillars - competence, autonomy, relatedness - which is the self-determination triad, the standard model of intrinsic motivation. wrench_chronicle and uptime_guardian sit under competence; safety_sentinel and skill_climber under autonomy; hive_architect and voice_of_hive under relatedness. Somebody designed this to answer 'why would a worker care' rather than 'what features do we have', and that is the difference between a progression system and a list of badges named after modules. ★THE HONEST LIMIT: the descs name the ACTIVITY, not the THRESHOLD. 'Complete PM tasks on time' tells a worker what to do and not how many, so 'what do I need for my next badge' - this trajectory's plan-your-next-badge probe - is answerable only in direction, not in distance. trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the SC 2.5.7 drag question ANSWERED platform-wide). ★THE WALK'S PREMISE WAS WRONG AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS SO: it listed 'touch drag/reorder alternative (SC 2.5.7)' as dayplanner's remaining risk, and dayplanner has NO drag machinery at all - no draggable, no dragstart, no touchmove reorder. There was no drag to provide an alternative for. Swept every production surface instead: only THREE drag hooks exist. integrations' CSV drop zone is exemplary (role=button, tabindex=0, onclick -> file-input.click(), and visible copy reading 'Drop file here or click to browse' - drag is the shortcut, not the door), and the other two are nav-hub's and companion-launcher's FAB repositioners. ★THOSE TWO ARE ALLOWED BY A RULE RATHER THAN BY NAME, because a name-based exemption would be a licence: the gate decides on what the handler WRITES. Both assign only style.left/right/top/bottom - they move a control and confer no capability, since opening the hub is a tap and `didDrag` exists precisely so a drag does not fire it. And the need a reposition serves - a fixed control covering content - is already met for everyone structurally by the reserve and lift rules in that same file (read while fixing T184 this session). If such a handler ever starts mutating data (insert, splice, sort_order) it stops matching the position-only test and the gate speaks up - proven by a teeth test that adds a dragstart calling splice(). The registry's duplicate-id guard caught the first; a diff against HEAD caught and exactly repaired the second (865 = 803 HEAD + 62 program gates, 0 missing, no dupes, both halves re-run green). T117's findings - session-timeout's touchstart as an activity SIGNAL, wh-persona's draggable=false, the .wh-scroll-x keyboard trap closed centrally - were recovered from its registry label and folded back in. The PM rail reads '30 of 80 PMs': a display slice that names its whole. The code shows this is deliberate rather than lucky - the query carries count:'exact' with a comment saying WHY ('the .limit(30) below is a DISPLAY slice, and the header next to this rail states a number. Without the count it stated data.length'), and the label is conditional, falling back to a correctly pluralised 'N PM' / 'N PMs' when nothing is being truncated. The logbook rail states its source in the same breath ('2 open items from Logbook'), and every overdue PM card carries its asset, its make/model and its due date rather than a bare 'Overdue'. Zero page errors at 390. || ★THE DAY PLANNER SHOWED THE DAY OUT OF ORDER - found, fixed, proven (2026-08-28). It IS a planning tool, not a read view: six insert/update/upsert/delete paths, and the item form collects a Start Time and End Time (#m-start / #m-end, type=time). But loadSchedule ordered by .order('date').order('id') and NOTHING ELSE, so two items on the same day never sorted chronologically. Worse than creation order: schedule_items.id is a TEXT key like 'svc-<uuid>', so the tiebreaker sorts on a random string. Measured on real rows, one worker's day read 10:30 -> 09:00 -> 07:00 -> 08:00. A planner that asks when a job starts and then lists the afternoon above the morning is not showing the worker their day, and 36 same-date multi-item days exist in local data alone. ★FIX: .order('start_time', {ascending:true, nullsFirst:false}) between date and the id tiebreaker. start_time is TEXT in zero-padded HH:MM, so a lexicographic sort IS chronological - no cast needed. nullsFirst:false is the load-bearing half: 126 of 228 rows are UNTIMED, and the default nulls-first would have floated every untimed to-do above the scheduled work, making the majority case worse than the bug I was fixing. Timed work now reads in order, untimed follows. PROVEN on the same rows: 07:00 -> 08:00 -> 09:00 -> 10:30. ★AND THE DATA HAD TWO SPELLINGS OF 'NO TIME SET': 126 NULL plus 2 empty-string starts (3 empty ends). They mean the same thing to a person and sort oppositely to a database - '' precedes '07:00', so those rows would have floated to the TOP of the day while NULLs correctly fell to the end, the same untimed item landing in opposite places depending on which spelling was stored. Migration ...004 normalises '' -> NULL and adds a CHECK so the pair cannot drift again - fixing the representation rather than widening the sort to special-case it. VERIFIED THREE WAYS: teeth (an empty start_time INSERT is rejected by name), non-breakage (a NULL start_time still inserts, so the 56% untimed majority still saves), and idempotency (re-run yields UPDATE 0 / UPDATE 0 and no duplicate-constraint error). ★VALIDATED NEGATIVE: no drag/reorder machinery exists anywhere on this page - no draggable, dragstart, sortable or touchstart - so WCAG 2.5.7 (dragging movements needs a single-pointer alternative) is not violated here; there is no dragging to provide an alternative for. The only 'drop' match was backdrop-filter in CSS. Sorting by time is also what makes reorder unnecessary: the day orders itself from the times the worker already enters. ★SUPERSEDED WITHIN THE SAME TURN, and the correction matters more than the original: the CHECK described above was the WRONG SHAPE and I removed it in migration ...005. Walking T192 immediately afterwards asked what dayplanner actually SENDS, and the answer was '' - an empty <input type="time"> yields empty string at :1988 and the quick-add path coerces to '' at :2084 - so that CHECK would have REJECTED every untimed task, i.e. 126 of 228 rows, the majority case. There is NO edit. So a supervisor holding an AI-drafted failure mode that is NEARLY right must either approve it as written or delete it and re-author from scratch — and on FMEA that asymmetry has teeth, because these rows drive maintenance strategy and risk scoring. The cheap path is to approve, so an imprecise mode ('bearing wear' where the truth is outer-race spalling from misalignment) gets published because editing costs more than accepting. ★THE PATTERN ALREADY EXISTS ON THIS PLATFORM: resume's review sheet renders each extracted item as an EDITABLE input (data-review-value, resume.html:1224) — accept / amend / reject per row — which is the shape this trajectory's own spec asked for. So the gap is not that the idea is unproven here. ★WHAT MAKES IT MORE THAN A COPY IS A PROVENANCE QUESTION WITH NO OBVIOUS RIGHT ANSWER: the rows carry a fmea-source-pill, and ai-draft-shows-its-basis locks that the basis is shown. If a supervisor rewrites an AI-drafted mode, what does the pill say afterwards? Keep 'AI' and the platform overstates what the model contributed; switch to 'human' and it erases that AI seeded a safety-relevant record. Both are defensible, and AI6 makes it a truth question rather than a styling one — so the edit path is specced with its provenance semantics rather than guessed at on a surface where the record outlives the session. Remaining: that provenance decision, then the edit path; empty-history honesty; per-suggestion grounding drill. || ★THE OPEN QUESTION FOR IAN IS ANSWERED BY THE ARCHITECTURE - RETIRING THE FORK (2026-08-27). The pending question was: does the source pill still say AI after a human rewrites an AI-drafted failure mode? Measured rather than debated. THERE IS NO IN-PLACE REWRITE: the only two writes to rcm_fmea_modes are an INSERT (new mode) and an UPDATE that sets ONLY approved_by + approved_at, guarded with .is('approved_at', null) so the first approver's name cannot be overwritten - a guard whose comment records the live-proven last-write-wins bug it fixed ('writerB re-approve affected 1 row and overwrote Supervisor A'). A human therefore never edits an AI row's text; they APPROVE it, or they author a separate manual one. ★SO THE TWO FACTS NEVER COLLIDE: `source` records who DRAFTED (ai_logbook / ai_template / manual / imported, CHECK-constrained), `approved_by` + `approved_at` record who VETTED, and the row renders BOTH - the AI/manual pill and the approved/pending status side by side. The pill staying 'AI' is correct rather than stale, because it is not a claim about who endorses the mode; the approval chip is. LIVE STATE: 300 modes, 85 carrying ai_confidence, 245 approved. The question only had force under an assumption the code does not make - that editing and drafting share a field. ★AND MY OWN FIRST QUERY INVENTED THE TABLE: I asked asset_fmea_modes, got an empty column list, and could have read that as 'no provenance is stored'. The table is rcm_fmea_modes and it carries source, ai_confidence, created_by, approved_by and approved_at - a fabricated name producing a false absence, the same class as this session's fabricated hive UUID. pct -> 88. pct -> 100.

The fixture had today's brief present, so the honest state was unobservable; today's row was moved to a sentinel shift_date (one row, by id), the page walked, and the row restored and verified (shift_date 2026-08-27 / approved, one row for today, zero sentinel rows left). WHAT A SUPERVISOR SEES on a morning the 6am cron did not run: 'NOT GENERATED — No brief was generated for this shift. The brief is written at 6am PHT and has not run for today. trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25): REACHABILITY MAPPED first (the trajectory's own bar): the global Cmd+K palette is EXACT-KEYWORD over four truth views (assets/jobs/parts/PMs, click jumps to source) while the semantic-search fn is consumed ONLY inside assistant.html as RAG context (JWT-forwarded tenancy, 6s ceiling, proceed-without-RAG fallback) - the capability is reachable CONVERSATIONALLY, a legitimate split, but a natural-language phrase typed into the palette dead-ended ('No matches. The knowledge RPCs (search_fault_knowledge, search_all_knowledge, match_procedural_memories) all take the hive as a CLIENT-SUPPLIED parameter - search_fault_knowledge(query_embedding vector, match_hive_id uuid, match_count int) with WHERE hive_id = match_hive_id - which on its own would be injectable: pass another hive's id and ask for its knowledge. ★WHAT MAKES IT SAFE IS TWO FACTS THAT HAVE TO HOLD TOGETHER, and both were checked rather than assumed. The function is SECURITY INVOKER, not DEFINER, so the caller's RLS applies; and fault_knowledge / knowledge_graph_facts have RLS ENABLED with the policy 'auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND hive_id IN (SELECT hive_id FROM hive_members WHERE auth_uid = auth.uid() AND status = active)'. trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25): REACHABILITY MAPPED - digestion surfaces to users THROUGH the RAG consumers (agentic-rag-loop, ai-gateway, temporal-rag-orchestrator read canonical_period_summaries; T91's structured week-diff drew on this machinery); no direct digest page exists (by design). BUILT + PROVEN: (1) the self-fanning mode in hierarchical-summarizer (empty body + service-role -> previous WEEK for every hive with logbook activity in the window, + previous MONTH in a month's first 7 days; per-hive bodies unchanged); (2) migration 20260825000002 arms 'hierarchical-summaries-weekly' (Sun 21:00 UTC = Mon 05:00 PHT, portable-URL pattern) re-runnably; (3) live test: fan-out wrote Baguio's week summary (1->2 rows, correct scoping - only the hive with last-week activity), validate_hierarchical_summaries 16/16 PASS, validate_cron_schedule_integrity 4 PASS/0 FAIL, fn header updated so L5 sees header+cron agree. Remaining: digest-grounding drill (summary claim -> source rows via source_row_ids), E4 answer-not-working bar on the summary_text, staleness stamps at the consumer end (wave close). DEPLOY NOTE: fn redeploy + db push in the release. || ★THE DIGEST-GROUNDING DRILL CANNOT BE WALKED AS BUILT (measured 2026-08-27) - source_row_ids can never populate, and a comment asserting the opposite is why it went unnoticed. THE CHAIN, each link checked: canonical_period_summaries holds 2 rows and 0 carry source_row_ids. The producer DOES write the column (hierarchical-summarizer :346) but filters first - :334-335 keep only ids matching a UUID regex, guarded by the comment 'the local seeder uses string IDs like log-XXX ... Production logbook IDs (gen_random_uuid()) always pass this filter.' THAT PREMISE IS FALSE, and not only locally: the baseline migration declares logbook.id as "text" NOT NULL with NO gen_random_uuid() default (20260420000000_baseline.sql :874), and the app writes id: Date.now().toString() (logbook.html :4958) - a millisecond timestamp string. So every logbook id fails the UUID filter, validSourceIds is always [], and source_row_ids is empty in PRODUCTION too. The column is typed uuid[] while its only source table is keyed by text, so the two ends were never able to meet. CONSEQUENCE: a digest on the glass cannot be drilled to the rows it summarises - the affordance is structurally absent, not merely unbuilt, which is what the remaining item assumed. THE FIX IS A FORK, not a slice: either widen source_row_ids to text[] to match the key its sources actually use (small migration, no data movement), or move logbook to uuid ids (large, touches every attribution join that reads logbook.id as text). Recorded rather than chosen - re-keying the logbook is not a call to make from a grounding probe. || FIXED 2026-08-27, and the 'fork' above was over-cautious - I called it a decision for Ian, then checked what the small end actually costs and it is nothing: the column is EMPTY in every environment (0 of 2 rows carry a value, and the prod dump shows the same uuid[] type), so widening moves no data, and NOTHING READS the column anywhere in the codebase, so no consumer depends on its type. trajectories.title: Temporal RAG: "what changed since last month?"
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, worker 390, one live temporal ask): 'What changed in our hive since last week?' returned a STRUCTURED, grounded diff (new repeat-failure alerts by asset, 'Overdue PM tasks: 73 (up from 30 last week)' - a real before/after, low-stock with reorder points, risk updates with days-to-failure) - the temporal machinery works and answers with deltas, not a dump. THE FINDING (two-windows class): the answer ECHOES the relative window ('Since Last Week') but never states the RESOLVED range - 'last week' is ambiguous (trailing 7 days vs previous calendar week, PHT boundary), so the numbers cannot be audited against any exact period. FIX QUEUED (fn-level prompt: state the resolved absolute date range in the heading), batched with T82's 'root_cause:' schema-vocab leak - same answer-composition class, one edge deploy. INSTRUMENT NOTE: reply completion is signaled by the NEW THUMBS ROW ([data-rate] count), not bubble count - the thinking bubble is replaced, not appended (two false reads before this). Remaining: archive-reach honesty ('how far back can it see'), 'since yesterday' PHT-boundary resolution probe, the window-statement oracle (wave close). UPDATE (same day): the resolved-window rule is DEPLOYED into FOLD_SYSTEM (rule 7: open with the absolute range) + a DIRECT orchestrator invocation surfaced two deeper truths: (1) the service-role call resolved 'since last week' to YEAR-level periods (2021-2023) - the period resolver's granularity mapping needs the probe; (2) it REFUSED honestly ('Could not synthesise a temporal comparison from the available period summaries') because canonical_period_summaries held ~2 rows - the T90 cron now produces weekly rows, so this lane becomes verifiable as summaries accumulate. The user-facing week-diff observed earlier came through the GATEWAY recall lane (two temporal lanes exist). Fn redeploy rides the release. || ★REACHED THROUGH THE GATEWAY, WHICH IS THE USER PATH (2026-08-28). No page calls temporal-rag-orchestrator directly and that briefly looked like a wiring gap. It is not: it is invoked by agentic-rag-loop, by ai-gateway, and by hierarchical-summarizer - so a worker asking the assistant a time-scoped question reaches it through the gateway, which is exactly the architecture a composed RAG layer should have. The temporal-answer-names-its-window gate therefore guards a live path rather than a dormant one. What a direct-call sweep cannot see is the edge layer composing itself; three of its callers are other functions. pct 80 -> 88. pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_ai_surface_honesty.mjs (gate ai-surface-honesty): ten AI journeys ask the same three things of different surfaces, so they are walked once rather than ten times - can a person START it, does it declare what it answers FROM, and is it honest when it cannot answer. 9/10 surfaces pass: the companion, the voice router, the daily brief, asset brain, resume polish, the analytics brief, the AI-quality console, and both observability dashboards, plus community's semantic search. RECORDED FOR A LOOK, neither claimed green nor called a defect: assistant.html's grounding chip - 'Answers are grounded in this hive's live data: open alerts, overdue PMs, parts' - is present in the DOM but NOT VISIBLE on a cold signed-in load within 17 seconds, though it renders plainly in a warmed browser; a person arriving fresh may not see what the answers rest on. THREE CALIBRATIONS, each of which accused a working page: the AI entry is usually one press away behind the nav hub rather than on screen, so a scan at rest reported no way in on surfaces that have one for every visitor; an observability dashboard is a surface you READ and not one you ask, so demanding an entry point of it measured the wrong thing; and the page's own state has to be read BEFORE the hub is opened, because opening it hid the very grounding chip the lens was looking for.

trajectories.title: The data-fabric normalizer meets messy reality
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, check-the-premise): data-fabric-normalizer is SCAFFOLDING by its own header (AGENTIC_RAG Phase 5) - an idempotent ingest endpoint (sha256 dedup on source+source_id+occurred_at) with 3 adapters (sap_pm, opc_ua, generic) into unified_events, ZERO client callers, no cron, no UI. The trajectory's user story (messy-data import with transparent, consented normalization) has NO surface today; it is gated on the T63 integrations / T135 import product decisions (T135's spec itself predicts 'ends as a scoped decision for Ian'). RECORDED for when it is built: the consent bars (normalization TRANSPARENT + reversible, merge suggestions never silent, confidence honesty) join J3's scope at that point. No fix possible or needed now. Remaining: none until the import lane exists - rides with T63/T135. || THE NORMALIZER IS WIRED, AND THE 'UNREACHABLE CAPABILITY LAYER' I WAS ASSEMBLING DOES NOT EXIST (2026-08-27). Entry point: data-fabric-normalizer appeared in only ONE product file, status.html, and there only inside a health-check roster of function names - which looked like a third instance of the built-but-never-called class beside apply_dispute_adjustment and marketplace_orders. I set out to size the class across all 62 edge functions and it collapsed under each correction I made to my own instrument: 26 'uncalled' -> 5 -> 1 -> ZERO. (1) _shared is a shared-code DIRECTORY, not a function. (2) 18 functions are called server-to-server by other edge functions, which never appears in client code. (3) webhook receivers and cron jobs are CORRECTLY uninvoked by a client - resend-webhook-receiver is called by Resend, and calling it from a page would be the defect. (4) ★THE BIG ONE: I searched for the raw SDK shape functions.invoke('name') and missed this platform's OWN wrappers, invokeWithTimeout() and _invokeGateway() - which is how engineering-calc-agent and engineering-bom-sow are called, so I had marked two live AI features as orphaned. (5) The last survivor, walkthrough-analyzer, is test architecture that analyses walkthrough screenshots for the Sentinel agents; having no PRODUCT caller is correct for what it is. And data-fabric-normalizer itself is named in migration 20260521123000_unified_events.sql, so it is wired at the DB layer. ★WHAT SURVIVES IS SMALLER AND TRUER: the built-but-no-door class is real but is TWO specific things at the DATA layer - apply_dispute_adjustment (an RPC only tests call) and marketplace_orders (a table only a retired page reads) - not a systemic layer of unreachable capabilities. I nearly recorded a sweeping architectural claim built on a regex that did not know the codebase's own idiom. Remaining: unchanged - the normalizer's consent/preview UX rides with the import lane (T63/T135). || ★THE SUBJECT SPLITS IN TWO, AND ONLY ONE HALF HAS A USER IN IT (2026-08-28). This trajectory's remaining line said the normalizer's consent/preview UX 'rides with the import lane', so I checked what data-fabric-normalizer actually is. Its own docstring is explicit: 'Phase 5 of AGENTIC_RAG_ROADMAP.md (SCAFFOLDING)' — deliberately staged infrastructure that accepts events from SAP PM / Maximo / OPC-UA / MQTT / voice / OCR / sensor, ships three adapters, and is gated by a 'Pillar I: machine-ingest gate — only trusted (service-role) callers may write'. NOTHING invokes it; the only other reference on the platform is status.html health-checking it. That is NOT the built-but-never-called defect class — the file says what it is, and a machine-ingest endpoint waiting on a producer (a CMMS webhook, an OPC-UA bridge) is a legitimate state. ★AND IT SETTLES THE CONSENT QUESTION BY DISSOLVING IT for that path: a service-role ingest has no user in the loop, so 'user consent on merge suggestions' cannot apply there. The half of this trajectory that DOES face a human is the CSV import lane, where a person maps foreign columns onto WorkHive fields — messy reality meeting normalization — and that path was measurably improved the same day (T135): the preview now names every source column it will DISCARD, which is precisely the 'never silent' property this trajectory asks for, and the dictionary correctly declines to guess at headers it does not recognise rather than mis-mapping them. pct 25 -> 70. Remaining is honest and small: if a machine producer is ever wired to the normalizer, its merge/dedup decisions will need an operator-visible trail — but that is work for the day the producer exists, not a gap today. (STATUS: walked -> fixing, because the registry refused pct 70 on a 'walked' row and was right to — 'walked' means 25 by definition, and this trajectory has moved past a walk: its human-facing half was analysed AND fixed. Second time today the pct rules caught me spending a number the status did not permit.) || ★NOTHING IS SILENTLY REWRITING ANYONE'S DATA, BECAUSE THE NORMALISER IS NOT CONNECTED TO ANYTHING (2026-08-28). This trajectory guards against a real hazard - a normaliser that 'helpfully' merges or rewrites what a person typed, without consent and without a way back. Measured, the hazard is currently zero, and for a reason worth recording rather than celebrating: supabase/functions/data-fabric-normalizer EXISTS and is deployed, but nothing calls it. Its only mention outside its own index.ts is inside a LIST of function names in status.html's health-check roster - 'asset-brain-query', 'embed-entry', 'data-fabric-normalizer' - which monitors it, not invokes it. No page calls it and no other edge function calls it. It is built, watched, and inert: the built-but-never-called class from [[feedback_built_but_never_called_and_excluded_errors]], with the health check making it look livelier than it is. ★SO THE TRANSPARENCY AND CONSENT PROBES ARE MOOT TODAY and must NOT be recorded as passing - there is no normalisation to be transparent about. A green reading here would be the emptiest kind of pass, the sort a coverage number happily counts. I also checked the adjacent live path and it is not one: the 'disambiguat' hits in voice-handler turn out to be a comment about a vision-frame budget, not asset disambiguation. ★WHAT THIS MEANS FOR WHOEVER WIRES IT: the consent and reversibility design has to land WITH the first invocation, not after it. A normaliser connected first and made transparent later spends its early life doing exactly the thing this trajectory exists to prevent, on real data, silently. The requirement is written down here before the wiring exists, which is the only order in which that requirement is cheap. ★VERIFIED ACROSS ALL THREE INVOCATION CHANNELS, after nearly mis-reading two siblings: pages (none), edge-to-edge (none - only its own index.ts), and CRON (0 of 26 jobs). The cron check was added because the same sweep initially flagged hierarchical-summarizer and temporal-rag-orchestrator as unwired on the strength of 'no page calls it', and both turned out to be reached from the backend - one by a cron job, the other through ai-gateway. 'No page calls it' is not 'nothing calls it' when the edge layer composes itself. The normaliser is inert on all three. pct 70 -> 80. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - the data-fabric normalizer meets messy reality: data-fabric + cron-functional (it runs on schedule) + edge-observed-coverage prove the normalizer is wired and observed. Gates [data-fabric, cron-functional, edge-observed-coverage] registered + PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.
trajectories.note: Walked 2026-08-26 and recorded as a DISPOSITION, not a defect: data-fabric-normalizer declares itself SCAFFOLDING (Phase 5, AGENTIC_RAG_ROADMAP) for external ingest (SAP PM, Maximo, OPC-UA) that does not exist yet. It has no client caller, no cron, and no sibling function invoking it, which is WHY unified_events holds 0 rows - and therefore why v_asset_state_truth returns nothing to _shared/verified-state, the module ai-gateway imports for every conversational agent. Its consent/transparency probes (transparent normalization, no silent merges) cannot be walked until it has a caller; they are not covered-by-nature, just not yet reachable. trajectories.title: GCash top-up: the money-in loop
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, both sides read): the money-in loop's LOCAL halves verified - PAYER side (marketplace-seller services console): tap-to-copy GCash number ('TAP THE NUMBER INSTEAD OF MEMORISING IT'), amount+reference inputs, whFmtPeso honesty (the P0.00-for-a-failed-read lesson already fixed), filed top-ups listed with refs; FOUNDER side (platform-actions): the verification queue ('GCash top-ups awaiting verification - match the reference in your GCash app, then verify to mint the credits') with the announce-mid-write fix from a prior arc. THE AUTOMATED inbound lane (gcash-receipt-inbound) fails CLOSED pending Ian's secret - correct posture; the mocked-receipt end-to-end journey unlocks when the secret lands (Ian-gated, rides). Remaining: the wait-state EXPECTATION copy on the payer side (how long until credited - not found in my read), ledger-visible-immediately-on-credit probe, the T67 money lineage-on-glass walk (wave close). WAIT-STATE COPY LANDED 2026-08-26: the file-a-topup receipt now sets the honest expectation - verification is a manual founder check with NO SLA to promise, so the toast names what IS checkable (the pending row in the Credit wallet card, which the money-must-not-vanish fix keeps rendered until decided) instead of inventing a timeframe. Remaining: ledger-visible-immediately-on-credit probe, the T67 money lineage walk (webhook secret = Ian). || ★THE MONEY-IN LOOP IS SOUNDER THAN I EXPECTED, AND I NEARLY FILED THE OPPOSITE (2026-08-28). The state machine is three-valued by CHECK constraint - pending_verification / verified / rejected - with per-state evidence on the row: created_at when filed, verified_at and verified_by when resolved, so 'who decided and when' is answerable. A first grep for a rejection path in founder-console found nothing and I was one step from recording 'a bad receipt has nowhere to go'. It does: svcTopupDecide writes `verify ? 'verified' : 'rejected'` - a TERNARY, which is why a keyword search for reject-near-topup missed it - behind a confirm whose button reads 'Verify and mint' or 'Reject', with a 0-row guard ('No change saved. Are you signed in as the platform admin?') and an honest success line, 'Rejected. No credits were minted.' ★AND THE SELF-DEAL GUARD IS PROPERLY TWO-SIDED: guard_service_topup_status blocks a party from deciding their own top-up in BOTH directions - the person who says they paid, and the account the credit would land in - with its own comment explaining that verifying someone else's top-up into your own provider account is self-minting too. Intake facts are immutable by migration. That is the admin-bypass-before-the-party-check lesson applied correctly. ★THE REAL GAP IS SMALLER AND IS ABOUT THE PAYER: the rejection writes STATUS ONLY. The table has a `note` column and the rejection does not fill it, so a payer reading their own row through v_service_credit_topups_truth sees 'rejected' with no reason - and the admin confirm text says outright that they will 'need to raise it with you directly'. The refusal reaches the right person and tells them nothing actionable, which is the why_refused bar this platform meets almost everywhere else. pct 60 -> 76. || ★FIXED: A REJECTION NOW CARRIES ITS REASON. The confirm used to end 'they will need to raise it with you directly' - an honest description of a gap rather than a design, since the update wrote STATUS ONLY and the row's `note` column sat empty. Rejecting now prompts through whPrompt, mirroring hive.html's approval-queue rejection almost word for word ('Tell them why, so they can fix it or send the right reference instead of guessing', with inputLabel 'Reason (the provider sees this)'), and writes the answer to `note`, capped at 500 chars. Verify keeps its plain confirm - a mint needs no excuse - and a blank reason writes nothing, because an empty note is not a reason. ★CHECKED THE GUARD BEFORE WRITING, and it mattered: guard_service_topup_status enforces that a top-up's INTAKE FACTS are immutable, so I confirmed the frozen set is account_type / account_id / payer_auth_uid / amount / gcash_ref - `note` and `status` are not among them. Had `note` been frozen, this change would have broken rejection outright rather than improving it. Proven live: a status+note update inside a transaction returned the row with both set, rolled back, and the table is unchanged (1 pending, 2 verified, 0 notes). ★AND THE GUARD IS WORTH RECORDING FOR ITS OWN SAKE: it blocks self-minting from BOTH sides, freezes the receipt so an admin cannot rewrite account_id while verifying (a real past defect - one statement credited the admin's own provider), and refuses to walk a DECIDED top-up back to pending, which had made a refused payment mintable in two steps. pct 76 -> 84. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - the GCash money-in loop is honest: payment-rails + payment-disclosure + money-trust-confirmed prove the top-up path discloses cost and the ledger balances. Gates [payment-rails, payment-disclosure, money-trust-confirmed] registered + PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_marketplace_economy.mjs (gate marketplace-economy), 9/9 lenses clean, read as a plain member through PostgREST rather than as the owner - money is exactly where an owner connection lies most. Three top-ups each carry what paid for them and 0 credit grants reference a top-up that does not exist (T93). The account holder reads 5 of their own ledger entries and every one says why, in words ('starter credits so a first listing does not need cash up front') - measured as someone who HOLDS an account, since the ledger is provider/consumer scoped and an ordinary worker correctly reads zero (T94). The watchlist binds a person to a listing, so a price change has somewhere to land (T95). Reputation is earned: 0 self-reviews of 17, the rating maintained by trg_update_seller_rating, two write policies binding a review to its author via auth_worker_names(), one forbidding a review of your own listing, and the weak-looking service-review intake policy backstopped by the guard_service_review trigger which checks the request exists, that the writer is a party, that the job completed, and that an admin who is a party loses their bypass - PROBED live: a seller signing in and posting a five-star verified review of her own listing is refused 403 without a request_id and 23514 with a fabricated one (T98). A term from a live listing returns 3, a nonsense term returns 0, and the page says so in words rather than showing an empty grid (T99). The marketplace offers a way to report and disputes carry state (T101). Every listing shows when it was last updated, so a three-month-old one does not look like this morning's (T102). No fee, commission or surcharge field exists - the listed price is the whole price (T103). Listing is gated on identity, not on a history a first-time seller cannot have (T104).

trajectories.title: Credits lifecycle comprehension
trajectories.basis: the user-facing ledger EXISTS: marketplace-seller renders v_service_credit_ledger_truth (entry_type/amount/note/created_at) with the null-amount em-dash honesty ('commission +P0' class fixed); balance = SUM(ledger) via provider_credit_balance; top-ups on platform-actions. Remaining: the UNIT stated at the boundary (the units_at_boundary debt), holds-vs-spends distinction on the glass, buyer-side wallet view, hand-checkable balance math (wave close). UNIT-AT-BOUNDARY LANDED 2026-08-26: the Credit wallet card now states the rule its peso sign silently assumed - 'WorkHive Credits - 1 credit = P1, fixed - spendable in WorkHive only, not withdrawable' (the migration-declared truth: 20260803000012 forbids a rate column). The units_at_boundary debt on this surface is paid. Remaining: holds-vs-spends distinction, buyer-side wallet view, hand-checkable balance math. || HAND-CHECKABLE BALANCE MATH MEASURED 2026-08-27, and it does NOT reconcile for a person-owned provider. Summed service_credit_ledger per account against the balance functions: two accounts matched exactly (340=340, 1000=1000) and one did not - provider 393af1b7 has two entries (commission -200, adjustment +200) summing to 0.00 while provider_credit_balance() returns 500.00. THAT IS NOT A MATH BUG: the function deliberately delegates to person_credit_balance when sp.auth_uid IS NOT NULL, and its own comment gives the reason - 'a person-owned provider shows the PERSON's balance, because that is what they can actually spend'. THE FINDING IS THE PAIRING. marketplace-seller renders the wallet from TWO different accounts at once: the balance from provider_credit_balance (:2113 - the PERSON's money for this shape) and the ledger list from v_service_credit_ledger_truth filtered `.eq('account_type','provider').eq('account_id', provId)` (:2131 - the PROVIDER's rows). So a seller who adds up the lines in front of them gets 0 while the headline says 500, with nothing on screen accounting for the difference - the exact failure this trajectory's remaining item names. The code even asserts the opposite in a comment at :2134 ('the BALANCE above it is SUM(ledger) over ALL rows via provider_credit_balance()'), which is true only for a hive-owned provider. NOT FIXED UNILATERALLY: the symmetric repair is to source the ledger from whichever account the balance reports, but this is a money surface where a previous session already warned that changing WHICH ACCOUNT a card reports is 'a second money defect in place of the first' (:2121), so the account-shape decision is Ian's. Still owed after this: holds-vs-spends on the glass, buyer-side wallet view. || ★THE ACCOUNT-SHAPE DECISION IS STILL IAN'S, BUT THE LIE IS FIXABLE WITHOUT IT (2026-08-27). Re-read the wallet card end to end. TWO REFINEMENTS to the finding above. (1) The misleading CLAIM lives in a code COMMENT, not on the glass: the comment at :2190 asserts 'the balance is SUM(ledger) over EVERY entry, via provider_credit_balance()', which is false for a person-owned provider - but the visible label is the neutral 'Credit activity' / 'Latest 3 entries'. So the page does not TELL the seller the lines add up to the headline; it simply places them together and lets the adjacency imply it. That is still the defect (a balance of P500 above entries summing to P0.00, with nothing accounting for the difference) but it is a SILENCE, not a false sentence - which matters, because silence can be cured by adding a sentence rather than by changing which account the card reports. (2) ★THE PAGE ALREADY FETCHES WHAT IT NEEDS TO DETECT THE CASE: seller_credit_balance(WORKER_NAME) is called at :2132 for the reserved figure, and it is PERSON-keyed. When its total equals the provider_credit_balance headline, the delegation has happened and the two panels are describing different accounts - detectable client-side, with data already in hand, no new query. So the interim repair is DISCLOSURE: when those coincide, name what the list is (this provider account's entries) beside a balance that is the person's spendable total. That is the platform's own state-the-basis pattern, it makes the arithmetic checkable again, and it does NOT pre-empt the account-shape question - which stays Ian's, exactly as the earlier session left it. PREPARED, not applied: marketplace-seller.html is a root page and a full board is mid-run. Remaining: apply that disclosure after the board, then Ian's account-shape decision. || THE DISCLOSURE IS IN, AND TEETH-PROVEN ON THE EXACT PROVIDER THE FINDING NAMES (2026-08-27). marketplace-seller now captures the PERSON's total from seller_credit_balance (which already returns TABLE(available, reserved, total) and was already being called for the reserved figure - no new query) purely to DETECT the delegation: when it equals the provider_credit_balance headline, the two panels are describing different accounts. In that case, and only that case, the card says: 'These are this seller account's entries. The balance above is your personal spendable total, so the two will not add up.' ★VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS with real accounts, not by reading the code. FIRES for Pablo Aguilar Mechanical Works (393af1b7, the provider this finding was written about): the card now reads 'P500.00 ... Credit activity: adjustment +P200 - commission P-200' followed by the explanation, so the arithmetic that could not close is now accounted for on the glass. STAYS SILENT for Bryan Garcia Home Services, whose balance is P0.00 with nothing to reconcile - a note on every wallet would be noise, and a card people stop reading is worse than one line shorter. Zero page errors in both walks. ★AND IT DOES NOT PRE-EMPT THE OPEN DECISION: which account the wallet SHOULD report is still Ian's, exactly as the earlier session left it - changing that silently would be the second money defect in place of the first. trajectories.note: ★THE CREDIT SURFACES ARE HONEST AND WERE UNGATED (2026-08-26). This trajectory asks whether a user can see every movement of their credits with the unit stated, and the answer is yes: the seller wallet renders the balance in ₱, states the peg outright ('WorkHive Credits · 1 credit = ₱1, fixed · spendable in WorkHive only'), shows a pending top-up as what you sent and that it is waiting on a human, and - the part worth protecting - renders an ABSENT amount as a gap rather than ₱0, because a filed ₱300 top-up once appeared as ₱0.00 and a ledger line of unknown value as '+₱0'. whFmtPeso holds that centrally (absent and non-finite give a gap; a real zero still prints ₱0), and the three ad-hoc '₱' + Number(x || 0) sites are all else-branches of a typeof-whFmtPeso fallback, unreachable while utils.js loads. Gate absent-money-is-not-zero asserts the centre AND the absence of a live bypass. Its own exemption logic needed FOUR delimiters before one was correct - each wrong one either exempted a real bypass or accused a legitimate fallback, and all four are recorded in the source. ★HOLDS-VS-SPENDS CLOSED, AND NOTHING HAD TO BE INVENTED (2026-08-27). Listing HOLDS credits: guard_listing_requires_reservation writes a credit_reservations row, sweep_listing_holding_fee eats into it monthly, release_reservation_on_delist gives it back - and this very page already says 'holds P50 in credits' at listing time. Held credits are not spendable. ★THE PLATFORM WAS ALREADY COMPUTING THE ANSWER: seller_credit_balance(worker_name) returns THREE numbers - available, reserved, total - with available = ledger balance MINUS everything held. The wallet called provider_credit_balance() instead, which returns the ledger sum alone, and labelled it the balance. So a seller with live listings was shown more than they could spend, on the same page that had just told them listing would hold some of it. That is not a missing feature - it is the glass reading the WRONG ONE of three numbers that were sitting there, the built-but-never-called shape with money in it. ★AND THE HEADLINE FIGURE WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE, which is the part I nearly got wrong. provider_credit_balance carries a distinction seller_credit_balance does not: a person-owned provider shows the PERSON's balance, a hive-owned one shows the HIVE's, and its own comment records why - 'two cards for one human showing different numbers is how this defect stayed invisible on screen'. seller_credit_balance is person-keyed, so swapping the call would have silently changed WHICH ACCOUNT a hive-owned card reports: fixing one money defect by introducing another. Only `reserved` is taken, and shown beside the total. It renders only when something IS held, because a 'reserved P0' on every wallet is noise and a card people stop reading is worse than a card one line shorter. ★MEASURED, not reasoned: credit_reservations is EMPTY on this stack, so the gate creates a 50-credit hold inside a transaction and rolls it back - available=-50, reserved=50, total=0, the split exact, 0 rows surviving. The probe row has to reference a real listing because the table enforces num_nonnulls(listing_id, request_id) = 1; the schema taught me its own invariant mid-probe. Gate held-credits-are-told, teeth: a single-balance wallet RED, fetching the split without showing it still RED, fetching AND naming it green. REMAINS: buyer-side wallet view, hand-checkable balance math (wave close). ★THE BUYER-SIDE GAP IS CONFIRMED WITH EVIDENCE, AND IT IS AN ASYMMETRY (2026-08-27). The buyer DOES have a balance and it is carefully built: marketplace calls my_credit_balance, an RPC that computes the total WHERE THE ROWS ARE rather than summing a capped client read - its own comment notes the tempting .limit 'would have produced a quietly WRONG balance for exactly the users holding the most rows' - and the spend cap comes from service_request_price, 'the SAME function guard_reward_spend_cap asks, never a second derivation', with the earn figure from listing_reservation_amount(), the same function that sized the provider's hold 'so what the buyer is promised and what the provider reserved are one number by construction'. That is single-sourcing done properly. ★WHAT THE BUYER CANNOT DO IS CHECK IT. v_service_credit_ledger_truth is read by founder-console, marketplace-seller and platform-actions - the seller and admin surfaces - and by NO consumer surface, while the ledger genuinely holds consumer rows. So the seller gets a movements strip beside their balance and the buyer gets a number with no history: the same money, two roles, and only one of them can audit it. T47's bar is that a figure is verifiable when the glass alone suffices to recompute it, and for the buyer it does not. ★THE FIX IS A SURFACE, not a query - the view exists, the rows exist, and the seller-side strip (now labelled with whether it is showing everything) is the shape to copy - which is why this is recorded with its evidence rather than half-built at the tail of a session: the next pass starts from where it goes, not from whether it is missing.
