trajectories.title: Order/inquiry lifecycle: buyer and seller converge
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, two contexts: bryan buyer 390 + davidvelasco seller 390): the INQUIRY HOP proven end-to-end - the ?listing= deep link opens the detail sheet cold, the inquiry form's guards are honest ('All fields are required.' + the anti-spoof 'Send this under your WorkHive name' identity check), the buyer gets a receipt WITH the expectation set ('Inquiry sent! Seller responds within 48 hours'), and the seller's inbox shows the same object (buyer name, 'Re: <listing>', message, volunteered contact, Send Reply / Mark Replied / Close controls) - DB row 'pending' naming both parties; probe row cleaned. The CONTACT-EXCHANGE boundary is by-design explicit (the buyer volunteers contact in a labeled field at inquiry time). INSTRUMENT NOTE: the first run under-filled the form and the honest refusal toast expired before the read - a probe must fill every required field before accusing the pipeline. Remaining: the REPLY hop back to the buyer (where does the buyer read replies?), the goods lifecycle states beyond inquiry (agreement/handover/confirm two-sided), non-response timeout honesty (wave close). THE REPLY HOP BUILT 2026-08-26 - a real SILENT-WORK defect closed: sellers answer into marketplace_inquiries.reply_text/replied_at (their console writes it; mkt_inq_read lets the BUYER read their own rows) but NO buyer surface ever read those columns - an answered inquiry looked identical to an ignored one, so the seller believed they replied while the buyer saw nothing. FIXED: marketplace now renders 'Replies to your inquiries' (truth-view read, bounded 10 newest with a total order, silence-is-golden when empty, deep link back to the listing). Live-proven as the buyer on a staged replied inquiry, probe row cleaned. Remaining: goods lifecycle states beyond inquiry (agreement/handover/confirm two-sided), non-response timeout honesty. || THE GOODS LIFECYCLE IS FULLY DEFINED IN THE SCHEMA AND HAS NEVER BEEN EXERCISED (2026-08-27). marketplace_orders carries a CHECK constraint enumerating six states - pending_payment, escrow_hold, buyer_confirmed, released, refunded, disputed - which is a genuine escrow flow with both a happy path (pay -> hold -> buyer confirms -> funds released) and its two exits (refund, dispute), and it answers T96's 'do both sides see the same states' question at the schema level: there is ONE status column, so buyer and seller cannot be looking at different vocabularies for the same order. ★BUT THERE ARE ZERO ORDERS, AND NOTHING CAN MAKE ONE: marketplace_orders appears in exactly one place in the seeder tree - reset.py's TRUNCATE list - so the fixture layer knows how to DELETE orders and has never known how to create one. The lifecycle is therefore unproven end to end: no state transition on this table has ever been walked, and 'the constraint allows it' is not 'the product does it'. This is the build-the-structure case rather than a ceiling - the move is to write the order fixture (a seeded order per state, then a two-context walk asserting buyer and seller read the same state at each step, plus the non-response timeout). SEQUENCED, NOT DEFERRED: writing rows into a table while a full board is mid-run is the data twin of mutating schema under a running gate, and this session has already voided one board that way, so the fixture lands once the board clears. Remaining: build that order fixture, then the two-sided state-agreement walk and non-response timeout honesty. || THE FIXTURE IS BUILT, WIRED AND RUN - THE GOODS LIFECYCLE IS WALKABLE FOR THE FIRST TIME (2026-08-27). Rather than write a new one-off script, extended the EXISTING test-data-seeder/seeders/marketplace.py with seed_marketplace_orders(client, log, ctx) in the same shape as its siblings, and wired it into orchestrator.py right after seed_marketplace_sellers - a seeder nothing calls would have been the same built-but-never-called trap this session found in apply_dispute_adjustment. RUN FOR REAL against the local stack: 6 rows, one per state, verified in psql - pending_payment, escrow_hold, buyer_confirmed, released, refunded, disputed, with real buyers, sellers and prices taken from seeded listings. ★THE ROWS ARE INTERNALLY CONSISTENT, WHICH IS THE PART A FIXTURE USUALLY GETS WRONG: a released order carries BOTH buyer_confirmed_at and released_at; buyer_confirmed carries only the first; pending, escrow and disputed carry neither; refunded carries a confirmation because it was confirmed before it was refunded. A fixture that contradicts its own schema teaches a walker the wrong thing about the product, and every later assertion inherits the lie. ★AND ONE PER STATE RATHER THAN A RANDOM SPREAD, deliberately: the two-sided walk needs to FIND a buyer_confirmed order to look at, not hope one was rolled. Remaining: the two-sided state-agreement walk itself (buyer and seller reading the same state at each step) and non-response timeout honesty - both now unblocked. || ★I SEEDED THE WRONG TABLE FIRST, AND FINDING OUT WHY IS THE REAL RESULT (2026-08-27). marketplace_orders looked like the goods lifecycle - a full escrow flow in a CHECK constraint - so I built its fixture. Then I checked who READS it: exactly one page, marketplace-admin, which is RETIRED behind an overlay. The live goods path is contact-only, stated plainly in the seeder's own docstring ('contact-only flow per current launch plan'): a buyer sends an INQUIRY against a listing, the seller replies, contact details are exchanged and the deal completes off platform. marketplace-seller reads v_marketplace_inquiries_truth in SIX places and never reads orders at all. So marketplace_orders is a FUTURE escrow model, not a gap - and 'the schema describes it' was never evidence that the product does it. The orders fixture is kept (the table is now walkable if that model is ever switched on, and its rows are state-consistent) but it is NOT the current flow. ★THEN BUILT THE ONE THAT MATTERS: seed_marketplace_inquiries, six rows across pending / replied / closed, wired into the orchestrator beside its sibling. Replied and closed rows carry BOTH reply_text and replied_at, since a reply with no timestamp is a state the UI cannot render honestly. ★WALKED IT LIVE as a seller and the two-sided view works: the Inquiries tab names the buyer, shows the message and the state, and the 'New Inquiries' tile reads 0 for Bryan Garcia - which is CORRECT, because his two inquiries are replied and closed, not pending. A count that could have looked like a bug is the page being precise about what 'new' means. Zero page errors. Remaining: the buyer-side view of the same thread (does the asker see the reply), and non-response timeout honesty. || ★THE BUYER CANNOT SEE THEIR OWN UNANSWERED QUESTION - PROVEN WITH TWO ACCOUNTS (2026-08-27). The buyer lane exists: marketplace.html's loadMyInquiryReplies() reads v_marketplace_inquiries_truth filtered .eq('buyer_name', WORKER_NAME) into #mk-my-replies. But it also filters .not('reply_text','is',null) - it renders ONLY inquiries a seller has already answered - and returns early when that comes back empty. MEASURED with two real signed-in buyers against the seeded threads: Romeo Beltran, whose inquiry was REPLIED, sees his thread and the counterparty; Pablo Aguilar, whose inquiry is PENDING, sees NOTHING - no message, no state, no acknowledgement that he ever asked. Same page, same code, opposite experience, decided entirely by whether the other party has gotten round to it. ★THAT IS WORSE THAN A TIMEOUT PROBLEM, which is how this trajectory's remaining item framed it. A late reply is a wait; an invisible SENT MESSAGE is indistinguishable from one that never sent - the buyer cannot tell whether to follow up, re-ask on another listing, or give up, and the platform holds the answer the whole time. It is the same shape as this session's other findings where a SILENCE does the lying: the record exists, the reader is simply not shown it. ★THE FIX IS SMALL AND THE SECTION'S NAME IS THE ONLY REAL QUESTION: dropping the reply_text filter and rendering a state ('Waiting for a reply - sent 3 days ago') would show the whole thread, but #mk-my-replies is literally 'my replies', so including unanswered asks changes what that section IS. Recorded rather than redesigned unilaterally: the evidence is unambiguous, the shape of the fix is known, and what the section should be called is Ian's call. Remaining: that decision, then the pending-state render. || FIXED AND PROVEN ON BOTH SIDES (2026-08-27). Dropped the .not('reply_text','is',null) filter so the buyer's panel carries EVERY inquiry they sent, re-ordered by created_at (the newest ask leads whether or not it has been answered - replied_at is NULL for pending and does not sort usefully), renamed the heading from 'Replies to your inquiries' to 'Your inquiries', and gave the unanswered rows their own line: 'Sent to <seller> <date> - waiting for a reply'. The date is not decoration; the buyer's actual question is HOW LONG it has been, and 'waiting' with no date is the same silence one step quieter. VERIFIED with the two accounts that produced the finding: Pablo Aguilar, who saw NOTHING before, now reads 'YOUR INQUIRIES - 1 | You asked: What's the hour meter reading... | Sent to Leandro Marquez Aug 19, 2026 - waiting for a reply'; Romeo Beltran's replied thread renders exactly as before. Zero page errors on either. ★AND THE 'NAMING DECISION' I NEARLY DEFERRED ON WAS NOT A FORK. I recorded this as needing Ian because including unanswered asks changes what the section IS - but mk-my-replies is an internal id, the only user-visible string was one heading, and 'Your inquiries' is strictly more accurate than 'Replies to your inquiries' for a panel that now shows both. A label is not a product decision when the alternative is a buyer who cannot see their own sent message. That is the manufactured-fork shape: naming something Ian's to make deferring it feel principled. Remaining: nothing owed on the two-sided goods flow beyond the wave-close re-earn. || LOCKED as 'your-own-message-is-visible', holding four clauses - unfiltered read, rendered pending state, a sent DATE, and the buyer_name scope (a panel showing OTHER buyers' inquiries would pass the first three and be a privacy defect, so the gate that protects visibility also has to protect the boundary). Selftest 6/6 including the exact pre-fix filter as a resurrection case. ★THE GATE'S OWN FIRST RUN FAILED ON THE FIXED FILE: it matched the T96 fix COMMENT, which quotes .not('reply_text','is',null) verbatim while explaining why it was removed. A detector that reads comments will always convict the best-documented fix, because the clearest fixes are the ones that quote what they took out - the fourth time this session that prose about code was mistaken for code. It now strips comments before auditing, like selection-is-exposed. || ★LOCKED 2026-08-31 (post_board_close): every named gate read PASS on the fresh FULL board 2026-08-31T16:45. pct 96 -> 100.

trajectories.title: Dispute resolution end-to-end
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, entry-map code walk with prior-arc receipts): all three parties' doors EXIST and are honest - BUYER: 'Report a problem' on the completed-job card with the objection WINDOW stated in words ('confirm payment, or report a problem by <date> (N days left). After that it settles automatically') + whPrompt reason capture + credits returned on dispute (mig 29) - 'the buyer's stop button. Without it the window is one-sided'; PROVIDER: disputed jobs hold their OWN bucket ('The client reported a problem') after the 2026-08-04 vanish-bug fix (a disputed job used to disappear from the console entirely); ADMIN: apply_dispute_adjustment + the fused founder-console lane (T69). Remaining: the LIVE three-party walk (hail->accept->complete->dispute->adjudicate->both-see-outcome - needs the full T35 service-lifecycle fixture, the wave-close two-context harness), evidence attachment probe, appeal/finality statement (wave close). || ★THE DISPUTE SYSTEM HAS AN ADJUDICATION HALF AND NO FRONT DOOR (2026-08-28). This trajectory opens on 'dispute entry findability from the transaction'. There is no entry. Traced every reference to marketplace_disputes: the ONLY client code that touches it is marketplace-admin.html - one READ for the moderation queue and one UPDATE for the verdict. No page inserts a dispute. Not marketplace (the buyer's surface), not marketplace-seller, not any edge function. ★EVERYTHING ELSE IS BUILT, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH RECORDING PRECISELY RATHER THAN AS 'disputes are missing': the table exists; RLS carries a real INSERT policy (mkt_disp_insert), so the database is already willing to accept a filing from a party; the admin console has a queue with an honest empty state ('All clear, no open disputes at this time'); the settlement mechanism exists as apply_dispute_adjustment; and hive.html even defines open_dispute as an AUDIT ACTION with an icon and a Filipino label, so the system anticipates the event it cannot receive. The platform is ready to resolve disputes nobody can raise. ★THAT IS THE 'a queue with no producer' CLASS, and the empty state makes it invisible: 0 disputes reads as 'no problems' rather than 'no way to report one', which is the same shape as a trust signal with no living producer. The remaining build is smaller than it looks - an intake form and a party-facing case view, onto machinery that already exists - but it is a build and a product decision (who may file, against what, within what window), so it goes to Ian. pct 60 -> 70. || ★I TRIED TO GENERALISE THIS INTO A SWEEP AND THE SWEEP WAS NOT TRUSTWORTHY, so it is recorded as an instrument note rather than banked. Asked the catalog for every table carrying an RLS INSERT policy with no app-side insert: 32 of 63. Spot-checked four before believing any of it, and two were plainly false - hive_members is written constantly (via .upsert, which my pattern did not look for) and alert_dismissals is written by every alert dismissal (through a chain longer than my 120-character window). A 50% false-positive rate on the cases I could verify by memory means the other 30 are unreadable, and 32 accusations would have been mostly slander. ★THE DISPUTE FINDING ABOVE DID NOT COME FROM THAT SWEEP - it came from tracing every single reference to one table and reading what each one DID, which is slower and is why it is reliable. A pattern that scales the question does not scale the answer. || ★THE THREE-ROLE LANE EXISTS AND IS PROPORTIONED SENSIBLY - but it has never been walked (2026-08-28). The machinery is real: a marketplace_disputes table, an apply_dispute_adjustment function for the credit consequence, and UI on all three surfaces the lifecycle needs - marketplace (4 references, where a buyer raises it), marketplace-seller (16, where the seller responds), and marketplace-admin (48, where it is adjudicated). That distribution is itself a good sign: adjudication carries by far the most surface, which is right, because the party deciding needs evidence, both accounts and the adjustment control, while the party raising needs one honest door. ★WHAT IS NOT PROVEN: marketplace_disputes holds ZERO rows, so nothing about the flow has been exercised end to end - not the both-parties-see-the-same-state property this trajectory turns on, not the adjudication's credit effect, not whether either party learns the outcome. Existence of the surfaces is not evidence that the three views agree during a live case, and the three-context harness (T24's shape, reused for buyer/seller/admin) is what would settle it. supabase/functions/{agentic-rag-loop,visual-defect-capture} (delimiters + error surfaced)

trajectories.note: ★A COMMA IN THE SEARCH BOX RETURNED HTTP 400 (2026-08-26, measured live). PostgREST splits or=(a,b) on top-level commas, so an unquoted comma inside a value rejected the whole filter - and 'Bearing, spherical roller, 22320 E1 XL C3, SKF' is simply how a part is named, the platform's own example elsewhere. Four sites escaped the LIKE wildcards % and _ and left the DELIMITERS alone: the logbook feed, the logbook EXPORT, community's feed and the global search overlay. marketplace was the exception - it strips them - which is why the same phrase worked there and nowhere else. The page renders the 400 as a failed READ, so a legitimate search looked like an outage. Fixed centrally with utils.whSafeSearchTerm (delimiters removed, wildcards escaped) at all four sites; verified end to end, the same read now returns 200 with an empty array. Gate search-term-survives-punctuation, teeth proven on both clauses. ★AND THE AI'S OWN RETRIEVAL HAD IT, SILENTLY (2026-08-26). agentic-rag-loop's logbook lane sanitised the user's natural-language QUESTION for LIKE wildcards but not for the PostgREST or() delimiters - and commas in a question are the common case, not an edge case. Worse, it read the result as `const { data: logs } = await q`, discarding the error; supabase-js RETURNS {data:null,error} instead of throwing, so the 400 never reached the catch and became an ordinary empty result. The AI simply answered with less grounding and nothing said why. visual-defect-capture passed an asset TAG into an .or() with no escaping at all. Both fixed (delimiters stripped, wildcards escaped, the error logged rather than discarded) and covered by search-term-survives-punctuation, which now also fails the `const { data } = await q` shape that makes such a failure invisible. NOTE the sanitiser's comment cited the data-engineer skill: the author followed it correctly and the SKILL was incomplete - it covered wildcards, not delimiters. NEEDS A DEPLOY (Ian's gate): both are edge functions. ★PART-NUMBER FORMAT VARIANTS, MEASURED (2026-08-27): the search is exact about spacing and punctuation, and a buyer who types the number the way it is PRINTED ON THE BOX finds nothing. Driven against the real catalogue with the same ILIKE the page uses: '6313 C3' -> 3 hits, '6313C3' -> 0, '6313-C3' -> 0; 'ACS580' -> 1, 'ACS-580' -> 0, 'acs 580' -> 0; 'GA75' -> 3, 'GA-75' -> 0. Every variant a person would plausibly type is a dead end. ★AND A ZERO-RESULT SEARCH IS THE WORST FALSE NEGATIVE A MARKETPLACE CAN PRODUCE, because it does not read as 'your spelling missed' - it reads as 'they do not have it', and the buyer leaves. The listing exists, the seller waits, and neither side ever learns why. ★THE FIX IS NOT CLIENT-SIDE, which is why this is recorded rather than shipped at the tail of a long turn: the client builds a PostgREST .or() filter, and PostgREST cannot apply an expression like regexp_replace(title,'[^a-z0-9]','') in a filter. Matching a normalised term needs DB-side support - a generated normalised column with an index (cheapest, keeps ILIKE), or a search RPC. That is a schema change with an index decision behind it, so it is Ian's call rather than a quiet addition. The measurement above is the evidence for making it: this is not a hypothetical tolerance nicety, it is eight typed strings of which five return nothing against listings that are sitting there.

trajectories.title: Listing quality & the AI assist
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, davidvelasco 390, one live assist invocation): the AI assist VERIFIED-GOOD - it names its own inputs ('drafts a category and description from your title, part number, and photo'), and from the bare title 'bearing 6205 skf new' produced a BOUNDED 173-char description with zero invented specs (no fabricated dimensions/load ratings/brands - everything derivable from the title; the T84 invention-guard bar holds on this sample), with an AI-drafted/review marker present (AI6). The composer carries the 10%-hold cost truth (T34) and a character counter (T130). THE GAP recorded: NO preview-as-buyer affordance exists on the composer (the J3 preview bar + the spec's draft-preview==published-render parity check) - a scoped enhancement. Remaining: photo-grounded assist probe (does a photo change the draft honestly), quality feedback ('what's missing for a GOOD listing'), the preview decision, photo ergonomics at 390 (T9's bar) (wave close).  || THE RECORDED GAP IS CLOSED 2026-08-26: the composer now has a PREVIEW AS BUYER control. Posting is a commitment - it spends a credit hold, it goes to moderation, and it is the first thing a stranger judges the seller by - so J3's preview-before-irreversible bar applies. The preview reads the SAME inputs the insert reads, so it cannot show a seller one thing and publish another, and it renders in the BUYER's vocabulary: a blank price reads 'Negotiable' and a filled one goes through whFmtPeso, which is how a buyer actually sees money. It says plainly that nothing has been posted, because a preview that looks like a confirmation is worse than none. ★THE FIX FAILED TWICE, SILENTLY, AND BOTH FAILURES LOADED WITH ZERO CONSOLE ERRORS. First: the handler called getElementById at script-parse time and returned early because the composer was not in the DOM yet - the button rendered perfectly and did nothing, the declared-but-never-wired class. Second: rewritten as a delegated listener, it was inserted INSIDE the submit handler's function body, so it only registered once a seller pressed Post - the one moment a preview is useless. A live CLICK found both; a source check or a page-load error check would have been green through each. That is why the gate clicks rather than greps. LOCKED BY gate listing-preview (4 behavioural assertions), resurrection RED both ways - with no control at all, and with the listener deliberately un-wired. Remaining: photo ergonomics at 390 (the T9 photo bar) and the draft-quality feedback the spec asks for. || THE INVENTION GUARD IS REAL, AND IT IS TWO DIFFERENT KINDS OF GUARD (2026-08-27). The listing assist's risk is a model that writes confident specifications a photo cannot support - '5,000 hours', 'fits Grundfos CR 95-3', 'CE certified' - which on a used-parts marketplace is not a bad sentence but a false claim a buyer may act on. TWO LAYERS, and the distinction matters. INSTRUCTIONAL for prose: the system prompt says 'NEVER invent specifications, dimensions, model compatibility, running hours, warranty, or certifications', which is the only kind of guard a free-text description can have. STRUCTURAL for enumerations: the category, urgency and mode the model returns are validated server-side AFTER the call - cats.includes(String(out.category)) ? ... : null - so an off-list value does not become a warning or a best guess, it becomes null. The model cannot widen the taxonomy no matter what it emits. ★THAT SPLIT IS THE RIGHT ARCHITECTURE rather than an inconsistency: you can whitelist an enum and you cannot whitelist a sentence, so the enum gets enforcement and the prose gets instruction plus human review before publish. Worth stating explicitly because 'the AI is guarded' otherwise reads as one uniform claim, when half of it is a promise and half of it is a mechanism. Remaining: photo ergonomics at 390 (the T9 photo bar) and the draft-quality feedback the spec asks for. || ★THE ONE GAP THIS TRAJECTORY FOUND IS CLOSED AND GATED LIVE (2026-08-28). The walk had already cleared the AI half - the listing assist names its own inputs and invented no specs from a bare title, which is the invention guard T84 asks of every AI-drafting surface. The single recorded gap was that a seller could not see their listing AS A BUYER WILL before publishing, and publishing is not a soft action here: it spends a credit hold and puts the listing in front of other plants. validate_listing_preview now passes live on six assertions - opens, showsTheDraft, blankPriceIsNegotiable, pricedViaHelper, closes, and zero page errors - with the verdict 'a seller can see the listing as a buyer will, before it becomes a commitment.' ★TWO OF THOSE ASSERTIONS ARE THE INTERESTING ONES. blankPriceIsNegotiable means a seller who leaves the price empty sees 'Negotiable' in the preview rather than ₱0 - the absent-is-not-zero discipline (T133) carried into the one screen where a wrong zero would be read by a BUYER as an offer. And pricedViaHelper means the preview renders money through whFmtPeso rather than its own formatter, so the preview cannot drift from what the marketplace will actually show. A preview that formats differently from the real thing is worse than no preview, because it is confidently wrong at the moment of commitment. pct 72 -> 90. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED (fix+gate) - all assigned gates PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] pct -> 100. No page cancels a paste event, and 14 pages tell the browser what their fields are with 11 opting a field out deliberately - so a person copying a part number out of a PDF is not retyping it, and autofill is not guessing a bin location (T123). trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, commit-point read sweep): every economic commit point STATES its cost at the moment of commitment, in ONE vocabulary - listing publish ('No fees are charged on sales... No fix needed at this bar. Remaining: the consolidated fees-summary surface decision (scoped - none exists), the fee-parity oracle (stated <-> charged, psql-checked), price-change notice policy, the standing admin-price decision (T67, Ian) (wave close). The gate checks the literal is still on the page AND every rate the DB could charge equals it (union of default + all hive overrides; one divergent hive fails, no averaging). TEETH-PROVEN: a 7.00 override turned it RED, revert green. Today's state: 10% stated == 10.00% charged. Remaining: the consolidated fees-summary surface (scoped - none exists), price-change notice policy, the standing admin-price decision (Ian). || THE HOLD IS CONFIGURABLE, THE COPY IS NOT, AND ONE KNOB IS DEAD (2026-08-27). Traced the listing hold end to end. ENFORCEMENT IS HIVE-AWARE and correct: guard_listing_requires_reservation calls listing_reservation_amount(hive_id, price), which computes the hold from service_knob_pct(hive, 'reward_pct') with a floor. So a hive CAN change what publishing costs. ★BUT THE RATE IS HARDCODED IN EVERY PLACE A PERSON READS IT: marketplace-seller states '10%' in four separate strings ('Publishing holds 10% of the price in credits. It is not a fee: it comes back in full...'), and the guard's own exception message hardcodes '(10%% of the price)'. Set a hive's reward_pct to 15 and the platform would hold 15% while both the UI and the refusal that stops you still say 10 - the stated-versus-charged parity this trajectory exists to prevent, in the one place a seller is deciding whether to publish. Latent today (hive_service_settings has ZERO rows, so every hive is on defaults) which is exactly when it is cheap to fix. ★AND THERE IS A DEAD KNOB WITH A MISLEADING NAME: holding_fee_pct exists on hive_service_settings, has NO default, and is read by nothing - the hold runs on reward_pct instead. Remaining: source the displayed rate from the knob (or state that it is fixed), retire or wire holding_fee_pct, plus the consolidated fees-summary surface. ★CORRECTION, AND I MADE THE SAME MISTAKE I HAD ALREADY DIAGNOSED TODAY: holding_fee_pct is NOT a dead knob. It is read by sweep_listing_holding_fee, which computes service_knob_pct(hive_id,'holding_fee_pct')/100.0 and skips with `continue when v_rate <= 0`. So the two knobs are two DIFFERENT economics, correctly separated: reward_pct sizes the REFUNDABLE reservation held while a listing is live, and holding_fee_pct is a RECURRING FEE swept from published listings - a real charge, currently inert because the rate is unset, which makes it a disabled feature rather than a dead column. I called it dead after scanning PAGES for readers, and its reader is a database function. That is precisely the error this same session already caught with is_marketplace_admin - invoked by 29 RLS policies and zero pages - and I repeated it two hours later on a different table. The lesson does not transfer by having been written down once: when asking WHO READS THIS, the corpus is pages AND edge functions AND DB functions AND policies, every time. ★WHAT STANDS UNCHANGED is the actual finding: the RATE is hive-configurable while every place a person reads it - four strings in marketplace-seller and the guard's own refusal message - hardcodes 10%. || ★THE FEE-PARITY ORACLE IS SATISFIED STRUCTURALLY, NOT BY COINCIDENCE (2026-08-28). trajectories.title: The marketplace's first-time seller conversion (supply growth)
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, premise-first + live walk): THE INVITE SURFACE EXISTS AND IS WELL-DESIGNED - inventory's Marketplace bridge shows 'Sell surplus' ONLY on rows holding 3x+ their minimum (2 live buttons on the Baguio fixture: Bearing 6313 39/min 3 etc.), with the WHY in the control's own title ('You hold 3x+ your minimum of this part: list the surplus on the Marketplace for another plant') - contextual, honest, non-pushy (no DP pressure), exactly the natural-moment invite the spec asked about; clicking hands off into the marketplace flow, and the listing chain carries cost transparency (10%-hold) + the marketplace-listing-assist AI (invoked from inventory's bridge code). BONUS: the sibling 'Find on Marketplace' on low/out rows (3 live) answers T30's 'does the buy hop exist' - it does. Remaining: the handoff's intent-preservation detail (does the composer land PREFILLED with the part's name/number/qty), the worker->seller identity-bridge comprehension copy, first-listing hand-holding continuity (T100 seam) (wave close).  || THE HANDOFF'S INTENT-PRESERVATION QUESTION ANSWERED 2026-08-26, and the answer is VERIFIED-GOOD. Driven through the exact deep link sellSurplus() builds, against a real surplus row chosen by the same 3x rule the button uses: the composer arrives OPEN and PREFILLED with the part's title, its part number, its quantity (carried into the description), an auto-classified category, and the source inventory id preserved so the listing stays linked to the row it came from. Nothing is retyped. That matters most here because this is the least-motivated user in the whole funnel - a worker listing a spare part for the first time - and a handoff that drops what the system already knows is the same intent-loss as a wall that forgets where you were going. ★THE PRICE IS DELIBERATELY NOT PREFILLED, and the gate now asserts that ABSENCE: what a plant PAID is not what it should ASK, and a guessed price is the one field a seller must own - prefilling it would be the system making a commercial decision on their behalf. The mutation test proved that arm independent: with the prefill disabled, every other assertion flipped RED while priceLeftToTheSeller stayed green. LOCKED BY gate inventory-listing-handoff (7 assertions), which picks its surplus row dynamically so a reseed cannot make it a false red, and SKIPs when the fixture has none. Remaining: the worker->seller identity-bridge comprehension copy, and first-listing hand-holding continuity (now partly served by T100's preview-as-buyer). || THE SUPPLY FUNNEL HAS EVERY INPUT AND NO PATH - MEASURED (2026-08-27). The question was whether anything invites a worker to sell at the natural moment. It does not, and the gap is sharper than 'a missing button' because the platform already HOLDS the evidence. In the Baguio hive, 16 of 27 inventory items sit well above their minimum: Bearing 6313 C3 at qty 39 against min 3 (thirteen times), spiral wound gasket DN50 at 25 against 8, ISO VG46 hydraulic oil at 158 against 40. ★AND THE MARKETPLACE SELLS THE SAME PART: its catalogue carries 'New (boxed) Bearing 6313 C3 - SKF'. So the system knows who is holding thirteen times what they need of a bearing, knows that exact bearing trades on its own marketplace, and never puts the two together. The only invitations to sell live ON the marketplace ('list your own parts', 'list yourself as a service provider') - addressed to someone who has already decided to be a seller. Inventory, where the surplus actually sits, says nothing. ★WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN BUILT: an inventory nudge is net-new product surface, and T104's own spec says it must arrive 'without being pushy' - a prompt that reads as 'sell your spares' on a maintenance page can easily become the dark pattern the DP dims exist to prevent. Whether the platform should invite supply, and how gently, is Ian's call; the evidence that it COULD is now concrete rather than hypothetical. Remaining: that decision, then the worker->seller identity-bridge copy. || ★THE SUPPLY-SIDE INVITATION EXISTS, IS CONDITIONAL, AND EXPLAINS ITSELF (2026-08-28). This trajectory asks whether any surface INVITES selling at the natural moment without being pushy - the platform knows who holds excess stock, and the question is whether it uses that knowledge honestly. It does: inventory renders a 'Sell surplus' control, and the board's gate confirms it appears ONLY on rows holding 3x or more of their own minimum. The control's title carries the reason - 'You hold 3x+ your minimum of this part: list the surplus on the Marketplace for another plant.' ★THREE THINGS RIGHT IN ONE AFFORDANCE. It is CONDITIONAL on a real fact about the worker's own shelf, so it cannot become ambient nagging - a plant with no surplus never sees it. It is SELF-JUSTIFYING: the title answers 'why am I being shown this?' at the moment of the question, which is the difference between a suggestion and an advertisement. And it is FRAMED TOWARD THE PEER - 'for another plant' - which matches what the marketplace actually is here, a way for one Philippine plant to source from another, rather than a monetisation prompt aimed at the worker. That is the conversion-invite honesty oracle this trajectory specs, met without a dark pattern anywhere near it. ★WHAT REMAINS is the far end of the funnel: whether a worker who accepts the invitation completes their FIRST listing (T34's economy comprehension from zero, T100's assist), and whether the worker-to-seller identity bridge reads as one account gaining a capability rather than a second role to learn. pct 72 -> 86. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED (fix+gate) - all assigned gates PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_marketplace_economy.mjs (gate marketplace-economy), 9/9 lenses clean, read as a plain member through PostgREST rather than as the owner - money is exactly where an owner connection lies most. trajectories.title: Push notification permission & first value
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, permission census): exactly TWO Notification.requestPermission sites, both respecting the timing ethic - (1) marketplace-seller's svcEnablePush: USER-INITIATED ('Enable job alerts' tap), support+auth pre-checked, denial respected honestly ('Alerts stay off until you allow notifications' - no re-nag); (2) voice-handler: gated behind an explicit spoken OPT-IN vocabulary (EN+FIL 'turn on alerts / sige, alert mo'), permission states pre-checked (no re-prompt when denied). ZERO first-paint permission begs anywhere. Remaining: the first push's deep-link fidelity (T43) via the existing push-runtime-delivery harness, preference granularity probe (wave close).  || DEEP-LINK FIDELITY DRIVEN 2026-08-26 (the walk's second half, and it found a real defect). sw.js's notificationclick matched an already-open tab with c.url.includes(target.split('?')[0]) - the PATH, with the query thrown away - and returned c.focus(). Every url notify-push sends carries its destination in the QUERY (the default alone is ?tab=services), so a provider who already had marketplace-seller open on ?tab=listings tapped a job-offer push, watched their existing view get focused, and was never taken anywhere: the push's promise evaporated with nothing on screen to say a destination had been missed. Same class as a sign-in wall that drops the return-to (T4/T8/T43). FIXED: the handler now focuses the matching tab AND navigates it when the target differs, leaves a tab that is already there alone (a navigate would reload the page under someone mid-task), and CACHE_NAME moved v239 -> v240 so installed PWAs cannot keep the worker that drops the link. LOCKED BY: gate push-deeplink (tools/validate_push_deeplink.py -> tools/prove_push_deeplink.mjs), which loads the SHIPPING sw.js, installs the listener it registers and dispatches a synthetic click against a fake clients registry - it tests the file that deploys, not a re-implementation of its logic. Resurrection: RED on the pre-fix worker for the wrong-query case ONLY; the no-tab and already-there cases stay green in both worlds, which is how a specific oracle should behave. REMAINS (why 80): preference GRANULARITY is still one on/off switch per surface - a provider cannot say 'job offers yes, marketing no' - and that lane's home is the same scoped decision T107 leaves open. || ★PERMISSION TIMING IS RIGHT, AND UNUSUALLY SO (2026-08-28). This trajectory exists because asking for push at first paint is the classic way to lose it forever. Both call sites were checked and neither does that. marketplace-seller requests it inside svcEnablePush - an explicit button. The companion's is better: _requestPushPerm fires only from _isPushOptInReply, a matcher over the user's own TRANSCRIPT for an affirmative ('yes, alert me' / 'sige, alert mo' - both languages), so the person is ASKED IN CONVERSATION and consents in words BEFORE the browser dialog appears. It then fires only when Notification.permission is still 'default', and the code notes it does so while 'the user-gesture window is open', which is what makes the browser accept it at all. ★AND A DENIAL IS RESPECTED: _requestPushPerm short-circuits on both 'granted' and 'denied' before ever calling requestPermission, so a person who said no is never re-prompted - the re-nag loop this trajectory names as the failure mode cannot occur. That is consent asked in the user's own words, in their own language, at a moment they raised. ★WHAT A STATIC READ CANNOT SETTLE: whether the companion OFFERS the opt-in after an event worth pushing about, or merely somewhere convenient. The value-stated half of the probe needs a live conversation walk. pct -> 80. || ★PERMISSION IS ASKED WELL AND THE PUSH NOW LANDS WHERE IT PROMISED (2026-08-28). Permission TIMING, verified under T46: Notification.requestPermission is reached from exactly two places platform-wide, both behind a deliberate act - an 'Enable job notifications' button on marketplace-seller, and a VERBAL opt-in in voice-journal guarded by pushState==='default' so somebody who already declined is never asked again. Nothing fires at first paint, and denial is respected rather than re-nagged. ★DESTINATION FIDELITY IS FIXED AND THE FIX IS THE INTERESTING PART: notificationclick used to match an already-open tab on PATH only and return focus, so every push whose destination lives in the QUERY (?tab=services, ?asset=, ?post=) landed a provider on whatever view they already had open - a promise made and silently missed. Now the path match only FINDS the tab; the handler then compares full URLs (new URL(target, c.url).href === c.url) and NAVIGATES when they differ, focusing after, with a focus fallback on error. A push aimed at a job offer opens the job offer. ★AND THE CACHE HISTORY RECORDS A SUBTLER BUG WORTH REMEMBERING: before v239, exactly ONE root-scope register() existed - on report-sender, a supervisor page - so a WORKER who installed the PWA from index got no shell precache, no offline fallback, and serviceWorker.ready that hung forever. The marketplace-seller push-alerts hang was that hole. A service worker registered on the wrong page is indistinguishable from one that does not exist, for everybody who never visits that page. pct 80 -> 90. pct -> 90. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED (fix+gate) - all assigned gates PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

trajectories.note: ★BROWSER PERMISSION IS NOT A SUBSCRIPTION - FOUND AND FIXED (2026-08-27). Found by sweeping for WRITE-ONLY TABLES (the table-level twin of the captured-columns sweep): of 54 tables the UI writes, 2 are read by no page after resolving reads through views, and push_subscriptions is one. marketplace-seller WRITES a subscription on enable and never reads one back, and the in-context push card renders only while `Notification.permission !== 'granted'` - so the moment permission is granted the card disappears FOREVER and nothing ever confirms a subscription row exists. Those are two different facts about the world. A push subscription is lost routinely - the browser rotates the endpoint, the service worker is replaced, the upsert failed, the row was cleared - and permission stays 'granted' through every one of them. The provider is then shown NOTHING while believing the page's own promise that they will 'hear new hails with this tab closed'. A claim no query enforces, on the one capability whose whole value is working while nobody is looking. trajectories.title: Quiet hours & notification pressure (PHT reality)
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, pressure census): the notification pressure surface is MINIMAL by construction - no unattended emails (T106), push ONLY for explicitly-enabled job alerts (an opt-in work-finding channel where piercing quiet is arguably the point), and the 6am PHT AMC cron writes an IN-APP brief, not a push. Quiet hours therefore have almost nothing to govern today - an honest absence, not a gap; the posture becomes a real design question only when personal notification lanes (T107/T108) ship. PHT correctness: crons schedule in UTC with PHT-labeled intent (amc 6am PHT = 22:00 UTC; my summaries cron Mon 05:00 PHT). Remaining: shift-aware delivery + urgency tiers WHEN a personal lane ships; timezone boundary probes (T132 seam) (wave close). MEASURED 2026-08-26: there are NO quiet hours anywhere - push_subscriptions carries no window or timezone column, notify-push has no time gate, and no preference exists. Checked the other half too, which is what makes this honest rather than a gap report: NOTHING CLAIMS quiet hours - no page, no policy line, no notification copy promises a window - so the platform is silent, not lying. What DOES exist to build on: an urgency vocabulary already distinguishes 'Urgent job nearby' from 'New job nearby' at broadcast time, and shift-brain holds real shift schedules, so a night worker's 'morning' is knowable. The build would need a per-user quiet window + timezone + an urgency tier that pierces it (safety-critical always delivers, a digest never) - schema, preference UI and delivery logic together, i.e. a scoped product decision rather than a slice. All eight (mention, reply, best answer, assignment, approval decision, report, pending submission, service completion) fire from a person acting; NOT ONE is clock-driven, and no cron enqueues a push. So a phone cannot buzz at 3am unless somebody in that hive acted at 3am, which on a round-the-clock plant is a night shift and is legitimate news. trajectories.title: Notification storms under real activity
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, architecture map): the push path is OUTBOX-MEDIATED - a DB fn enqueues (consumer 'notify-push', auth_uids+title+body+url) into service_outbox, drained by the 1-min cron to the notify-push fn - so the drain is the natural batching point, and volume is bounded by real broadcast traffic; but NO per-user collapse exists ('5 replies = one line' - each outbox row becomes a push). Acceptable at today's event volume (opt-in job alerts only); becomes a storm risk when personal lanes (T107/T108) ship. Remaining: the storm-injection probe (N outbox rows for one user -> pushes counted) on the EXISTING push-runtime-delivery harness (tests/), catch-up UX after a storm, badge-list cap discipline (T19's lesson) (wave close). COALESCING MEASURED + THE SAFE SLICE SHIPPED 2026-08-26. Measured first: there is NO coalescing anywhere in the lane - enqueue_user_push inserts one outbox row per event and the drain sends one push per row, so in a busy hive a worker can be pushed the same sentence several times a minute (two triggers on one PM going overdue, a supervisor's repeated save, a retrying client). Migration 20260826000001 adds the narrow, safe half: an identical push (same recipients+title+body+url) still UNSENT within a 2-minute window returns the PENDING row's id instead of enqueueing a second - callers unchanged, since the contract is still 'an id comes back'. Deliberately NOT done here: digest-style merging of DIFFERENT notifications ('3 new replies'), which is a wording+cadence design decision, and suppression of a repeat whose predecessor was already DELIVERED - that is news, not a duplicate. PROVEN in a rolled-back txn: identical -> same id (2 rows not 3), different body -> its own row. Remaining: the digest decision, storm-injection probe on the push-runtime harness, catch-up UX after a storm. (2026-08-26, T61's measurement: the enqueue layer is already O(1) rows per event - recipients travel as an array - so the dedupe window added here is the right and only place the storm can be bounded before delivery.)  || THE DEDUPE WINDOW IS NOW LOCKED (2026-08-26). It had shipped with NO gate, and the same day it became load-bearing: four new producers landed (T108's mentions/replies/best-answer plus a trigger on every pending submission), and the submission trigger depends on this window BY DESIGN - its copy names no row precisely so a bulk CMMS import of 200 assets collapses to ONE push. An unlocked storm guard underneath four new storm sources is the gap worth closing before any further producer. Gate push-dedupe-window holds FIVE assertions, and the third is what separates a correct dedupe from a mute button: a repeat whose predecessor was already DELIVERED must get its own row, because that is news, and suppressing it would silently drop real notifications. It also holds that a different body and a different RECIPIENT each get their own row - a blanket one-per-user-per-window would swallow different news and merge two people's deliveries. The whole gate runs inside a transaction that is ROLLED BACK and then verifies nothing survived, so it writes nothing it must clean up. Resurrection: with the dedupe removed (also inside a rollback - DDL is transactional, so the mutation could never escape) identical pushes returned different ids and wrote 2 rows, RED on both. REMAINS (why 80): the digest-style merge of DIFFERENT notifications ('3 new replies') is a wording+cadence design decision for Ian, and catch-up UX after a storm is unbuilt. || GATE RECORDED 2026-08-27: push-dedupe-window (registered, verified exit 0). The basis called it a gate and described its resurrection - identical pushes returning different ids and writing 2 rows with the dedupe removed - but the gates field was empty, so the registry did not know this trajectory owned an instrument. push-runtime-delivery is deliberately NOT recorded: the basis names it as the EXISTING harness in tests/ that the storm probe will run on, which is a tool this trajectory USES, not one it owns. The distinction matters because a scan that matched any registered id inside a basis proposed 61 refs across 50 trajectories, most of them page names colliding with gate ids - recording those would have put other trajectories' instruments in this one's ledger. || 2026-09-01 DESIGN FINDING: coalescing needs a CATEGORY dimension the enqueue_user_push contract lacks (payload = auth_uids/title/body/url, no type). Cleanest honest paths: (a) add p_category param (signature change, all callers default it), or (b) key coalescing on recipient-set + url-tab. Fixed with a partial unique expression index (mig 20260826000004) rather than a check-before-insert, because two near-simultaneous retries both pass a SELECT-then-INSERT; the receiver now writes [svix_id=...] and treats 23505 as SUCCESS so the provider stops retrying something already stored. (2) FOUND WHILE BUILDING THE PROOF, not by looking for it: automation_log's CHECK allows success|failed|skipped|warning, and the receiver wrote 'failure' while send-report-email's circuit breaker wrote 'deferred'. Both refused with 23514 - and NEITHER read the insert error, so the errors vanished and both functions reported success. The bounce lane would have answered Resend 200 'recorded' while storing nothing: a permanently empty bounce surface with every layer above it healthy. Fixed by growing the vocabulary honestly (mig 20260826000005 adds 'warning', because a delayed delivery is genuinely neither a completed failure nor a skip and forcing it into 'failed' would over-report real problems), correcting 'failure'->'failed', and mapping the breaker to 'skipped', which already means exactly 'we did not attempt this'. LOCKED BY two gates: bounce-idempotency (4 assertions incl. a real concurrency race - two writers, one row, one refusal) and automation-log-status (the CLASS gate: every status literal allowed, checked against BOTH the migration and the live constraint, plus a forward-only ratchet on unchecked inserts). Resurrection on both. REMAINS (why 70): the HTTP round trip - a real signed webhook hitting the deployed function twice - is still Ian-gated on the secret, and the edge fns need a REDEPLOY. || ★THE CLASS GATE GREW ITS MISSING HALF (2026-08-28). automation-log-status asserts every status literal is PERMITTED by its CHECK constraint. That answers 'may this value be stored' and never 'does anything downstream know what it means' - and the second question is where the real defect was hiding. cmms-push-completion wrote external_sync.sync_status='failed' as the durable marker for a completion that never reached the CMMS; the CHECK permits five values so a constraint-shaped gate passes it happily, but v_external_sync_truth buckets exactly three (is_active/is_deleted/is_error), so the marker built to make a lost completion VISIBLE landed in the one value that made it invisible to the truth view as well. New gate status-literals-are-classified asserts the other half: every status literal the code WRITES must be one the consuming view CLASSIFIES. It reads the LIVE view definition rather than a migration, so it measures what the database actually buckets. Resurrection-proven - restoring 'failed' names the orphan value and its exact line. ★AND ITS COLUMN PATTERN CARRIES A WORD BOUNDARY, which cost a wrong reading earlier the same day: without one, `sync_status` matches the tail of `last_sync_status` - a different column, on a different table, with its own vocabulary ('failed'/'success') and its own reader at integrations.html:1792. Two columns whose names overlap are not one column. || ★AND THE NEW GATE HAD THE FALSE-GREEN SHAPE ITSELF, FOUND BY REVIEWING MY OWN WORK THE SAME DAY (2026-08-28). status-literals-are-classified reads the LIVE view definition, so on a machine where the database is unreachable every pair SKIPPED, `problems` stayed 0, and the run printed PASS - a zero meaning 'I could not look' rendered identically to a zero meaning 'nothing wrong'. That is the skipped-partition-reads-as-covered shape this whole board exists to prevent, shipped inside the gate written to prevent a cousin of it. It now counts what it actually CHECKED and fails when that is zero: 'NOTHING was checked: the database was not reachable, so this run has no opinion about the code. That is not the same as finding it clean.' The convention was already here to follow - fb1_webhook_idempotency_live raises on an unreachable psql rather than shrugging. TEETH-PROVEN by pointing it at a container that does not exist: FAIL, not PASS; restored, exit 0, and the PASS line now states how many column/view pairs were examined so the reader can see the denominator rather than trust the verdict. || ★THREE WEBHOOK CLASSES, THREE DIFFERENT ANSWERS TO 'DOES IT REACH A PERSON?' (2026-08-28). The platform receives three kinds of external event and they land very differently. trajectories.note: ★THE BOUNCE CLASS REACHES THE SENDER - TRACED END TO END (2026-08-27). T112 asks whether an external event becomes visible truth for the affected user, and for email delivery it does. The chain: Resend calls resend-webhook-receiver, which records the event into automation_log under job_name 'report_email_bounce'; report-sender READS those back (hive-scoped, last 30 days, limit 200) and maps each lowercased address to what happened, parsing bounced / marked as spam / delayed out of the detail. The reasoning is written above it and is exactly right: 'a full mailbox or a retired address is accepted with a 200, and the failure arrives later as a webhook … without reading them here the report is "sent" forever and nobody is told.' ★TWO DETAILS WORTH KEEPING because both are lessons this platform paid for elsewhere: the read is ordered by triggered_at AND id, a TOTAL order, because two bounces can share a timestamp and a non-total order paginates unstably; and a FAILED read leaves the map untouched rather than empty, so the page 'does not claim either way, rather than claiming everything is fine' - the failed-read-is-not-empty discipline applied to a surface where the empty reading would be 'every address is fine'. ★WHAT IS STILL PENDING IS IAN'S, not the code's: the Resend signing secret, without which no real event reaches the receiver. The pipe is built and honest; it is waiting to be turned on.

trajectories.title: Small phone 320: the floor viewport
trajectories.basis: the floor JOURNEY ran (not just rest-state): the full logbook wizard at 320x640 - picker, all fields, 3 steps, save - completes with NO horizontal scroll and the entry lands visibly; save button in-viewport and tappable (86x107 - wraps tall-narrow sharing its row at 320, cosmetic note). Z2 rest-state coverage pre-existing in the lens. FIXED-CHROME BUDGET AUDIT DONE 2026-08-26 and locked. The individual pieces of furniture were each reasonable and had never been measured TOGETHER, which is how a floor screen quietly loses a third of itself before one row of content is drawn. Measured across the eight pages a field phone lives in: mean 26.1% of the 320x640 viewport is persistent chrome, worst 36.6% (pm-scheduler), and on SEVEN OF EIGHT the largest single contributor is the same 64px page-guide chip - the component already on record for covering every modal's Save. Coverage is a UNION of viewport rows, never a sum, so overlapping chrome costs one band rather than inventing a number nobody experiences. VERDICT: 26% is a real cost but not a defect, so the honest outcome is a locked forward-only measurement rather than a fix hunting for a problem - chrome may shrink, never grow. ★THREE INSTRUMENT CORRECTIONS BEFORE ANY NUMBER WAS BANKED. Run 1 reported index.html at 87.5% and blamed #cursor-glow, a 440px pointer-following gradient that is pointer-events:none, z-index 0 and 5% alpha - decoration sitting BEHIND everything, costing a person nothing. Run 2 reported logbook at 50.9% and blamed a 280px div.card that turned out to be the Log a Repair FORM, sticky top-6 and 843px tall on a 640px screen: sticky cannot engage for something taller than the viewport, so it scrolls exactly like the content it is. Banking either would have sent someone deleting furniture that does not exist or a panel a worker needs. The rules that survived - chrome INTERCEPTS A THUMB or gets ANNOUNCED, and chrome PERSISTS WHILE CONTENT MOVES UNDER IT - are what the gate now encodes. MODALS AT THE FLOOR DONE 2026-08-26, and they were not clean. The dialog prover swept 390/641/1280 - the widths with banked rows - so 320 had never been measured. Made the sweep overridable (default UNCHANGED, because silently adding a fourth width would change what the registered cj_dialog_layout gate MEANS without anyone deciding to) and ran the floor: THREE real defects. (1) pm-scheduler's PM COMPLETION SHEET hung its primary action 21px past the panel - a worker on a budget Android reaching for a Save button whose right edge was off the sheet, in the core field flow. btn-primary is width:100% by design but shares a flex row with Cancel, and at 320 the content box is 278px, which cannot hold both however the remainder is divided; two attempts to make them SHARE went 21 -> 10 -> 14px, which was the measurement telling me the premise was wrong, so they stack at the floor. (2) analytics' results panel pinned three columns by inline style and pushed tiles 52px past it; auto-fit now drops to two. (3) public-feed showed a 229x12px link - and it was NOT a floor defect: it lives in whListError, so it sat in ~20 PAGES' read-failure states and was failing at 390 too, unnoticed, in the exact state a person reaches when something has already gone wrong. It was also MY OWN edit from earlier the same day (the T71 status-page pointer), written as a bare inline anchor while the correct idiom - inline-flex + min-height:44px - already existed two functions away in the same file. AFTER THE FIXES: 43 of 50 gradable dialogs pass at 320 with zero failures, and the default 390 sweep went from 1 failing to 0. LOCKED BY gate dialog-floor. The prover's own rail earned its keep: the first 320 run reported 0 of 50 graded (my override collided with a hardcoded 390 reference) and it REFUSED to call that a pass - 'zero failures over an empty denominator is not a pass' - so a probe bug cost five minutes instead of banking 'the floor is clean'. Remaining: T10/T13 journeys walked end-to-end at 320. || HANDED OVER FROM T45's N1 WALK 2026-08-27 — a real floor-viewport finding, language-independent. The '← Back to Basic Worker' link (a.btn-secondary.text-xs.py-2.px-4) extends past a 390 viewport by +45px on inventory and +35px on logbook, with its parent computing overflow:visible, so it is cut at the viewport edge rather than clipped deliberately. Verified in BOTH languages at the same offsets, so it is a layout bug and not a translation-length one. The page does not scroll horizontally, which is why it has survived: nothing about it trips a scroll-based check, but part of a tappable control sits off-screen on the floor viewport this trajectory owns. || FIXED 2026-08-27 — and the ROOT was not the element that looked wrong. The '← Back to Basic Worker' link measured +45px (inventory) / +35px (logbook) past a 390 viewport, so the obvious move was to shorten the button. I did, and it was WRONG twice over: the label span used `hidden sm:inline`, and wh-tw.css compiles NO .sm\: variants at all — so the span was hidden at EVERY width and desktop silently lost the full label — while the link, now only 101px wide, STILL sat at 438 in a 390 box. The measurement that ended it was the container's own numbers: navScrollW 438 vs navClientW 384. The row was over-full because the LEFT group ('Digital Logbook' / 'Inventory Monitor' with tracking-widest) would not shrink — a flex item defaults to min-width:auto and refuses to go below its content width, so it held the row open and pushed the button off-screen. THE FIX is min-w-0 on the left group plus truncate on the section label, letting it ellipsize instead: both pages now read the FULL button label at 390 with linkRight 364 < 390 and navScrollW == navClientW == 384. Re-swept 8 pages at 390: 7 clean, the 8th a JS-injected span carrying the document title inside an overflow:hidden parent — clipped by design, not visible overflow. mobile, link-target-existence and jargon all green over the change. ★WHY IT SURVIVED THIS LONG: the page never scrolls horizontally, so every scroll-based check reads clean while part of a tappable control sits past the edge — worth a probe of its own on the floor viewport. || GATE BUILT + REGISTERED + RESURRECTION-PROVED 2026-08-27: control-within-viewport (tools/prove_control_within_viewport.mjs). The fix alone was not the lock — the reason that overflow survived is a HOLE in what the floor-viewport checks look at, and the hole outlives the one navbar. Scroll is a SYMPTOM of overflow, not a definition: this page never scrolls horizontally, so every Z2 / WCAG 1.4.10-shaped check reads clean while a button hangs past the edge. The gate asks the question those checks cannot — at 390, does any rendered element with its own text (or any link/button) extend past the right edge without a scrolling or clipping ancestor? Fixed and absolute decoration is ignored, so it reports only what a thumb genuinely cannot reach. Walks 16 pages signed in as supervisor; currently 0 offenders. TEETH, and a real red->green rather than a synthetic one: removing min-w-0 from the flex group turns it RED (exit 1, naming a.btn-secondary at +228px AND #hive-chip-name at +5px, a second overflow the same root was hiding), restoring it turns it GREEN (exit 0) — files backed up and verified restored either side. Narrowed --page runs write their own report, so a spot-check cannot clobber the sweep. || ★THE GATE WAS GUARDING THE WRONG BOX (2026-08-27). This trajectory IS 'the floor viewport, 320', and the gate I registered for it ran at 390 and called that the floor. 390 is the common phone, not the floor; the declared floor is 320 (WCAG 1.4.10). Re-pointing it found TWO more off-screen elements the same day, both invisible at 390: (1) community's post action row - a supervisor viewing their OWN post gets FIVE icon buttons instead of four (edit, pin, public, flag, delete), and the fifth is Delete, which also carries a deliberate 22px Z3 gap so a destructive control is never adjacent to a routine one. Those 22px are exactly what pushed it 15px off-screen, so the delete control was unreachable on precisely the posts its owner is most likely to manage - and only for the author, which is why every four-button row read clean. (2) analytics' 'Stage 3' badge 10px past, because .hdr-right is deliberately flex-shrink:0 (its EN/FIL buttons owe 44px on BOTH axes) so the row had nowhere to give. ★BOTH FIXED BY WRAPPING RATHER THAN SHRINKING, which is the point: the obvious fixes - trim the Z3 gap, let the 44px buttons shrink - would each have bought viewport space by spending a different guarantee. Wrapping keeps the destructive-adjacency separation AND the touch minimums AND puts the control back on screen; rows that already fit are unchanged. Width is now a parameter defaulting to the FLOOR, a non-default width writes its own report, and 320 and 390 are both green over 16 pages. Remaining: T10/T13 journeys walked end-to-end at 320. || T10/T13 WALKED END-TO-END AT 320 + GATED 2026-08-27 (flow-fits-the-floor). ★THE REASON THIS NEEDED ITS OWN INSTRUMENT: control-within-viewport walks pages AT REST, and the controls that decide whether work gets RECORDED do not exist at rest. The PM completion sheet, the deferral control and the add-task sheet are built or revealed mid-flow, each a different layout from the page hosting it — so the resting sweep can be green over all 16 pages while the Save button of the sheet a worker must press sits off the edge. Same class this trajectory already found twice, one interaction deeper than any resting check can reach. Walks T10 (complete a PM, plus its honest alternative, recording a DEFERRAL) and T13 (the clock-in handover) at the floor; all clean, 7 controls in the sheet and 124 on the handover. ★IT ARRIVES THE WAY A WORKER DOES: alert-hub hands pm-scheduler an ?asset=, the detail opens, a REAL scope item's mark-done control is clicked. My first cut called openSheet() by hand and measured an EMPTY sheet — the same seven controls whatever the task, because markDone() is what fills in the item text, asset name, frequency badge and findings. That would have proved the sheet's chrome fits, not the sheet. ★AND THE FIRST RUN CAUGHT ITSELF: page.evaluate takes ONE argument and I passed three, so every flow errored — reported as UNREACHED rather than as three tidy clean surfaces, which is the rule this arc keeps re-learning (an empty reading is the instrument, never the property). PROACTIVE guard, so teeth are synthetic negatives, one per independent failure mode, 4/4 verified: off-screen control, absent required control, absent surface, and the real sheet clean. A width negative alone is NOT enough — at --width 200 the handover went RED while both PM sheets still passed, which is exactly why the missing-control half needs its own negative. Gate registered (973 total). Remaining: the wave-close re-earn, same as its siblings. || ROSTER WIDENED 16 -> 23 PAGES, AND THE SEVEN NEW ONES HELD A THIRD DEFECT (2026-08-27). The sweep guarded 16 pages while 22 are banked, so a third of the roster was left to be discovered by a user; project-report is walked WITH its ?project_id= because a paramless walk is a different page. FOUND on project-manager: all FOUR project cards - each a tappable control that opens its project - sat exactly 8px past the right edge at 320. ROOT: .card-grid used repeat(auto-fill, minmax(310px, 1fr)), and a bare 310px floor is a floor the CONTAINER can be narrower than. At 320 main's 18px padding leaves 284px of room, auto-fill still produced one 310px column, and 18 + 310 = 328 - the +8px the gate measured, identical on every card because it is the grid track, not the content. FIXED with minmax(min(310px, 100%), 1fr) in BOTH grid rules (the second one, under .group-content, would otherwise have kept the bug for grouped views - the same fix-every-path discipline that caught the second discipline/category refusal earlier today). Desktop verified unchanged: 1280 still lays out 3 columns at 404px across 2 rows. All 23 pages now green at 320 and at 390. || AND THE DIALOG DENOMINATOR MADE THE PLATFORM'S, NOT MINE (2026-08-27, gate dialogs-fit-the-floor). flow-fits-the-floor walks four flows I picked by hand, and a gate whose subject list I wrote can only ever find what I thought to look at. tools/dialog_targets.mjs is already the ONE source of truth for how each V2/V3 dialog opens - every entry's path read from source, with the `ref` line that establishes it - so this gate consumes it, and any dialog added there is covered for free. 42 subjects, 26 measured, ZERO unreachable controls at 320x844. ★THE SUBJECT TEST IS THE WHOLE GATE, and the first run got it wrong.
