trajectories.title: Zero, one, some, many: the cardinality sweep
trajectories.basis: the raw-plural census ran: 59 candidate sites without an n===1 branch on-line (integrations 12, resume 10, analytics-report 9) - the list carries known false positives (unit abbreviations 'hrs/days', verbs) so NOTHING banked; the platform's earlier counted-noun sweep covers the majority class. n=0-vs-failed split locked in prior arcs; the four-cardinality fixture lanes (0/1/2/50 per list surface) = wave close on the grow/age fixtures.  || THE n=1 GRAMMAR HALF MEASURED AND RATCHETED 2026-08-26. First pass counted 82 offenders and that number was DISHONEST: most were windows like ${period} days, which is 30/60/90 by construction and can never read '1 days'. A census padded with cases that cannot occur produces a figure nobody trusts and a gate everyone learns to ignore, so it was narrowed to counts that can GENUINELY be 1 - a .length, a *Count, a *_count, a *Total - giving 30 real sites across 13 files. FIXED the one a worker meets every day: the counter under the LOGBOOK's search box said '1 entries found' the moment a search narrowed to a single result, on the platform's most-used page. Written with the codebase's own existing idiom (${n} entr${n === 1 ? 'y' : 'ies'}) rather than introducing a helper - code that reads like the code around it. Baseline now 27. NOT mass-edited, deliberately: the rest sit on secondary and admin surfaces, and rewriting 27 render paths in one unreviewed sweep for a grammar nit is a bad trade - so gate counted-noun-ratchet holds the number from GROWING and says plainly that zero is not the goal. Teeth-proven by injecting one new offender: RED, then removed. Remaining: the n=0 vs failed-read re-verify at journey level, n=2 layouts, and sort/filter controls at n=1. || n=1 GRAMMAR SWEPT, AND THE FINDING COUNT FELL 274 -> 39 -> 24 -> 12 AS THE INSTRUMENT GOT HONEST (2026-08-27). The first pass matched any count rendered into a plural and produced 274 hits - which was a statement about my regex, not the product. Each narrowing removed a class of false positive I could NAME: a verb read as a noun ('${top_machine} accounts for'), a period filter that is 7/30/90 and never 1 ('${period} days'), vendored maplibre, my own instrument files whose output nobody reads, counts STRUCTURALLY bounded away from one by their guard (dayplanner's overdue line lives inside `overdueCount >= 3`), the 'N of M nouns' idiom where the plural attaches to the category rather than the count, and the already-honest 'log(s)' form. Of the 24 survivors, 4 were LLM PROMPT context (voice-handler's RAG blocks, assistant's journal header) where '1 entries' reaches a model and no person, and one was a cap constant ('the first N assets of'). ★12 REAL USER-VISIBLE SITES FIXED, and the best of them was in the a11y layer: community's reaction button builds aria-label `${d.count} reactions`, so a screen reader said 'Helpful, 1 reactions, you reacted' - at the count that is by far the COMMONEST for a reaction. Also analytics (machines/failures/parts-at-risk badges), hive's top-risk bullet, integrations' import warning ('1 rows have' -> '1 row has'), logbook's filled-fields receipt, plant-connections' sensor hero, project-manager's item chip, ph-intelligence and founder-console. Fixed with the platform's OWN inline-ternary idiom rather than a new helper: the codebase already does this three consistent ways and index.html even wraps it in _t() for Filipino, so a fourth idiom would have been the invention, not the fix. All 9 edited pages re-loaded live: zero JS errors, no stray '1 <plural>' anywhere on the glass. Remaining: the n=0-vs-failed-read re-verify at journey level, n=2 layouts, and sort/filter controls at n=1. || ★THE n=1 SWEEP FOUND THAT THE COUNTED-NOUN RULE STOPPED AT THE NOUN (2026-08-28). Walking pm-scheduler at 390 I read 'DUE SOON (14D) 1 · 1 asset need PM this week'. The template pluralises the NOUN correctly and leaves the VERB alone: `${n} asset${n===1?'':'s'} need PM this week`. Swept the class across every page - a pluralised noun followed by an unconditional verb - and found THREE MORE, all in hive.html: '${overdue} asset${...} have overdue PMs', in the verdict sub and in two next-step lines, each reading '1 asset have overdue PMs' at n=1. All four fixed, and analytics.html's near-miss was correctly left alone: its 'are' agrees with 'intervals', not with the counted assets - checking what the verb actually refers to is what kept a correct line from being 'fixed' into a wrong one. Verified live on both pages: '1 asset has overdue PMs' / '3 assets have overdue PMs' / '1 asset needs PM this week' / '4 assets need PM this week', with no 'asset have' or 'asset need ' string left in either document and zero page errors. The lesson for this trajectory's sweep: n=1 is a SENTENCE-level check, not a word-level one - the discipline has to carry the whole clause, not just the word next to the digit. pct 62 -> 70. || ★A METHODOLOGY CORRECTION FOR EVERY WALK PROBE IN THIS PROGRAMME (2026-08-28): innerText IS NOT A VISIBILITY FILTER. Walking resume.html my scan reported '⚠ You're offline: changes are saved on this device and will sync when you reconnect' on a page that was plainly online, which looked like a false-offline banner - the kind of defect worth stopping for. Measured instead of filed: navigator.onLine true, the banner without its .show class, computed display none, height 0. It is correctly hidden. The probe was wrong, and per spec: innerText on an element that is NOT BEING RENDERED returns the same value as textContent, so a display:none empty-state reads exactly like a visible one. The same run surfaced 'No tools match your search.' the same way. CONSEQUENCE for the empty-state half of this sweep: a walk that harvests innerText will report hidden empty states as shown, so any n=0 finding must be confirmed with computed style or a bounding box before it is banked. CHECKED BACKWARDS over today's other finds, because a bad instrument casts doubt on everything it touched: the voice-journal chip counts were confirmed against entry-count AND the rows, hive's '3 things' against the source plus a targeted textContent read, achievements' '+-20' against the expanded card plus a unit check of the helper, pm-scheduler's '1 asset need' against the template, and alert-hub's rag-label via getAttribute. None of them rests on this confusion - but only because each was verified a second way, which is the actual lesson. || ★A SECOND METHODOLOGY CORRECTION FOR THE WALK PROBES, from the same family as the innerText one (2026-08-28): A BOUNDING BOX IS NOT VISIBILITY EITHER. Walking marketplace-admin my visibility-aware probe - the one I had just fixed to check display, visibility and box size - happily reported the page's live admin figures, because the page is covered by a position:fixed inset:0 z-index:100000 retirement overlay and everything BEHIND it still has a non-zero box and display:block. Occlusion is invisible to every property I was checking. For any walk that must distinguish what a person can SEE, the test is document.elementFromPoint at the element's centre (or Playwright's own visibility + an overlay check), not the element's own style. Neither of today's banked findings rests on this - both were confirmed against source or DB - but the probe would have reported a retired page as a live one. || ★THE THREE PROBE FAILURES BECAME ONE TOOL (2026-08-28). Three false alarms in a single session, each caught only because the finding was verified a second way, were all the same mistake wearing different clothes: asking the DOM a question that SOUNDS like 'is this visible' and is not. innerText falls back to textContent on non-rendered elements (a display:none banner read as 'You're offline' on an online page); a bounding box says nothing about OCCLUSION (marketplace-admin's live figures read straight through a position:fixed inset:0 z-index:100000 retirement overlay); and a top-N sample is not a page (project-report's 'No project specified' and 'not found' refusals sat below the cut, and I nearly filed a defect against a page that had already solved it). tools/walk_page.mjs replaces the ad-hoc scripts with the one check that answers all three: for each candidate, is document.elementFromPoint at its own centre itself or a descendant? That single question accounts for display, visibility, zero boxes, off-screen position AND occlusion. It also returns `dropped` alongside the lines, because a caller who cannot see that a result was truncated cannot tell a page from a sample. VALIDATED against both pages that fooled the old method: resume now returns its real controls with no phantom offline banner (dropped 29, disclosed), and marketplace-admin returns ONLY the retirement overlay with dropped 0 - the occluded admin figures correctly absent. Every remaining walk in this programme should use it. || ★THE n=1 GRAMMAR PROBE COMES BACK ALMOST CLEAN, AND THE ONE EXCEPTION IS FIXED (2026-08-28). Swept every page for the naive shape - a count concatenated straight onto a plural noun - and the platform is in good order: alert-hub branches on n===1 seven times, analytics and analytics-report six each, ai-quality twice, achievements once. Somebody has cared about this consistently. Exactly ONE site had not: audit-log's filter summary built 'N of M entries' unconditionally, so a log holding a single entry read '1 of 1 entries'. ★A DETAIL WORTH GETTING RIGHT RATHER THAN JUST PLURALISING: the noun belongs to the TOTAL, not the filtered count, so the branch is on _entries.length - '1 of 1 entry' is correct while '1 of 3 entry' would not be. A careless fix here would have pluralised on items.length and produced a new wrong sentence in a different place. Re-swept after: zero naive concatenations remain in any user-facing string. ★SCOPE, STATED: this sweep catches `count + ' noun'`. A plural built inside a template literal would not match, so 'clean' here means clean of THIS shape rather than of every possible one - the n=1 rendering of list cards, empty-vs-one layouts and sort controls at a single row are the rest of this trajectory's cardinality question and are not claimed. pct 70 -> 82. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate counted-noun-ratchet re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Dates, times & the PHT lens
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, Playwright clock.install + fastForward on logbook): temporal REFRESH machinery exists and fires - under a controlled +2h fast-forward, a timer-driven repaint ran and painted TODAY date-group headers that were not in the pre-forward read (something in the page re-derives temporal groupings as time passes rather than freezing the load-time rendering). The canonical whFmtDate + the two-clocks lesson stand as prior receipts. Remaining: the midnight-PHT boundary flip probe (23:58 -> 00:02 'today/yesterday' regroup), relative-time STALENESS assertions per surface ('5m ago' after an hour open), viewer-TZ policy statement, week-start (Monday PH) checks, date-input locale probes (wave close). TWO TEMPORAL PROBES RUN 2026-08-26 with Playwright clock control. (1) MIDNIGHT BOUNDARY: CORRECT - an entry stamped 23:50 reads 'Today' at 23:58 and 'Yesterday' at 00:02; the dayLabel toDateString comparison regroups exactly at the local day flip, no off-by-one. (2) RELATIVE-TIME STALENESS on a page held open: labels are computed AT RENDER, and a grep across every page finds NO timer that re-renders them - the periodic timers that exist are data refreshes (alert-hub 60s loadAll, analytics status bar, marketplace service tracking) which incidentally repaint their own labels. So a surface that neither polls nor receives a realtime event shows a frozen 'x ago' until something else re-renders it. Severity is honest: the platform's visible labels are mostly DAY-granularity ('49d ago'), where an hour of drift is invisible; the exposure is minute-granularity labels on a long-open board. Probe lessons: my first staleness probe matched SCRIPT and JSON-LD text (childElementCount===0 does not mean visible), and the second compared a pre-render empty read against a post-render one - render timing masquerading as refresh. Remaining: a minute-granularity staleness case on a seeded fresh entry, viewer-TZ policy statement, week-start checks, date-input locale probes. || WEEK-START AND DATE-INPUT LOCALE: BOTH CLEAN, AND THE SECOND ANSWER ONLY BECAME TRUE AFTER I FIXED MY OWN REGEX (2026-08-27). WEEK START - the Philippine norm is Monday, and dayplanner carries the ISO idiom explicitly: `const dow = today.getDay() || 7; // Sun=7 instead of 0`, which maps Monday=1..Sunday=7 rather than JS's Sunday=0. The only other getDay() uses are days[d.getDay()] label lookups, which carry no week-start assumption at all. DATE INPUTS - every real date field uses a native <input type="date">, so the rendered format is the browser's locale job and the value is always ISO yyyy-mm-dd on the wire; there is no hand-rolled text date field to disagree with a Filipino user's dd/mm reading. ★THE FIRST PASS SAID OTHERWISE AND WAS WRONG BY SUBSTRING: matching (date|day|when|due|start|end) anywhere in the tag reported THREE type=text date fields in asset-hub - and all three were prose. 'ask-input' matched the word 'When' in a free-text question ('When did this asset last fail? Why?'), and BOTH rcm fields matched 'end' inside 'trend' ('Vibration trend at bearing housing'). Re-run with word boundaries and restricted to id/name/aria-label rather than placeholder prose: 4 date fields, all native, zero non-native. A pattern without   does not search for a word, it searches for letters - the same class as this session's plural census and the role=tab comment match. Remaining: the minute-granularity staleness case on a seeded fresh entry, and the viewer-TZ policy statement. || ★THE DEVICE'S CLOCK REACHES PERSISTED BUSINESS TIMESTAMPS - and the platform already knows the cure, it just applied it unevenly (2026-08-28). Hunted the dangerous half of the temporal lens: not how times are RENDERED, but which ones are WRITTEN from the client. Found client-computed new Date().toISOString() flowing into DB writes across marketplace.html, marketplace-seller.html, marketplace-admin.html, logbook.html, inventory.html and project-manager.html - and crucially not only into updated_at housekeeping but into MEANINGFUL business columns: settled_at and cancelled_at on service_requests. ★WHY IT BITES: service_requests carries SIXTEEN triggers - settlement commission, cashback minting, payment guards, push fanout - and NOT ONE of them is a touch trigger, so a client-supplied timestamp is stored exactly as sent. Compare projects, which HAS trg_projects_updated_at and therefore overrides whatever the browser claims. The platform already knows this pattern and simply did not apply it to the marketplace tables (marketplace_orders, marketplace_listings, service_providers are likewise untouched). service_requests even has 2 columns defaulting to now(), so server-authoritative time is the established convention on that very table - just not for these columns. ★IMPACT IS REAL, NOT THEORETICAL: sweep_service_completions reads settled_at/cancelled_at, so a phone whose clock is wrong - common, and the premise of this trajectory's sibling T150 - can shift when a request is swept, on the same table whose objection and settlement windows the marketplace's fairness rests on. ★NOT FIXED IN THIS PASS, deliberately and with the reason stated: the fix is a touch trigger (or a DEFAULT now() plus dropping the column from the client payload) on the MOST guard-dense table in the schema, where a new trigger's firing order against sixteen existing ones - settlement, reservation release, availability sync, push fanout - decides whether it helps or breaks writes that already work. That is precisely the class recorded in [[feedback_a_new_guard_breaks_the_triggers_that_already_write]], and it deserves its own careful slice with a per-trigger interaction walk rather than being appended to a turn that already landed one migration. The evidence above is what that slice starts from. ★SCOPE CORRECTION applied while measuring: community.html:2290's created_at: new Date() is an OPTIMISTIC local row unshifted into the rendered list, not a DB write, and was excluded - a grep for this pattern catches UI objects and persistence with equal enthusiasm. pct 68 -> 80. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - dates/times honor the PHT lens: temporal-answer-names-its-window + temporal-orchestrator prove a temporal answer decomposes its window correctly, not off a raw client clock. Gates [temporal-answer-names-its-window, temporal-orchestrator] registered + PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Numbers, units & rounding truth
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, one-datum three-way parity, worker 390): the hive's open-jobs count read from v_logbook_truth (9) EQUALS index's ops-home tile ('9 OPEN JOBS') - live rendered==DB parity on the headline datum (my logbook stat-pill read missed only because I guessed the wrong element id - instrument, not page). The units machinery stands (units_visible x3 gates, counted-noun discipline, whFmtPeso). Remaining: the cross-surface numeric-parity MATRIX (same datum, every rendering - index/logbook/analytics/asset-hub), rounding-consistency sweep (sum-of-rounded vs rounded-sum), currency formatting census, precision-to-domain review (0.1h vs 6min) (wave close).  || CURRENCY-FORMATTING CENSUS DONE 2026-08-26 and it found REAL money defects on three surfaces. whFmtPeso exists for one recorded reason: Number(null) is 0 and finite, so a null amount renders as a confident PHP0.00 - a filed top-up of PHP300 once did exactly that. THE FINDINGS: (1) FOUNDER-CONSOLE, the owner's own cockpit, had ZERO adoption and a formatter that was literally Number(n || 0) - the bug itself - while the same file already carried a note saying a money number frozen at zero 'does not read as by design, it reads as a feed that died'; its GCash top-up row used Number(r.amount) with no null guard, so an absent amount printed NaN on the screen where money enters the business. (2) MARKETPLACE-SELLER's earnings formatter used Number(n), printing NaN on the dashboard of the person being PAID. (3) MARKETPLACE's service picker guarded `<= 0`, which catches null (Number(null) is 0) but NOT undefined - NaN <= 0 is FALSE - so an absent rate reached a buyer as NaN. All routed through the helper; five money pages verified live with 0 pageerrors. ★THE GATE'S OWN FIRST RUN PRODUCED FOUR FALSE POSITIVES AND I DID NOT ACT ON THEM: a ternary spans lines, so the GUARDED FALLBACK half of `whFmtPeso(n) : '<peso>' + Number(n||0)` looked hand-rolled because the helper sat on the line above. 'Fixing' those would have damaged correct code whose fallback exists precisely so a page still renders when utils.js has not loaded - verify the instrument before the page. LOCKED BY gate money-formatting, scoped to money surfaces with the one deliberate local formatter allowlisted by name and reason (platform-actions' measured 'Negotiable (listed at PHP0)' branch). Remaining: the cross-surface numeric-parity MATRIX, rounding consistency (sum-of-rounded vs rounded-sum), and precision-to-domain review. || ROUNDING CONSISTENCY PROBED STATICALLY, PLUS THE FORMATTER-ADOPTION CENSUS (2026-08-27). Checked first for the sharpest version of the defect - the SAME metric rendered at different precision on different pages, which makes two surfaces appear to disagree about one number. Across mtbf/mttr/oee/compliance/availability/downtime/spi/cpi, only MTBF is formatted through an explicit .toFixed and it is precision 1 at both sites: no inconsistency found by that probe. ★BUT THE PROBE COVERS ONE IDIOM, so 'no finding' is not 'no defect'. The census: toFixed( 694 uses across 25 pages, Math.round( 336 across 42, toLocaleString 123 across 14, against whFmtPeso 49 across 12 and whFmtNum 30 across 7 - the platform HAS a formatter family in utils.js (whFmtNum/Peso/Date/Duration/Ago) and roughly 6% of numeric rendering goes through it. That is not automatically a defect: a one-off toFixed on a locally computed value is fine, and T133's property is that ONE DATUM reads the same everywhere, not that every call site uses the helper. ★WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY THE IDIOM COUNT CANNOT SETTLE IT - the parity question is about a VALUE traced across surfaces (the same MTBF on index, analytics and asset-hub), and no amount of counting format calls answers it. Remaining: the cross-surface numeric-parity MATRIX as a LIVE trace (same datum, every rendering, compared), which is deferred past the running board rather than run against a shared local stack a gate is querying; plus sum-of-rounded vs rounded-sum and the precision-to-domain review. || THE CROSS-SURFACE MATRIX RAN, AND THE DISAGREEMENT IT FOUND IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN ARITHMETIC (2026-08-27). Traced four data against DB truth across index, asset-hub, inventory and hive. Inventory (27) and open logbook entries (9) agree exactly. ASSETS DO NOT: index shows 'PM OVERDUE (29 OF 30 ASSETS)' while asset-hub shows 'TOTAL ASSETS 25'. ★NEITHER PAGE IS INTERNALLY WRONG - THEY COUNT DIFFERENT REGISTRIES. pm_assets holds 30 rows; asset_nodes holds 30 rows of which 25 are approved (the rest pending or rejected), and asset-hub counts only approved. So the word 'assets' means PM-schedule rows on one page and approved asset nodes on the other, and a supervisor comparing the two sees their plant contain 30 machines or 25 depending which page they are on, with nothing on either explaining the difference. ★AND THE TWO REGISTRIES ARE NOT LINKED: pm_assets has NO foreign key to asset_nodes - it carries its own asset_name, tag_id, location, category - yet they describe the SAME machines: 21 distinct names on each side, all 21 present in both, zero exclusive to pm_assets. Two tables, one plant, joined only by a string. That is the name-is-not-an-identity shape at the schema level, and it is why the counts can drift apart silently: nothing structurally forces them to agree, so a rename or a rejected asset moves one number and not the other. ★MY PROBE ALSO NEARLY FILED THE WRONG BUG: the regex matched '30 ASSETS' out of a PM-overdue sentence and compared it to the approved-asset count, which is comparing two different things and calling it a defect. Reading the actual line is what turned a false arithmetic claim into a true structural one. Remaining: the naming/denominator decision (do these two counts need one vocabulary, or one registry), plus sum-of-rounded vs rounded-sum and the precision-to-domain review. || ★ROUNDING-CONSISTENCY SWEEP: A CLEAN NEGATIVE, RECORDED AS EVIDENCE RATHER THAN SILENCE (2026-08-28). This trajectory's sharpest probe is 'the same value rounded differently on two surfaces = apparent disagreement'. Swept every .toFixed() call across all root pages plus utils.js and voice-handler.js, resolving each to the EXPRESSION being rounded and grouping by domain metric (mtbf, mttr, oee, availability, compliance, risk_score, uptime, performance, quality, confidence). Two candidates surfaced and BOTH survive inspection as deliberate, not drifted: (1) analytics-report renders MTBF at 0dp on line 1228 and 1dp on lines 1563/1692/1695/1805 — but 1228 is `mtbfDays`, the FLEET AGGREGATE headline, while the others are `p.mtbf_days` / `r.mtbf_days`, PER-ASSET detail. Different variables, different scopes; a coarse headline over fine detail is an editorial choice, and no single value is shown twice at two precisions. (2) risk_score is 2dp in voice-handler's AI grounding and 0dp in the report — grounding wants precision for a model, a report wants readability for a person, and again it is not one value rendered two ways. `compliance` is consistent at 0dp throughout. ★RECORDED BECAUSE A NEGATIVE THAT WENT UNRECORDED IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A PROBE NEVER RUN — the sweep happened, the method is repeatable, and the answer is that this class is currently clean. My first pass at this DID produce false hits ('class', 'const', 'null') by capturing whatever token preceded .toFixed rather than the rounded expression; those were discarded as instrument noise, not filed. The un-swept remainder of this trajectory is sum-of-rounded vs rounded-sum and currency formatting, which this scan does not reach. || ★I BROKE THIS TRAJECTORY'S OWN RULE AND ITS GATE CAUGHT ME (2026-08-28). Earlier in this same session I added a mint-voucher confirm to founder-console - a good change, naming the consequence before a live discount code exists - and built its terms string by hand: kind === 'percent' ? value + '%% off' : '₱' + value + ' off'. The money-formatting gate went RED on it within the hour, on the exact ground this trajectory was written to defend: an absent value renders as '₱ off' or '₱undefined off' instead of a gap, and whFmtPeso exists precisely so that absent and zero stop looking alike. The same file already used the helper six times; I reached for string concatenation anyway. ★FIXED and re-verified PASS ('5 money surfaces render amounts through the helper that tells absent from zero'). ★THE PART WORTH KEEPING: this is what a gate is FOR, and it is a stronger endorsement of the rule than any of my earlier reasoning about it. The confirm I wrote is the last thing an owner reads before minting a code that costs real money on every redemption - the single worst place on the platform for a number that renders confidently and wrongly - and I still had to be caught by the machine rather than by care. A rule that only holds while its author is paying attention is not a rule; the gate is what makes it one. pct 70 -> 84. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate money-formatting re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-06 with the Playwright MCP + the postgres MCP via tools/prove_tile_canonical.mjs (gate tile-canonical): 15/15 rendered tiles on hive.html and inventory.html equal the canonical query behind them - PM overdue 29, low stock 2, own open jobs 6, readiness 52, open WOs 10, members 3, adoption risk 39, jobs today 0, approval badge 30, parts 27/2/1/1/2/0. Three of my four first mismatches were MY query, not the page: v_logbook_truth.wo_state is NULL on all 944 rows (an optional field logbook.html guards), the low tile counts low+critical, and healthy stock is stockStatus()'s MIDDLE band excluding 21 surplus parts. The fourth was real and benign: v_asset_truth ends WHERE status='approved' so the 3 pending asset_nodes are invisible to it - the badge is right because asset-hub reads the raw table, the view's COMMENT states the contract, and the drift auditor reports 0 drift reads.

trajectories.title: Media truth: photos at scale and in trouble
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, live gauntlet on logbook's photo capture, worker 390): OVERSIZE (21MB fixture) -> humane refusal WITH the limit stated ('Photo too large (max 20 MB).') and the input CLEARED for retry; WRONG FORMAT (a PDF wearing image bytes) -> the pipeline attempts compression then announces honestly ('Could not read the photo: Image decode failed'), no preview, no crash, zero pageerrors. The 5MB tier guard exists on the entry-photo path (logbook:3637) and the compression-fallback refusal at 5051. NIT: 'Image decode failed' is slightly technical (names the truth, could name the remedy). Remaining: mid-upload interruption (T122 choreography), photo-in-offline-queue (T14 seam), storage-full injection, deletion-deletes-storage verification (T164 seam), thumbnail strategy under throttle (wave close). DELETION-DELETES-STORAGE PROBED + FIXED 2026-08-26: platform-wide there was NO storage delete ANYWHERE (only two upload sites, both marketplace), and the marketplace-listings bucket is PUBLIC - so deleting a listing left its photo permanently reachable by URL while the confirm said 'This cannot be undone', true of the row and quietly false of the image. FIXED: handleDelete now derives the object key from the public URL minted at upload (bucket/<uuid>.jpg) and removes it AFTER the row delete, best-effort so a storage hiccup can never block the delete the person asked for. PROVEN live end-to-end: probe object uploaded, the SAME key-derivation returned the exact key, remove() succeeded, storage.objects back to 0 probe rows. Remaining: mid-upload interruption (T122 choreography), photo-in-offline-queue (T14 seam), storage-full injection, thumbnail strategy under throttle. FIX-EVERY-PATH pass same day: the orphan had a SECOND, more frequent source - REPLACING a listing image on edit left the old object in the public bucket, and edits run far more often than deletes. Now cleaned on the edit path too, guarded so it only removes when the URL actually changed AND the old object is ours (a seller may paste an external URL), best-effort after the row update so cleanup can never cost the seller their edit. Coverage CHECKED not assumed: marketplace.html's two delete sites are saved-searches and watchlist rows - neither deletes a listing - so the seller page owns both image lifecycles. || LOCKED 2026-08-28. Both image lifecycles were fixed and left ungated - and this is the class where an ungated fix is most likely to half-rot, because the two blocks are NEAR-IDENTICAL and sit far apart in one file: an edit to one reads as complete. Gate a-removed-image-actually-leaves requires TWO remove() sites, the edit path's changed-and-ours guards, and TWO best-effort catch blocks so cleanup can never throw into the write. Selftest 5/5. ★AND ITS OWNERSHIP NEGATIVE WAS VACUOUS ON THE FIRST CUT for the same reason the code was fragile: a whole-file search for indexOf(_marker) is satisfied by the DELETE path's own copy, so deleting the EDIT path's guard left the file matching and the test passed while detecting nothing. Scoped to the edit block. Remaining: storage-full injection, thumbnail strategy under throttle (T37's lane). pct -> 82. pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-06 via tools/prove_cap_honesty.mjs (gate cap-honesty) paired with tools/prove_data_honesty.mjs (gate data-honesty), using the postgres MCP for the truth behind each cap: 52 capped LIST reads have rows hidden behind them today and every one sits on a page carrying cap wording or a has-more control; 155 caps have nothing behind them yet and are reported n/a, never ok; and on the glass, 28/28 surfaces state their basis, agree with their own source-chip windows, and show no cap as a total. Three calibrations: a .limit(1) is a lookup, not a cap (eight single-row reads were flagged first); a fixed character window is the wrong scope, because logbook.html's capped read sits at line 1865 while the 'Showing N entries (load more below)' label that explains it is at line 4241, 2,400 lines away; and EITHER cap wording OR a has-more control is enough, since index.html's Top-5 risk teaser needs no pagination.

trajectories.title: Legacy import: the Excel plant onboards
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, premise resolved POSITIVE): the CSV import EXISTS on integrations.html - PapaParse (CSV) + SheetJS (xlsx) lazy-loaded after file pick (A4 CWV discipline), the cmms_import_v1 capture contract governs the payload, and the copy matches the learn cluster's migration promise ('Export a CSV and upload it here. One upload brings your whole history into WorkHive') plus the post-import Live Sync story - the cmms-vs-excel content's claim has a real implementation behind it (claim-honesty resolves clean). Remaining: the MESSY-CSV walk (naming chaos fixture through the import - preview/consent per T92's bars, duplicate-name handling T127, encoding survival T128), field-mapping ergonomics, a failed-row report probe (wave close).  || WALKED LIVE 2026-08-26, AND THE TRAJECTORY'S PREMISE IS REFUTED. The spec expected the import path to be ABSENT and this trajectory to end as a scoped product decision with the learn articles' claims trued down. The opposite is true: integrations.html ships a working CSV/Excel importer, and the learn-page claims about it are ACCURATE. Driven as an operator, not by poking internals: pick a source system (sap_pm / maximo / generic / auto) -> pick an entity (work_order / asset / pm_schedule / inventory) -> upload -> Step 3 field mapping. A generic asset export (asset_id, name, type, location, manufacturer) came back with 5 OF 5 COLUMNS AUTO-MAPPED CORRECTLY (external_id<-asset_id, name<-name, type<-type, location<-location, manufacturer<-manufacturer), 0 pageerrors. The specific marketing claim - 'The CSV importer includes a visual column-mapping step' - is TRUE: buildMappingTable() renders a map-table with a per-field select, a confidence cell and a preview table, plus an Auto-suggest button backed by per-system dictionaries (SAP's EQNR/EQKTX, Maximo's ASSETNUM, and a generic set). ★FOUR INSTRUMENT ERRORS ON THE WAY, NONE BANKED, and they are the reusable lesson for this page: (1) I counted '.map-table select' when the matcher keys on [data-field]; (2) I jumped straight to goStep(3), leaving _entityType at its work_order default while feeding ASSET headers, which correctly matched almost nothing; (3) I set window._entityType and read window._headers when the real state lives in CLOSURE variables inside the page's IIFE - unreachable from outside; (4) I tried to click the entity cards before choosing a SOURCE, and #entity-section is display:none until then. Every apparent failure was mine; the product was correct each time. Remaining: the post-import verification walk (do the rows land as approved/pending assets, and is the T92 consent/preview bar met), and the SAP/Maximo dictionary accuracy against a real export. (Recorded as WALKED/25 rather than a higher pct: the registry's own gate refused 'walked' with pct 40, and it was right to - the pct is a status marker, not a quality score, and no product fix was needed because nothing was broken. The depth of the walk belongs in this basis, not in a number that would imply fixes that do not exist.) || THE POST-IMPORT VERIFICATION WALK IS DONE, AND IT FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN THE CONSENT SURFACE (2026-08-28). Drove the whole five-step wizard live as the supervisor with a 4-column Maximo asset export. WHERE THE ROWS LAND, answering this trajectory's own question: as status 'approved', NOT pending - submitted_by and approved_by both the importer, approved_at set, so a bulk import bypasses the review queue by design. Provenance IS kept (external_ids {source_external_id}, plus an external_sync row per asset and one cmms_audit_log entry), which is what makes the auto-approval defensible rather than silent; whether an import SHOULD bypass review is a product decision, not a defect, and it is recorded here rather than changed. ★THE DEFECT IS WHAT THE PREVIEW DOES NOT SAY. Step 4 warned when a WORKHIVE FIELD had no source column and NEVER when a SOURCE COLUMN had no WorkHive field - the first protects the schema, the second protects the user's data, and carrying data across is the whole point of a legacy import. MEASURED: my export's EQTYPE header is in neither dictionary, so all three assets landed iso_class 'General' with the equipment type simply gone, under a preview reading '3 rows - 3 ready to import - all valid' and an EMPTY warnings box. Someone bringing five years of plant history across has no other moment to notice a column did not make the trip. FIXED: the preview now names every unmapped source column and points at Step 3 - live 'i 1 column in your file is not mapped and will not be imported: EQTYPE.' Deliberately INFO, not a warning, because an unmapped column is often intentional; it must be said, not made alarming. ★AND THE DICTIONARY IS VINDICATED, which I nearly recorded the other way: rerunning with Maximo's REAL header ASSETTYPE mapped all four columns and raised NO notice, so the dictionary knows the true column and my synthetic EQTYPE was the non-standard one - the product declined to guess, correctly. That clean-file control is now half the gate, because a notice that fires on every import is furniture nobody reads. ★A FIFTH INSTRUMENT ERROR for this page's list: my first Import click used a has-text selector that never reached startImport(), so the walk reported 'results not shown' with the DB untouched - I checked the baseline before believing it had failed. Locked as gate import-names-dropped-columns (6 assertions, teeth-proven: disabling the notice fails exactly the three that assert it), and READ-ONLY by construction - it stops at the preview, verified leaving the DB at its 96/16/14 baseline. STATUS locking/80: the walk and the consent fix are done and gated; the SAP dictionary still wants a real export to check against, which needs a file I do not have. || ★THE UNDO DID THE REVERSE OF ITS JOB - THE SESSION'S WORST DEFECT, FOUND BY PULLING ON THE CONFIRM COPY (2026-08-28). Sweeping confirms for 'names a control that does not exist' I read rollbackBatch's text: it promises to remove 'the corresponding rows created in that batch'. Its query matched target rows by worker_name + created_at BETWEEN the audit row's timestamp and +5min, and BOTH HALVES FAIL, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. The audit row is written AFTER the data rows - measured 51.3ms for asset_nodes and 88ms for external_sync - so every row the import created sits just BEFORE the window and .gte() excludes it; meanwhile anything the same person creates in the following five minutes is INSIDE it. MEASURED END TO END: imported 2 assets, hand-made 1 unrelated asset 10s later, pressed undo - the two IMPORTED assets SURVIVED, the unrelated one was DESTROYED, and the toast said 'Import rolled back successfully.' The control a person reaches for in a panic deleted the wrong data and reported success. Work orders were worse: logbook rows carry the SOURCE system's created_at (often years old) and logbook has NO external-id column, so an import-time window can never match them - that path was a guaranteed no-op. ★FIXED by matching BATCH MEMBERSHIP instead of time: external_sync is now READ before it is deleted (hence the order read -> targets -> sync -> audit), each entity's key recomputed exactly as the import wrote it (asset->tag, inventory->part_number, pm_schedule->tag_id from the stored payload), and the read is bounded by the batch's own recorded rows_written - the last N sync rows at-or-before the audit stamp ARE that batch, and the limit stops it reaching into an earlier one. Work-order rollbacks now SAY they cannot remove logbook entries automatically rather than silently no-op'ing, and the toast reports the count actually removed instead of a flat success. MEASURED AFTER: 'Import rolled back - 2 imported rows removed', with the bystander the only survivor. ★A NEARBY DESIGN GAP RECORDED, NOT FIXED: external_sync carries a workhive_id column meant for exactly this linkage and the importer never populates it; filling it at import time would make the rollback exact rather than merely bounded, but it changes the write path for all four entity types and this fix was already load-bearing. Locked as gate import-undo-removes-the-import (7 assertions, keeps a BYSTANDER row present throughout because 'the import was removed' and 'nothing else was' are two different claims; resurrection-proven - restoring the inverted window reddens exactly the imported-rows-gone and row-count assertions; writes and cleans up after itself, asserting no WH-PROBE-UNDOGATE row survives). pct 80 -> 92. || CLASS SWEPT, not just the instance (2026-08-28): the danger was never 'a time window' - most of the ~25 .gte('created_at') uses on the platform are relative DISPLAY windows ('last 7 days', 'today') where a row falling outside simply is not shown and nothing is lost. What made the rollback different is that it was a DESTRUCTIVE operation bounded by a window anchored on a record written AFTER its own subjects. Swept for that exact shape - a .delete() paired with any time bound - across every html/js file: ZERO remain. The rollback was the only one, so the class is extinct rather than the single case being patched. pct -> 100.
trajectories.note: ★PREMISE REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT, and worth recording as such rather than inventing a gap. The spec expected the answer to be 'no import path exists, so true up the learn articles' claims and spec one for Ian'. It exists and it WORKS. Driven live: integrations.html step 2 accepts a CSV through #file-input (PapaParse + SheetJS, lazy-loaded only after a file is chosen), and a 2-row/4-column CMMS export was read back as 'csv 2 rows - 4 columns - detected as GENERIC' with a Map Fields step offered next. 0 page errors. The first probe reported nothing because it set the file input while the wizard was still on step 1 - the wizard was right and the probe was wrong, which is the usual direction. AND THE CLAIMS ARE TRUE: connecting-workhive-to-sap-maximo-cmms promises 'batch CSV export and import for plants without API access', which is exactly what ships; cmms-vs-excel is cautionary ('do not attempt a full-plant migration'), not overselling. Nothing to true up here - the claim-honesty defect on this subject was on integrations.html's SYNC CADENCE and is fixed under T63. REMAINS: the mapping and commit steps (3-5), which write data and need probe hygiene; duplicate/merge consent on import (the T92 seam); and what an import does to a hive that already has assets.

trajectories.title: Seed/demo data honesty
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, 8-table probe-marker sweep on the local DB): ONE leaked probe row found and removed - a pm_completion from 2026-08-19 ('probe: checked, within tolerance', a prior session's residue; compliance recomputes on next read) - all other tables CLEAN (logbook/inventory/community/project_items/fmea/inquiries/schedule_items = 0), confirming this session's per-walk cleanup discipline held. Example-labeling: the Weibull worked-example pattern (Example... prefixed, baseline-exempt) verified in T26's walk; empty-state illustrations render as sentences, not fake rows. Remaining: the PROD sweep (Ian-gated - the prod smoke hive is his to delete), the sweep formalized as a scheduled gate (probe_marker_sweep in the Platform group), example-labeling coverage across the other worked-example surfaces (wave close).  || THE SWEEP WIDENED 2026-08-26 AND FOUND 245 SURVIVING MARKER ROWS. The earlier pass checked 8 tables and called them clean; a sweep across EVERY text column of the user-facing tables found: 3 rows in VOICE_JOURNAL_ENTRIES - probe transcripts AND the AI's replies to them, sitting in the platform's most private surface, inside a worker's own journal; 1 in LOGBOOK.knowledge ('probe: checked, within tolerance') - and note T136's earlier pass found and removed the pm_completion TWIN of that exact probe and missed the logbook copy, so one probe had two homes; and 241 in HIVE_AUDIT_LOG. ★THE AUDIT ROWS WERE MINE, FROM THE SAME DAY, and they are the lesson: my pending-submission prover created probe assets and deleted them, and the audit trigger honestly recorded every deletion. Those rows are TRUE - they describe things that really happened - but they describe objects that were never real, in a compliance-class table that the retention gate I built hours earlier correctly forbids any scheduled job from purging. A PROBE THAT TOUCHES AN AUDITED TABLE LEAVES RESIDUE ITS OWN CLEANUP CANNOT REACH, because the residue lands in a DIFFERENT table than the one it wrote to. Removing it required a deliberate, scoped, one-time delete - never a cron. AND THE GATE EARNED ITS KEEP ON ITS FIRST RUN: after my targeted WH-T108B cleanup it still found 34 rows under a marker I had not thought of (WH-EFFECT-PROBE, dating to 2026-08-18), proving the point that per-walk memory is not a mechanism. All 245 now removed and re-counted to zero; hive_audit_log holds 8,840 genuine rows. LOCKED BY gate no-probe-residue, scoped to user-facing tables and deliberately NOT the seeder's fixtures, since demo DATA is legitimate and a gate that could not tell seeded plant data from probe residue would fire forever. Remaining: the PROD marker sweep (Ian-gated) and the example-labeling check. || ★TWO GATES WERE FAILING ON DIRTY STATE, AND CLEARING THEM CHANGED A VERDICT (2026-08-28). This trajectory's own gate, no-probe-residue, was RED on one row: a hive_audit_log entry 'create_inventory_item / WH-EFFECT-PROBE-72872' from 2026-08-26, left behind when a scoped cleanup removed the inventory item but not the audit trail of its creation (0 live items carry the marker now, so the row was genuinely orphaned). One row is not much until you consider where it sits: a supervisor reading their plant's audit log saw a part creation that never happened. Removed; the gate is PASS. ★AND THE SECOND ONE MATTERED MORE. validate_cold_page_teaches was also RED, but not because a page failed - it REFUSED TO MEASURE, aborting because a probe account (wh-t175-probe@auth.workhiveph.com, 2026-08-27) was still standing. That is the right behaviour for a prover and it had a cost nobody had paid: with the gate silent, I had spent this same session concluding from ABSENCE that per-page first-run orientation was not a platform pattern. Removing the account (2 analytics_events rows, no hive membership) and re-running produced the real reading - 19 pages walked cold, 0 near-empty, 0 throwing - which REFUTES what I had written and corrected T175 from 72 to 88. ★THE POINT FOR THIS TRAJECTORY: probe residue is not only a cosmetic pollution of user-facing data. A leftover probe object also DISABLES the instrument that would have told the truth, and a disabled instrument is quietly replaced by somebody's inference. Cleanup discipline protects the measurements as much as the data. pct 70 -> 92. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: cleaned the WH-EFFECT-PROBE residue this gate flagged [1 voice_journal_entries AI-reply plus 2 hive_audit_log create_inventory_item rows in the Baguio hive] via a verified DELETE; no-probe-residue now PASSES. Awaiting the next full-board earn for locked. || LOCKED 2026-09-03: post-board promote - every named gate PASS on the 2026-09-02 full board (1028 PASS run). pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_data_reality.mjs (gate data-reality), 8/8 lenses clean, every RLS-sensitive read made as the person through PostgREST rather than as the owner. Three assets share the name 'Atlas Copco GA75+ VSD' and all three carry a distinguishing tag_id, so a person picking one is not guessing (T127). A 66-character entry mixing Filipino, an enye, a degree sign, an emoji and CJK round-tripped byte for byte (T128). The largest logbook this reader belongs to holds 944 entries and pages 50 at a time in order over 9 supporting indexes (T129). Demo data is named as demo on a page a person reads (T136). Four tables keep deleted rows recoverable and 8 audit triggers record who changed what (T137). A second save holding the updated_at it read MISSES once the row has moved, so concurrent edits are arbitrated rather than silently overwritten - confirmed only after the FIRST write was verified to have moved the stamp (T138). All 204 foreign keys now declare their delete behaviour; the one that did not is fixed in migration 20260907000001 (T139). The hive name is stored once, on the hive, so a rename reaches every surface that reads it (T140).
trajectories.note: ★A KILLED PROVER LEAVES RESIDUE ITS OWN CLEANUP CANNOT REACH (2026-08-26). Found a 'WH-T6T7-PROBE Plant' standing in the database ~14 hours with a live membership - not carelessness: prove_invite_code_round_trip's cleanup is in a finally AND asserts leftBehind===0, but a finally does not survive SIGKILL and a suite timeout kills. The cost was MEASUREMENT, not storage: it made the shared test account look two-hive, showed up in that account's switcher during an unrelated seating verification, and inflated the member counts read while sizing T61's fixture. TEN hand-rolled OC guards exist across EIGHT pages - asset-hub:3037, community:2179, founder-console:3053, integrations:1743, logbook:4417, platform-actions:1228, pm-scheduler:2216 and project-manager at 1971/2463/3208 - plus inventory through the central ocUpdate. AND THE PROPERTY THAT MATTERS HOLDS EVERYWHERE: all ten detect the ZERO-ROW case and TELL the person. That is the half that decides whether a guard helps at all - filtering on updated_at is easy, but if nothing notices the update changed nothing, the write vanishes, the form closes, and the person walks away believing they saved work that no longer exists. FALLBACK-LABELING PROBE RUN + A REAL FIX 2026-08-26 (via T143's ws-block): with the websocket blocked, hive's renderPresenceFallback said 'Members offline' and painted EVERY member with an offline dot - a positive claim about PEOPLE made from a fact about the NETWORK. Gate presence-unavailable-is-not-absent holds four clauses - names the LINK, asserts nothing about members, renders the hollow UNKNOWN dot rather than the solid away-dot (the dot is what people read at a glance), and carries EN+FIL. ★THE FOURTH CLAUSE KEEPS THE OTHER THREE HONEST: renderPresence()'s 'No one online yet' must stay DISTINCT, because that is TRUE when the link is UP and nobody is present - collapsing them would trade this defect for its mirror image, a real empty room reported as a network fault. trajectories.title: Live updates vs the user's focus (the repaint discipline)
trajectories.basis: flagship injection ran (community, realtime INSERT mid-typing): DRAFT SURVIVES (proven), the arrival renders via surgical stub-prepend + IO (no full re-render), the arrival is ANNOUNCED not imposed ('X posted in the hive' toast). The focus question is UNCONFIRMED: activeElement read BODY after inject but the tracer recorded NO focusout and NO node removal - a contradiction that means my evaluate-based focus may never have held at inject time (five-faults-toward-false-failure). NOT banked as a defect. The proper harness (real page.keyboard typing + initial-state control) = wave close.  || SUBJECT SET NARROWED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-08-26. T118's idle sweep established that the platform has exactly ONE polling surface: alert-hub, setInterval(loadAll, 60000) - every other page makes ZERO requests at rest, and the realtime consumers use websockets rather than repaint-on-a-timer. So the poll-destroys-focus class has one candidate, not twenty-four. TESTED IT, and the answer is that the class has no live instance THERE: alert-hub has no page-owned text input at all. It is a read-and-triage board of filter chips and buttons. The five inputs a naive scan finds are all visibility:hidden + pointer-events:none, belonging to CLOSED overlays (the nav-hub search, the AI widget, the feedback panel) - so a 60s refresh has nothing to steal focus from. ★TWO INSTRUMENT ERRORS ON THE WAY, NEITHER BANKED: the first run focused the closed hub's search box, got `active: false` BEFORE the refresh, and would have reported 'focus lost' from a control that never held focus - a vacuous red. The probe now ASSERTS the precondition and refuses to grade a control it could not focus. The second was the filter itself: getClientRects() is NON-ZERO for visibility:hidden, so hidden overlay inputs looked visible; display:none would have been excluded but visibility:hidden is not. REMAINING, and now precisely scoped: the REALTIME consumers (hive, community) are the real subjects - an arriving websocket update while someone types or reads. Their repaint discipline, not alert-hub's timer, is where this trajectory's risk actually lives. || FIXING->60 (2026-08-26): the repaint discipline of both named subjects MEASURED, and it holds - the risk this trajectory was opened for does not materialise on the live surfaces. community updates a single card via _updateRenderedCard() for the ordinary case and rebuilds #feed-list ONLY when a pin moves, which is a genuine reorder; and both composers sit OUTSIDE that container (the post box on the page, the reply box inside #thread-overlay). hive's realtime handlers reload targeted display cards (loadAdoptionCard, loadMaturityStairway) that hold no inputs at all. ★CONFIRMED IN THE LIVE DOM, NOT FROM SOURCE: a character-offset reading had suggested the post composer was NESTED inside #feed-list, which would have been a real defect - it is not, because #feed-list is an empty div that JS fills, and el.contains() says so. Static nesting analysis is exactly the thing that keeps being wrong here. Locked as 'repaint-spares-typing', which asserts CONTAINMENT rather than focus survival: a container a realtime handler replaces must hold no typing surface. That is the structural property that makes every path safe, versus focus-restoration code that has to be right every time. ★THE FIRST TEETH TEST DID NOT FIRE and the reason is worth keeping: a textarea pasted into the empty #feed-list markup is wiped by the page's own render before the probe looks. The faithful test puts one in the CARD TEMPLATE so the render places it inside the rebuilt container - the gate then reports 16 typing surfaces and fails. REMAINING: the arriving-update-announcement question (a '3 new entries' affordance versus the list moving under the reader) at wave close. || GATES RECORDED 2026-08-27: repaint-spares-typing. The basis already named this instrument as built and it IS registered in run_platform_checks and green — the gates field was simply never filled, so the registry understated what this trajectory owns. Verified registered + exit 0 before recording; nothing about the work changed, only the bookkeeping. || THE ANNOUNCEMENT QUESTION IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS BETTER THAN THE PATTERN I WENT LOOKING FOR (2026-08-28). I searched every page for a '3 new entries' affordance and found none, which read like an absence until I read what the live surfaces actually DO. community's postgres_changes handlers are surgical rather than wholesale: INSERT unshifts the row into state and calls _prependPostCard(payload.new) - one card inserted, NOT a list re-render - and announces the arrival with a toast that prioritises a mention over the generic notice ('X mentioned you in a post' beats 'X posted in the hive'). UPDATE computes whether the post is even onScreen before touching the DOM. DELETE calls _removePostCard(id) rather than rebuilding. That is the property the affordance pattern exists to buy - freshness that does not repaint the list under a reader - obtained by never repainting the list at all, so a draft, a focus ring and a scroll position all survive an arriving update by construction. The residual is honest and small: a prepend still shifts content down for someone scrolled to the very top, which one card at a time is a different class from the 15s poll that threw a keyboard user to body. pct 60 -> 75. Remaining: the same reading for the other live surfaces, and a mid-typing injection to prove focus survives rather than inferring it from the DOM strategy. || ★THE FOCUS-DESTROYING REPAINT IS NOT PRESENT ON THE FASTEST TIMER, AND THE DISCIPLINE IS APPLIED WHERE IT MATTERS (2026-08-28). The recorded hazard for this trajectory is a live poll repainting a region a keyboard user is typing in, throwing focus to body every cycle. Traced the actual timers: only 11 pages use setInterval at all, and the FASTEST anywhere is marketplace's 10-second tick. Read it - it updates a live service-job tracking MAP and a text note (note.textContent), not a form and not a list. There is no focusable content inside what it repaints, so the hazard cannot arise there. It also degrades honestly: when the job leaves the active window it writes 'Tracking ended: the job is no longer active.' and clears its own interval, rather than polling forever against a request that is over. ★AND THE PAGES THAT DO REPAINT FORM-BEARING REGIONS CARRY THE GUARD: community, index, logbook, project-manager and resume all reference document.activeElement, which is the fix this class needs - capture what has focus, repaint, restore. That the five are exactly the surfaces with composers, filters and editable lists, while the map-updating page does not bother, is the shape of a discipline applied deliberately rather than sprayed everywhere. ★WHAT IS NOT PROVEN is the harder half of this trajectory: that an arriving update while a user is mid-scroll ANNOUNCES itself rather than imposing itself ('3 new entries' versus a list that jumps). That needs the mid-interaction injection this trajectory specs, and is not claimed. pct 75 -> 86. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED (fix+gate) - all assigned gates PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] pct -> 100. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_interrupted_person.mjs (gate interrupted-person), 5/5 lenses clean. The shared layer notices the page being backgrounded and returning, and all 5 composing surfaces hold a draft across it, so a phone call mid-form does not cost what was typed (T122). Six pages repaint on a timer and ALL SIX consult where the person's focus is before redrawing - the discipline this platform learned after a 15-second poll threw a keyboard user to body (T142). Nothing streams, so there is no stream left running against a quota when someone walks away (T146). A platform-wide search ships, backed by a registry of destinations rather than one page's list, reachable from 32 of 38 pages (T173). FIXED: 10 of 38 pages offered a person opening them for the first time NO explanation at all - analytics-report, founder-console, integrations, inventory, marketplace, pm-scheduler, project-manager, resume and skillmatrix now each carry a 'How this page works' disclosure written for that page in the platform's existing wh-help idiom, and promo-poster is excluded with its reason stated, being a printable poster rather than a surface anyone navigates (T175). THE LENS WAS WRONG FOUR TIMES AND THE LAST ONE IS THE LESSON: it counted a 250ms registration RETRY as a repaint that steals focus; then swung to counting ZERO because setInterval(loadAll, 60000) passes a bare function reference and it demanded an inline body; then named architecture.html unexplained though it opens with 'How to read this map'. I chased that last one through three plausible theories - an injected guide chip, a too-narrow class name, my own strip() eating the markup - and every one was wrong. The actual cause was invisible: writing the file through a shell heredoc had turned two word-boundary escapes into literal U+0008 BACKSPACE bytes, so the pattern was hunting for a control character no page contains. WHEN A REGEX DISAGREES WITH THE SAME REGEX RUN ELSEWHERE, COMPARE THE BYTES BEFORE COMPARING THE LOGIC.

trajectories.title: Realtime degradation honesty
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, routeWebSocket block on the flagship realtime surface): with all 4 realtime sockets REFUSED at connect, hive.html is HONEST - the conn pill paints 'Offline' (red, surfaced only when degraded per its silence-is-golden design), renderPresenceFallback paints the roster from the DB read, and the feed shows its loaded rows; the connTimeout + status-callback machinery (utils rtConn's class) held. ONE RETRACTED false finding: my probe hunted 'presence unavailable/updates paused' vocabulary and missed the actual pill - the oracle-vocabulary lesson, third instance today. THE NIT recorded: the source chip's 'Live data' (true about the LOADED data) sits adjacent to the pill's 'Offline' (true about the LINK) - two true notices that read as a contradiction (the two-notices class); a wording review for the degraded state. Remaining: the ws-block SWEEP across the other realtime consumers (38 subscriptions - which freeze silently without rtConn), auto-recovery on unblock, polling-fallback presence probes (wave close). UPDATE (same day, the nit FIXED + verified): setConn now patches the source chip's freshness word when the link degrades ('Loaded data - live updates paused', restored on reconnect) - under the ws-block probe the two notices now agree; degradedSaid flipped true. hive.html rides the v239 shell bump. WS-BLOCK SWEEP MEASURED + 10 HANGS GUARDED 2026-08-26. Census across every realtime consumer: guarded already (achievements, alert-hub, dayplanner, inventory, logbook, marketplace, pm-scheduler, project-manager); UNGUARDED were hive (7 bare subscribes), community (2) and asset-hub (1) - the silent-freeze class, since supabase's subscribe callback may never fire at all when a plant firewall eats the websocket. All 10 now ride rtConn(), verified: channels still establish normally (hive 7, community 3) with zero pageerrors. HONEST FINDING on the second half: those three pages were NOT silent to the user - each already reports link state ONCE at page level (hive/community setConn + presence fallback, asset-hub setLiveChip), which is the right shape per the degradation-precedence draft (one notice, not one per channel). So the gap was the HANG, not the notice, and the hang is closed. Instrument note: wrapping window.rtConn to count settlements does NOT work - utils.js's top-level function declaration re-creates the global binding after an addInitScript accessor, so the observable consequence (the conn pill) is the honest probe. Remaining: auto-recovery on unblock, polling-fallback presence probes. || AUTO-RECOVERY ON UNBLOCK — PROVEN 2026-08-27, and the product is fine: with the websocket blocked the channel degrades correctly (getChannels 1, joined 0 - the subscription exists and is simply not connected), and within ~15 SECONDS of the path being restored it rejoins (joined 1). A plant firewall blip does not cost the rest of the shift, and nobody has to press anything - which matters most on the surfaces that have no one standing at them. ★GETTING THERE TOOK THREE PROBES AND THE FIRST TWO WERE BOTH WRONG, in ways worth writing down because the second was genuinely convincing. (1) CDP Network.setBlockedURLs does NOT block a WebSocket upgrade - it governs HTTP - so the 'blocked' phase measured a perfectly healthy connection (joined 1) while I believed I was testing an outage. (2) Switching to routeWebSocket blocked for real, but Playwright serves a ROUTED socket from the handler unless connectToServer() is called, so after the block lifted my handler stopped closing and simply never forwarded - every client retry hung against my mock. That probe reported joined 0 across EIGHT polls over TWO MINUTES, which is exactly the shape of evidence that gets believed: consistent, repeated, and patient enough to look rigorous. It would have banked 'realtime never auto-recovers' against a client that reconnects in fifteen seconds. The tell was structural rather than statistical - an intercepted socket must be forwarded, or the handler IS the outage. ★THE OBSERVABLE IS NOW KNOWN for future probes: db.getChannels() with state==='joined', not the connectivity pill, which reads 'Online' throughout because it reports NETWORK reachability and a blocked websocket is not an offline device. Remaining: polling-fallback presence probes. pct -> 85. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: BUILT + registered lock gate realtime-degradation-honest (setConn(offline)+renderPresenceFallback wired on the same degrade path); teeth + real-file PASS. Awaiting board earn. pct -> 92. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Notification/badge count races
trajectories.basis: convergence baseline PROVEN on the real element (.wh-hub-tile-badge): backdated seen + injected post -> badge '1' on logbook; visiting community stamps seen; back on logbook the badge is CLEARED (cross-page coherence via the shared key). Probe note: my first read matched the connectivity pill's decorative dot - selector discipline again. Self-exclusion pre-proven (the reference memory's badge-3-not-4). Remaining: the true RACE (mark-read WHILE a post arrives) + negative/stuck-count impossibility + two-tab coherence (wave close choreography). BADGE INTEGRITY WALKED + A LATENT WRONG-NUMBER FIXED 2026-08-26. Convergence half was already right: loadReplyCounts REBUILDS the map from the server on every feed load, so a stale or double-counted badge self-corrects, and the realtime handler skips your OWN replies so the optimistic +1 is never doubled. The real defect was the COUNT ITSELF: it was derived by fetching up to 500 reply ROWS and tallying them in the browser, so once a hive passes that cap every post's reply count reads LOW with nothing saying so (the row-cap-is-not-a-count class). Latent today (0 replies in the fixture) - which is exactly when it is cheap. FIXED: ask for the exact count alongside the rows and, only when the cap bit, tally each VISIBLE post with a head-count (bounded by page size, no N+1 on the normal path). PROVEN by forcing saturation against 7 seeded replies with the cap at 3: the old path would have shown 3, the fix returns 7; probe rows cleaned. Noted en route: the platform's own community_reply_rate_limit trigger refused a 7-row bulk insert by one author - the abuse guard working. Remaining: the true mark-read-WHILE-arriving race, two-tab coherence. || A BADGE RACE WAS ALREADY FOUND AND FIXED HERE, WITH THE RIGHT PATTERN (2026-08-27, read from the code). alert-hub's Plain-Read summary used to DOM-SCRAPE the rendered anomaly badge, and the comment records what that cost: 'the fire-and-forget loadAnomalyEngine could leave the verdict reading "All clear" for up to 60s while critical signals were still loading'. A verdict that says all-clear while the data is still arriving is the worst possible direction for that particular error - it is the alert page telling a supervisor there is nothing to look at. FIXED by holding the canonical count in module state, set by the renderer rather than read back off the DOM. ★AND IT STARTS AT null, NOT 0 - 'not yet known' is a THIRD state, distinct from 'no anomalies', and initialising to 0 would have reproduced the same false all-clear through a different door. That is the same distinction this session kept meeting elsewhere: an empty reading is not a measured zero. Also confirmed: alert_dismissals holds 0 rows, so the read-state store is unexercised in the fixture - which is why the remaining race is cheap to test now rather than after it has data. Remaining: the mark-read-WHILE-arriving race and two-tab badge coherence, both needing a seeded dismissal plus a two-context walk. || TWO-TAB COHERENCE WALKED LIVE, AND IT CONVERGES ON A STATED LAG (2026-08-27). Two tabs, one signed-in supervisor, one hive. Tab A acknowledged an alert through the real control ('Mark this alert as seen (keeps it, dims...)'): A's toggle went 0 -> 1. Tab B, untouched, still read 0 - and after a reload read 1. So the ack IS hive state that survives and propagates, and the only question is HOW FAST. ★ANSWERED FROM THE CODE RATHER THAN GUESSED: startRefresh runs setInterval(loadAll, 60000), so an untouched tab converges within 60 seconds; there is no realtime subscription on alert_dismissals (the postgres_changes channels on this page watch other tables), which for a low-frequency crew action is a reasonable trade rather than an omission. ★AND THE POLL PAUSES WHEN THE TAB IS HIDDEN (visibilitychange -> stopRefresh), which is the right call on a phone in a pocket and means the practical lag for a background tab is 'until you look at it again' - the moment a person could act on it anyway. So the badge is coherent within a bounded, deliberate window rather than stale forever, and acking is correctly HIVE state: the alert leaves the crew's unseen list, not just the acker's. Zero page errors across both tabs. Remaining: the mark-read-WHILE-arriving race itself, which needs a write landing during the 60s window rather than between polls. || LOCKED 2026-08-28. The two-tab measurement established the badge converges on a bounded, deliberate poll; what had no gate was the SEMANTIC half - that acking is hive-wide. Gate the-ack-scope-matches-its-promise holds the scope and the SENTENCE as one property: keyed hive_id+alert_key (never the actor), actor still recorded, and the toast naming both. If onConflict ever gained the actor, every teammate would have to ack the same plant condition separately AND the toast would become false - one edit breaking a behaviour and a promise together, which is why they are gated together rather than apart. Convergence is gated too (setInterval + the visibilitychange pause). Selftest 6/6. ★THE ATTRIBUTION NEGATIVE WAS VACUOUS TWICE BEFORE IT WAS REAL: first a whole-file search for `actor: WORKER_NAME` that an unrelated upsert and two comments satisfied, so deleting it from every dismissal still passed; then a mutation that removed the upsert prefix along with the field, tripping 'no upsert found' while the case was labelled 'losing attribution' - a negative that detects something real and proves nothing about the clause it names. Now a named helper removes only the field, verified to leave the statement intact and to fire exactly the attribution clause. Remaining: the mark-read-WHILE-arriving race, which needs a write landing inside the 60s window rather than between polls. || ★THE BADGE WAS COMPUTED ONCE PER PAGE LOAD AND NEVER AGAIN (2026-08-28). Probing convergence rather than the arithmetic: the arithmetic is already safe - _communityUnread = Math.max(0, pc+rc) cannot go negative, and both counts are head:true exact counts, so there is no drift to converge FROM. The failure is that nothing ever re-runs. nav-hub.js has NO storage, visibilitychange, focus or pageshow listener and NO interval; checkCommunityActivity has exactly ONE call site, scheduleCommunityCheck, which fires once at load with bounded retries. Meanwhile the freshness fact lives in localStorage - community.html stamps wh_community_last_seen:<hive> on visit and nav-hub reads it as the `since` bound - and localStorage is SHARED across a browser's tabs. So the information needed to clear the badge was already reaching every open tab; no listener consumed it. ★THE COST: a worker with the dashboard and community both open reads the posts, and the dashboard keeps saying '3 new' until they reload it - chrome advertising work already done, the same class as the phantom count T149 fixed one layer down, arrived at from the opposite direction (there the count was wrong, here the count was right and stale). Full page navigations recompute, which is why the common single-tab path always looked correct and this survived. ★FIX: a debounced `storage` listener keyed to that prefix. The event fires only in the OTHER tabs, which is precisely the gap - the visiting tab recomputes on its own next load. Debounced at 400ms because a re-check issues two counted reads. Deliberately NOT polling: a timer would re-read on every open page forever to serve chrome that is best-effort by design, and this codebase already has the 15s-poll lesson. ★VERIFICATION SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY: I verified the WIRING - the file parses, the listener's prefix matches BOTH writer spellings in community.html character-for-character, and _whNavClient (438) is in the same closure as the listener (569). I did NOT run a live two-tab round trip: checkCommunityActivity returns early without a session, so the full path needs an authed browser pair, and asserting my own re-implementation of the listener would be a test whose branches agree. ★KNOWN REMAINING: this converges a tab whose data went STALE; it does not wake a tab that missed NEW activity. A long-lived page - the wall-mounted display of T126 - still shows the count it loaded with. That needs realtime or polling and is a deliberate non-decision here, recorded not invented. ★LEDGER NOTE: I first recorded this as fixing/75, having set the new pct WITHOUT reading the old one - T144 was already locking/90 with a registered gate, so the write DOWNGRADED a locked trajectory and moved the programme backwards (80.69 -> 80.62). Caught by the total falling when the work had only grown. A new finding on an already-locked trajectory ADDS to it; it never erases the lock. Restored to locking/90 - this fix does not complete the remaining 10 (the lock's own verification) and does not reduce it either. Second occurrence of this exact slip in one session (T44 lost 14 points the same way): READ the current status before writing a pct, every time. pct -> 90. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: The approval race (T56's sharpest case)
trajectories.basis: THE RACE RAN under true concurrency (Lucena's two supervisors, unawaited-parallel Approve on one pending item): exactly-one-outcome in the DB (approved by Christine), the winner got the full receipt ('approved and published to hive'), and the LOSER was told kindly and truthfully ('That item was already handled by another supervisor') - the P6-C1 optimistic lock end-to-end with humane loser UX. Zero fixes needed. Remaining: register the two-context race choreography as a standing harness + audit-shows-one-action check (wave close).  || THE CHOREOGRAPHY IS NOW A STANDING HARNESS (2026-08-26) - this trajectory's own remaining item. The race had passed once by hand; a one-off pass protects nothing, because the optimistic guard is one .eq('status','pending') away from being deleted by somebody tidying a query, and the failure is INVISIBLE in normal use - you only meet it when two people happen to act at once. Re-measured through the harness: Christine Dizon won, Pablo Aguilar's update returned ZERO ROWS (a no-op the UI explains, not an error), the row ended approved by exactly one person, and the audit trail holds exactly ONE approval - the audit-shows-one-action check this trajectory asked for. ★IT PICKS ITS HIVE BY THE PROPERTY IT NEEDS, not by a hardcoded id: the first version pinned Baguio, which has ONE supervisor, and SKIPped - and a race test that cannot find two racers is not a pass. A pinned fixture would have quietly disabled this gate the day the seed changed. It now selects any hive with two active supervisors (Lucena, as the original walk used) and SKIPs honestly when none exists. ★CLEANUP ORDER MATTERED AND THE FIRST RUN HAD IT BACKWARDS: deleting the audit rows BEFORE the asset leaves the asset's own delete_asset_node row behind, because the delete itself fires the trigger. Row first, then the audit trail it wrote on the way out - the same audited-table residue lesson T136 recorded, met again from the other direction. LOCKED BY gate approval-race. || ★RACED IT FOR REAL, AND IT HOLDS (2026-08-28). This trajectory's sharpest question is whether two supervisors approving the SAME pending item within a second produce exactly one outcome. Tested with TRUE concurrency rather than two awaited calls - two separate psql transactions, each opening, sleeping 300ms so their windows genuinely overlap, then running the client's own guarded statement. Result: A returned UPDATE 1 and B returned UPDATE 0; the row ended approved by Supervisor A alone. The compare-and-set (.eq('status','pending') inside the WHERE) is what does it - B's update matched zero rows because A had already moved the status, so the second write cannot re-flip a resolved item. Baseline captured before the race and the row restored to pending afterwards (12 pending before, 12 after, approved_by null). ★AND THE LOSER'S UX IS ALREADY RIGHT, which is the half this trajectory cared about most: the client .select('id')s after the update precisely to detect the 0-row no-op, and on detecting it says 'That item was already handled by another supervisor.' - in English AND Filipino - then prunes the item from the local queue and re-renders. It is a clean return, not an error path, so the loser is told what happened rather than shown a failure for a thing that did not fail. ★BOTH PATHS, NOT JUST THE WALKED ONE: reject carries the identical optimistic lock, the identical 0-row branch and the identical message. The 'fix every path' discipline was applied here before I arrived. ★THE ONE GAP vs this trajectory's own spec ('told already handled by X'): the message says 'another supervisor', not WHICH one. Naming the actor needs a read-back of the row that resolved it, and is a small improvement rather than a defect - the current sentence is honest and actionable without it. pct 60 -> 84; what remains is the two-context UI-level walk and the audit-shows-one-action assertion at the glass. || ★EXACTLY-ONE-OUTCOME PROVEN IN THE DATABASE, AND THE LOSER IS TREATED WELL (2026-08-28). The guard is a genuine compare-and-set, not a blind update: the approval writes .eq('id',id).eq('hive_id',HIVE_ID).eq('status','pending').select('id'), so the predicate refuses a second writer AND the returned rows tell the caller which one it was. PROVEN on a real pending row rather than argued: two updates carrying the same status='pending' predicate against one asset_node gave writer A 1 affected row, writer B 0 affected rows, final status approved - one outcome, and the loser is distinguishable. (The probe ran inside a transaction that rolled back, so no approval state moved.) ★AND THE LOSER'S UX IS THE PART MOST IMPLEMENTATIONS GET WRONG. Zero rows is handled as its own branch, separate from `error`, with its own sentence: 'That item was already handled by another supervisor' - bilingual, and the Filipino is idiomatic rather than translated ('Naunahan ka na ng ibang supervisor diyan' - someone got ahead of you). It is not an error, not a silence, and not a retry prompt for something that cannot be retried. Then it PRUNES the item from the local queue and re-renders, so the loser's screen converges to the truth instead of holding a phantom pending card they would click again. The error branch is separately honest about state - 'The approval did not go through. The item is still pending' - which tells the supervisor what is true of the ITEM, not merely that something failed. ★WHAT REMAINS is the instrument, not the behaviour: this trajectory specs a two-CONTEXT concurrent-write choreography, two real browsers racing the same card, which would prove the whole path end to end rather than its database and client halves separately. The behaviour is verified; the live race is not yet automated. pct 84 -> 92. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: the fix is verified and the registered gate approval-race PASSES standalone (re-run this session). Awaiting the next full-board earn to promote to locked. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Streaming AI responses & interruption
trajectories.basis: receipts assembled: the platform's AI replies are not streamed (bubbles land whole - T16), so the cancel semantics live on the LONG-RUN surfaces: analytics-report now has the flagship (AbortController + calm cancelled state + no zombie paint, proven mid-run); navigate-away orphan-writes are answered by T12's persist-first (the note is banked before the reply; an abandoned reply leaves reply=null, never a lost note).
