An unbounded call to a slow endpoint has no failure mode at all, only a spinner, which is worse than an error because an error tells someone what to do next. ★THE GATE WRITTEN TO LOCK THAT FIX IMMEDIATELY FOUND THREE MORE: report-sender's transcribe, voice-handler's transcribe, and analytics' ORCHESTRATOR - the longest-running call on the platform, where a supervisor waiting on an AI report could not distinguish 'still thinking' from 'never coming back'. All four now route through the platform's own fetchWithTimeout rather than a second hand-rolled controller (the install-the-guard rule): it already owns the AbortController, the transport-retry policy and the null-on-abort contract, and each site now says what happened and what survived. ★BOUNDS SIZED FOR THE SLOWEST LEGITIMATE SUCCESS, NOT A DEVELOPER'S PATIENCE: 45s for a long spoken entry over a weak uplink, 120s for a full analytics phase. A timeout tuned short turns working software into a lottery for the plants furthest from the server. LOCKED BY gate long-fetch-bounded (11 slow fetches, all bounded). Remaining unchanged: the mid-stream choreography IF streaming ever ships - the platform's AI replies still land whole, so there is no stream to interrupt today. || ★A ZOMBIE FROM ONE QUESTION COULD MISLABEL THE NEXT ONE - found, fixed, proven (2026-08-28). This trajectory asks whether a cancelled or superseded AI call can 'mutate later'. On the assistant it could. The request is BOUNDED, which is the good half: _raceGatewayData races the gateway invoke against a 25s ceiling and falls back to the personal assistant rather than hang behind the gateway's own 60s budget, so there is no never-settling promise here. But Promise.race does not CANCEL the loser, and the losing invoke's .then/.catch still wrote window.__whGatewayFailure whenever it eventually landed. That global is reset at the top of every call and read afterwards to choose the sentence the person sees - rate-limited, timed out, or failed. So: ask A times out, worker asks B, A's invoke finally resolves and overwrites the global, B fails and is explained using A's cause. ★THE COST IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE TAXONOMY: whAiError exists to send someone to the RIGHT remedy, and this hands them the wrong one - told to wait out a rate limit when a retry would work, or told to retry into a wall. And it needs no unusual conditions: one slow ask followed by any second ask. ★FIX: each race is stamped with a generation and a late handler may only write while it is still current. The zombie still resolves - it cannot be cancelled - but it can no longer speak for a question nobody asked it. ★PROVEN, AND MY FIRST TEST DID NOT PROVE IT: I set the zombie to write the same value the second request wrote, so guarded and unguarded produced identical output and the test discriminated nothing. Re-run with A rate-limited and B a plain error: unguarded, B's 'error' becomes 'rate_limit' when A lands; guarded, it stays 'error'. A test whose two branches agree is not a passing test, it is an unasked question. ★WHAT REMAINS: there is still no user-facing STOP - a worker who changes their mind waits out the 25 seconds. pct 60 -> 78. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED (fix+gate) - all assigned gates PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] pct -> 100. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_interrupted_person.mjs (gate interrupted-person), 5/5 lenses clean. The shared layer notices the page being backgrounded and returning, and all 5 composing surfaces hold a draft across it, so a phone call mid-form does not cost what was typed (T122). Six pages repaint on a timer and ALL SIX consult where the person's focus is before redrawing - the discipline this platform learned after a 15-second poll threw a keyboard user to body (T142). Nothing streams, so there is no stream left running against a quota when someone walks away (T146). A platform-wide search ships, backed by a registry of destinations rather than one page's list, reachable from 32 of 38 pages (T173). FIXED: 10 of 38 pages offered a person opening them for the first time NO explanation at all - analytics-report, founder-console, integrations, inventory, marketplace, pm-scheduler, project-manager, resume and skillmatrix now each carry a 'How this page works' disclosure written for that page in the platform's existing wh-help idiom, and promo-poster is excluded with its reason stated, being a printable poster rather than a surface anyone navigates (T175). THE LENS WAS WRONG FOUR TIMES AND THE LAST ONE IS THE LESSON: it counted a 250ms registration RETRY as a repaint that steals focus; then swung to counting ZERO because setInterval(loadAll, 60000) passes a bare function reference and it demanded an inline body; then named architecture.html unexplained though it opens with 'How to read this map'. I chased that last one through three plausible theories - an injected guide chip, a too-narrow class name, my own strip() eating the markup - and every one was wrong. The actual cause was invisible: writing the file through a shell heredoc had turned two word-boundary escapes into literal U+0008 BACKSPACE bytes, so the pattern was hunting for a control character no page contains. WHEN A REGEX DISAGREES WITH THE SAME REGEX RUN ELSEWHERE, COMPARE THE BYTES BEFORE COMPARING THE LOGIC.

trajectories.title: Optimistic UI honesty audit
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, oracle-family census): the honesty machinery EXISTS as measured families - did_it_land ('after a slow action the person can tell whether it landed, without guessing') runs in the per-view interaction dims, PP3 governs the 0.1s ack, and this session added two reconciliation receipts (T88's landed-gated 'Noted' note - the ack only after the insert succeeds - and T56's approval loser toast). THE REMAINING HALF is the trajectory's real ask: the optimism REGISTRY (enumerate every surface painting success before server confirmation) + failure-reconciliation INJECTION per entry (does the optimistic paint roll back with an explanation) - the wave-close instrument. (wave close).  || THE REGISTRY WAS ATTEMPTED 2026-08-26 AND THE MECHANICAL APPROACH DOES NOT WORK - recorded as a NON-RESULT rather than banked, because a number I cannot defend is worse than none. The heuristic tried was 'a DOM paint followed shortly by an awaited write in the same handler', which returned 35 candidates across 8 pages; reading them, almost all are ORDINARY RENDERS (el.innerHTML = data.map(...), array builds, empty-state paints) and only community.html's allPosts.unshift is a genuine optimistic paint - and that one is the OFFLINE-QUEUE path, where optimism is correct because a queue stands behind it. A regex cannot tell 'painted before the server agreed' from 'rendered what the server just returned', and a gate built on this count would be argued with forever, the same trap prove_route_numbers.mjs refused to bank. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY WORK, for whoever picks this up: the optimistic set is very nearly the OFFLINE QUEUE set - the 8 pages that register a write queue are optimistic BY CONSTRUCTION, they paint success while holding the write, and T14's queue-drain work already covers whether that optimism reconciles. The residue beyond those is small enough to enumerate by READING each write handler, which is a per-surface human judgement rather than a pattern. Enumerating it that way is the real remaining task; the failure-reconciliation injection then hangs off that list. || FIXING->60 (2026-08-26): went at the enumeration this trajectory asked for and found something better than a list. ★THE PREMISE NEEDED CORRECTING FIRST: community's toggleReaction, the obvious optimistic-UI candidate, is NOT optimistic - it awaits the write and paints only `if (!error)`, which is the safe pessimistic pattern. The defect was the other half of that shape: BOTH branches had no else, so a failed reaction changed nothing and SAID nothing. Tapping an emoji and watching the count sit still is indistinguishable from a dead button, and the natural next move is to tap again - which is how a silent refusal becomes repeated writes. Fixed with the page's own vocabulary (submitReply uses whWriteError), and the add path names the one case where doing nothing IS correct: a duplicate reaction (23505) says 'You have already reacted with this emoji' rather than reporting a failure nobody can act on. VERIFIED LIVE with an injected 500 - the count correctly does not move AND the toast now reads 'Your reaction was not saved. Tap again to retry.', 0 pageerrors. Censused the shape platform-wide: 223 awaited db writes destructure `error`, and ZERO now guard with a bare `if (!error)` and no else. Locked as 'write-failure-speaks', resurrection-proven (removing the new else-branches puts it back to 1). ★THE GATE IS NARROW ON PURPOSE: it does not demand a message on every write - many correctly stay quiet because the render that follows IS the receipt - only on the shape where the code destructured the error, branched on it, and dropped it, which is never intentional. REMAINING: the genuinely OPTIMISTIC surfaces (paint before the await) still need enumerating; this pass establishes that the reaction path is not one of them. || GATES RECORDED 2026-08-27: write-failure-speaks. The basis already named this instrument as built and it IS registered in run_platform_checks and green — the gates field was simply never filled, so the registry understated what this trajectory owns. Verified registered + exit 0 before recording; nothing about the work changed, only the bookkeeping. || ONE OPTIMISTIC SURFACE READ END TO END, AND IT IS EXEMPLARY - PLUS AN HONEST FAILURE TO ENUMERATE THE REST (2026-08-27). alert-hub's acknowledgeAlert is genuinely optimistic: it toggles _seen and calls renderFeed() BEFORE awaiting the write. Every part of the contract is there. It refuses BEFORE the toggle when offline (whRequireOnline), because the earlier shape let an alert read as acknowledged while nothing was recorded. On an ONLINE failure the catch restores the exact prior value - `if (wasSeen) _seen[key] = true; else delete _seen[key]` - re-renders, and TELLS the person, bilingually: 'Could not save, restored' / 'Hindi na-save, ibinalik'. Paint, rollback, explanation. That is the reference implementation for this trajectory. ★I COULD NOT ENUMERATE THE OTHERS STATICALLY, AND SAYING SO IS THE FINDING. A sweep for 'a paint before an awaited write' returned 78 functions, 67 of them supposedly without rollback - and the list opens with hexToRgb (a colour utility), _personaLabel, renderFilters and loadSchedule: painters, loaders and helpers, not mutate-then-write flows. Checking the most plausible survivor, community's togglePin, showed it awaits the write FIRST and is not optimistic at all. The true pattern needs a LOCAL STATE MUTATION before the paint, which a regex cannot reliably distinguish from a render call that merely appears earlier in a function. So the count is not 67 and I will not record one. ★THE RIGHT INSTRUMENT IS RUNTIME, not static: intercept writes, fail them deliberately, and observe whether the UI reverts - the failure injection this platform already does for reads. Remaining: that injection sweep, which enumerates optimistic surfaces by BEHAVIOUR instead of guessing them from shape. || MORE EVIDENCE FOR THE SAME CONCLUSION, and it points the same way (2026-08-28). Re-attacked the enumeration statically from two fresh angles - a local boolean flip followed by a paint before an awaited write, and a classList mutation followed by an awaited write - and BOTH returned only false positives: asset-hub's hit was a modal close on an error path, index's was a signup error branch. Checked community's other two toggles by hand, toggleFlag and togglePublic: like togglePin before them, both AWAIT the write first and paint after, so they are not optimistic either. Three of three sampled toggles on the platform's most toggle-heavy page are await-first, which is weak evidence that optimistic painting is RARE here rather than widespread - but it stays evidence, not a count, for exactly the reason recorded above: a negative cannot be proven by failing to find positives with an instrument already shown to mis-classify. The runtime injection sweep remains the only thing that can answer this, and it remains the named next unit. || ★THE RUNTIME INSTRUMENT IS BUILT, AND IT HAS ITS FIRST SUBJECT (2026-08-28). This basis said the only thing that can answer the question is failure injection, not a regex. tools/prove_optimistic_ui_reconciles.mjs is that: it refuses every watchlist WRITE (reads pass through so the page still renders) and watches the control. FIRST SUBJECT, found the way the basis said surfaces must be found - by recorded BEHAVIOUR rather than shape: T95's walk had already noted marketplace's watchlist heart is 'optimistic either way'. RESULT: it is a textbook-correct optimistic surface. The heart fills before the server answers, a refused write takes the paint back to its real state, and the person is told why ('Could not update watchlist. Try again.'). ★THE PROVER ASSERTS THE OPTIMISM ITSELF, FIRST, and that assertion immediately earned its place: checking only 'the heart is empty after a failed write' passes just as happily on a heart that never filled - vacuously - which is the same shape as a gate that cannot go red. ★AND IT CAUGHT ME OUT ONCE: the first run reported 'the paint is not optimistic' (before=false, during=false) while the error toast proved the write had run and been refused. A Playwright route handler answers in MICROSECONDS, so the whole paint -> refusal -> rollback cycle finished before the first sample at 150ms - the instrument outran the thing it was measuring and reported absence. The refusal is now delayed 1.5s, which is what a real slow network would do, and the optimistic window becomes observable. Locked as gate optimistic-ui-reconciles. pct 68 -> 80: the instrument exists and one surface is proven; the remaining work is pointing it at the other write-bearing controls, which is now a matter of adding subjects rather than of not knowing how. || ★THE ENUMERATION IS DONE, AND THE ANSWER IS ONE (2026-08-28). Two failed static attempts are recorded above - 'a paint before an awaited write' returned 78 functions and 67 false positives, and a classList-then-write sweep found only error branches - because both searched for the SETUP of an optimistic write, which looks like ordinary code. The durable signature is the CLEANUP: an optimistic surface must, in its catch, REVERSE the local mutation it made before the await. Nothing else has a reason to mutate a Set/Map/array inside a catch. Searching for that shape across every page returns FIVE hits and only ONE is real: marketplace's toggleWatchlist, whose catch literally reads '/* Rollback the optimistic change */'. The other four are not UI rollbacks at all - two are test harnesses pushing to a results array (companion_battery, companion_surface_battery), one hides a BOM loader on failure (engineering-design), one hides an offline badge when the queue read throws (logbook), and hive's maturity gate hides a card when the gate check fails. CROSS-CHECKED against the behavioural evidence already gathered: community's togglePin, toggleFlag, togglePublic and toggleReaction all AWAIT the write first and paint on success - toggleReaction's success branch only touches the DOM inside `if (!error)`. So this platform paints optimistically in exactly one place, and that one place is proven by optimistic-ui-reconciles to paint before the server answers, take the paint back on a refusal, and say why. STATUS locking/95: the question this trajectory asked - WHICH surfaces are optimistic, and do they reconcile - is answered for the platform as it stands. What remains is standing vigilance rather than a search: the gate holds the one known surface honest, and the catch-reverses-a-mutation signature is now written down so the next one is found the cheap way. || ★THE OPTIMISM REGISTRY ATTEMPT — AND WHY ITS FIRST READING WAS DISCARDED RATHER THAN BANKED (2026-08-28). This trajectory calls for enumerating the surfaces that paint success before the server confirms. Built a static pass over all root pages finding a DOM mutation (classList/textContent/innerHTML) followed within 400 chars by an awaited db write: 22 sites across 10 surfaces, led by integrations (6), marketplace (6) and marketplace-seller (3). ★THEN SAMPLED THREE OF THEM AND THE READING COLLAPSED. marketplace:1573 is `btn.disabled = true; setAttribute('aria-busy','true'); textContent = 'Sending…'`; resume:1034 is the same shape with 'Deleting...'; skillmatrix:973 is not even a pre-write paint but a control RESET on an early-return path. All BUSY states, which are the CORRECT pattern and the opposite of the defect this trajectory hunts — the regex cannot tell a paint that says 'working' from a paint that says 'done', and only the second is optimism. 22 would therefore have been a fabricated denominator; it is recorded here as an instrument failure and NOT banked as a finding. ★THE INCIDENTAL POSITIVE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE INTENDED ONE: every sampled committing control sets `disabled` AND `aria-busy` alongside a verb-ing label, so the busy-state discipline (T41's double-tap concern, and its screen-reader half) is broadly adopted rather than spotty. The genuinely optimistic case remains marketplace's watchlist heart, which already has a prover (prove_optimistic_ui_reconciles.mjs, asserting the optimism itself so it cannot pass vacuously). A real registry needs a discriminator keyed to WHAT is painted — a success/final state versus a pending one — which the next pass owes. pct -> 72. || ★PCT FIELD CORRECTED DOWN TO MATCH THIS BASIS (2026-08-31). The field read 95 while the basis's own last word was 72 - a later note revised the number and only the prose was updated. Every one of the six rows found this way was inflated, never deflated, which is the direction drift always takes when nothing checks it: the number a reader trusts drifts up while the narrative underneath it says otherwise. Now gated by pct-matches-basis. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Multi-tab sanity
trajectories.basis: two-tab walk: sign-out in tab A cleared shared identity but tab B sat PAINTED-AND-STALE (looked signed in, identity gone; writes already T38-guarded). FIXED centrally in session-timeout.js (~24 pages): the storage event on wh_last_worker->null routes through the SAME return-carrying redirect as idle expiry - proven: tab B lands on index.html?signin=1&return=logbook.html%3Fstatus%3DOpen (exact page+params kept). First fix attempt guarded on ===null while activeWorker() returns '' - the falsy check was the fix. Remaining: draft-collision (same form two tabs), realtime socket multiplication count, hive-switch propagation (wave close). TWO REMAINING ITEMS MEASURED 2026-08-26. (1) DRAFT COLLISION, two tabs on one form: NO data loss - each tab keeps the text its user typed there, because applyDraft only fills fields that are UNTOUCHED, so a restore can never overwrite live typing. The stored slot is last-writer-wins ('TAB TWO text'), which is the defensible single-draft-per-form model: one person, one draft; a reopened tab picks up the most recent. Measured, not assumed - tab 1 refocused and kept its own text. (2) SOCKET MULTIPLICATION: 3 tabs on hive.html open 3 websockets and 7 channels EACH - 21 subscriptions for one person reading one board. That is the real cost item (server-side connection limits, battery on a phone left with tabs open); the platform has no cross-tab leader election. Recorded with numbers rather than adjectives; a shared-worker/leader-tab design is a scoped decision, not a silent default. Remaining: sign-out propagation across tabs, hive-switch propagation. || CROSS-TAB PROPAGATION — BOTH HALVES WALKED 2026-08-27 with two real tabs. SIGN-OUT already works and works WELL: clearing identity in tab A sent tab B to index.html?signin=1&reason=othertab&return=pm-scheduler.html - it noticed, NAMED the reason, and kept the destination so the person returns to what they were doing. HIVE SWITCH did not propagate at all: after switching to Manila Electronics Assembly in tab A, storage said Manila while tab B still rendered Baguio Textile Mills. That is the cross-tenant confusion T51 exists to prevent, and it is worse than an ordinary stale number because the person JUST switched and believes they are looking at the new plant. ★THE FIX TELLS RATHER THAN RELOADS, deliberately: auto-reloading somebody's other tab would discard a half-typed entry to fix a DISPLAY problem, and this platform's whole posture on interruption is that typed work survives. The notice names BOTH hives - 'You switched to Manila Electronics Assembly in another tab. This tab is still showing Baguio Textile Mills.' - so the reader knows which figures are in front of them, and offers Reload at a 44px target for when they choose. ★AND THE FIRST CUT NAMED THE SAME HIVE TWICE: a switch writes SEVERAL keys and storage events arrive one per key in write order, so reading wh_hive_name the instant the ID event landed read the name the switch had not replaced yet - 'You switched to Baguio... still showing Baguio', which reads like a bug in the switch rather than a stale tab. Deferred one tick, plus a guard that says 'another hive' neutrally if the name has not moved. Verified on 7 pages: session-timeout mounts, no stray notice, no errors. || GATE cross-tab-identity-propagates REGISTERED - and the registry gate caught the overstatement FIRST, for the second time today: 'locking' was set with the fix landed and no gate built, and validate_trajectory_registry.py refused it in the same words it used for T119. It holds six required clauses and one FORBIDDEN one - the hive handler must not call reload() itself - because the failure mode here is not only 'nothing happens' but 'something too aggressive happens'. trajectories.title: Broadcast semantics: hive announcements
trajectories.basis: reach proven two-context: supervisor posts an Announcement (category gated to supervisors in the composer) -> the WORKER's community feed carries it top-visible AND the cross-page hub FAB dot fires on logbook (the retention-badge primitive doing broadcast duty). The announcement-lock (hive vs public) pre-proven in its arc. Remaining: edit-doesnt-renotify probe + ack/read-tracking for safety notices (scoped decision for Ian - a real plant need) - wave close.  || EDIT-DOESN'T-RE-NOTIFY PROVEN 2026-08-26, and the proof corrected an assumption worth writing down. Editing a post does NOT re-notify the people it names - verified by BEHAVIOUR rather than by grepping call sites, since a grep that matched a comment instead of a call has fooled this project before. ★BUT THE REASON IT IS SAFE IS STRUCTURAL, NOT DEFENSIVE. The obvious assumption was that the 2-minute push dedupe would catch a re-notify if one ever slipped through. MEASURED: it does not. The dedupe compares WHOLE PAYLOADS, the push body carries the post's content snippet, and an edit changes that snippet - so the repeat reads as different news and a SECOND PUSH FIRES. The only thing standing between a supervisor's typo fix and a second buzz for everyone named in a safety announcement is that the EDIT PATH DOES NOT CALL notify_post_mentions (one call site, on create). Anyone adding that call in good faith would create a re-notify bug, and the dedupe would not save them. That fact is now asserted in gate community-notifications and recorded there as a blind spot rather than dressed up as a defence. NAMED RESIDUAL, the flip side: an edit that ADDS a new mention never notifies the newly-named person. That is the smaller harm - a missed notification beats spamming a hive on every typo - but it is a real asymmetry, not an oversight. Remaining: ack/read-tracking for safety notices, which stays Ian's decision (a real plant need, and a schema question). || ★A MODERATED POST STILL ANNOUNCED ITSELF TO EVERY WORKER - found, fixed, proven under real RLS (2026-08-28). Walking the reach test: an announcement is a supervisor-only POST CATEGORY, and community_posts carries ELEVEN triggers (rate limit, XP, daily cap, hive quota, announcement guard, submitter bind, touch, visibility/delete XP, moderation fields) - not one of them notifies. notify_post_mentions is the only notify path and it fires on explicit @mentions at CREATION only (one call site, keyed to _newPostId), so the repeat-edit probe PASSES cleanly: editing an announcement re-notifies nobody. That leaves the nav-hub badge as an announcement's ONLY reach - and the badge was counting posts the reader could not see. ★THE MECHANISM: the feed hides flagged posts in the CLIENT (community.html renderEntries gives non-supervisors or('flagged.eq.false,author_name.eq.<me>')); RLS does NOT - the member branch of community_posts_read is `auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND hive_id IN (my active hives)` with no flagged test at all. Only the PUBLIC branch checks flagged. So the row stays readable, and nav-hub.js counted v_community_posts_truth filtering only deleted_at. ★PROVEN AS THE WORKER, NOT FROM THE PREDICATE: seeded one flagged post by another author inside the 3-day window, set role authenticated with a real member's sub claim, and counted - badge 1, feed 0. RLS handing back that row is the empirical half; reading the policy only predicted it. Whole probe ran in a transaction that ROLLBACKed, so no cleanup step could fail: 0 probe rows after. ★THE COST: a supervisor REMOVES a post from worker view and it keeps advertising itself as unread activity to every one of them - moderation defeated at the badge layer, plus the plain 'N new' that opens to fewer. ★FIX: mirror the feed's own rule, role-aware via WHRoles.isSupervisor() (NOT getMode(), which is a user-switchable VIEW preference - a supervisor can set their hub to field). Supervisors keep counting flagged posts because their feed shows them; absent WHRoles we filter, so the failure direction is under-count rather than resurrecting a moderated post. After: badge 0 = feed 0. community_replies has NO flagged column, so replies are unaffected - the fix is posts-only. ★WHAT REMAINS, AND IT IS IAN'S CALL not a defect: an announcement gets NO announcement-shaped signal - it lands in the same undifferentiated 'N new' count as a good-morning post, and there is no acknowledgment/read tracking, so a supervisor cannot know who saw a safety notice. Both are product decisions (the roadmap itself flags ack tracking as 'maybe scoped-new'), so they are recorded, not invented. pct 60 -> 80. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - new gate validate_announcement_reach_moderation: the nav-hub badge (an announcement's only standing reach) filters .is('deleted_at', null) so a MODERATED post no longer lights it (RLS does not exclude soft-deletes for members), and trg_guard_community_announcement enforces supervisor-only broadcast. trajectories.title: Clock skew & device time lies
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, client-time write census): 16 client-side new Date().toISOString() stamps across logbook(8)/inventory(6)/pm-scheduler(2), including DOMAIN-time fields (pm_completions.completed_at) - a 30-min-fast phone writes future completions, and near midnight lands them on the WRONG DATE, touching both the (scope_item, worker, date) dedup uidx and the compliance day. THE DESIGN TENSION named honestly: client stamps are REQUIRED for offline-capture correctness (a queued completion synced 3 days later must carry its CAPTURE time, not the sync time), so server-default timestamps are NOT a blanket fix; the containable mitigation is skew DETECTION (a server-delta check on boot -> a banner when minutes off) + per-field review of which stamps are capture-time vs record-keeping. DB created_at defaults are server-side. Remaining: the skew-detection banner build, the per-field capture-vs-bookkeeping classification, clock-offset injection probes on temporal renderings (T132 shared) (wave close). SKEW DETECTOR BUILT + CLASSIFICATION MEASURED 2026-08-26. Measured exposure: 47 `*_at` fields across 12+ pages are written from the BROWSER's clock (approved_at, acknowledged_at, resolved_at, acted_at...), so a phone 30 minutes fast files an approval 30 minutes in the future and every relative time lies - capture timestamps are server-defaulted, the BOOKKEEPING ones are the exposed class. FIXED centrally rather than at 47 sites: utils.js gains whClockSkew(), which reads the server's own `Date` response HEADER (free on every request - no RPC, no table dependency), compares it to the MIDPOINT of its own request window so latency cannot masquerade as skew, and past a 3-minute tolerance paints a persistent banner naming the direction, the size, and the consequence ('times recorded when you approve or complete work will be off by that much'). WARN-ONLY by design: silently rewriting a user's timestamps would be its own lie. PROVEN both directions with Playwright clock control: silent at 0s delta (no false alarm), and at +40min it says '40 minutes ahead of real time'. Remaining: moving the bookkeeping writes server-side (a 47-site migration - scoped), clock-offset injection probes on temporal renderings (T132 shared). || THE CLOCK-SKEW SCAN RAN, AND THE FIRST READING WAS A FIXTURE ARTIFACT I ALMOST FILED AS A PRODUCT DEFECT (2026-08-28). Measured 69 write payloads across 17 files setting a timestamp from the CLIENT clock (new Date()/Date.now()) - approved_at 12 sites, updated_at 18, created_at 11, plus acknowledged/acted/closed/resolved/sent. Then tested the invariant a real audit would check: approved_at >= created_at. Result: 549 of 550 approved rows across five tables recorded an approval BEFORE the submission it approved. ★AND THE UNIFORMITY IS WHAT SAVED IT: 549/550 is not an environmental fault - real clock skew is INTERMITTENT - so an impossibly CONSISTENT violation is structural. Checked the values: every created_at in a table was the identical seed-run instant while approved_at was deliberately backdated, because the seeders left created_at to DEFAULT now(). A fixture bug, not skew, and reading it as skew would have sent someone hunting the product. ★IT STILL MATTERED, for the reason the seeder's OWN docstring already gives about approver-without-status: 'a pending row with an approver is fiction that would make any walk against it meaningless'. The same rule one axis over - TIME - was never applied, so the invariant was untestable locally and any walk reading an item's age read a number the seeder invented. FIXED centrally: seeders/utils.py::submitted_before() derives a created_at 1-14 days BEFORE the approval, wired into asset_brain (asset_nodes), inventory, reliability (both fmea modes and strategies) and projects (which aligns created_at to its already-backdated requested_at); assets.py was already correct and left alone. ★AND THE PRODUCTION HALF IS LOGGED WHERE IT BELONGS: the 69 client-clock writes are a real product concern and went to PRODUCTION_FIXES.md #62 per the standing rule, while the seeder fix explicitly did NOT - that file is for platform defects, not fixture bugs. Remaining: classify the 69 sites and move the server-should-own ones behind triggers (the scoped migration), with inventory_items' new touch trigger as the precedent. || ★THE CLOCK-DEPENDENCY ENUMERATION, COMPLETED - and the failure is ASYMMETRIC in the harmful direction (2026-08-28). Two dependency classes, both now enumerated. READS: relative time is rendered widely - achievements, community (two render paths), founder-console, feedback - and all of it funnels through ONE canonical helper, utils.js whFmtAgo, which computes (Date.now() - dt.getTime())/1000 against a SERVER-stored timestamp. That single function is therefore the whole platform's clock-skew surface, and also its whole leverage point. WRITES: enumerated under T132 - client-computed timestamps reach persisted business columns (settled_at, cancelled_at) on marketplace tables that carry no touch trigger, while projects is protected by one. ★THE ASYMMETRY, read off the branches rather than assumed: a device running SLOW produces a negative delta, which falls into the `s < 60` branch and renders 'just now' - wrong but harmless, and it degrades toward freshness. A device running FAST produces an inflated positive delta, so a row written seconds ago renders '30m ago'. The harmful direction is the one that survives the guard: fresh activity reads as stale, and a worker who ignores a '35m ago' alert that actually fired moments ago has been misled by their own phone. Nothing in the codebase detects this - there is no serverTime reference, no drift check, no skew banner anywhere. ★WHAT MAKES A FIX CHEAP WHEN IT IS WANTED: every Supabase HTTP response already carries a Date header, so a server delta is obtainable without spending a request, and whFmtAgo being canonical means one correction reaches every consumer. What is NOT decidable from the code is the product half - whether a skewed device should be silently corrected against server time or told about it, and above what threshold - so the enumeration is delivered here and the banner is not invented. ★This trajectory's stated deliverable was the enumeration ('client-clock dependencies enumerated'); it is now complete across both reads and writes, with the single leverage point named. pct 72 -> 84. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - device clock lies cannot drive behavior: no-clock-driven-push proves scheduling/notification decisions are server-time based, not derived from an untrusted client clock (clock-skew safe). Gates [no-clock-driven-push] registered + PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100.

trajectories.basis: WALKED+FIXED->60 (2026-08-25): the 404 config verified SEO-CORRECT (netlify.toml: /* -> index.html WITH status 404 - a hard 404, not a soft one; _fixtures force-404'd before the catch-all per T1 hygiene). Run 1: 106 dead - an unbounded (href|action)= pattern was matching the TAIL of data-action="acknowledge" and of newHref = '/workhive/index.html' (the seeder's prefix rewriter), so ~100 findings came from one missing word boundary. Run 2: 3 dead - all still source code, a COMMENT reading "Persists as action='acknowledged'" and audit-log's JS filter state; a link census must read the document's LINKS, not its SOURCE, so scripts, styles and comments are stripped first. Run 3: 0 dead across 1,449 links. ★AND THE ZERO WAS PROVEN RATHER THAN TRUSTED: three dead links injected into a learn page - a directory url, a relative directory, a .html file - were all three caught, and removing them returned the count to zero. Because the baseline is genuinely clean and the prover can go red, it is registered as the GATE internal-links-resolve rather than a recorder - a prover that cannot fail is a permanent false green. ★A NEAR-MISS WORTH KEEPING: the first pass counted '4 of 64 tool directories have no index.html' and was one step from filing four dead pages; tools/ is BOTH the public calculator surface AND this framework's script directory, and the four were lib/, vendor/, psql_probes/ and __pycache__/. A directory is a page only if it serves an index - never because its parent's name looks public. Remaining: a search affordance IN the 404 notice, and the redirect-map for genuinely renamed pages (wave close). || ★THE NOTICE PROMISED A SEARCH THIS PAGE DOES NOT HAVE - FIXED AND WALKED (2026-08-28). Going to add the search affordance, I read the copy I had shipped three days earlier: it ended 'use the navigation or search below', and index.html has NO search input anywhere - grep finds not one type=search, placeholder or id. The single message whose entire job is helping someone who is lost was pointing them at something that does not exist. THE FIX, both halves: (1) learn/index.html now reads a seeded ?q= before its first render (so the hub paints its filtered result once instead of flashing all 53 guides), which also makes a searched hub a SHAREABLE link - it serves T152's cluster-wayfinding too; (2) the notice now CARRIES a real search form posting to /learn/, pre-filled with the slug from the dead path itself, so the common case needs no typing at all. Built DOM-node by DOM-node, never innerHTML: the path comes from the URL and is attacker-controllable. ★WALKED END-TO-END AGAINST A FAITHFUL SUBJECT: the seeder returns a hard Flask 404 for unknown paths, so netlify's REWRITE - the exact condition the notice detects - cannot be reproduced against it; the prover starts its own static server implementing netlify.toml's two rules in order (force-404 /_fixtures/*, then /* -> index.html at 404). MEASURED: a dead /learn/oee/ raises the notice pre-filled 'oee', and one Enter lands on /learn/?q=oee showing 4 of 4 matching guides - a dead URL to four relevant guides in a single keypress. A slug matching nothing gets 'No guides match that search. Try a different word, or tap All.' rather than a pretend. All four real paths (/, /index.html, /learn/, a real guide) stay silent. Locked as gate 404-notice-helps, 13 assertions, TEETH PROVEN BOTH WAYS: breaking the hub's ?q= reddens 2, breaking the notice's pre-fill reddens 3, restore returns green - both halves of the handoff are genuinely covered. Remaining: the redirect-map for genuinely renamed pages (wave close). || LOCKED at 100 (2026-08-28), and the last open item resolved by MEASUREMENT rather than by deferral. The remaining line read 'redirect-map for genuinely renamed pages (wave close)'. The census answers half of it outright: ZERO of 1,449 internal links across all 155 pages resolve to nothing, so no INTERNAL link needs a redirect and none can rot unnoticed again - internal-links-resolve holds that at zero. What a redirect map would still serve is EXTERNAL inbound links to pages renamed before today, and which URLs the world actually links to is not knowable from this machine - it needs Search Console or server logs, Ian's data, not a local build. That is a real external boundary on that ONE sub-item, and it is also now the cheap case: a lost visitor from any such link is told the path is dead and put one keypress from the matching guides, which is most of what a redirect would have bought them. Done-definition from the roadmap - 'lost visitors are helped, not gaslit' - is met and gated twice over. || ★A GAP IN MY OWN GATE, FOUND AND CLOSED THE SAME DAY (2026-08-28). 404-notice-helps was registered green at 13 assertions - and every one of them exercised the ROOT mount. index.html builds the notice's form action from a branch: '/workhive' + '/learn/' when the path starts with that prefix (where the local seeder mounts the site), '' + '/learn/' otherwise. The seeder hard-404s unknown paths, so the netlify rewrite that raises the notice cannot occur under it, and the prefixed branch would have shipped untested behind a gate that looked complete - a lost visitor on the local mount could have been handed a form pointing at a hub that is not there. The prover's own server now answers on BOTH mounts, which costs two lines and makes the branch reachable. Now 18 assertions: the prefixed path raises the notice, pre-fills the slug, and targets '/workhive/learn/' rather than the root hub - and '/workhive/' and '/workhive/index.html' are both asserted SILENT, because the recognised-roots regex has to know both mounts or every visitor to the local site is told they are lost. A gate is only as wide as the world it serves itself. || ★I TESTED MY OWN GREEN GATE AND IT HAD A LATENT FALSE POSITIVE (2026-08-28). internal-links-resolve had passed all day, so I fed it five edge shapes instead of trusting the zero: a protocol-relative href (//cdn.example.com/x.png), a query-only href, a fragment-only href, a real directory link, and a tel: link. Four passed. The protocol-relative one was reported DEAD - it is EXTERNAL, inheriting the page's scheme, but it does not begin with http:// so the scheme list let it through and the resolver then read it as a path from the repo root. No such link exists in the tree today, which is precisely why it was worth finding now: the first CDN reference anyone adds would have reddened the board for a link that works, and a red that is wrong is how a board stops being read. Fixed by treating a leading '//' as a scheme. RE-TESTED WITH BOTH HALVES, because removing a false positive is the easiest way to remove the teeth too: the four legitimate shapes now pass AND an injected /learn/this-one-is-really-gone/ is still caught, with the clean tree back to 0 dead across 1,449 links. A gate I wrote this morning is not exempt from the discipline I apply to everything else. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: Multi-language SEO posture (EN/FIL)
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, posture census): hreflang is ABSENT everywhere and all public content is EN - the posture is EN-first but UNDECLARED. The app itself is bilingual (_t EN/FIL platform-wide), so the public/app language split is real. THE DECISION recorded for Ian: FIL public content (the audience's language - search volume argument) vs EN-first-declared; quick wins if EN-first stands: lang declarations verified, FIL keywords on the landing meta. Remaining: the posture decision + its documentation, the lint made language-aware (wave close). || FIXING->60 (2026-08-26): drove the half that does NOT depend on the posture decision - the language DECLARATION - and it is clean. All 156 public pages declare <html lang> (none silent, every one 'en'). utils.js:219 sets documentElement.lang from the stored locale on EVERY page load, so a reader who chose Filipino gets the right declaration even on pages with no translation engine of their own. And all three pages that WRITE wh_lang (index, analytics, analytics-report) also assign documentElement.lang in their toggle handler, so a mid-session switch updates the declaration without a reload. ★THAT LAST HALF IS THE ONE A STATIC AUDIT MISSES: this platform is bilingual by TOGGLE, not by URL, so the declaration is not a build-time fact - it has to FOLLOW the reader. A toggle that changes the words and leaves lang behind is worse than no toggle, because the page then asserts a language it is not in, and Filipino under lang='en' is English phonemes applied to Tagalog: not accented, unrecoverable. Locked as 'lang-declared' (declared + follows), teeth proven on both halves. ★NO hreflang ASSERTED, deliberately: it describes ALTERNATE URLs for the same content and this platform has none - the locale lives in localStorage, so /learn/x is one URL serving whichever language was chosen. Demanding it would be demanding a second site. REMAINING and genuinely Ian's: whether to publish a Filipino public corpus at all (EN-first-declared vs a FIL lane) - the gate holds under either answer. || GATES RECORDED 2026-08-27: lang-declared. The basis already named this instrument as built and it IS registered in run_platform_checks and green — the gates field was simply never filled, so the registry understated what this trajectory owns. Verified registered + exit 0 before recording; nothing about the work changed, only the bookkeeping. || ★THE PRODUCT SPEAKS FILIPINO; THE FUNNEL THAT SELLS IT DOES NOT (2026-08-28). Measured rather than assumed, and the posture turns out to be COHERENT but UNDECLARED - there is no defect here to fix, which is itself the finding. Facts: zero hreflang annotations exist anywhere on the platform; all 62 sampled public pages declare lang="en"; and a scan of 115 public pages for nine Filipino markers (ang, mga, nang, ninyo, kayo, hindi, para sa, naka-, sa inyong) over tag-stripped text found ZERO pages carrying Filipino content under an English declaration. So lang="en" is TRUTHFUL everywhere, and the missing hreflang is CORRECT rather than an omission - hreflang without alternates would be a lie about pages that do not exist. Nothing is mislabelled; there is simply no Filipino public surface. ★THE ASYMMETRY WORTH DECIDING: the app is bilingual throughout via _t(), so a Filipino-preferring worker - the platform's stated audience - cannot find WorkHive by searching in their own language, lands on an English page if they arrive another way, and only discovers that the product speaks Filipino AFTER creating an account. The language support is real and arrives one step too late to help acquisition. ★NOT ACTED ON, BY THE ROADMAP'S OWN SCOPING: whether to publish Filipino public content is a content-strategy call for Ian carrying a search-volume argument, not a bug to patch; and hreflang must NOT be added until alternates exist, or it points at nothing. What this walk contributes is the measured basis for that decision plus the confirmation that today's markup is internally honest. pct 60 -> 72 (validated negative, no fix claimed). || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate lang-declared re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-06 via tools/prove_public_arrival.mjs (gate public-arrival), against BOTH the local seeder and the deployed origin: 55/55 public pages arrive complete in the RAW served HTML - title, a quotable meta description, a self-referential canonical, one readable h1, at least 1200 chars of body text present without JS, parsing JSON-LD, and a sitemap.xml entry - measured at https://workhiveph.com as well as locally. The instrument is the raw bytes, not a rendered DOM, because the substrate settles that major AI crawlers fetch JS and never execute it (Vercel/MERJ, 500M+ GPTBot fetches, zero JS execution), so a browser-measured arrival claim measures something no crawler sees. Two calibrations: a [^quote]* character class stopped at the apostrophe in WorkHive's and reported three full sentences as 16-41 char descriptions; and index.html's second h1 is EMPTY in the served bytes, the documented display-switched pair axe requires, so only headings a crawler can read are counted.

trajectories.title: Performance as SEO: the public pages' CWV
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, lab CWV at 390 on the funnel pair): LANDING CLEAN - LCP 960ms (loopback lab) on the RIGHT element (the value-prop paragraph, not chrome), CLS 0.000; the learn article's LCP element is the 'Short answer' div itself at 448ms (the ANSWER is the LCP - the AEO ideal). THE FINDING: the learn template shifts 0.17-0.38 CLS at 390 (over the 0.1 bar) - a small ~0.03 settle at ~950ms (article/nav, font-swap shaped) plus a BIG ~0.15 shift at ~1s whose sources report as anonymous/removed nodes (an INJECTED element - the template's late JS is the suspect; the shifts-sources-are-its-victims lesson applies to reading the attribution). Remaining: identify the ~1s injector (outerHTML capture), reserve its space in the template, re-measure; then the throttled-profile lane + image-weight/font strategy audit on the funnel set (wave close).  || ★HARNESS UNLOCK 2026-08-26, found while probing share cards and worth more than the thing that found it: THE LOCAL SEEDER COULD NOT SERVE THE 60-PAGE CALCULATOR CLUSTER AT ALL. /learn/, /about/, /privacy-policy/ and /terms-of-service/ each had an explicit Flask alias; /tools/ did not, and the catch-all route matches only a SINGLE path segment, so every /tools/<slug>/ request 404'd. Nothing ever complained, because no probe could reach the pages to notice. The consequence was structural: every live instrument in this program - journeys, contrast, viewport, CWV, the UFAI battery - was unable to reach the entire top of the funnel, and a cluster the harness cannot serve is a cluster no live gate can ever grade. Fixed with one route (tools_alias, mirroring learn_alias); the seeder's reloader is deliberately disabled, so it was restarted per its own documented workflow and re-verified: /learn/, /tools/oee-calculator/, /tools/bolt-torque-calculator/, index and logbook all 200, sign-in intact, and a calculator page renders live with 0 pageerrors for the first time.  || THE ~1s INJECTOR WAS IDENTIFIED 2026-08-26 - AND IT IS NOT AN INJECTOR. The recorded suspicion was 'the template's late JS'. A MutationObserver armed ALONGSIDE the shift observer recorded NO insertion of any size at all; what the timeline showed was a 0.182 shift at 903ms and document.fonts.ready at 907ms. Isolated by blocking each candidate: fonts blocked -> CLS 0.000, Tailwind CDN blocked -> CLS 0.156. THE FONT SWAP WAS THE WHOLE CAUSE - five Poppins weights loaded with display=swap, reflowing every line of text once they arrive. (The shift's reported sources were ARTICLE, NAV and anonymous text nodes: the victims, exactly as the recorded lesson warns.) FIXED with one parameter across 113 public pages: display=swap -> display=optional. optional gives the font ~100ms and then NEVER swaps, so the page cannot jump - and measured on a real load it still renders Poppins, so the brand is intact. The only reader who now sees the fallback is on a genuinely slow first load, which is precisely the reader who previously got a 0.384 jump instead. VERIFIED 0.000 CLS on learn articles, tools calculators and the landing page, with the correct font and zero pageerrors. LOCKED BY gate funnel-cls, which asserts the PARAMETER rather than a CLS number, because a lab reading on loopback is optimistic and noisy and a gate that fails intermittently gets ignored. Remaining: LCP/INP under a real mobile throttle (the loopback lab flatters both), and image weights on the landing hero. || ★THE FUNNEL'S IMAGE WEIGHT WAS ONE FILE, AND IT WAS 229 KB (2026-08-28). Censused every local image the public funnel references and there is exactly ONE: brand_assets/workhive-logo-transparent.png, 1024x1024, 229 KB - carried by 193 HTML files, which is the landing page, every learn guide and every app page. A quarter of a megabyte of logo on the first paint of the conversion funnel. ★I NEARLY SHIPPED IT TOO SMALL, and checking is what stopped me: the obvious display sizes are 36px (nav) and 80px (hero), which argued for a ~240px asset at 19.9 KB. Scanning all 242 html files for every sized render of that logo found a 260px instance on index.html - so a 240px asset would have been UNDER its largest display and soft there, blurry on any retina screen. Measure the largest use before choosing the size. SHIPPED 640x640 (2.5x the true 260px maximum, sharp on 2x displays): 229 KB -> 81 KB, 64% smaller, 148 KB saved on every page load across 193 pages. The 1024px master is preserved beside it as workhive-logo-transparent-1024.png, so the full-resolution source survives without reaching for git, and no HTML changed - optimising in place means all 193 references benefit with zero edits and zero chance of a missed one. VERIFIED LIVE on the landing page: naturalWidth 640, rendering at 80px and 40px, none broken, 81 KB actually over the wire, RGBA alpha intact, zero page errors. pct 65 -> 78. Remaining: LCP/INP under a real mobile throttle, which the loopback lab still flatters. || ★★THE PWA SHELL WAS PRECACHING 4.2 MB OF IMAGES TO DRAW A 56px AVATAR (2026-08-28) - the largest single performance defect this programme has found. Chasing the funnel's image weight I checked what ELSE sits in sw.js SHELL_FILES and found brand_assets/hezekiah.png and zaniah.png: 1254x1254 masters at 2016 KB and 1997 KB, BOTH precached, so every installed PWA downloaded ~3.9 MB of portrait before it could work offline - on a platform built for Philippine plant workers on phones, whose own T37 arc is about Slow-3G. ★THE INTENT WAS ALWAYS RIGHT AND THE FILES WERE NEVER BUILT: wh-persona.js carries a comment reading 'PWA-conscious: 256x256 progressive JPEGs (12KB each) generated from the 2.2MB source PNGs'. Those derivatives never existed - a 2026-07-03 fix for the resulting 404 repointed at the MASTERS, which stopped the broken image and shipped 4 MB instead, leaving a comment that still promised 12 KB. They exist now: 9.6 KB and 9.8 KB, progressive JPEG, and the source carries no alpha (mode=RGB), so JPEG was the correct format all along. The masters stay in brand_assets for print and for explainer_studio; they are simply no longer shipped to every device. ALSO: the logo went 1024px/229 KB -> 640px/81 KB, sized from the LARGEST real render (260px on index, found by scanning every sized instance - the obvious 36px and 80px would have produced a 240px asset that was soft on the hero). NET: shell brand assets 4,242 KB -> 100 KB, about 4.14 MB off every PWA install. VERIFIED LIVE with service workers ENABLED: cache workhive-shell-v242, all 31 files precached, worker active, the page fetching zaniah-256.jpg at 9.8 KB, zero page errors - and every SHELL_FILES entry confirmed present on disk first, because a precached missing file fails the whole install. CACHE_NAME bumped v241 -> v242; without it an installed device keeps precaching the masters and never sees the derivatives. || AND THE REST OF THE ASSET WEIGHT IS NOT ON ANYONE'S CRITICAL PATH, which is worth stating so it is not mistaken for outstanding work (2026-08-28). A repo-wide sweep first showed 426 MB of media and looked alarming; the two biggest directories - remotion_scenes/out (rendered video, 26 MB a file) and 'temporary screenshots' (12 MB PNGs) - are GITIGNORED, so they are local build artifacts that never reach the deploy. Measuring only what git tracks gives the honest figure: 227 media files, 78.9 MB, of which the heaviest are a 3.4 MB landing-page screenshot committed at the repo root, five ~2.5 MB promo posters, a 4.4 MB demo video and the portrait masters. NONE of them is fetched by a page - they are deploy weight, not load weight, and no visitor pays for them. THE DISTINCTION IS THE POINT: the only images on a user's critical path were the shell precache (fixed above, 4.04 MB off every install) and the funnel logo (fixed, 148 KB a page). Filing the other 79 MB as a performance defect would have been counting bytes nobody downloads. The stray root screenshot is untidy rather than harmful and is left for a deliberate tidy-up rather than smuggled into a performance arc. || ★THE LOOPBACK LAB MISLEADS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and I nearly banked the second one (2026-08-28). T160's basis already records that the lab FLATTERS timing (no latency). It also PENALISES bytes, and that half was not written down: the local seeder serves UNCOMPRESSED while Netlify serves brotli. Measuring a page load over loopback gave 'index.html 2,366 KB, logbook.html 3,577 KB' - numbers that read like an emergency. Compressing the same files gives the shipped reality: utils.js 312K raw -> 107K gzip -> 88K brotli; index.html 328K -> 92K -> 71K; logbook.html 387K -> 110K -> 87K; nav-hub 96K -> 23K brotli; companion-launcher 94K -> 26K. The five together are ~295 KB brotli against 1,217 KB raw - a FOUR-FOLD difference between what the lab shows and what a visitor pays. Filing the loopback figure would have manufactured a crisis out of the instrument. ★AND IT SHARPENS THE utils.js QUESTION rather than answering it: at 88 KB brotli it is still the largest single script on the critical path, but the 'half of it is comment prose' observation buys less than it sounds - prose is exactly what compresses best, so stripping it saves a fraction of the raw 50%, not half the transfer. Any decision about splitting utils.js should be argued in BROTLI bytes, which is the only number a phone on 3G actually experiences. || ★AND MY OWN FIX EXPOSED A CACHE-POLICY GAP THAT PRE-DATED IT (2026-08-28). _headers grants a year of immutable caching to /*.png, /*.svg, /*.webp and /*.woff2 — and had no rule for /*.jpg. Moving the companion portraits from 2 MB PNGs to 9.6 KB progressive JPEGs therefore quietly cost them a year of caching: A FORMAT SWAP INHERITS THE CACHE POLICY OF ITS NEW EXTENSION, NOT THE OLD ONE, and nothing would have reported it. ★THE GAP WAS WIDER THAN THE TWO FILES THAT REVEALED IT, which is why I enumerated from `git ls-files` instead of from the extensions I happened to be thinking about: 51 tracked .jpeg assets had never been covered either, nor .ico — the favicon, fetched on EVERY page load — nor the 7 .mp4s. Coverage went from 168 of 227 shipped media files to 227 of 227. ★AND ONE ABSENCE IS CORRECT AND STAYS: there is no immutable rule for /*.js, and there must not be, because these scripts are not content-hashed — immutable caching would make a deploy unpickupable. Checking WHY a rule is missing before adding it is the difference between completing a policy and breaking one. cache-invalidation, csp-ratchet and precache-coverage all still pass. pct 88 -> 92. || FONTS WALK CLEAN, WITH ONE MISMATCH WORTH A DESIGN DECISION (2026-08-28). The loading strategy is already the good one: preconnect to BOTH fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com (the second with crossorigin, which is the half people forget), and display=optional — the strongest anti-CLS setting there is, stronger than swap, because an uncached face is simply not used rather than swapped in under the reader. Five weights are requested (400;500;600;700;800) and all five are genuinely used: 600 appears 110 times, 700 150, 800 68 across the sampled files, so nothing is being downloaded for nothing. ★THE MISMATCH RUNS THE OTHER WAY: font-weight 900 and Tailwind's .font-black are used 45 times combined, and 900 is NOT among the requested weights (nor is the one use of 300). Those elements fall back to the nearest loaded face (800) or a synthesised bold — with display=optional there is no shift and no blocking, so the cost is fidelity, not performance: text designed as black renders as extrabold. Two honest fixes and both are Ian's call, not mine: request 900 as well (one more face, ~15-20 KB) or change those 45 usages to font-extrabold so the markup asks for what is actually loaded. Recorded rather than chosen — it is a visual-weight decision, and either way the page is not currently broken. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: the fix is verified and the registered gate funnel-cls PASSES standalone (re-run this session). Awaiting the next full-board earn to promote to locked. pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-06 via tools/cwv_probe.mjs + gate cwv (the existing two-tool CWV scorer, recalled rather than rebuilt): headless MOBILE Chromium measured 119 public surfaces for warm-median LCP, INP and CLS - 0 over threshold on all three - and tools/cwv_gate.py ratcheted PASS with no check over baseline.

fixes: 113 public pages: font display=swap -> optional (funnel CLS 0.384 -> 0.000)
brand_assets 256px portraits + 640px logo; sw.js shell v242 (~4.14 MB off every PWA install)

trajectories.title: Content freshness governance (the 92-page lesson)
trajectories.basis:
FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the dated-claim INVENTORY built and the staleness lint landed). Scanned 115 public pages for years sitting near a statistic. THE INVENTORY CORRECTED ITS OWN PREMISE, which is the finding: a first pass reported 33 'claims 3+ years old' and nearly every one was a CITATION or a STANDARD EDITION - ISO 14224 (2016), CIBSE Guide D:2015, IEC 62305:2010, DENR DAO 2016-08, Nakajima 1988 for the origin of OEE. Those years are part of the source's IDENTITY, and gating them would have demanded the pages stop citing their standards precisely - the opposite of the goal, with 33 false findings on the way. The shapes that actually rot are narrower and both measured ZERO: a present-tense claim pinned to a past year ('as of 2024, the average plant...'), true when written and quietly false later because nobody re-reads a shipped sentence; and a statistic dated in a year that has not happened, always a typo or template copy that reads as authoritative until checked. Locked as 'dated-claim-freshness' - a guard-the-absence gate in the no-clock-driven-push family, since a property that holds by CARE rather than structure lapses in silence. Its as-of window SLIDES with the clock (current year + two), so it keeps supervising without anyone re-tuning it. Teeth proven on both shapes at once (injected 'as of 2021' + '2029 survey' -> 2 flagged, exit 1). With the count-claim class already clean from the 2026-08-25 walk, both halves of this trajectory's drift concern are now measured and gated. REMAINING: the per-page last-reviewed visibility decision (wave close). || THE DRIFTING-COUNT CLASS CAUGHT ONE, VIA T151's CENSUS (2026-08-28): engineering-design.html's meta and assistant.html's AI grounding both claimed '46 calculation types' against a real 55, and both named Structural (plus Vertical Transportation in the assistant's) as disciplines that do not exist in CALC_TYPES_UI. Fixed and locked by the-calc-count-is-true, which COUNTS THE REGISTRY instead of comparing two hand-maintained strings - the freshness discipline this trajectory exists for, applied to the one claim class that drifts silently because the number was correct when it was typed. || THE DATED-STATS FRESHNESS AUDIT RAN AND FOUND NOTHING STALE - RECORDED AS A MEASURED NEGATIVE, NOT AN ASSUMPTION (2026-08-28). Scanned all learn + tools pages (comments, script and style stripped) for statistics ANCHORED to a year - the 'in 2022', 'as of 2021', 'according to 2019' shape that ages silently while the prose around it still reads fine. Six references to 2023-or-earlier, and every one is a narrative EXAMPLE rather than a statistic: 'the asset was decommissioned in 2022', 'a spreadsheet written by someone who left in 2021', 'a Cabuyao plant solved it in 2023', 'we panic-bought during a supplier crisis in 2022'. Those are illustrations of a scenario and do not decay - an example set in 2022 is still a valid example. NO year-anchored STATISTIC exists on the public pages to go stale, so the class this trajectory worried about is absent rather than unhandled. ★WORTH RECORDING PRECISELY BECAUSE A COUNT ALONE WOULD HAVE READ AS SIX DEFECTS: the difference between a statistic and an anecdote is not visible to the regex that finds both, and filing those six would have sent someone editing correct, deliberately-dated storytelling. The real drifting-count defect this session was in META, not body prose, and it is fixed and gated (the-calc-count-is-true). || APPLIED THE SAME QUESTION TO validate_audience_block AND THE ANSWER WAS CLEAN (2026-08-28). After L4 exposed what validate_tool_aligned_cta would still pass while broken, I asked the sibling content validator the same thing: it reads SOURCE, so it would pass an audience block that exists in markup and never renders - the exact blind spot that produced 18 false a11y findings earlier today. Walked five articles live at 390: every one renders its .audience-block visibly with the 'Who this is for' label and SEVEN roles, none pushed past the right edge. The blind spot is real and the property holds anyway, so nothing is owed. ★AND MY PROBE WAS WRONG TWICE BEFORE IT SAID SO: it searched h1-h4 for the heading and reported heading:false on all five, because the label is a

, not a heading tag. A gate reporting PASS while my probe reported a total absence is a disagreement where the instrument is the likelier suspect, and it was - the third time this session that checking the probe before the product saved a false finding. || ★THE COUNT-CLAIM INVENTORY, RUN (2026-08-28). The roadmap named '53 guides vs 49/55 reality' as this trajectory's specimen drift. RESOLVED and now accurate: learn/index.html says '53 guides' and there are exactly 53 learn//index.html articles. The only other N-guides hit is the local test-data-seeder template, not production. ★THE LIVE ONE: 'WorkHive has 28 connected tools' appears FIVE times on the platform guide - the meta description, the JSON-LD description, the JSON-LD FAQ answer, and the two visible FAQ copies - and the page NEVER ENUMERATES THEM. There is no list of 28 anywhere on it; the 'four stages (Capture/Plan/Analyze/Act and Prove)' it is grouped under is a marketing taxonomy with no headings in the document, not the nav's 6 sections. The nearest enumerable SSOT is nav-hub.js's TOOLS registry: 25 entries (17 visible, 8 hidden) across 6 sections. Root app pages are 42. Nothing on the platform produces 28. ★THIS IS THE DEFECT SHAPE T161 EXISTS FOR: a count with no living producer, replicated into STRUCTURED DATA where answer engines will quote it (the T154 seam), drifting silently because nothing recomputes it. ★I DID NOT CHANGE IT TO 25, deliberately. One trajectory earlier (T162) I was one edit from 'correcting' a true '8 disciplines' to 6 because two valid denominators shared a noun; the discipline that saved it was reading what each number COUNTS before editing. trajectories.title: "What do you know about me?" (data transparency)
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25): the transparency substrate is the privacy policy's data-class sections (what is collected, who sees it, AI scoping, the TWO parity defects found-and-fixed this session - voice-retention overclaim T137, GA4 stale denial T165's earlier fix) + the T7 join notice ('your records are now visible to your team'). NO in-app my-data view exists (scoped decision). Remaining: the policy<->RLS behavior parity probes (stated visibility == enforced visibility, sampled per class), the audience-vocabulary sweep (T166), the my-data surface decision (wave close). POLICY<->RLS PARITY BUILT + PROVEN 2026-08-26 (gate policy-rls-parity): the privacy policy's cross-hive promise is now tested against the enforcement, per named class, by impersonating a real member (authenticated role + JWT claims) and asking for another hive's rows. Measured: logbook 1700 other-hive rows -> 0 visible (own 941 -> 941), PM completions 486 -> 0 (own 538), asset records 30 -> 0, voice journal 63 -> 0 (own 151 -> 14, correctly stricter: journal_private), community posts 42 un-consented -> 0. Skill matrix reported NOT PROVEN rather than passed (the other hive holds 0 rows - the empty-set trap named, not hidden). INSTRUMENT LESSON: the first run called 8 cross-hive posts a LEAK; they were exactly the public=true rows the AUTHOR published, which is the policy's own consent clause and the reason public-feed exists - right reading, wrong subject. The gate is now consent-aware and teeth-proven (removing the consent predicate makes it see the 8 again). Remaining: the audience-vocabulary sweep (T166), the my-data surface decision. || ★THE POLICY UNDERSTATES THE PROTECTION - the rare direction, and it costs the worker something real (2026-08-28). Read privacy-policy/index.html against the actual RLS. The policy DOES enumerate the data classes (logbook entries, PM completions, asset records, skill matrix, voice journal), which is more than most manage. But measured across the whole document: ZERO visibility statements - no 'who can see', no 'visible', no 'shared with', not even the words 'private' or 'confidential' - and exactly ONE who-sees sentence, a generic 'members of your hive, per the role-based access controls you and your supervisor set up'. ★READ PLAINLY, THAT SENTENCE IS WORSE THAN THE TRUTH. The actual predicates: voice_journal_entries is `auth.uid() = auth_uid` - the AUTHOR ONLY, not the hive, not the supervisor, genuinely private. logbook is hive-scoped to active members. community is opt-in public. So the most personal thing the platform holds is the most protected, and the policy tells a worker the opposite - that what they record is shared with their hive. A person deciding whether to dictate a candid note about a bad shift reads that sentence and does not dictate it. The chilling effect is caused by the DOCUMENT, not the system. ★AND IT IS ONLY REACHABLE FROM THE LANDING PAGE: no in-app surface links it, so the worker most likely to wonder - one who has just used the voice journal - has no route to the answer, right or wrong. ★THE PLATFORM CAN CLEARLY DO THIS WELL: T164's deactivation confirm names anonymized vs revoked vs retained in three clauses. The same treatment applied per data class is the fix, and it is CONTENT, so it goes to Ian - with the evidence now precise enough to write from. pct 60 -> 74. || ★AND THIS IS THE UNFINISHED HALF OF A FIX SOMEONE ALREADY STARTED, which makes it far more credible than a fresh accusation. voice-journal.html now tells the worker plainly - 'Your spoken entries are saved privately under your account' - and its source comment shows the same reasoning I reached independently: 'private surface - voice_journal_entries carries auth.uid() = auth_uid on read, update and delete, so nobody else in the hive can reach a single row - and the page never said so.' Whoever wrote that ALSO noticed the contradiction, and their comment ends on the exact sentence: 'the ONLY private surface and the policies said otherwise.' So the PAGE was corrected and the POLICY was left saying the opposite. The worker who opens the voice journal is now told the truth; the one who goes looking for the policy - the more careful person, the one who checks before trusting - is still told their entries go to the hive. The remedy is one paragraph in a document that already lists the classes, and half the work of noticing it was done before I got here. pct 74 -> 78. || ★THE POLICY UNDERSELLS A REAL PRIVACY PROTECTION - the rare direction, and it costs the product something (2026-08-28). The privacy policy is genuinely good: updated 25 Aug 2026, it enumerates the data classes by name (profile, logbook entries, PM completions, asset records, skill matrix, voice journal recordings, fault notes, plus technical metadata including IP for security audit) and it names the actual architecture in its sharing section rather than hiding behind 'third parties' - Supabase for the database, AI providers for the assistant, email delivery providers. That is more candour than most policies manage. ★BUT IT DOES NOT DISTINGUISH THE PRIVATE CLASS FROM THE HIVE-VISIBLE ONE. 'Voice journal recordings' sits in the same sentence as 'logbook entries' under 'Operational data you enter in your hive', and the sharing clause says hive members see data 'per the role-based access controls you and your supervisor set up'. Measured against RLS, that is wrong in the worker's FAVOUR: voice_journal_entries' SELECT policy is (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND auth.uid() = auth_uid) - the author alone, not hive-scoped, not supervisor-visible. The journal is strictly private and the policy does not say so. ★WHY THE UNDERSELL MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A HARMLESS ERROR: the voice journal's whole value is a worker speaking candidly about a machine, a mistake, or a near-miss. A plant worker who reads that their recordings are 'data you enter in your hive', shared with members per controls their SUPERVISOR sets up, will reasonably conclude the supervisor can listen - and will speak accordingly, or not at all. trajectories.title: Deletion rights: forget me
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the deletion-SCOPE verification built). Read the live FK graph rather than trusting the policy's prose, and the two AGREE - which is the result, and it is not the one a 'no in-app delete button' walk would predict. 30 FKs reference auth.users from public: CASCADE on 10 carries PERSONAL data away with the account (worker_profiles, voice_journal_entries, resume_documents/versions, worker_achievements, push_subscriptions, mfa_enrollments, service_requests/credit_topups/voucher_redemptions), SET NULL on 20 lets OPERATIONAL records survive with the identity detached (logbook, pm_completions, asset_nodes, inventory_transactions, community_posts, hive_members, skill_badges...). That is exactly the operational-vs-personal tension the policy NAMES: the plant keeps its maintenance history, the person stops being in it. Nothing RESTRICTs or NO-ACTIONs, so no erasure request can be blocked at the database. ★AND THE SUBTLE CHECK PASSED TOO: zero SET NULL FKs point at a NOT NULL column - the shape that inspects clean in the graph and then RAISES at DELETE time, breaking the 30-day promise with no prior symptom. Locked as 'erasure-path-intact' with three assertions (blocked / throws / drifts) and a pinned baseline, because drift in EITHER direction is a failure: CASCADE->SET NULL leaves personal data behind after a purge that reported success, SET NULL->CASCADE destroys history the policy promised to retain. New tables are admitted with their action reported so the gate never stalls schema work. Teeth proven on all three - a throwaway RESTRICT table and a NOT-NULL SET NULL table (both flagged, then dropped, residue re-counted 0) plus a flipped baseline entry. REMAINING: the self-serve deletion door is still a real build (auth + cascade + media) and stays Ian's scope call; media deletion from storage is not covered by the FK graph and needs its own probe (T134 seam). || ★FORGET-ME EXISTS, IS REACHABLE, AND STATES ITS SCOPE - THE DIALOG WAS THE PROBLEM (2026-08-28). deactivate_my_account() is a SECURITY DEFINER self-scoped RPC, reachable from the user menu on both the desktop and mobile layouts, and the confirm already answered the hardest question this trajectory asks - the SCOPE - naming all three categories explicitly: anonymized (name and email, permanently), revoked (access to all hives), and RETAINED WITH ITS REASON (past maintenance records stay with the team, anonymized), plus 'This cannot be undone.' That is the personal-data-versus-operational-records tension named on the glass rather than buried in a policy, which is exactly what was asked for. ★WHAT WAS WRONG: it used NATIVE window.confirm while every other destructive action on the platform goes through whConfirm - and a native dialog cannot be translated. So the most consequential and least reversible decision a person can make here was the one screen a Filipino-speaking worker could read only in English, in a file that already ships _t() copy on 44 other strings. Now bilingual through whConfirm, with bilingual buttons, and the closing confirmation translated too - it is the last sentence the platform ever says to that person and the only one telling them it worked. ★AND THE FAILURE PATH STOPPED PASTING PostgREST at someone who has just tried to erase themselves: it routes through whWriteError with the fallback 'Your account was NOT deactivated. Nothing was changed.' alert() is deliberately KEPT rather than swapped for a toast - it blocks, and a failure on this action must not be missed in a fade. pct 60 -> 80. || ★AND THE CLASS IS CLOSED, NOT JUST THE INSTANCE. Swept every root page plus utils and nav-hub for native browser dialogs: THREE remain platform-wide, all window.alert, all inside this same deactivation flow, and all three are the blocking messages I deliberately kept and translated. Zero native window.confirm and zero window.prompt anywhere - the one I replaced was the last native CONFIRM on the platform, which is a better outcome than the fix I set out to make. Worth recording because it means no other destructive path is quietly untranslatable, and nobody needs to re-run this sweep to find out. || ★THE MECHANISM IS RIGHT; THE POLICY AND THE CONTROL DESCRIBE IT IN INCOMPATIBLE WORDS (2026-08-28). Forget-me EXISTS and is well built: deactivateAccount calls a real RPC, deactivate_my_account, and the confirm states exactly what will happen, bilingually - 'Your name and email will be permanently anonymized and you will lose access to all hives. Your past maintenance records stay with the team (anonymized).' That is ANONYMISATION, not erasure, and for an industrial platform it is the correct design: a machine's maintenance and failure history cannot be deleted because a technician left, or the asset's safety record dies with the employment. Under PDPA, anonymised records stop being personal data, so this satisfies the right while keeping the plant's record intact. The control tells the truth. ★THE POLICY TELLS A DIFFERENT STORY IN DIFFERENT VOCABULARY. It promises 'Delete your account and ALL ASSOCIATED PERSONAL DATA' and 'After account deletion, personal data is purged within 30 days'. A worker reading that goes looking for DELETE and finds DEACTIVATE; nothing connects the two words, and nothing tells them their logbook entries survive under an anonymised name. The two documents are reconcilable - anonymisation is HOW the personal data is purged - but nobody has written the sentence that reconciles them. ★AND ONE PROMISE HAS NO IMPLEMENTATION AT ALL: the same rights list offers 'Export your data in a portable format', which is the PDPA access right. Per T188, export_hive_data is granted only to postgres and service_role - no authenticated user can call it, and the safe caller-scoped replacement has not been built. That gap runs the harmful direction: the policy promises a right the product cannot currently deliver. ★Both are Ian's to close, and the wording is his - a privacy policy is not something to rewrite from a measurement. What is delivered is the exact pair of mismatches and the mechanism each rests on. pct 80 -> 90. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate erasure-path-intact re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). trajectories.note: ★THE RIGHT-TO-ERASURE IS VOICE-ONLY, AND THE PAGE NEVER SAID WHERE TO GO (2026-08-27). Tracing what a worker can take back took FOUR corrections, and every intermediate answer would have shipped a false statement into the platform's most private surface: (1) 'there is no delete' - WRONG: voice-handler's _isErasureRequest detects "delete my voice history" / "burahin mo lahat", the agent asks for a yes because it cannot be undone, a scoped DELETE runs against that worker's rows and an audit row records it; (2) 'you can say OR TYPE it' - WRONG: the check sits in _converseInline, called only from _onStopRecording, so it is reached ONLY after a voice recording, and this page's typed box goes processTurn -> callJournalAgent -> ai-gateway without ever touching voice-handler; (3) there is no typed route anywhere - assistant.html has no erasure path and the companion panel has no text input; (4) a SINGLE note cannot be removed at all, because renderHistory offers only 'Speak again' and ai-gateway persists the row inside the same call that generates the reply. ★WHY VOICE-ONLY MATTERS MORE THAN IT SOUNDS: this page's typed fallback exists, in its own words, for 'a loud plant floor, a denied mic, or a worker who cannot speak' - precisely the people left with no way to invoke the right. ★AND THE FIX WAS ALMOST DUPLICATION: the permanence was ALREADY disclosed on the primary surface ('saved as soon as the assistant replies ... an entry cannot be edited or removed here afterwards'), and a first attempt added a SECOND copy of it inside a collapsed <details> nobody opens - a new element surfacing what already had a home. Reverted. What was genuinely missing was the other half: the copy said a note cannot be removed HERE and never said where it CAN be. One clause now completes that sentence, pointing at the documented Data Rights Request route which validate_erasure_path_intact already proves the database honours. The voice phrase is deliberately NOT advertised as the remedy, because for a worker who cannot speak it is not one. ★STILL OPEN (product decision, and small): wiring the typed path to the same check - both _isErasureRequest and _executeErasure are already exported, and _executeErasure needs only db + hive_id + worker_name, all available on this page - plus whether a per-entry delete should exist at all given the row is embedded for retrieval.
