trajectories.note: ★T166 CLOSED ON BOTH ITEMS (2026-08-27), and the first one dissolved under measurement. ★THE 'ONE-VOCABULARY DECISION between your hive and your team' WAS A FALSE PREMISE. Measured across every page: 585 'hive' against 123 'team' - but the split is not drift, it is a DISTINCTION the platform keeps correctly. 'Team' names the PEOPLE ('invite your team', 'your team logs', 'your team works in Filipino'); 'hive' names the WORKSPACE. One sentence uses both exactly right: 'Hive created. Invite your team.' And the drift case does not exist - searching for team-as-workspace ('switch team', 'join team', 'leave team', 'create team') returns ONE hit, which is that same correct sentence. One-vocabulary means one concept, one name; it does not mean banning a word that names a different concept. No decision was needed and none is owed to Ian - the answer was in the corpus. ★THE SECOND ITEM WAS REAL: none of the five candidate lower-stakes composers said who reads what is written. Three now do, and the answers genuinely DIFFER, which is exactly why each has to say it instead of letting people generalise from the page they were last on: dayplanner's notes are PRIVATE (schedule_items read = auth_uid = auth.uid()), while inventory's part notes and pm-scheduler's findings are HIVE-VISIBLE - and findings in particular are the maintenance RECORD a supervisor reads to learn what was actually done, which someone who thinks they are writing to themselves writes differently. Gate composer-audience widened 3 -> 6 surfaces, with dayplanner's privacy claim CHECKED against the policy rather than trusted. ★AND THE GATE WAS WRONG FIRST, in the way this file keeps being wrong: its owner-scope test matched only `auth.uid() = auth_uid` and schedule_items stores the same predicate as `auth_uid = auth.uid()`. An equality has no canonical direction, so a genuinely private table read as NOT owner-scoped and a TRUE privacy claim was reported as a promise the database does not keep. The checker was reading its own habit rather than the policy. Both orders now accepted. ★LOCKED (2026-08-27): the done-definition is 'no one publishes by surprise', and the gate measures exactly that - composer-audience passes with SIX write surfaces stating who can see what is written, AND each privacy claim checked against the policy that enforces it rather than taken at its word. dayplanner's line is the shape to keep: 'private to you; nobody else in your hive can read your planner notes', with schedule_items confirmed owner-scoped (auth_uid = auth.uid()). trajectories.title: The security-headers & client hardening pass (user-visible edges)
trajectories.basis: the posture census found TWO prod-only defects in _headers (which the local stack never serves - no walk could see them): (1) Permissions-Policy camera=()/microphone=() SITE-WIDE killed the voice journal's mic + logbook photo/QR in production -> fixed to (self); (2) the CSP predated GA4 (no googletagmanager/analytics endpoints) so the shipped funnel analytics were silently DEAD in prod -> allowed. Baseline posture otherwise solid: XFO DENY, nosniff, referrer-policy, frame-ancestors none, backup-page + artifact noindex, immutable-media caching, sw no-store. Remaining: HSTS decision + security.txt + the curl-based deployed-origin headers gate (prod smoke family) - wave close. Memory saved: feedback_headers_file_is_prod_only_behavior. || AN UNAUDITED PRIVILEGE SURFACE: 8 SECURITY DEFINER RPCs THAT NOTHING CALLS AND ANYONE CAN (2026-08-27). Asked which client-callable RPCs have no caller, and narrowed it honestly: 285 grantable routines -> 103 that are OURS (excluding pgvector's array_to_halfvec/binary_quantize and trigger-returning functions, which are called BY triggers) -> 76 with no DB-side caller (asking pg_proc.prosrc and pg_policies rather than grepping files, because is_marketplace_admin is invoked by 29 RLS POLICIES and no page) -> 18 with no caller anywhere: not a page, not an edge function, not another function, not a policy. ★8 OF THE 10 THAT NOTHING AT ALL CALLS ARE SECURITY DEFINER - acknowledge_alert, suppress_alert, toggle_feedback_upvote, publish_service_showcase, fetch_session_memory, rerank_kb_chunks, ai_cache_bump, ai_cache_sweep_expired - so they run with the definer's rights, bypassing RLS, and every one is granted to authenticated. A function nobody uses is a function nobody reviews, which makes it the most comfortable place for a privilege bug to sit. ai_cache_bump and ai_cache_sweep_expired are plainly internal cache maintenance that no end user should be able to invoke at all - this is the recorded definer-cron-helper-is-user-callable-by-default class, recurring. MITIGATION ALREADY PRESENT: all 8 pin a search_path (2 the stronger 'pg_catalog, public'), so the classic search-path hijack is closed; the exposure is the GRANT, not the definition. ★AND THE FEATURES THEY LOOK LIKE ARE NOT BROKEN: alert-hub's acknowledgeAlert writes alert_dismissals DIRECTLY (delete/upsert under RLS) rather than calling acknowledge_alert, so acking works and the RPC is an unused parallel implementation - redundancy, not absence, which is why nothing looks wrong from the glass. Remaining: decide per function whether to REVOKE the grant (internal helpers) or adopt the RPC and retire the direct write (feature paths) - either resolves the drift, and leaving two implementations is what lets them diverge. ★CORRECTION TO THE ABOVE, MADE BY READING ALL FOUR RATHER THAN GENERALISING FROM THE CATEGORY: there is NO cross-tenant exposure among them. The worry was an IDOR - DEFINER functions that take a caller-supplied ID bypass RLS, so they must do the scoping themselves. Each of the four that takes an id DOES: fetch_session_memory filters `am.worker_id = auth.uid()`, so a guessed session id returns nothing that is not yours; suppress_alert requires an active hive_members row matching auth.uid() for that alert's hive; publish_service_showcase refuses unless client_auth_uid = auth.uid(). These are correctly-written DEFINER functions - they carry the check that RLS would otherwise have carried. ★AND THE FOURTH IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF PROBLEM: rerank_kb_chunks reads NO table at all. It is a placeholder that echoes the ids you passed with a hardcoded 0.95 score ('actual reranking via LLM happens in edge function'), so there is nothing to leak - but if anything ever adopts it, every chunk comes back with the same fabricated confidence and the caller believes reranking happened. That is the proxy-oracle class: a function that reports success while the payoff is missing. Inert today because nothing calls it; a landmine the moment something does. ★SO THE FINDING IS SMALLER AND MORE PRECISE THAN THE CATEGORY SUGGESTED: not a privilege hole, but (a) unnecessary GRANTs on internal helpers - ai_cache_bump and ai_cache_sweep_expired are cache maintenance with no business being user-callable - and (b) a placeholder that will lie confidently if adopted. Remaining: revoke the internal-helper grants, and either implement rerank_kb_chunks or drop it so it cannot be adopted by mistake. || ★FOUR SHIPPED FEATURES WERE DEAD IN PRODUCTION, BLOCKED BY OUR OWN CSP — found by sweeping the class instead of patching the instance (2026-08-28). T169's Turnstile finding was the THIRD prod-only failure recorded in `_headers`, so rather than fix it and move on, every external host referenced by shipped code was enumerated and checked against the policy. Four more were blocked, every one a live feature on a live page: analytics.html loads Plotly from cdn.plot.ly via <script src> (charts never render); engineering-design.html loads html2pdf from cdnjs (PDF export dead); engineering-design.js calls engineering-calc-api.onrender.com for /pdf and /diagram (both dead on connect-src); and marketplace.html's map is dead TWICE OVER — tiles.openfreemap.org missing from connect-src, and MapLibre builds its renderer in a Worker from a blob: URL while `worker-src` appeared ZERO times in the file, so it inherited default-src 'self' and blocked the worker outright. None of this fails locally: `_headers` is served only by Netlify, and the sole symptom is a console message in someone else's browser. ★THE MAP IS THE CASE WORTH REMEMBERING, because nobody was ignorant: wh-map.js states the requirement in its OWN header — 'Prod CSP needs connect-src https://tiles.openfreemap.org + worker-src blob:'. It was written down, correctly, by the person who knew it, in the file that needed it, and never reached the file that ENFORCES it. A note in the consumer is not a change in the policy. That is the identical shape as the Turnstile switch, one abstraction layer over. FIX: script-src gains cdn.plot.ly + cdnjs.cloudflare.com, connect-src gains tiles.openfreemap.org + engineering-calc-api.onrender.com, and worker-src 'self' blob: is declared — granting exactly what ships, nothing wider. ★LOCKED BY A NEW GATE, csp-covers-what-ships, registered in Platform. It runs TWO independent checks because the failures arrive two ways: MECHANICAL (every external <script src> and stylesheet <link> host must be permitted) and DOCUMENTARY (any 'CSP needs <directive> <value>' written in a source comment must be honored) — the second is precisely what the map incident asked for. Teeth-proven by reverting all four grants and watching it name all four, including that an absent worker-src is a DENIAL rather than a neutral omission. Self-test: 7 cases. ★TWO INSTRUMENT FLAWS FOUND AND FIXED BEFORE THE GATE WAS TRUSTED, both by sampling its own output: (1) it read 90 characters past an href looking for rel=stylesheet, reached into the NEXT <link> on the following line, and reported 8 pages as loading a remote stylesheet from supabase.co when all 8 were rel='preconnect' — eight fabricated defects, avoided by matching the whole tag; (2) its requirement parser ended a sentence at the first '.', which lands inside a hostname, so wh-map.js's requirement was read as 'connect-src https://tiles' and the '+ worker-src blob:' half was never parsed — the gate was silently checking one of the two things it existed to check. ★HONEST SCOPE: connect-src is NOT checked against every https:// literal in the source. Those are dominated by things CSP does not govern (anchor hrefs, JSON-LD @context, canonical URLs, placeholder examples), and a check that noisy gets muted — which is worse than no check. So the onrender.com API constant is fixed but not gated; the documentary half covers that class where it matters, since whoever adds a remote API is exactly the person who writes the requirement down. pct -> 88. || ★THE PUBLISH-ROOT EXPOSURE: the missing piece was never the fix, it was the EVIDENCE that a targeted fix is safe (2026-08-28). netlify.toml sets publish = '.', so every gate baseline, audit report and platform-check log in the repo root is fetchable at the live domain — by the file's own count ~276 files, several over 70KB, whose text narrates internal architecture, table names and security findings. `_headers` marks them noindex and says plainly that 'the real fix is excluding them from the publish step', and the reason that was never done is recorded right there: design-system.html legitimately reads *_baseline.json, so a blanket block breaks a live page. ★MEASURED WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEEDED, which nobody had: exactly EIGHT root data files are fetched by shipped code — api_adoption_baseline.json, api_component_registry.json, component_adoption_baseline.json and design_component_registry.json (design-system.html), field_impact_preview.json (impact-preview.js), learn_links.json (learn-link.js), and VALIDATOR_REGISTRY.json + platform_health.json (validator-catalog.html). None is a .log, a .jsonl, a *-output.txt or a *_report.json — so those four families can be force-404'd with zero effect on any page, following the precedent already in netlify.toml, where /_fixtures/* is blocked exactly that way. Only the *_baseline.json family genuinely must stay reachable, and only two of its members. ★NOT SHIPPED, DELIBERATELY: netlify.toml is itself PROD-ONLY — nothing local serves it — so a redirect I cannot execute here is a change whose first real run is on Ian's site, and a pattern that over-matches would 404 a working dashboard rather than fail loudly. That is a deploy decision on his gate, not a default for me to pick while he is away. The evidence is what was missing, and it is now recorded: the block is safe for four families, unsafe for the fifth, and the exact eight exceptions are enumerated. || ★A SIXTH INSTANCE, IN THE OTHER HEADER — AND IT WAS LEFT BEHIND BY THE FIX FOR THE FIRST TWO (2026-08-28). The Permissions-Policy incident this file already documents fixed camera and microphone and left `geolocation=()` untouched, because nobody asked whether anything used it. Something does: marketplace-seller.html publishes a service provider's LIVE LOCATION to their client during an active job — watchPosition, one write per 15s for battery, a visible '📍 Sharing your live location with this job's client' indicator, stopping when the job set empties, with the column readable only through v_service_job_tracking. An EMPTY allowlist denies every origin INCLUDING self, so in production that feature never started. ★AND IT FAILED INVISIBLY IN THE CRUELEST WAY: its own error callback calls _svcGeoIndicator(false), so a blocked permission hides the very indicator that would have shown something was wrong — the provider sees exactly what 'no active job' looks like, and the client waiting to see them move sees nothing, with no error anywhere. Fixed to geolocation=(self), matching what camera and microphone already had. ★THE GATE NOW COVERS BOTH HEADERS, because they are one class: csp-covers-what-ships maps the browser APIs the code actually calls (geolocation / camera / microphone) to the policy features that gate them, treats `feature=()` as the denial it is, and correctly ignores an UNDECLARED feature (which defaults to allowing self) and vendored bundles like maplibre-gl that reference APIs we may never invoke. Teeth-proven by reverting to geolocation=() and watching it name the file and the reason; self-test now 10 cases. trajectories.title: Abuse resistance as UX: rate limits meet real users
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the at-the-cap journey driven live). Drove the community composers at their real DB caps (community_posts 2000, community_replies 1000, report details 500 - all CHECK constraints, verified in pg_constraint). THE COOLDOWN REFUSALS ALREADY MEET THE BAR: 'Slow down, wait Ns before posting again' names both the limit and its reset, which is exactly what rate_limit_legible asks for. ★THE DEFECT WAS THE SILENT HALF OF THE SAME PAGE: community.html had built the right pattern and applied it unevenly - the post composer (2000) and report box (500) each carried a live 'n / max' counter, the reply box (1000) carried none. A maxlength with no counter is a SILENT WALL: the textarea stops accepting keystrokes and the person reads that as a broken keyboard, not a rule, losing the thought they were part-way through. Added the counter in the page's own idiom, wired its input listener, and reset it at BOTH clear sites (thread open + after a reply posts) because a counter holding the last message's length is a stale reading, worse than none. Live-verified all three: '37 / cap' while typing, '0 / cap' when cleared, 0 pageerrors. ★AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG TWICE BEFORE THE FINDING SURVIVED: a static scan inferring the counter id from the field id ('<id>-char-count') reported #post-content as uncounted - its counter is #post-char-count, so the convention is not a convention. It also listed 42 'uncounted' fields platform-wide, most of them 200-char part-number boxes that need no counter. Neither was banked. The prover is therefore LIVE and types into each field, because a counter is whatever visible element MOVES WHEN YOU TYPE. Locked as 'composer-caps-visible' (teeth: counter id disabled -> 'reply-content: no counter', exit 1). REMAINING: burst-sizing review for bulk-approving supervisors, and the appeal/raise path statement (wave close). The AI-quota classes ride with T39. || ★THE RESET-TIME CAPABILITY EXISTS IN ONE DOMAIN AND IS ABSENT IN THE ONE WORKERS ACTUALLY HIT (2026-08-28). This trajectory asks whether each quota's refusal names the limit AND when it clears. Split answer. THE MARKETPLACE SIDE DOES IT: marketplace.html carries _retryAfterSeconds(err), which reads err.retryAfter / err.retry_after and even digs a digit out of err.hint, with a comment noting 'most gateways answer a rate limit with Retry-After, in seconds or as an HTTP date' - and marketplace-seller and marketplace-seller-profile use the same helper. So a rate-limited buyer or seller can be told how long. ★THE AI SIDE CANNOT, AND THE REASON IS UPSTREAM OF THE COPY: ai-gateway never emits Retry-After at all - zero references in the function - so there is nothing for the client to surface, and whAiError's 429 branch accordingly says only 'You have hit the AI rate limit. Wait a moment and try again.' (bilingual, and honest as far as it goes). That is the quota a worker meets most often, because the AI budget is shared across the whole platform and drains on a busy Friday. 'Wait a moment' is exactly the sentence that makes someone retry immediately and hit it again. ★SO THE FIX IS NOT COPY: the gateway has to emit the window it already knows about, and only then does the taxonomy have something true to say. An edge-function change, and one that depends on whether the upstream provider hands back a retry window at all - which is why it is recorded rather than guessed at. The rest of the taxonomy is strong: the 401 branch names the cause AND the state of the user's work ('your typed work is still on this page'), which is the bar the 429 branch has not got the data to meet. pct 60 -> 74. || ★BUILT THE CAPABILITY THAT WAS MISSING, because the window was computable all along (2026-08-28). _shared/rate-limit.ts now carries retry_after_seconds on the BASE RateLimitResult - the base, because all six limiters share that shape and any of them can be the one that denies, notably the per-user limiter a worker meets first at 25/hour. Two helpers compute it honestly: secondsToNextHour() for the route limiter, whose counter is bucketed to the hour so the reset is EXACT; and secondsToWindowEnd(start, span) for the rolling windows, which falls back to the FULL span when a start is unreadable - over-stating the wait rather than under-stating it, since an under-stated wait sends someone straight back into the wall. Both deny paths in checkAIRateLimit populate it, day and hour, using the window starts already in hand. rateLimitedResponse now emits it three ways: a real sentence ('Try again in about 4 minutes' rather than 'in an hour'), BOTH body spellings retryAfter and retry_after (because the existing client helper _retryAfterSeconds looks for both), and an actual Retry-After header. When no window is known it keeps the old wording rather than inventing a duration - a wrong 'try again in 2 minutes' is worse than a vague hour. ★VERIFIED NUMERICALLY, since no deno is available here: both helpers were run against hour boundaries (00:00 -> 3600, 59:59 -> 1) and window ages (10 min in -> 3000, 59 min in -> 60, stale -> 1, null and garbage -> full span). All correct. ★AND A SECOND FINDING FELL OUT OF IT: rateLimitedResponse takes a `scope` parameter and NOT ONE of its ten callers passes it. So a DAILY limit hit has always reported 'Try again in an hour' - wrong by up to a day, in the direction that makes someone retry uselessly. ★WHAT IS OWED: the callers must pass rl.scope and rl.retry_after_seconds, and the gateway's composite result needs to carry them out of checkClassedRateLimit. That is plumbing across 10+ edge functions I cannot deploy or live-test from here, so it is left named rather than half-done. The hard part - knowing WHEN the window reopens - is built and proven. pct 74 -> 82. || ★AND THE WIRING IS DONE FOR THE PATH THAT MATTERS, after finding the ROOT of why nobody ever passed it. ai-gateway annotated its rate-limit result with an INLINE STRUCTURAL TYPE - { allowed, remaining, hive_remaining?, user_cap? } - narrower than what the limiters actually return. So `scope` and the new `retry_after_seconds` were discarded at the door by the type annotation itself, rateLimitedResponse got neither, its `scope` parameter defaulted to 'hour', and a DAILY ceiling reported 'Try again in an hour' - wrong by up to a day, in the direction that makes someone retry uselessly. That is why none of the ten callers passed scope: the value was there and the type said it was not. ★THE SAME DISCARD APPEARED THREE MORE TIMES INSIDE THE LIMITERS: checkClassedRateLimit and checkUserRateLimit's hive gate both call an inner limiter, receive its verdict complete with window, and flatten it away one line later. All three now propagate. checkSoloRateLimit's two denies and checkUserRateLimit's per-user deny compute their own from the window_start they already read - and the per-user one matters most, because at 25/hour it binds BEFORE the hive's 50, so it is the refusal a worker actually meets. Both 429 builders now emit a real sentence, both body spellings, and a Retry-After header. userRateLimitedResponse already did the kindest part - telling the person their teammates are unaffected, so they do not think they broke the platform - and simply never said how long. ★VERIFIED AS FAR AS IS POSSIBLE WITHOUT DEPLOYING: both window helpers tested numerically across hour boundaries and window ages, and the message formatter across every threshold (1s singular, 45s, 1 minute, 2 minutes, 1 hour, 24 hours, and the undefined case falling back to the old wording rather than inventing a duration). validate_edge_config and validate_edge_contracts both green. What remains is the other nine callers of rateLimitedResponse, which still pass neither argument and therefore keep the old behaviour - safe, just not improved. pct 82 -> 88. || ★THE WIRING IS COMPLETE: 53 CALL SITES, 0 BARE. All four 429 builders now receive the window everywhere they are called - rateLimitedResponse 12, routeRateLimitedResponse 19, soloRateLimitedResponse 19, userRateLimitedResponse 3 - across every edge function, verified by an argument-counting audit rather than a grep, because the count is the claim. The two sibling builders got the same treatment as the first: routeRateLimitedResponse said 'Try again later' while its counter is bucketed to the hour and therefore the MOST exactly knowable of the three; soloRateLimitedResponse said 'in an hour' to someone 55 minutes into a rolling window who needed five. ★AND MY OWN ENUMERATION WAS WRONG TWICE, BOTH TIMES BY A SILENT CAP - the lesson this platform already records as 'no silent caps'. I reported 'ten callers' from a grep piped through head -10; there were TWELVE, and voice-logbook-entry and voice-report-intent only surfaced when a later uncapped listing showed them. Then a pattern requiring a string-literal route missed ai-gateway and platform-gateway, which pass the route as a VARIABLE. Both were caught by re-auditing with no limit instead of trusting the sweep that did the work - a count taken from a truncated list is not a count. ★VERIFIED: four scripted edits spot-read back in full, validate_edge_config and validate_edge_contracts green, no stray .tmp files from the scripted rewrites. What remains needs a deploy to observe, which is Ian's gate. pct 88 -> 94. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: the fix is verified and the registered gate composer-caps-visible PASSES standalone (re-run this session). Awaiting the next full-board earn to promote to locked. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: The Turnstile & bot-defense experience
trajectories.basis: posture read: su-turnstile div ships INERT (no sitekey configured) = bot defense is OFF in prod today; the wiring is one dashboard sitekey away (GoTrue captcha + the client's conditional mount both exist). Whether to ARM it is Ian's posture decision (signup friction vs bot pressure - the prod smoke signed up unchallenged). Remaining: the defense-active prod-smoke check once armed + challenge a11y (wave close). || THE BOT-DEFENSE POSTURE READ IN FULL: DELIBERATE, FAIL-SAFE, AND CURRENTLY UNARMED (2026-08-27). Turnstile is wired configure-to-enable: mountTurnstile() returns immediately unless window.WH_TURNSTILE_SITEKEY is set, and WH_TURNSTILE_SITEKEY is set NOWHERE in the codebase - it appears only in the read itself and in two comments describing the arming procedure. So bot defense is OFF today, by choice rather than by oversight, and the choice is documented at the call site. ★THE WIRING IS CORRECTLY COUPLED, WHICH IS THE PART THAT COULD HAVE BEEN SUBTLY WRONG: a captchaToken is sent ONLY when a widget actually exists, because GoTrue REJECTS a token when captcha is disabled in the project - so a half-armed state (client sending tokens, server not expecting them) would break signup completely for everyone. The inert path therefore runs signUp() exactly as before, no token attached. Arming is genuinely two-sided and external: a Cloudflare sitekey AND the Supabase Auth > Bot Protection toggle, both Ian's to set. Remaining: unchanged - the defense-active prod-smoke check once armed, and challenge a11y (T48 seam) at wave close. || ★THE SWITCH COULD NOT BE THROWN — A LATENT FRONT-DOOR OUTAGE, ARMED AND WAITING FOR THE CONFIG CHANGE THAT WOULD FIRE IT (2026-08-28). First, the posture question this trajectory asks is answered and the answer is deliberate: bot defense is OFF. window.WH_TURNSTILE_SITEKEY is set NOWHERE in shipped code — only in tests/auth-identity-arc-i.spec.ts, using Cloudflare's always-passes test key — and the Arc I integration is a genuine configure-to-enable design (inert loader, no captchaToken sent when unconfigured), which is the right shape for a feature waiting on a provider. ★BUT THE SWITCH WAS DOCUMENTED AS TWO STEPS AND HAD A SILENT THIRD, in `_headers` — a tracked local file nobody flipping that switch would think to open. CSP script-src did not permit challenges.cloudflare.com, and NO frame-src was declared at all, so it inherited default-src 'self' and would have blocked Turnstile's challenge iframe. The consequence is not a degraded widget, it is SIGNUP DYING PLATFORM-WIDE: script blocked => window.turnstile never defined => mountTurnstile()'s render() returns early => _turnstileToken() returns null => signUp() sends no captchaToken — while step two of the very same switch tells Supabase Auth to reject exactly that. The feature meant to protect the front door would have closed it, the only evidence a console CSP violation, and `_headers` is PROD-ONLY so nothing local reproduces it. This is the third instance of that class in this file ([[feedback_headers_file_is_prod_only_behavior]]: Permissions-Policy killed mic+camera, CSP kept GA4 dead) and the first LATENT one. FIX: script-src gains https://challenges.cloudflare.com and frame-src is declared for it — Cloudflare's documented requirement — granted now, while the feature is off, so the switch is TRUE when someone finally throws it. ★AND THE GATE'S OWN SCOPE CLAIM WAS WRONG: validate_signup_bot_protection's docstring called the remainder 'the PROVIDER half = attributed, out of local scope', when one of those steps was entirely local — a ceiling written into a tool's docstring ([[feedback_a_ceiling_written_into_a_tools_docstring]]). The gate now audits the edge half too, with an ABSENT frame-src treated as a FAILURE rather than a neutral omission, because CSP's fallback makes the omission and the denial the same header to a browser. Teeth-proven on the real file (pre-fix policy => 2 FAILs naming both halves, green after) and in a self-test carrying the exact shipped policy plus a frame-ancestors decoy, since frame-ancestors answers the opposite question from frame-src and must not be mistaken for it. pct 25 -> 80; the remainder is challenge accessibility and the errored-challenge retry path, both un-probed while the widget cannot render. || ★MY OWN FIX WAS ONE KEYSTROKE FROM SHIPPING THE SAME BUG IT REPAIRED — caught by auditing my change instead of assuming it was purely additive. Declaring frame-src REPLACES the default-src fallback rather than adding to it, so introducing the directive `frame-src https://challenges.cloudflare.com` silently REVOKED same-origin framing. assistant.html lazily embeds voice-journal.html for its Journal tab (:498, frame.src = 'voice-journal.html?embedded=1'), so the Turnstile fix would have broken the assistant in production — invisible exactly the way the original defect was, since _headers has no local equivalent and a blocked frame throws nothing the page can observe. Corrected to `frame-src 'self' https://challenges.cloudflare.com`, and the gate now asserts it: a declared frame-src missing 'self' FAILS by name, with the near-miss policy added to the self-test (7 cases, all passing). The lesson generalises past this directive — a CSP directive that inherits by absence becomes exclusive the moment it is written, so ADDING one is never purely additive. (The two phrases above were eaten once already: written through a shell that evaluated their backticks as command substitution, leaving 'introducing  silently REVOKED' and 'Corrected to ,' in the record. Repaired via a quoted heredoc — the same trap, and the same fix, as the earlier regex-escape incident this session. A record that loses the exact string it is about is worse than no record, because it still reads as complete.) || ★PCT FIELD CORRECTED DOWN TO MATCH THIS BASIS (2026-08-31). The field read 86 while the basis's own last word was 80 - a later note revised the number and only the prose was updated. Every one of the six rows found this way was inflated, never deflated, which is the direction drift always takes when nothing checks it: the number a reader trusts drifts up while the narrative underneath it says otherwise. Now gated by pct-matches-basis. pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_privacy_consent.mjs (gate privacy-consent), 6/6 lenses clean after TWO real defects were fixed and four false findings were traced to the prover's own lens. FIXED: export-hive-data had shipped since Phase 5 Track A as the PDPA Article 16 right-to-access export and NO page invoked it - the right lived in the repository and not in the product - so it is now reachable from the hive menu beside Leave Hive, supervisor-gated to match the function's own contract, with 403 and network failure named rather than swallowed (T164). And asking to be ERASED had no mechanism anywhere: migration 20260907000002 adds data_deletion_requests with own-row RLS and no self-resolve, and hive.html now lets any member ask and tells them it landed - it records the ask rather than purging, because a hive's logbook is someone else's audit evidence (T164). FIXED: analytics fired with no consent state at all; index.html now declares a DENIED Consent Mode default BEFORE gtag config, replays a stored answer before config so a choice survives a reload, and asks once in a fixed-position notice that cannot shift the layout, with 'No thanks' remembered as a real answer (T165). Five sharing surfaces all say who will read what is written there (T166). No shipped page carries a secret VALUE and a CSP reaches the deployed origin (T167). The Turnstile widget is inert until a sitekey is configured and is verified by Supabase Auth's own bot protection, not by our code (T169). One legal page exists and the schema collects zero age-or-school fields (T172).
trajectories.note: MEASURED, so the decision can be made on facts rather than a guess. Bot defense is OFF on BOTH halves and deliberately so: window.WH_TURNSTILE_SITEKEY is assigned NOWHERE in the codebase (so mountTurnstile() is a no-op and the #su-turnstile div stays empty), and GoTrue's GOTRUE_SECURITY_CAPTCHA_ENABLED is empty. The code is correct as written - it is inert-by-default behind a documented TWO-condition arm (a sitekey AND Supabase Auth > Bot Protection), and signUp() sends no captchaToken while disabled, which matters because GoTrue REJECTS a captchaToken when captcha is off. So arming one half alone would break signup; both must move together. WHAT PROTECTS SIGNUP TODAY: GoTrue rate limits are live - verify 30/hr and anonymous 30/hr - so the door is throttled even unguarded, and there is no abuse signal to act on (0 signups in the last day on this fixture). ★NOT ARMED BY ME, AND NOT A CEILING I AM HIDING BEHIND: the provider half needs a Cloudflare sitekey and a dashboard toggle, both outside this repo, and turning it on changes who can sign up - Ian's call, made cheaper by the numbers above. Left at walked rather than advanced, because the trajectory's own done-definition is 'posture chosen, wired, humane' and only the measurement is mine to finish. REMAINS once armed: challenge accessibility (the T48 seam) and the failure path when the challenge itself errors.

trajectories.title: Sensitive-data display hygiene
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25): the class receipts - the B5 no-raw-internals dim + this session's T69 fix (a credentials-location pointer removed from a page ANY signed-in user could open - the exact screen-share hazard) + password show-toggles with aria-pressed exist on the auth modal. Remaining: the sensitive-render sweep formalized (patterns: keys, tokens, full contact chains on roster views), partial-masking decisions for emails/phones, admin-page screen-share audit (wave close). SENSITIVE-RENDER SWEEP MEASURED + ONE REAL FIX 2026-08-26. Secrets are already covered by three registered gates (hardcoded-secrets, prod-path-leak, env-secret-coverage), so the unique half is CONTACT CHAINS on the glass. Swept every render site: the founder console's 13-digit GCash reference and the seller's buyer contacts are legitimate AT THE POINT OF USE (the founder must check that reference in the GCash app; the seller must dial that number) and RLS scopes both to the party who needs them - masking them permanently would break the job. The REAL exposure was volume: the seller inbox rendered EVERY buyer's phone/email at once, so one screenshot (this platform's own share culture, T125) hands over the contact details of everyone who ever asked. FIXED with reveal-on-demand: a 'Show contact' control per inquiry that replaces itself with the copyable value on tap - zero cost when calling one buyer, no leak when not. LIVE-PROVEN as the seller on a staged inquiry: hidden before the tap, visible after, probe cleaned. Remaining: partial-masking decisions for roster emails/phones, admin-page screen-share audit. || ★A NEW PASSWORD WAS BEING TYPED IN THE CLEAR, BECAUSE AN OPTION WAS SILENTLY DROPPED (2026-08-27). index.html:2953 asks for a new password through whPrompt with { inputLabel: 'New password', inputType: 'password', okLabel: 'Update password' }. Measured live: the rendered field was type="text" with no autocomplete - the password visible on screen as it was typed, on a platform whose station tablet is shared by a whole crew and whose own T121 work exists because people look over each other's shoulders. The author asked for masking; nothing masked, and nothing said so. An unsupported option that throws no error is the worst failure mode available: the caller believes the request took effect and the evidence is invisible until somebody renders it. ★IT TOOK TWO FIXES, AND THE FIRST ONE LOOKED LIKE A FAILURE: _mount did not READ inputType (added, allow-listed to text/password/email/number/tel/url so a caller cannot inject an arbitrary type), and after that change the field STILL rendered text - because whPrompt builds an explicit object for _mount and never FORWARDED the option. Two boundaries had to agree before masking could work and only one did, so fixing the visible half changed nothing and read exactly like a fix that had not worked. Verified live: type="password", autocomplete="new-password" (correct for a NEW password rather than a remembered one). Blast radius checked across 10 pages that load utils.js - whConfirm and whPrompt present everywhere, all painted, zero page errors. Remaining: the masked-field show-toggle, and the roster email/phone masking sweep. || GENERALISED THE CLASS ACROSS EVERY SHARED HELPER, AND IT IS REAL EXACTLY ONCE (2026-08-27). Having found one silently-dropped option, the obvious question is how many more there are: 19 wh* helpers take an options object, so I compared what each READS against what callers PASS. First pass reported four - whAutoSaveDraft/auto, whModalA11y/onClose, whConfirm/danger, whGcashPasteWire/receipt - and THREE were my instrument. (1) whModalA11y DOES read onClose: it calls opts.onClose() on Escape, with a fallback that clicks the modal's own close control if none is given. My scan read only the first 2600 chars of each function and onKey sits deeper, so a fixed window turned a correct helper into a defect. (2) whAutoSaveDraft reads auto for the same reason. (3) whGcashPasteWire never receives 'receipt' at all - my key-matching regex found 'receipt:' INSIDE the string 'Read your receipt: ' in an onFill toast. ★WHAT SURVIVES: whConfirm ignores 'danger', passed only by design-system.html, a component showcase no user acts on. So the password inputType was the ONE production instance of this class, and it is fixed. ★THE AUDIT WAS STILL WORTH RUNNING - a class that costs a plaintext password once is worth checking twenty helpers for - but the honest result is that the platform's helper contracts are otherwise kept. Both correction mechanisms were the same discipline: read the WHOLE function, and do not let a pattern match inside a string. || THE CONTACT-EXPOSURE SWEEP, INCLUDING AN ANON WRITE TEST THAT LOOKED ALARMING AND IS NOT (2026-08-27). Eight tables hold contact data. THE ROSTER IS CLEAN: hive.html contains exactly one mention of 'email' and it is a COMMENT about password recovery - member emails are never rendered to the crew. Inquiry contacts are scoped to the two parties by the reads themselves (.eq('seller_name'...) / .eq('buyer_name'...)), so a contact reaches only the person transacting. ★THE ALARMING PART, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: anon holds INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and SELECT GRANTS on the base marketplace_listings table, and its write policies are roles={public}, which includes anon. That reads like an open door. It is not: every write policy predicates on seller_name IN (SELECT auth_worker_names()), which for an unauthenticated caller is an empty set. PROVEN as the anon role rather than argued - INSERT raised 'new row violates row-level security policy'; UPDATE of another seller's listing reported UPDATE 0; zero probe rows remained. Grants are broad and RLS is the gate, which is this platform's stated posture and it holds. ★AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT PROVED NOTHING: my test row priced at PHP1 was refused by guard_listing_meets_minimum, a BUSINESS rule, before RLS was ever consulted - a refusal is not evidence of the refusal you are testing, so the price had to be made valid before the security question could be asked at all. ★ONE THING WORTH STATING RATHER THAN FIXING: v_marketplace_listings_truth exposes seller_contact and anon may SELECT it - which is the contact-only marketplace working as designed (the flow IS contacting the seller), and also means a scraper can harvest every seller's number. That is a product posture, not a bug, and it deserves to be a stated choice. Remaining: the masked-field show-toggle. || THE SHOW-TOGGLE EXISTS AND IS BUILT CORRECTLY - LAST ITEM CLOSED (2026-08-27). All four password fields on the platform are type=password (index's sign-in, sign-up and repeat, plus integrations' CMMS token with autocomplete=off, which is right for a pasted API secret). All three on index carry a reveal control: onclick="togglePwd('si-password', this)" with a 44px square tap target for a gloved hand. ★AND togglePwd UPDATES THE STATE THAT MATTERS, not just the pixels: it flips input.type, recolours the button, and sets BOTH aria-label ('Show password' <-> 'Hide password') and aria-pressed. So a screen-reader user learns the control's current state AND what pressing it will do next - the same property this session's selection-is-exposed gate enforces for tab sets, applied correctly here without a gate telling it to. ★MY SEARCH MISSED IT TWICE: a scan for controls flipping an input type found ZERO, because the pattern wanted a quoted literal and this assigns a TERNARY; only the three aria-labels saying 'Show password' proved the toggles existed and forced a second look. The labels were the evidence my code-shape pattern could not see. So T170's exposure surface is measured end to end: roster clean, inquiry contacts party-scoped, anon writes RLS-denied (proven as the anon role), the prompt now masks, and reveal is a real, accessible affordance. Remaining: nothing owed beyond the wave-close re-earn; the public seller_contact stays a stated product posture rather than a defect. || LOCKED 2026-08-28. Gate a-secret-stays-masked holds both halves: every password field ships type=password and whPrompt FORWARDS inputType (the measured gap - _mount honoured it while whPrompt built its own options object and dropped it, so a caller asking for a masked prompt got a plain text box and a secret was typed in the clear, with nothing looking wrong to anyone), and the reveal toggle flips BOTH aria-label and aria-pressed, so the person who cannot check by looking is told what the control does AND whether their password is on screen right now. ★THE GATE ANCHORS ON THE ACCESSIBLE NAME, NOT THE CODE SHAPE, for the reason this trajectory already recorded: a search for controls flipping an input type found ZERO twice, because it expected a quoted literal and togglePwd assigns a ternary - the three aria-labels were the only evidence the toggles existed. Selftest 8/8. Remaining: the wave-close re-earn; the public seller_contact stays a stated product posture. || ★LOCKED 2026-08-31: the wave-close re-earn landed and every gate this row names read PASS on a FULL board (a-secret-stays-masked). That was the only item its basis still owed. pct 97 -> 100.

trajectories.title: Compliance evidence on demand (the ISO-minded client)
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the sales-claim alignment sweep run and locked). Swept all 117 public pages for certification and compliance language. THE POSTURE IS HONEST AND NOW MEASURED rather than asserted: no WorkHive self-certification exists anywhere - no SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR-compliant, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, bank-grade or military-grade. All 30 raw hits were a standard the CUSTOMER is audited against (ISO 9001/14001/45001, DOLE OSHS), a PERSON's credential (TESDA NC II/III, CMRP, PSME/IIEE), or the skill matrix's own 'certified level' vocabulary. ★ONE REAL OVERCLAIM, AND IT WAS A CATEGORY ERROR RATHER THAN A BOAST: dole-iso-audit-trail-from-logbook claimed logbook entries 'satisfy Clause 10.2', the PM dashboard 'satisfies Clause 7.1.5', safety observations 'satisfy Clause 9.1.1'. A clause is satisfied by an ORGANISATION's management system, evidenced by records - software holds the evidence, it cannot confer conformity. It reads as reassurance, so a plant could enter a surveillance audit believing a feature had covered them. Rewritten to 'gives you the records Clause 10.2 asks you to retain' / 'evidences Clause 9.1.1' plus a callout stating the distinction outright; live-verified styled and visible, 0 pageerrors, and the false wording is gone from the rendered page. Locked as 'compliance-claim-honesty' with two assertions and a deliberate NON-catch: 'the digital record satisfies three properties' and 'export patterns that satisfy auditors' both survive on that same page, because a record CAN satisfy a property and an export CAN satisfy a sampling need - only a NUMBERED clause as the object is the error. The self-certification half is guard-the-absence at zero, since that is the most tempting sentence to add to a sales page and the most expensive to be wrong about. Teeth proven on both halves. REMAINING: the evidence STORY as an assembled artifact (a compliance page or PDF) is scoped content and stays Ian's call; compliance-relevant export verification rides with T49. || ★THE ENTERPRISE CLAIM IS REAL; ITS REFUSAL WAS THE ROUGH PART - found, fixed (2026-08-28). The probe asks whether the sales-facing enterprise claims are true, with the SSO button named as the specimen. VERDICT: it is genuinely WIRED, not decoration - signInWithSSO prompts for a company domain via whPrompt, calls db.auth.signInWithSSO({domain}), disables the button with a 'Redirecting to your identity provider' state, and follows data.url. So 'Enterprise SSO (Okta / Azure AD)' is backed by real code and is not a declared-but-never-wired claim. ★THE DEFECT WAS IN THE PATH AN EVALUATOR ACTUALLY HITS. The function had two failure branches of very different quality: the catch branch already said, bilingually via _t(), 'SSO not available for this domain. Contact your IT administrator.' - while the `error` branch three lines above toasted 'SSO error: ' + error.message, EN-only, with the provider's raw string pasted in front of the guidance. That asymmetry is the whole finding, because Supabase RETURNS an error object for a domain with no registered IdP rather than THROWING - so the rougher message was the common one, and the polished one was the rare one. An IT admin evaluating the platform, typing their domain before their team has registered anything, is exactly the person who got the raw internals. ★FIX: the error branch now carries the same bilingual sentence and a more actionable one ('Ask your IT team to register WorkHive as an SSO application in your identity provider'), with the raw error routed to console.error where it helps whoever is debugging. Verified: function brace-balanced, both branches use _t(), no error.message reaches a user, raw error reaches the console. This closes one T45 FIL-parity instance and one B5 no-raw-internals instance in the same edit. ★HONEST LIMIT: whether SSO SUCCEEDS in production depends on SAML being enabled on the Supabase project and an IdP registered - prod configuration I cannot read locally. What is verified here is that the control is real and that its refusal is now humane in both languages, not that any customer's login completes. ★CHECKER NOTE: my own verification first reported 'raw error.message still shown' and 'console.error missing' - both false. The first matched the word inside the COMMENT I had just written explaining the old behaviour; the second searched a substring missing a colon. A checker that reads comments as code, or matches an inexact literal, fails in both directions. pct 60 -> 78. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate compliance-claim-honesty re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.

trajectories.title: The child/underage & terms-eligibility posture
trajectories.basis: audit ran, two findings: (1) the terms contain NO age/eligibility clause at all - the posture is UNDEFINED, not merely unstated at signup (the spec's 'posture deliberate' ask -> Ian decision); (2) HEAVIER: terms :185 PROMISES 'You may export your data at any time and delete your account' while T77/T164 established neither export-my-data nor account-deletion exists - the terms are a claim surface making promises the product does not keep (claim-honesty at legal weight; PDPA-relevant). Either build the surfaces or the terms must state the real path (admin@ manual). Feeds T163/T164.  || FINDING (2) FIXED 2026-08-26, and it was the heavier one: the terms promised, in TWO places, a self-serve export and account deletion that do not exist. A marketing page overclaiming is bad; a TERMS page overclaiming is a promise at legal weight, made to a PH user exercising a PDPA right, and it is the document they would point to. THE FIX DID NOT DELETE THE RIGHT - the right is real, and the privacy policy already documents how it is honoured (email admin@workhiveph.com, subject 'Data Rights Request'). The terms now say exactly that and state plainly that it is handled by hand rather than through a button: same right, true sentence, no weaker. BOTH COPIES corrected - the HTML and its .md twin - because a promise surviving in either is a promise still unkept, which is the fix-every-path rule at legal weight. trajectories.title: Error-message comprehension census

It deliberately does not grade prose: a lint that guesses at sentences produces false reds, while a count of raw appends is objective and is exactly the regression signal. TEETH-PROVEN: a planted showToast('Something went wrong...') in a catch turned it RED; removing it returned green. Remaining: converting the long-tail pages (the ratchet now makes each conversion permanent). LONG TAIL STARTED same pass, ratchet 78 -> 65: inventory's 6 and pm-scheduler's 7 raw strings converted to whWriteError, each naming what happened to the WORK rather than echoing a driver message - 'The stock was NOT deducted. Nothing changed', 'The asset saved but its PM TASKS did not, so it has an empty schedule', 'Nothing was deleted - it is all still here'. Both pages re-proven live (rendered, 0 pageerrors). Parsed every showToast(..., 'error') call across the root pages and split it into top-level arguments: 63 route their message through a taxonomy helper (whReadError / whWriteError / whAiError / whListError / whAuthRequiredToast), 132 are hand-rolled — 32.3% adoption, and a real baseline where the trajectory previously had none. trajectories.note: ★'TRY AGAIN' FOR SOMETHING THAT CAN NEVER SUCCEED (2026-08-26). Generalised from T185's namesake defect by censusing every unique constraint on a user-write table (5: hive_members, hives.invite_code, worker_profiles auth_uid + username, asset_nodes tag). whWriteError passes DELIBERATE refusals through in their own words - the source even explains why, citing a seller who would 'retry forever' - but 23505 was not on that list, so a taken name/tag/username fell to the caller's 'Nothing changed; try again.' Measured by calling the real function, not by reading it. Fixed centrally: the sentence now says the value is already used and to change it, stays generic so no constraint name reaches a reader, and leaves deliberate refusals and unrelated errors untouched. Gate collision-is-not-try-again EXERCISES whWriteError; teeth proven twice, after the first attempt produced a FALSE red (Node 24's getter-only `navigator` broke the shim). ★THE RAW-ECHO CLASS IS EXTINCT, 34 -> 21 (2026-08-27). The long tail was not one job but two, and only one of them was mechanical. THE MECHANICAL HALF - a driver's own sentence pasted into a toast - is now gone from every page: project-manager's four ('Code gen failed: ', 'Create failed: ', 'Save failed: ' twice) and logbook's AI-analyze and two voice handlers. Each replacement names what happened to the WORK, which the echo never did: the change-order one says nothing was SUBMITTED (a CO is an approval request, so 'saved' was the wrong word), and the scope-item one says the entries are still in the form, because that modal stays open. ★THE SHARPEST FIND WAS NOT A TOAST: project-manager rendered `<option>Error: ${e(error.message)}</option>` into the link picker, so a failed read became a SELECTABLE CHOICE - a person could highlight 'Error: new row violates row-level security policy' as if it were a record to link. Now a disabled, non-selectable option carrying whReadError. ★AND THE STOCK ONE MATTERS MOST: logbook's inventory_deduct failure echoed the RPC while the ENTRY had already landed - the shelf and the system now disagree and only a person can reconcile them. It says that, in the same 'Entry saved. ...did NOT...' shape the PM-mirror line four lines above already used. ★NEW CENTRAL HELPER whVoiceError (utils.js), because the Web Speech API reports bare codes and three sites pasted them straight through ('Voice error: network', 'Mic error: aborted'). Closed specified vocabulary, mapped once: permission, no-microphone, network, language, aborted, plus a fallback - and every branch says the thing none of the three sites said, that dictation failing never discards what is already typed. Runtime-verified across all six codes plus an event object; the ratchet was taught it with the same admission test the other helpers passed. ★A PREMISE CHECK THAT PREVENTED A WRONG FIX: index.html:3228 says 'Sign-in failed. Check your connection' and I was about to call it the misattribution class - until reading ten lines up showed wrong credentials are answered ABOVE it at !_resp.ok ('Wrong username or password'), so that catch really does only fire on a transport throw. Left alone. The same check went the other way on logbook's three equipment reads, where 'Check your connection' WAS the only remedy offered for a read that also fails on an expired session or an RLS refusal - those now route through whReadError, so a dead session stops sending people to look at their wifi. ★WHAT 'DONE' MEANS HERE, AND WHY IT IS NOT ZERO: the 21 that remain are hand-written sentences that already name cause, work state and next step, and several are deliberately BETTER than any generic helper output - voice-journal's 'Your note IS saved - it is in the list below', marketplace-seller's 'unknown rather than zero', platform-actions' someone-else-changed-this. Driving a forward-only counter to 0 would eventually pressure someone into replacing those with 'Save failed. Try again.', which is the gate destroying the thing it exists to protect. The target was the RAW-ECHO class, and that is met; what remains is a per-string quality READ, not a mechanical conversion. ★A DIAGNOSIS WRITTEN AND THE STRING LEFT ALONE (2026-08-27). Sweeping for WRITE paths that blame the connection found three on dayplanner - and all three already routed through whWriteError, so the sweep nearly passed them. The defect was in the FALLBACK text, and the comment three lines above it had already diagnosed the problem in its own words: 'The network branch above already claimed anything connection-shaped, so "check your connection" was actively misleading here: what reaches this line is a REFUSAL.' The analysis was correct, was committed, and the string was never changed. ★A refusal answered with 'check your connection' sends someone to their wifi for a problem their wifi cannot fix. The fallbacks now state the outcome instead: 'Could not save that change. Nothing on your schedule changed.' and, for delete, the one certain consequence - 'It is still on your schedule.' ★THE TRANSFERABLE PART: a comment that names a defect is not a fix, and it reads like one to every later grep. Search for the STRING, not for whether a helper is present - all three sites looked compliant from the helper's point of view. ★THE 'SEARCH FOR THE STRING' LESSON APPLIED TO ITSELF, AND IT FOUND ITS OWN MISS (2026-08-27). T176's own transferable rule - search for the STRING, not for whether a helper is present - was run platform-wide, and the first thing it caught was T176's own incomplete fix: dayplanner's save has TWO failure paths and only the `error` branch was changed. The CATCH at :820 still said 'Save failed: check your connection' while both delete paths and the save's error branch had been fixed. ★AND THE BLAME THERE IS DOUBLY WRONG: that line is reached only AFTER the offline queue has already tried and failed to absorb the write, so if the problem really were the network the queue would have taken it. Now states the outcome, matching its sibling three lines above. ★THEN THE SWEEP FOUND A DIFFERENT AND WORSE CLASS. whReadError(err, what) does not PRINT `what`, it SPLICES it: 'Your session expired, so ' + thing + ' could not be loaded.' Four callsites passed a whole SENTENCE, so what shipped was 'Your session expired, so Could not load your equipment list. Check your connection. could not be loaded. Sign in again to see it.' MEASURED in the browser rather than reasoned. Every site had been CONVERTED to the taxonomy - the right move - with the old sentence forwarded into the slot; logbook even carries a comment above it explaining that the upstream sentence belongs in console.error and never in the notice. The author had the principle and still handed the helper a sentence. ★INVISIBLE TO EVERY OTHER CHECK: the helper is present so adoption sweeps pass it, no raw error text so the raw-echo ratchet passes it, nothing throws - and the garbled sentence only appears when a session dies mid-read, which is exactly when nobody is watching. Gate noun-slot-takes-a-noun locks it (52 callsites, 0 offenders), scoped to whReadError because whWriteError and whAiError take a fallback MESSAGE by design. ★FOUR FALSE LEADS DISCARDED ALONG THE WAY: four other connection-blaming strings sit in the `typeof whReadError === 'function' ? ... : '...'` ELSE branch, which fires only when utils.js did not load - where blaming the connection is exactly right, and 'fixing' them would have made them worse. ★A WRITE THAT CAME BACK EMPTY IS UNCONFIRMED, NOT FAILED - 4 SITES FIXED (2026-08-27). The error-string CENSUS T176 asked for was finally built (79 page-authored strings across 17 pages; what existed before was tools/error_taxonomy_baseline.json holding {"count": 20}, the forward-only counter T176's own note warns is the wrong instrument). Grading them surfaced a class nobody had named: 18 sites do `.insert(...).select(...)` and then branch on `if (!data || !data.length)` - and 8 told the user the write FAILED. It did not necessarily fail. supabase-js resolves with { data: [], error: null } when the INSERT SUCCEEDED and the RETURNING read was refused, because RLS gates SELECT separately from INSERT. ★THE ADVICE WAS THE DANGEROUS HALF: 'Request didn't save - please try again' on a service hail re-broadcasts a SECOND job to every nearby provider for work the client wants done once, and the registration equivalent creates a second provider profile. Both messages now say what is actually known ('may have been sent - we could not confirm it') and point at the LIST rather than the button. ★AND EACH ONE WAS TWO SITES, NOT ONE: the hail has a catalog path and a custom-scope path, registration has a hive path and a freelancer path, and my sweep's dedup-by-message had hidden the twins - the Edit tool refusing an ambiguous match is what revealed them. 4 fixed. ★THE PLATFORM ALREADY KNEW THE RIGHT SHAPE in four other places ('Couldn't update - the job may have moved on', 'No change saved: that top-up was already decided'), which is what makes the 8 a drift rather than a gap. ★NOT GATED YET, DELIBERATELY: 6 remain and they are the idempotent actions (availability, cancel, alert subscription, rating) where retrying costs nothing, so each needs its own verdict. A ratchet whose baseline holds untriaged entries launders unknowns as accepted - the lesson na-premise-holds was built on. They are the next slice. ★AND THEN THE TRIAGE WAS DONE, SO IT IS GATED AFTER ALL (2026-08-27, same session - correcting the line above that said 'not gated yet'). Each of the 6 survivors was checked against the SCHEMA rather than by eye: founder-console's voucher INSERT is protected by service_vouchers_code_key UNIQUE(code); the rating INSERT by marketplace_reviews_one_per_request_direction UNIQUE(request_id, direction); availability, cancel and the marketplace update are idempotent UPDATEs; the push subscription is an UPSERT with onConflict:endpoint. In every one a retry is either refused by the database or writes the same row, so 'try again' is honest advice even though 'didn't save' is imprecise - a wording item, not a hazard. THAT is what makes a baseline legitimate: 6 entries each carrying the constraint or the idempotency that justifies it. Gate unconfirmed-write-is-not-a-failure now runs over 170 write sites with 0 new offenders. ★AND THE GATE'S OWN FIXED WINDOW HID A FIFTH SITE (2026-08-27). The first version anchored FORWARD from each write with a 900-character horizon, and marketplace-seller's top-up has a seven-line comment between its .insert() and the branch - so the branch fell outside the window and 'Couldn't file the top-up. Try again.' went unreported on a MONEY action. It was found by READING the census rather than by the gate, which is the tell. Re-anchored to start at the BRANCH and look back for the write it belongs to, which has no horizon; the widened gate immediately flagged the site it had missed. That is the fixed-char-window class turning up inside the very instrument built to catch a different one - the third time today a window produced a false reading, and the first time it produced a false SILENCE, which is worse because nothing announces it. ★THE FIFTH FIX: re-filing a top-up is not destructive (service_credit_topups_ref_unique is UNIQUE on gcash_ref, so the same reference is refused), but the reader deserves to know the filing may have landed rather than be told their money went nowhere - which is exactly what the comment three lines above already argued about the sibling error branch. ★LOCKED (2026-08-27). T176's done-definition was 'the census green; new errors born compliant', and both halves now hold. THE CENSUS EXISTS: 79 strings the pages themselves author, across 17 pages, extracted and READ - not counted. What stood in for it was tools/error_taxonomy_baseline.json holding {"count": 20}, the forward-only counter this trajectory's own note warned was the wrong instrument, because driving a count to zero eventually pressures someone into replacing a precise refusal with 'Save failed. Try again.' ★EVERY FLAGGED STRING CARRIES A VERDICT rather than a fix-or-ignore: the six unconfirmed-write survivors are baselined against the SCHEMA (a unique index or an idempotent update makes the retry free); 'Cannot collect a rejection reason right now' names what cannot happen and gives the one safe action; and several my classifier flagged are simply good - 'Couldn't send the quote - the request may have closed', 'Nothing was saved, so reload and try again', 'You are offline and this report could not be saved. Keep this window open until you reconnect.' ★THE READ ALSO SHOWED WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT, which a defect list never does: this platform routinely tells a reader the STATE OF THEIR WORK ('nothing was sent', 'this action was not recorded', 'Your note was not saved') and refuses to let a failed read read as a zero - 'Your levels are unknown right now, not zero', 'Overdue and blocked work is unknown right now', 'This is a connection problem, not an empty day'. ★NEW ERRORS ARE BORN COMPLIANT via 4 gates: error-taxonomy-ratchet (raw echo), collision-is-not-try-again, noun-slot-takes-a-noun (a sentence spliced into a noun slot), unconfirmed-write-is-not-a-failure (an empty RETURNING claimed as a failure). All four registered and green; 10 strings fixed across 6 pages.

trajectories.title: Jargon & vocabulary census (the user-facing dictionary)
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the glossary REGISTRY built - this trajectory's named DELTA). Censused the domain vocabulary the product puts on the glass and asked, per term, whether the platform explains it anywhere a reader can reach: expanded in place on a page, or taught in the learn cluster. Both count. THE HABIT IS SOUND: 11 of 13 terms were already handled - MTBF, MTTR, OEE, RCM, FMEA, RPN, CPM, LOTO, SOP and P-F each have a learn guide that spells them out. ★THE ONE THAT WAS NOT: project-manager showed supervisors 'EVM: SPI 0.87, CPI 1.02, status ... (BAC ₱..., EV ₱...)' - SIX acronyms in one line - and nothing anywhere on the platform explained a single one. Earned value was the only vocabulary the product used without teaching, so 'SPI 0.87' was a number a supervisor could neither act on nor argue with. Expanded at FIRST USE in that line ('Earned value (EVM): schedule performance SPI ..., cost performance CPI ..., ... (budget at completion ₱..., earned value ₱...)') rather than by adding a glossary page, because a glossary a reader has to go and find is a glossary they do not read. Live-verified, 0 pageerrors. Locked as 'glossary-registry'. ★ONE EXCLUSION, STATED NOT SILENT: assistant.html carries a capability CATALOG describing every other page to the model ('...daily progress, EV/SPI/CPI, and sign-off') - model-facing text, not UI, which double-counts vocabulary belonging to the pages it names, and those pages are scanned on their own. Flagging it would demand a glossary inside a system prompt. Teeth proven by reverting the fix, reproducing the exact pre-fix finding. REMAINING: the standing enum-leak and one-vocabulary gates already cover raw-value leakage and term-splitting; first-use definition for NON-acronym jargon (reservation, staging, hive) is a wave-close judgement pass. || THE NON-ACRONYM PASS ATTEMPTED, AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS NOT GOOD ENOUGH TO CONVICT OR ACQUIT (2026-08-27). Ran a source census over reservation / staging / escrow / tier / hail / credits, asking whether each is explained near its FIRST use. It reported alarming numbers - 'hail' 14 occurrences across 6 pages with ZERO explained, 'credits' 13 across 5 with zero, 'staging' 7 bare in asset-hub. Spot-checking the three strongest signals dismantled all three: marketplace's only user-visible 'hail' is self-explaining IN THE SENTENCE ('Nobody is selling it right now - you can hail a service provider instead, or post a wanted listing') and its other hit is a CODE COMMENT about pm_scope_item_id; asset-hub's seven 'staging' hits do not survive a word-boundary grep of visible text at all, so they came from script or attribute content my strip did not actually remove; and marketplace's 'credits' first use IS the definition ('Publishing holds 10% of your asking price in credits; the hold is returned if you remove the listing'). ★SO THE CENSUS MEASURED SOURCE TEXT AND CALLED IT GLASS. A term's first-use context is a property of the RENDERED page - what a reader meets, in order - and a regex over HTML source cannot see that: it counts comments, dead branches, attribute values and script strings as if a person read them. This is the same shape as this session's 274-finding plural census and the role=tab count that matched a comment. Recording NO verdict either way: the evidence so far leans toward these terms being explained where they are actually visible, but three spot-checks are not a census. Remaining: run this over rendered innerText per page (the live-text instrument), not source - deferred past the board run so a browser probe cannot add load to gates that flake under it. || LIVE JARGON CENSUS ATTEMPTED, NOTHING BANKED - THE INSTRUMENT'S ESCAPING IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY (2026-08-28). Walked seven pages signed in and tested 18 domain acronyms against rendered innerText, asking whether each is glossed somewhere on the page it appears. It reported six pages clean and analytics.html carrying a bare 'PM' and 'ISO'. ★I DID NOT RECORD THAT AS A FINDING, because the follow-up that should have printed the surrounding sentences returned EMPTY for both terms - and a term cannot be simultaneously present enough to flag and absent enough to have no context. The cause is word-boundary escaping surviving three layers (bash heredoc -> file -> JS string -> RegExp), the same corruption class that has already bitten this codebase where a heredoc turned a \b into a literal backspace. When the detector and its own follow-up disagree about whether a string exists, neither reading is evidence. WHAT THE ATTEMPT DID ESTABLISH: the live-text approach is right - source-based jargon scanning cannot see what a person actually reads - and the census must be built with the regexes constructed IN the page (string literals in an .mjs file, never assembled through a shell heredoc) before any result from it is banked. Remaining: rebuild the census as a standalone .mjs with no shell-quoting layer, then run it. || REBUILT AS A STANDALONE PROVER, AND IT CORRECTS ITS OWN PREDECESSOR (2026-08-28). tools/prove_jargon_is_glossed.mjs builds every pattern as a literal INSIDE the .mjs - no shell heredoc, no re-escaping - and walks 8 pages signed in, asking of each rendered acronym whether the page also carries its expansion (in the visible flow, an <abbr>, a title, or an aria-label). ★IT REFUSES TO REPORT A BARE TERM IT CANNOT QUOTE: every finding carries the surrounding sentence, and a term the detector flags but cannot locate prints 'NO CONTEXT FOUND - detector disagrees with itself' rather than a clean count. That is precisely the failure the shell-assembled version hid. RESULT: 4 acronym appearances across 8 pages; analytics.html renders THREE and glosses all three - so the earlier 'bare PM and ISO on analytics' was the corrupted instrument, now retracted by a working one. ONE real hit: asset-hub renders KPI unglossed - '6 critical assets: these drive every reliability KPI'. Small, and arguably common business vocabulary, but this platform's stated audience includes new graduates and non-technicians, so it is recorded rather than dismissed. Registered as a RECORDER, not a gate (a term being bare is an audience judgement; gating it would invite deleting the word rather than explaining it) and wired into tools/read_recorder_findings.py so its output reaches someone. Remaining: the wider non-acronym vocabulary (hive, reservation, staging, deferred) and first-use definitions. || THE OVERLOADED-WORD HALF IS BUILT, AND ITS FIRST RUN IS VOID BECAUSE I MEASURED UNDER LOAD (2026-08-28). Extended the prover past acronyms to the harder class: ordinary words the platform redefines - 'reservation' sounds like a booking and means a credit HOLD, 'staging' sounds like a phase and means parts pre-picked, 'deferred' sounds like cancelled while the task is still due and still overdue. An acronym at least ANNOUNCES that it is jargon; these do the opposite, so a reader glides past with the wrong meaning and never knows to ask. Scoped deliberately - 'hive' is excluded as the platform's core noun, introduced at onboarding, where demanding a gloss everywhere would be noise that gets the check switched off. ★THE RUN REPORTED 0 BARE ON ALL 8 PAGES AND THAT IS NOT EVIDENCE: pm-scheduler rendered 872 visible characters where an earlier walk this same session measured 2,561, and asset-hub 956 against 3,132. A heavy locked-gate audit was running concurrently and saturating the local stack, so a 9s settle caught partial renders and the census read an under-loaded page as a clean one. The asset-hub KPI hit found minutes earlier also vanished, which is the tell. MEASURING WHILE A BOARD RUNS PRODUCES FALSE CLEANS - the same class as a voided board, one direction over: there the edits corrupt the run, here the run corrupts the measurement. Nothing banked from it. Remaining: re-run the census on a quiet stack, and give the prover a settle-floor that REFUSES to grade a page rendering far below its known character count rather than reporting it clean. || THE SETTLE FLOOR IS IN AND THE FINDING REPRODUCES ON A QUIET STACK (2026-08-28). Each page now carries a floor at roughly 40% of its measured healthy character count, and rendering below it is reported UNGRADED rather than clean - because a term cannot be found bare in text that never arrived. ★THE FIX IS PROVEN BY THE VERY DATA THAT MOTIVATED IT: during the saturated run pm-scheduler rendered 872 characters against its floor of 1,000, so that run would now be UNGRADED instead of reporting a clean sweep. Re-run once the stack eased: all 8 pages cleared their floors, 0 ungraded, and asset-hub's KPI hit came back with the same quotable context ('6 critical assets: these drive every reliability KPI') - so the finding is REPRODUCIBLE and the earlier disappearance was load, exactly as diagnosed. STANDING RESULT: 4 acronym appearances across 8 pages, one bare (asset-hub / KPI), zero overloaded terms reachable at rest - the overloaded half needs the flows OPENED (pm-scheduler renders 'Deferred' in its completion history, not at rest), which is the same at-rest ceiling prove_at_cap_fits had to drive past. Remaining: drive the overloaded terms behind their flows; decide whether asset-hub's KPI is worth glossing (a judgement about audience, hence a recorder and not a gate). || FLOW-OPENING WIRED, AND ITS HONEST ANSWER IS 'THE FLOW DID NOT OPEN' (2026-08-28). The overloaded words live where the work happens, not on a landing state, so the census now runs an `open` step before reading. pm-scheduler's completion sheet is the one that would expose 'Deferred', and the prover reports [no mark-done control] - the resting page has no such control (it needs the ?asset= arrival prove_flow_fits_the_floor already documents). ★THAT IS THE POINT OF WIRING IT: before, a term unreachable behind a flow reported as ABSENT, which on a census reads identically to 'present and explained'. Now a flow that fails to open SAYS SO and the term stays unmeasured rather than silently clean - the difference between 'no findings' and 'I could not look', which this session has had to correct in three separate instruments. STANDING: 4 acronym appearances, 1 bare (asset-hub / KPI, reproducible with quotable context), overloaded terms UNREACHED with the reason recorded. Remaining: give pm-scheduler's flow its ?asset= arrival so the completion sheet opens, then the overloaded half finally has a denominator. || ★THE OVERLOADED HALF HAS ITS FIRST REAL FINDING, AND IT PAIRS WITH T10 (2026-08-28). With the ?asset= arrival wired, pm-scheduler's completion sheet opens and 'deferred' is reachable. Rendered text: 'Couldn't do this task today? Record it as deferred (needs a reason)'. That explains HOW to defer and never what deferring MEANS - and the meaning is the whole point: T10 established, and now gates, that a deferral does NOT credit completion, so the task stays due and keeps counting as overdue. The word 'deferred' reads as 'cancelled, handled, off my list' to anyone who has not been told otherwise, and the one moment a worker needs that correction is the moment they are choosing it. ★THIS IS THE EXACT SHAPE THE OVERLOADED LIST WAS BUILT FOR: an acronym announces that it is jargon, so a reader knows to ask; an ordinary word quietly redefined does the opposite, and the reader walks away confidently wrong. The DB is correct, the gate holds it, and the person is not told - correct behaviour that fails to explain itself. Recorded rather than fixed in this pass because a board run is live and pm-scheduler is one of the pages its gates read; the fix is one sentence in the deferral copy ('it stays due and still counts as overdue'), and it belongs in the same edit wave as any other pm-scheduler change. || FIXED AND VERIFIED, AND THE ORACLE HAD TO LEARN THE FIX'S WORDS (2026-08-28). pm-scheduler's deferral control now reads 'Couldn't do this task today? Record it as deferred (needs a reason - the task stays due)', so the glass finally says what the database has always done. ★AND THE CENSUS WENT ON REPORTING IT BARE AFTER THE FIX LANDED: my oracle accepted exactly one gloss, 'still due', and the copy says 'stays due'. An oracle's VOCABULARY is part of the oracle - a detector that only accepts the phrasing its author imagined will convict the next good fix, and whoever wrote that fix reasonably concludes the check is broken and stops reading it. Every overloaded term now carries SEVERAL acceptable glosses. The result is non-vacuous: pm-scheduler still reports the term PRESENT (1) and now GLOSSED (0 bare), so the check is live rather than switched off. STANDING: 8 pages, 4 acronym appearances, ONE bare term left - asset-hub's KPI - and every overloaded term either absent or explained. ★AND I BROKE THE MARKUP ON THE WAY: the explanatory comment first landed INSIDE the <button> opening tag, between its class and its type attributes. Caught by reading the file back rather than by trusting the edit. || THE LAST BARE TERM IS GONE: THE CENSUSED SURFACE IS AT ZERO (2026-08-28). asset-hub's tile read 'these drive every reliability KPI' - the one unglossed acronym the live census found on any page. ★FIXED BY REMOVING THE ACRONYM, NOT BY GLOSSING IT: 'KPI (key performance indicator)' would have made a short tile clumsier for no gain, while 'these drive every reliability metric' simply reads better and needs no explanation. The gloss test is a proxy for the real property - can a person READ this - and the plain word satisfies the property directly rather than satisfying the detector. This platform's stated audience includes new graduates and non-technicians who should not need the abbreviation to read a tile. VERIFIED LIVE: asset-hub renders 3,137 characters (healthy, matching its 3,132 baseline), 'reliability metric' present, 'KPI' absent, no page errors. STANDING RESULT for the whole census: 8 pages, 3 acronym appearances all glossed, the one overloaded term reachable ('deferred' on pm-scheduler) now explained, ZERO bare terms. Remaining: widen the page roster and the term list - eight pages and fifteen terms is a real denominator but not the whole platform, and a zero over a narrow scope is a smaller claim than it looks. || WIDENED TO THE FULL 32-PAGE CHROME ROSTER, AND THE SCOPING MATTERED MORE THAN THE COUNT (2026-08-28). First widened run: 11 pages with a bare term. ★FOUR OF THOSE WERE PEOPLE'S OWN WORDS, not platform copy - community and public-feed flagged MTBF and CMMS inside worker POSTS ('what's your MTBF target on critical pumps?', 'Excel? CMMS? Anything better?'), voice-journal flagged OEE inside a worker's own note that literally ASKS 'What is OEE?', and shift-brain flagged LOTO inside seeded job data (BF-002 · LOTO · PTW-2026-3875). A check that demands the product gloss its USERS is the same category error as counting a vendored library's code as your own defect, and reporting 11 would have sent someone editing worker content. User-written regions are now subtracted before the read and restored after, per page, from the REAL markup (#history-list, #risk-list/#pms-list/#carry-list/#parts-list) after my first guessed selectors missed two of the four. ★AND THE DISCRIMINATION IS PRECISE, NOT BLUNT: shift-brain's seeded LOTO is excluded while its 'deferred' REMAINS flagged, because that one is platform copy explaining the plan. HONEST STANDING RESULT: 32 pages, 13 acronym appearances, 8 pages with a bare term - alert-hub (Staging), assistant (MTBF), hive (LOTO, CMMS), integrations (CMMS), ph-intelligence (MTBF, MTTR, OEE), plant-connections (CMMS), report-sender (OEE), shift-brain (MTBF, deferred). Left as a RECORDER finding rather than eight unilateral copy rewrites: several are supervisor-facing surfaces where the acronym may be the right register, and which of the 13 deserve glossing is an audience judgement that belongs to Ian. ★THE SETTLE FLOOR ALSO EARNED ITS KEEP IN NORMAL USE: marketplace-seller-profile rendered 250 characters against its 300 floor and came back UNGRADED rather than clean - the first time the mechanism fired on a real run rather than a contrived one. || LOCKING 2026-09-01: registered gate glossary-registry re-verified PASS standalone (static, read-only). Awaiting board earn for locked. pct -> 92. pct -> 100.
