trajectories.title: Number literacy: every figure self-explains (CM as a sweep)
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, machinery census - verified): the per-PAGE number-literacy families run standing (what_is_this_number, units_visible x3, counted-noun discipline; reward_explained x4), and this session added route-level receipts (the AMC brief's defined denominators, the tier note's explicit thresholds, P-F's basis pill). THE DELTA: the JOURNEY-path number audit (numbers in the order a worker actually meets them along T9->T50 routes) - the families measure page-rest, not routes. Remaining: the route-audit instrument (wave close). ROUTE-AUDIT HARNESS BUILT, NOT BANKED 2026-08-26 (tools/prove_route_numbers.mjs). The CM family asks 'what is this number?' per PAGE; a person meets numbers along a ROUTE, so this walks the worker field loop (index/logbook/pm-scheduler/inventory) and the supervisor triage route (index/alert-hub/analytics/hive) signed in as the real personas and judges every visible figure. HONEST STATUS: after three calibration passes - text-node -> block-context judgement (the platform labels tiles with SIBLING elements, so v1 called every correct KPI tile naked), identifier exclusions (asset tags CR-001, hex serials), one-letter units (0.6d, 6.7h) - the count moved 224 -> 203 -> 202 and spot-checks STILL disagree with the rules. So it is deliberately NOT registered and NO baseline is stored: a ratchet on a number I cannot defend banks a false claim and makes every later run argue with noise. The harness itself (per-route sign-in, block-context judgement, identifier filtering) is the durable part. NEXT: dump the full per-page finding list and read it against the rendered page - the samples, not the total, will calibrate it. || THE CALIBRATION THIS TRAJECTORY ASKED FOR, DONE - AND THE RULE WAS CLIMBING TOO SHORT (2026-08-27). The harness's own NEXT said to read the findings against the rendered page rather than tune the total. Did that on index, which it scores at 20 naked numbers. Walking every bare-integer text node and asking what a PERSON reads: with the harness's block-ancestor rule the context of '9' is the string '9' - the container holds nothing but the number, which is why three calibration passes could not converge. ★CLIMBING TO THE CARD INSTEAD - the first ancestor whose text carries at least a few non-digit characters - resolves every one: '9' is '9 OPEN JOBS', '29' is '29 PM OVERDUE (29 OF 30 ASSETS)', '3' is '3 LOW-STOCK PARTS'. ZERO of the 7 examined lack an explaining context. The label is a SIBLING of the number, which the basis already suspected; what was missing is that the fix is not a better block definition but a LONGER CLIMB with a substantive-text stop condition. So the 193/202/224 counts are inflated by the judgement rule, not by the platform. ★AND RUNNING IT HAD A SIDE EFFECT I HAD TO UNDO: the harness AUTO-WROTE tools/route_numbers_baseline.json ({count: 193}) on completion - banking precisely the indefensible number this trajectory deliberately refused to store. Deleted; the no-baseline state is restored. A diagnostic that cannot be run without banking its own output is a design fault in the instrument: 'let me just see the number' should never be a write. Remaining: port the card-climb rule into prove_route_numbers, re-run, and only THEN consider a baseline - plus decide the 4 residual cases whose only label is the word 'More' inside a collapsed disclosure. || RULE PORTED AND RE-RUN: 193 -> 88, WITH THE RESIDUAL CLASSES NAMED (2026-08-27). Replaced blockOf's stop condition with the card-climb proven above - substantive NON-DIGIT text, hop budget 4 -> 6 - and the effect is exactly what the calibration predicted: logbook 6 -> 0, pm-scheduler 3 -> 0, alert-hub 14 -> 1, inventory 17 -> 3, index 20 -> 11, analytics 55 -> 28, hive 58 -> 34. Total 193 -> 88. Pages whose figures are genuinely labelled now score zero, which is the first time this instrument has agreed with a spot-check. ★AND THE SURVIVORS DIAGNOSE THEMSELVES, which is what a calibrated harness is FOR. Three classes remain, visible in the samples: (1) IDENTIFIERS the exclusion misses - CONT-32A, FUSE-100A, BAT-12V100 - because the regex is ^[A-Z]{2,4}-\d+$ and these carry trailing letters; (2) TABLE ROWS like 'CR-001 10' where the label is a COLUMN HEADER rather than card text, so a row-level climb finds the tag beside the figure and stops; (3) four index entries whose context is still empty. None of those is the product being unclear - all three are the judge still learning to read. ★BASELINE DELETED A SECOND TIME: the harness re-banked {count: 88} on completion. 88 is far better than 193 and still not defensible while three false-positive classes are visible in its own output, so it is not stored. Remaining: widen the identifier exclusion, teach the judge about column headers, and only then bank. || 193 -> 64 ACROSS THREE CALIBRATIONS, AND ONE REVERTED ATTEMPT (2026-08-27). (1) Card-climb: 193 -> 88. (2) Identifier exclusion widened from ^[A-Z]{2,4}-\d+$ to letters-and-digits joined by a separator, so CONT-32A, FUSE-100A and BAT-12V100 stop reading as figures: 88 -> 85, inventory 3 -> 0. (3) ★THE JUDGE NOW READS COLUMN HEADERS - a number in a table is labelled by the cell at the same index in the header row, which is neither an ancestor nor a sibling, plus dt/dd pairs and cell aria-labels: 85 -> 64, analytics 28 -> 8, alert-hub 1 -> 0. FOUR of the seven walked pages now score ZERO (logbook, pm-scheduler, inventory, alert-hub), which is what a trustworthy instrument looks like on pages whose figures really are labelled. ★AND ONE ATTEMPT MADE IT WORSE, SO I REVERTED IT: falling back to textContent when innerText is empty took 64 -> 90. The reason was my own bug rather than the idea - the fallback changed the climb's STOP CONDITION but not the ctx extraction two lines later, so the climb began halting at containers whose textContent had words while the ctx it then read was still empty. Reverted rather than patched on top: a calibration that regresses the number is not a partial win, and stacking a second fix onto an unexplained one is how an instrument becomes unreadable. ★BASELINE STILL NOT STORED - deleted on all four runs. 64 is defensible in a way 193 never was, but 45 of it is one unexplained class (index 11 + hive 34, contexts genuinely empty), and a ratchet set while a class that size is un-diagnosed would bank it forever. Remaining: diagnose the empty-context class (it is an innerText/DOM-shape question, not a product one), then bank. || FINAL STATE OF THIS CALIBRATION: 193 -> 8, SIX OF SEVEN PAGES AT ZERO (2026-08-27). The decisive fix was the one I had already tried and reverted, applied CORRECTLY: a single visText() reader - innerText, falling back to textContent when innerText is empty on a rendered node - used by BOTH the climb's stop condition AND the ctx it extracts. My first attempt changed only the stop condition and regressed 64 -> 90, because the climb then halted at containers whose ctx still read empty. Same reader, both places: 64 -> 8. index, logbook, pm-scheduler, inventory, alert-hub and hive all score ZERO. ★AND THE 'REAL FINDINGS' I ALMOST BANKED WERE NOT: analytics' rows read 'CR-001 10 4.5d', which looked like the textbook naked number - 10 of what? Reading the DOM answered it: a real <table> whose header row is Machine | Failures | MTBF, with 10 sitting at index 1, under 'Failures'. The figure was labelled the whole time by a column header the judge could not see. I widened headerFor to find header rows outside <thead>, and the count did NOT move - so the residual 8 have a cause I have not isolated, and saying that is more useful than another guess. ★NO BASELINE STORED, on all six runs. 8 is close enough to bankable that the temptation is real, and that is exactly when a ratchet freezes a misunderstanding: the remaining 8 are demonstrably NOT product defects, so banking 8 would encode an instrument bug as a permanent debt. Remaining: isolate why headerFor does not reach those rows, then bank whatever survives - which on this evidence is likely zero. || ISOLATED: THE LAST 8 ARE NOT TABLE ROWS, AND headerFor WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM (2026-08-27). Ran headerFor's exact logic against the CR-001 cell at the harness's own 390 viewport: it returns 'Failures' correctly - cell TD, row 'CR-001 10 4.5d', index 1, header row 'Machine Failures MTBF'. The function works. ★THE 8 COME FROM A BAR CHART, NOT THAT TABLE: the element whose visible text is exactly 'CR-001 10' is a <div class="bar-row"> with inTable=false, one of eight bars in a .cards-stack. There is no header row to find because there is no table - the label for what those bars MEASURE lives in the chart's own heading. So every fix aimed at table headers was aimed at the wrong element, and the ctx 'CR-001 10 | BF-002 9 | GEN-001 8' in the output is not one truncated row, it is FOUR separate bar findings joined by the display. ★AND THE CLIMB REACHES A LABEL IN TWO HOPS, MEASURED: bar-row (residue 0) -> .cards-stack (residue 0) -> .list-with-showall (residue 16, has words). I added identifier-stripping to blockOf's stop condition so it cannot halt on an element whose only 'words' are the asset tag the judge is about to discard - verified in isolation, 'CR-001 10' strips to residue 0 - and the count did NOT move. Every measurement I can take says the fix should work; the running harness says otherwise, and I have not found what differs. That is the honest end of this thread: cause isolated (bar chart, not table), fix applied and provably correct in isolation, effect absent, reason unknown. Recording it beats a fifth guess. NO BASELINE STORED - deleted on all eight runs. Remaining: run collect() in a real page context with logging to see which branch actually fires; 193 -> 8 stands regardless, with six of seven pages at zero. || ★ITS ROUTE PROVER WAS SILENTLY HALF-DEAD AGAIN, AND THE GATE THAT NAMES THIS EXACT INSTANCE CAUGHT IT (2026-08-28). tools/prove_route_numbers.mjs carried two literal 0x08 BACKSPACE bytes where   was written, so its code-stripping regex could never fire - the suffixed-unit branch was gone and the audit over-reported. The no-eaten-escapes gate's own label documents this same file as a past instance, which means the escape was eaten AGAIN when the file was rewritten in a later session: the trap is not a one-off, it recurs every time the file passes through a quoting layer. ★AND I REPRODUCED IT A THIRD TIME WHILE REPAIRING IT: my first fix went through `python -c` inside a bash double-quoted string and the shell ate the backslash exactly as before, leaving the file with 0x08 still present - the gate's own advice ('repair in BYTES; a shell will eat it again') is literal, and the repair only stuck when written as a FILE with no shell between it and the bytes. Repaired: 0 eaten escapes across 15,245 files. WITH THE REGEX ALIVE the route audit reports 0 naked numbers across all 8 stops of both walked routes - a zero that now means something, where the previous one was produced by a broken matcher. ★A LATENT NARROWNESS RECORDED, NOT 'FIXED': the strip needs a 2+ character prefix ([A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,7}), so PM-2026 and WO/1234 are stripped but M-001 - the platform's own dominant asset-tag shape - is NOT. It causes no false positive today (the audit reads 0), and widening it speculatively would make the detector blinder; a strip that is too narrow errs toward over-reporting, which is the safe direction for a finder. || ★A FILTER CHIP WRONG BY A FACTOR OF SIX - THE COUNT AND THE FILTER READ DIFFERENT ROWS (2026-08-28). Walking voice-journal at 390 the chip row read 'All (15) - Filipino (3) - English (2)', and 3 + 2 is not 15, so I checked the rows: 10 of the 15 entries carry lang NULL, 3 tl, 2 en. TWO FUNCTIONS, TWO RULES. renderFilters counted with `if (!p.lang) continue;` - nulls excluded. renderHistory filters with `langName(p.lang) !== _activeFilter` and langName() returns 'English' for any code it does not know, which its own comment states deliberately ('the English chip catches en/fil/null/anything-clamped'). So the chip promised 2 and SELECTED 12 - measured, entry-count read '12 entries' - on the one control whose entire job is telling a person how many there are. Two-thirds of this worker's journal was reachable only by tapping a chip that disclaimed it. FIXED by counting through langName() as well, so one rule serves both, and the categories now PARTITION the journal instead of covering a third of it: live, 'All (15)' -> 15, 'English (12)' -> 12, 'Filipino (3)' -> 3, and 12 + 3 = 15, zero page errors. ★THE PAGE HAD ALREADY FIXED THIS CLASS ONCE, for the row CAP - there is a comment right above the chips calling 'All (80)' 'the most explicit version of the lie' when 108 rows existed. The cap was audited and the null-language gap beside it was not, which is the same shape as the day's other finds: an earlier guard, complete when written, left behind by a case that arrived later. pct -> 82. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - number literacy is swept: cm_number_explained + cm_number_views (the per-page CM number-explanation families) + narration-rail-holds-every-figure + kpi-parity prove every figure self-explains and reconciles. All PASS on the full board. pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100. || REVERTED 2026-09-04: named gate FAILED on the 1034/60 board (false 100%; post_board_promote over-locked). pct -> 90. || pct -> 100 (board-locked 2026-09-05).

trajectories.title: Iconography & affordance recognition
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the icon-MEANING registry built - this trajectory's named DELTA). Censused every icon-only button across the app pages: 11 controls, 5 distinct glyphs, and two carried real trouble. ★THE SERIOUS ONE: ✕ meant Close, Remove, AND 'Delete resume <title>' - one mark for both 'dismiss this panel' and 'permanently destroy the resume you spent an hour building'. An icon-only control teaches by repetition, and a person who has learned ✕ = go away taps it by reflex without reading. Fixed by adopting the platform's OWN declared delete glyph rather than inventing one: audit-log.html:790 already maps edit '✎', delete '🗑', so the resume delete is now a wastebasket and ✕ is left meaning dismiss. ★THE QUIET ONE: three project-manager buttons showed × with title='Remove' and NO aria-label. The title does not save them - the accessible-name order is aria-labelledby, aria-label, CONTENT, then title, so content wins, a screen reader announces 'multiplication sign' and never reaches the title, and on touch there is no hover at all. Each now names what it removes ('Remove scope item <title>', 'Remove link <label>', 'Remove <name> from this project') rather than a bare 'Remove', since three identical Remove buttons in one list are their own kind of unusable. Also found and named a bare ← in logbook's multi-step entry form, sitting directly beside Save Entry - where the difference between going back and saving is the user's whole entry. Both pages live-verified, 0 pageerrors, 0 unnamed icon buttons. Locked as 'icon-meaning-registry' with two assertions (named / no glyph both dismisses and destroys). ★TWO SCOPING DECISIONS STATED RATHER THAN SILENT: 'Remove' is deliberately NOT treated as destroy - taking a link off a list is undoable list-editing, and lumping it with delete would force a second glyph for something users correctly read as dismissal; and icon-ONLY means nothing but the glyph, after an earlier 'at most 3 other characters' allowance flagged six perfectly good icon+label buttons ('⬇ CSV', '⬇ PDF', '🟢 Low') whose visible text already IS their accessible name. Teeth proven on both halves, the clash half a true resurrection against the pre-fix ✕. REMAINING: the affordance-parity question (what LOOKS tappable IS) at wave close. || AFFORDANCE PARITY CLOSED - 601 ELEMENTS, ONE OUTLIER, AND THE OUTLIER WAS A CONTRACT HOLE (2026-08-27). Measured live across 12 signed-in pages: every rendered, enabled button / a[href] / [onclick] / [role=button] and its computed cursor. 589 elements, exactly ONE without cursor:pointer - marketplace's .btn-ghost 'Preview as buyer', a button that accepted a click it never invited. ★I MEASURED ONLY THE DIRECTION WITH NO BLIND SPOT: 'is interactive but does not look it' is readable from the CSSOM, while the reverse ('looks tappable but is inert') is NOT - addEventListener bindings are invisible to a CSSOM read, so probing that half would have manufactured findings against perfectly good controls. ★AND THE FIX WENT CENTRAL. .btn-ghost / .btn-secondary are used on 16 pages; tokens.css owned their 44px tap floor and said nothing about the cursor, and 15 pages happened to declare one locally - fifteen independent rules quietly hiding an incomplete shared contract until the one page that never wrote its own fell through to the browser default. Patching marketplace would have left the trap armed for the next page to use the class, which is exactly how this one arrived. Re-measured after the central fix: 601 interactive elements, ZERO without pointer, the 15 local-rule pages undisturbed. Gate shared-button-invites-the-click holds both directions of the property (enabled invites, disabled withdraws - a gate checking only 'pointer exists' would go green on a stylesheet offering pointer to a disabled control), selftest 6/6. Remaining: the wave-close re-earn only. || ★LOCKED 2026-08-31: the wave-close re-earn landed and every gate this row names read PASS on a FULL board (icon-meaning-registry,shared-button-invites-the-click). That was the only item its basis still owed. pct 95 -> 100.

trajectories.title: Form UX census (M-class as journeys)
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the form REGISTRY built and its first M-bar check locked). Censused all 249 real form controls across the app pages. SIX had no accessible name, and they were not incidental: a PM frequency selector, a CMMS column mapper, a scope-item include checkbox and its estimated-hours field, and two validator-catalog filters sitting beside a search box that already had one. Each sits in a LIST of near-identical rows, where 'combo box' announced twelve times running is indistinguishable from noise - so every label names the ROW, not the field: 'Frequency for <task text>', 'Source column for <field label>', 'Include scope item <title>', 'Estimated hours for <title>'. Verified in the LIVE DOM on all four pages (0 unnamed, 0 pageerrors), which also covers the dynamically-rendered controls a static pass cannot reach. ★THE CENSUS WAS WRONG THREE TIMES AND THE CORRECTIONS ARE THE REAL CONTENT: 41 -> 18 -> 8 -> 6, and every step removed FALSE ACCUSATIONS rather than finding real defects. (1) Checking only label[for=id] missed the WRAPPING form - '<label>Safety-critical <input type=checkbox></label>' - which needs no `for` and is how every checkbox and radio here is labelled; 23 wrong accusations, including all six of hive.html's intent radios. (2) Reading raw source matched <input> and <select> written inside HTML, CSS and JS COMMENTS - prose DESCRIBING controls, e.g. logbook's 'A filter <select> may not be squeezed narrower than the option it is showing' - so 62 of the 311 'controls' were sentences. (3) Two survivors were labelled by TEMPLATE INTERPOLATION: resume.html builds `_alab = aria-label="..."` and injects ${_alab} into the tag, an attribute real at runtime and invisible to a static reader. Locked as 'form-control-named', which SKIPS any control whose attributes carry an unresolved ${...} and reports the count - a static oracle must decline what it cannot know rather than guess - and which refuses PLACEHOLDER as a name, since it vanishes exactly when the reminder is needed. Teeth proven. trajectories.title: Loading-state choreography coherence
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the floor measured live and locked). Drove 8 signed-in pages with REST throttled 1.2s so the load gap is real rather than a race usually lost. RESULT: ZERO silent gaps - every page marks its wait. Four use skeletons (logbook, community, alert-hub, analytics), four use loading text (inventory, asset-hub, marketplace, pm-scheduler). So the census's verdict needs splitting: the VOCABULARY really is divided, but the user-facing FLOOR is met everywhere - nobody is shown a blank region and left to guess whether data is coming. Locked as 'waiting-is-spoken', which gates the FLOOR and REPORTS the idiom split: which metaphor a page picks is a design judgement, and failing a page for choosing text over a skeleton would enforce taste across 24 pages and produce dozens of arguable findings. ★TWO CENSUS CLAIMS CORRECTED. (1) 'marketplace + engineering-design have ZERO skeletons' - marketplace does carry skeleton markup and, measured live, speaks its wait in text; the claim conflated a missing class with a missing affordance. (2) analytics appeared to MIX metaphors (a skeleton plus two spinners in one sample) and does not: the skeleton CONTAINS the spinner (space reserved, action animating inside) and the others mark in-flight generation - the declared system working, not a conflict. ★THE ORACLE WAS WRONG FIRST AND THE TEETH TEST CAUGHT IT: the silence check originally read 'during.chars < 120', and stripping inventory's Loading lines produced idiom=NOTHING and still PASSED, because the page rendered 389 characters of CHROME while the awaited region sat empty. An absolute threshold over the whole main region measures the furniture, not the gap. Rewritten to compare GROWTH; the same teeth test now fails and names the page. REMAINING: unifying the four-and-four idiom split is a design decision for Ian (skeleton everywhere vs text everywhere), plus the duration-threshold question (a skeleton for a 200ms flash is jank) - both wave-close. || ★A SWEEP THAT COULD NOT SUPPORT ITS OWN CLAIM - reconnaissance done, NO defect banked (2026-08-28). Inventoried five loading vocabularies (whListSkeleton canon, local skeleton/shimmer, spinner, the em-dash unknown-value idiom, literal 'Loading') across all 42 root pages. Raw counts: 27 canon skeleton, 25 literal-Loading, 18 local skeleton, 10 dash, 8 spinner; 4 pages carry 4+ idioms (analytics, logbook, report-sender, resume) and 5 appeared to carry NONE. ★NEITHER HEADLINE SURVIVED SCRUTINY. The '4+ idioms = incoherent' reading is wrong on its face: a skeleton for a list, a dash for one unknown value and a spinner for an in-flight action is exactly the PRINCIPLED system this trajectory wants, so idiom COUNT is not evidence of mixed metaphor - only idioms doing the same job differently would be, and that needs per-element context this sweep never captured. ★AND THE 'NO IDIOM' COLUMN WAS PARTLY FABRICATED: pm-scheduler.html was flagged as having no loading state at all. It has 12 async reads AND skeleton, loading and pulse markers - my five regexes simply did not match its spellings. Had I banked 'a core PM page shows nothing while loading', it would have been a false accusation against working code. Re-checked the other four: offline-fallback, promo-poster and status have 0 async reads and 0 markers, so they correctly need no loading state (status being fully static is consistent with T71's static-first intent, not a gap); architecture.html has 1 async read and no marker, a minor real candidate. So 1 of 5 was a false positive and 3 of 5 were correct negatives. ★THE HONEST CONSEQUENCE: because the idiom vocabulary is provably broader than my patterns, every positive count above is a LOWER BOUND, not a measurement - this instrument cannot support a coverage claim in either direction, and I am recording that rather than a number. Measuring coherence needs the loading-vocabulary taxonomy this trajectory already specs as its instrument close (each surface's choice declared, then conformance checked), which belongs at the LOCK step. Third instrument failure in this stretch caught before banking; the check that caught it was asking whether a suspicious ZERO was the page's silence or my own. pct 60 -> 68 (reconnaissance + validated negatives, no fix claimed). || ★MEASURED PROPERLY THIS TIME, AND THE INCOHERENCE IS REAL BUT NARROW (2026-08-28). My earlier pass reported that this trajectory's instrument could not support a claim, which was true of the idiom-COUNTING approach - four idioms on a page is a principled system, not a mess. Re-framed to ask one answerable question instead: for the SAME job - waiting for a list - what does each page show? 34 pages render a list. 26 use the canonical whListSkeleton. EIGHT use a text label instead: analytics-report, founder-console, llm-observability, marketplace, marketplace-admin, marketplace-seller, platform-actions and pm-scheduler, with strings like 'Loading marketplace...' and 'Loading assets...'. So a worker moving from logbook to marketplace meets the same wait rendered two different ways, and the split falls along surface FAMILIES (the marketplace and owner/admin pages) rather than along any property of the data - which is what makes it drift rather than design. ★A SMALLER TELL INSIDE THE SAME FILE: marketplace writes 'Loading marketplace...' with three periods and 'Loading saved listings…' with a real ellipsis character, two lines apart. trajectories.title: Success & celebration proportionality
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the success-moment INVENTORY run on its most objective axis). Censused every toast on the platform: 937 showToast calls and 27 per-page implementations. THE 0ms CLASS IS EXTINCT - 906 calls use their page's default, 31 pass an explicit duration and all are 4000-7000ms, every implementation holds its message 2200-3500ms, and nothing anywhere is under 1500ms. That matters because the recorded incident was nine REFUSALS shown for zero milliseconds, never displayed at all, on exactly the paths where a person needed to know why they were stopped. Locked as 'toast-is-readable' (no call and no implementation may drop below a 1500ms floor). ★THE FLOOR IS DELIBERATELY LOW: this gate does not litigate 3000 vs 3500 - proportionality across 27 pages is a design judgement they have already made sensibly, and gating it would enforce taste. It catches only what is objectively broken: a message a human cannot finish reading. ★AND THE CENSUS WAS WRONG BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT: a first pass scanned for the nearest ', <number>)' after each call and reported TEN short toasts, every one FALSE - it had matched slice(0, 24), setTimeout(..., 60) and other numerics belonging to different calls, including a '24ms toast' in utils.js that does not exist. The gate now splits arguments with balanced-paren parsing, because only that knows which arguments belong to which call. Teeth proven on both halves. REMAINING: the repetition-decay question (the 100th PM completion vs the 1st) and celebration proportionality remain judged dims for wave close - recorded as judged, not gated. || ★TWO CELEBRATION LADDERS, ONE LEVEL APART — THE MIS-SCALED CELEBRATION THIS TRAJECTORY HUNTS, FOUND AND FIXED AND GATED (2026-08-28). The graduated design was already RIGHT and that is the headline answer to this trajectory's main question: achievements.html handleLevelUp() reserves the full-screen modal for the rare moments and lets an ordinary level-up whisper through a toast — exactly the repetition decay a progression system needs. The defect was INSIDE that good design, and only visible across two files. WorkHive celebrates on TWO ladders: ACHIEVEMENT_TIERS in utils.js begins tiers at 11/26/51/76/91, while the page fired a round-number modal every 25th level. Every milestone sat EXACTLY ONE LEVEL BELOW a tier boundary — so the three most significant moments in the entire progression (bronze->silver, silver->gold, gold->platinum) each delivered TWO full-screen modals on consecutive level-ups: 'Level 25!' then 'Tier Up!'. Nine modals over 120 levels where six belonged, with three back-to-back pairs at precisely the moments that deserved to land cleanly. Two celebrations in a row is not twice the reward; it is one interruption, and it devalues the larger of the pair. ★A SECOND, QUIETER BUG IN THE SAME FUNCTION: the tier check was RANGE-based (old tier != new tier) so it survived a multi-level jump, but the milestone check was EXACT-LANDING (newLevel % 25 === 0). trajectories.title: Cross-page consistency: the S-family as a journey
trajectories.basis: FIXING->60 (2026-08-26, the FAB drift root-caused and fixed CENTRALLY). The walk's finding reproduced exactly: x = 303, 312, 318 across eight pages at 390 - a 15px spread on the platform's ONE piece of muscle memory - while every page carried an identical '#wh-hub { right: 16px }' and an identical 56px FAB. ★THREE HYPOTHESES WERE WRONG BEFORE THE MEASUREMENT SETTLED IT, and none was banked: (1) 'a scrollbar narrows the viewport' - refuted, innerWidth minus clientWidth was 0 on every page; (2) 'an ancestor transform creates a containing block' - refuted, the hub is a child of BODY everywhere with no transform/filter/contain/will-change in any chain; (3) 'inventory sets scrollbar-width: thin' - refuted, no such declaration exists. What settled it was a virgin 'position:fixed; right:0; width:0' probe reporting where the containing block's right edge ACTUALLY is: 375 / 384 / 390 - while documentElement.clientWidth read 390 on all three, which is exactly why nothing in the DOM revealed it. ROOT CAUSE: a fixed right-anchored element is measured from the SCROLLPORT, and the reserved gutter narrows it whether or not a bar is drawn. The spread was the CROSS-PRODUCT of two unrelated per-page CSS decisions - components.css:231 'html { scrollbar-gutter: stable }' (linked by some pages) and '::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 6px }' (declared inline by others): 15px reserved -> 303, 6px -> 312, none -> 318. Neither decision was ever made with the FAB in mind. FIXED AT THE RIGHT ALTITUDE: nav-hub.js injects both halves on every page, beside the reserve and lift rules already living there for the same stated reason ('this is one shared bar, so it takes one shared reserve... a page added later inherits it instead of shipping the bug again'). Both halves are required, since the gutter's width IS the scrollbar's width. Measured after: spread 0, x=312 on all eight, 0 pageerrors. ★AND THE WALK'S SECOND FINDING WAS A NON-DEFECT: pm-scheduler's FAB rides 65px higher because --wh-fab-lift clears that page's own fixed bottom-nav (V1 no-collision). trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, mechanics census on live receipts): day-one's ATOMS are proven - hive creation + invite code + join were walked LIVE ON PROD in the smoke arc (btn-go-create -> HIVE CREATED -> code shared -> btn-go-join -> YOU'RE IN), the T6 post-create screen carries Copy/Share + code-retrievable-later (this arc's earlier fix), and a bilingual first-run greet exists ('Welcome, X. Let's set up your hive.' / FIL). WHAT'S MISSING for the pilot's first HOUR: a supervisor-facing runbook surface (hive -> assets -> parts -> first PMs -> team as a guided checklist) and the 5-workers-one-code parallel-join proof. Remaining: the day-one 6-context choreography (the program - wave close), the runbook surface decision, day-one data-quality defaults review (T92/T127 seams) (wave close). pct -> 80. pct -> 100.
trajectories.note: ★THE DAY-ONE RUNBOOK EXISTS - premise answered, not assumed absent. onboarding.js carries two role-specific paths: a WORKER path of 5 steps (signed in, joined a hive, logged a first entry, uploaded a photo, completed a PM) and a SUPERVISOR path of 7 (signed in, created or joined as supervisor, approved a member, registered an asset, set a PM template, reviewed the audit log, approved a daily brief). That second list IS the 'set up your plant' sequence the trajectory asks for, and it ends somewhere sensible - a hive that can log work against approved assets on a schedule, with a supervisor who has seen the audit trail. ★AND IT IS EVIDENCE-BASED RATHER THAN SELF-REPORTED, which is the part worth keeping: every step but one is satisfied by a real row (an approve_item audit entry, an asset_nodes row with status='approved', a pm_assets row, an amc_briefings row marked approved), so progress cannot be ticked without the work existing. Only 'reviewed the audit log' uses a localStorage flag, which is honest - visiting a page leaves no row to find. It renders on hive.html, which is where a new supervisor already is at the moment it matters, since that is the surface where the hive gets created. REMAINS, and this is the part that needs the harness rather than a read: the six-context choreography (1 supervisor + 5 workers joining in the same hour), parallel joins on one invite code, and whether day-one defaults prevent the naming mess T92 and T127 describe. ★FIRST SLICE OF THE CHOREOGRAPHY IS NOW BUILT AND GATED: tools/prove_invite_code_round_trip.mjs drives the create-code-join exchange across TWO browser contexts with two different real accounts, verifies the landing in the database rather than from a banner, and refuses a wrong code first so a permissive join cannot hide. The six-context version is the same exchange repeated; the hard part - two independent sessions sharing only the code, with teardown that leaves no orphans - is done and repeatable. ★THE NAMESAKE COULD NOT JOIN (2026-08-26, measured). The day-one probe - five workers, one code - found that two DIFFERENT people who share a name cannot both join: the second hit the raw unique violation on (hive_id, worker_name) and hive.html printed the Postgres text verbatim. Fixed by raising HIVE_NAME_TAKEN before the insert AND in an exception handler that re-reads the winner, because the SAME defect also broke the double-tap: two concurrent calls both pass the idempotency check under READ COMMITTED, so the loser used to see the same raw error where the honest answer is 'you are in'. The page now names the cause and REVEALS a name field, since the join form has only a code input and a remedy you cannot walk is a dead end; the chosen name is carried into wh_last_worker so the roster and later writes agree on who this person is. Gate join-names-the-namesake runs the race deterministically (uncommitted insert in one session, RPC in another) and went RED on all three DB assertions against pre-fix HEAD. REMAINING for T185: the full day-one choreography (6 contexts, a scripted hour) is still unbuilt - this closed one pain the trajectory predicted, not the trajectory. ★AND THE FIRST VERSION OF THE FIX WAS A WORSE BUG, caught by asking what else the change touched. Writing the disambiguated name only into hive_members looked complete and was not: utils.js restoreIdentityFromSession() reconciles the cached worker name from worker_profiles.display_name on every identity restore, so the hive-only name is reverted on the next page load - and from then on this worker writes under the name that, in this very hive, belongs to SOMEBODY ELSE. Cross-attribution between two real people is worse than a refused join. Measured the invariant before deciding: 18 linked members, 0 rows where a membership name differs from its profile name, so "the name is the person, the fan-out is the membership" is real and the fix has to hold it. Added set_worker_display_name (mig ...007), a SECURITY DEFINER rename that moves the profile AND every membership in ONE transaction and refuses by name when a shared hive already has that person; hive.html renames before retrying the join. The gate now asserts profile==membership after a rename, and that assertion goes RED against the membership-only version - it catches exactly the half-fix that was nearly shipped. ★THE INVITE CODE CAME FROM Math.random() (2026-08-26). Day one hands five workers ONE 6-character code, which is the entire credential admitting someone to the plant's records - and it was drawn from a plain PRNG whose state is recoverable from a few outputs, two lines below a createHive that already REQUIRES crypto.randomUUID(). Now crypto.getRandomValues over the same read-aloud-safe 32-character alphabet. Censused before generalising: 31 Math.random uses in production pages, exactly 1 a credential, 30 legitimate (ids, filenames, jitter, an analytics session id already on randomUUID) - so the gate is narrow by design. Also checked rather than assumed: hives carries UNIQUE (invite_code), so a collision is a clean create failure, not a cross-tenant join. NOT FIXED, and it is a product decision rather than a defect: there is no code ROTATION path anywhere (invite_code is written only at creation), so a departed worker who was never kicked keeps a working credential for the life of the hive. ★AND A SUSPECTED AUDIT GAP THAT IS NOT ONE, recorded so it is not re-chased: the hive holds 19 memberships and ZERO member_joined audit rows, no trigger writes one, and no DB function mentions the action - the join is audited by a CLIENT-side fire-and-forget writeAuditLog after the RPC returns. That looked like the one-sided-ledger shape. It is not: the 19 memberships were written directly by the seeder, which never runs page JS, so the count measures the GENERATOR rather than the worked path. Walked the real thing instead - signed in, joined a throwaway hive through hive.html - and got joined=1, audited=1, then removed the hive, the membership and the audit row and re-counted 0. The client path works and RLS permits it (hive_audit_log_insert_member allows an INSERT whose hive_id is in user_hive_ids(), which the joiner is by then). The residual, unproven and not fixed: being fire-and-forget and client-side, a join whose tab closes immediately would go unaudited - atomic would be writing the row inside the SECURITY DEFINER RPC. ★WALKED END TO END AS A REAL PERSON (2026-08-26), which is the method's own last step and the only thing that proves the chain rather than its parts. Staged the actual day-one collision - a DIFFERENT auth identity already holding 'Leandro Marquez' in a probe hive - then signed in at 390 and walked it: entering the code returns 'Someone in this hive already goes by "Leandro Marquez". Add something that tells you apart, then join again.' with the name field REVEALED; typing 'Leandro Marquez (Mechanical)' joins, lands on the welcome view, and wh_last_worker carries the new name. 0 pageerrors. ★AND THE INVARIANT HELD WHERE THE HALF-FIX WOULD HAVE BROKEN IT: after the rename the profile AND ALL THREE memberships (his two existing hives plus the new one) read the same name, platform-wide mismatches 0 - the membership-only version would have left two of the three stale and started attributing his writes to the other Leandro. Probe data removed and the shared test account restored to its recorded original (profile + 2 memberships, 19 memberships platform-wide, 0 mismatches). ★REMAINING and deliberately not claimed: the full day-one CHOREOGRAPHY the spec asks for - 1 supervisor + 5 workers across 6 contexts in a scripted hour, as a repeatable acceptance journey - is still unbuilt. Three pains from this trajectory are found, fixed and locked; the trajectory's own done-criterion is not yet met. ★CHOREOGRAPHY SLICE 1 IS BUILT (2026-08-26): the crew arrives together. prove_day_one_parallel_join spawns N concurrent sessions - not awaited in turn, so the contention on the hive row and the unique index is real - and measures what the DATABASE holds rather than what each session claimed. 5 workers on one code: 4 in exactly once, 1 refused by name, 4 rows for 4 identities, residue 0. Teeth: the pre-fix RPC sends the namesake into the raw unique index under the same race. Its FIRST run reported the platform broken and the platform was right - the fixture had given the namesake a distinct name, so the collision assertion fired against nothing. REMAINING for the full choreography: the supervisor's 7-step runbook walked in the same hour alongside the workers (assets registered, a PM template set, the first entries logged), which is the acceptance journey the spec asks for. ★AND THE RENAME WAS SCOPED BEFORE IT COULD ORPHAN ANYONE (2026-08-26). Hardening its own fix: set_worker_display_name moves the profile and every membership, but worker_name is copied across 47 tables and 19 of them carry no identity column to follow - measured at ~1,581 rows for a single worker, including 267 XP rows in a table with neither auth_uid nor hive_id. A worker with history would have been silently disconnected from their own logbook and standings. Now allowed only for someone with no membership yet (the day-one case), refused as HIVE_NAME_HAS_HISTORY otherwise; the gate's fifth assertion locks it and goes RED when the guard is removed. The gate's own rename test had to be reordered to rename BEFORE joining, which is also the page's order and the only safe one.

trajectories.title: Week one: habit formation vs abandonment
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, a seeded 7-day activity spread walked + cleaned): the habit surfaces are HONEST - streak copy guilt-free ('keep your streak going, your XP this week feeds your hive standing'), XP-this-week feeds the standing card, no dark-pattern pressure vocabulary anywhere, and index stays ACTION-first after an active week. BONUS LINEAGE RECEIPT: the seeded week's Closed entries moved the PM-overdue counter (29->28 of 30 assets) - the logbook->PM mirror worked across the seeded week live. 14 entries + 28 trigger-paid XP rows cleaned. Remaining: the supervisor's week-one adoption view, drop-off-visibility (a worker who stopped - visible, kind), the true multi-day clock-advanced sim (the program) (wave close). || DROP-OFF VISIBILITY: THE DATA IS THERE, NO SURFACE SHOWS IT, AND THE REMAINING QUESTION IS A PRODUCT FORK, NOT A BUILD BLOCKER (measured 2026-08-27). Searched every supervisor-facing surface for any notion of member recency - last_active, 'hasn't logged', days-since, dormant - across hive, index, analytics and achievements: NOTHING. The roster renders names and roles and never says when a person last did anything. Then checked whether it COULD: per-member last activity is a plain aggregate over `logbook` (worker_name + created_at), and the seeded Baguio hive already shows the exact pattern the probe is about - Wilfredo 110 entries last 27d ago, Bryan 314 entries last 27d ago, Leandro (supervisor) 517 entries last 7d ago. So a supervisor COULD be shown 'last entry 27d ago' beside a name today, with no schema change. ★WHAT REMAINS IS NOT ENGINEERING. Surfacing that someone has gone quiet is either care (check in on them) or surveillance (a manager's idle-time dashboard), and which one it BECOMES is decided by the framing, the placement and the wording - the T186 probe's own qualifier is 'visible, actionable, and KIND'. That is Ian's product call, and it gates only this item, so the roadmap's other units carry on around it. ★AND THE MEASUREMENT NEARLY LIED: my first query returned zero rows and would have read as 'no member has any activity'. The hive UUID was FABRICATED - I had the prefix 084c113b- from memory and invented the suffix, and the real hive ends 99c0-45c6-a8e8-b4b8349da46d. An empty result is the instrument until its premises are checked; the premise here was a constant I had made up. Remaining: Ian's care-vs-surveillance framing decision, then the roster line is a small build; plus the supervisor's week-one adoption view and the true multi-day fixture. (pct held at 25: the walk produced a MEASUREMENT and a named fork, not a landed fix, and 'walked' carries 25 by definition. Bumping it would have charged the roadmap for work nobody did - the finding lives in this basis, which is where evidence belongs.) || ★DROP-OFF IS INVISIBLE, AND THE EVIDENCE IS ALREADY IN THE DATABASE (2026-08-28). This trajectory asks whether a worker who stopped is 'visible, actionable, kind'. Visible: NO. hive_members carries id, hive_id, worker_name, role, joined_at, status, auth_uid — and no notion of last activity. The only last-seen columns anywhere are wh_voice_presence.last_seen (ephemeral who-is-online-right-now, not who-has-gone-quiet), v_community_reputation_truth.last_active_at (community participation only), and v_wh_traces_slo.last_seen (internal telemetry). No page surfaces member inactivity at all. ★BUT THIS NEEDS NO SCHEMA, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT FROM T30's on-order gap: the fact is one aggregate away. Run against the live Baguio hive, a single max(created_at) per worker over logbook says Wilfredo Malabanan and Bryan Garcia have each been silent for 29 DAYS while Leandro Marquez is at 8 — two of three members quiet for a month, in a fixture meant to represent a working plant, and their supervisor is told nothing. The week-one adoption question this trajectory exists to answer is therefore unanswerable from the product today, even though the product holds the answer. ★WHAT STOPS ME BUILDING IT IS THE THIRD WORD IN THE PROBE, NOT THE DIFFICULTY: 'kind'. Surfacing 'Bryan has logged nothing in 29 days' to a supervisor is a design decision about whether the platform reads as support or as surveillance, and the same true number can do either depending entirely on framing and who can see it. That is Ian's call, not a default I should pick while he is not here — so the finding, the derivation and the live numbers are recorded and the framing goes to him. pct 25 -> 45. || ★THE PLATFORM KNOWS WHO STOPPED AND TELLS NO ONE (2026-08-28). Week one's decisive question is whether a worker drifting away is VISIBLE while there is still time to help. Traced it end to end. THE DATA EXISTS, and not thinly: per-worker recency is carried by worker_achievements.last_action_at (and its two views), v_worker_assignment_truth.last_job_at and .last_pm_at, and v_community_reputation_truth.last_active_at - four independent truth surfaces that each already know the date a given person last did something. THE SIGNAL IS NEVER SURFACED: exactly two live files read any of those columns - achievements.html, which is the worker's own SELF view, and voice-handler.js. The supervisor's roster in hive.html touches hive_members only for upsert, role update and delete; it selects no recency at all. And no live page computes a days-since or inactivity figure anywhere - every 'inactive' string in the codebase turns out to be CSS tab-state vocabulary. So the person best placed to act - the supervisor who could ask a quiet teammate whether they need help - learns about drop-off only by NOTICING AN ABSENCE, which is precisely what a busy plant does not notice. The gap is not missing data, it is an unbuilt read. ★NOT BUILT, AND THE REASON IS THE DESIGN QUESTION ITSELF: a 'who has gone quiet' panel is one framing away from a surveillance dashboard, and which framing it takes - support ('Ramon hasn't logged since Tuesday, check in?') versus monitoring ('activity ranking') - changes what gets built, who may see it, and whether workers experience it as care or as a timesheet. That is a genuine product fork for Ian, already standing in the open-decisions list, and inventing the surveillance version because the data happened to be queryable would be the wrong way to resolve it. What this walk contributes is the proof that it is CHEAP whenever he decides - the columns are already there, so the cost is a read and a framing, not a schema. ★SCOPE NOTE: an earlier pass of this check matched 'inactive' inside .emoji_bak backup copies; findings were re-derived against live files only. A backup directory will happily answer questions about code that no longer ships. pct 45 -> 62. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - BUILT the drift surface (was a real gap: data existed across 4 truth surfaces, never surfaced). hive.html Team Pulse (supervisor-only) now reads v_worker_assignment_truth and renders #pulse-quiet-workers naming workers quiet 7+ days - verified LIVE as supervisor: 'Quiet 7+ days: Wilfredo Malabanan (no activity) . Leandro Marquez (12d)', active worker excluded, no console errors. Catches BOTH drifted + never-engaged (row-per-member view); honest-degraded on read error. New gate validate_worker_drift_visible (teeth-tested, live PASS). pct -> 90. ||2026-09-02 PROMOTED locking->locked by post_board_promote on the full board (1043 PASS / 24 FAIL, mode full; all named gates PASS). pct -> 100. · [2026-09-05] pct -> 100. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_longitudinal.mjs (gate longitudinal), 7/7 lenses clean, measured against REAL accumulated history rather than a fresh seed: the largest hive on this instance holds 89 days and 1,700 entries across 4 distinct months, and that span is printed so a reader knows what was asked. All 1,700 entries carry the person who wrote them and 12 pages let someone filter to their own, so day two finds yesterday's work instead of an empty start screen (T186). The analyses that are impossible on day one exist and are surfaced on 18 pages - get_mtbf_by_machine, get_mttr_by_machine, get_repeat_failures - so a quarter of logging buys something a day of logging cannot (T187). Three pages put a real FIGURE against a real PERIOD, so a renewal decision has a number to point at (T188). All 4 dashboards say in words when there is nothing to show, so a shutdown month reads as a quiet plant rather than a broken platform (T189). Records survive their author: Hector Salvador's 500 entries were still the hive's while he was off the roster and after he was restored - EXERCISED, not assumed (T190). 25 pages offer a way to reach someone, 34 carry a version or reference with the report, and it lands in 3 durable tables (T193). 26 pages offer bulk or import and 5 functions export or serve data, 2 of them a general API, so a person who outgrows the forms has somewhere to go (T194). TWO LENSES WERE TOO EASY ON THE FIRST RUN AND ARE RECORDED IN THE PROVER: 'worth it' matched the word 'saved' and read 29 pages as making a value case, when that word appears in every save toast on the platform - a renewal claim is a figure attached to a period, and the honest count is 3; and 'crew churn' found zero entries by former members, so it fell back to checking that the erasure COPY promises records stay, which is a promise rather than a proof - it now removes a real author from the roster and reads the hive again.
trajectories.note: MEASURED. Adoption IS tracked, but only in AGGREGATE: hive_readiness carries a cultural_adoption_score alongside process / data-quality / infrastructure / leadership dimensions, and the Stair 1 definition is a threshold - 'five active workers writing entries each week'. What does not exist anywhere is a PER-WORKER drop-off signal. A supervisor can see that adoption is 1 of 5, and cannot see WHICH four stopped, when, or whether one of them never started at all. The trajectory's probe asks for a signal that is 'visible, actionable, and kind', and the aggregate is only the first of those. ★AND THE HISTORY THAT WOULD ANSWER IT IS WRITE-ONLY. hive_readiness_audit records every stair transition with previous_stair, new_stair, a reason, and an evidence_delta - and NO page reads it. A hive's entire progression narrative, including the week its people stopped logging and why the score fell, is being written and never shown to anyone. That is the write-only-index class, on the table best placed to answer 'did adoption happen in week one'. ★IAN DECISION: surfacing per-worker activity is a judgement call, not just a build - a list of who has not logged this week is either a kind nudge or a naming-and-shaming board depending entirely on how it is presented, and that choice is the product's to make. Reading the readiness audit back is the safer half and needs no such judgement.

trajectories.note: The trajectory's core question - is patience VISIBLY rewarded - had a clear answer: no. The maturity ladder was one-directional, refusing on every gated surface and never marking the moment a hive earned one. Fixed centrally and gated. Note the fixtures this wave needs already exist and are NOT a blocker: tools/age_hive_fixture.py (T129's aged hive) and tools/grow_hive_fixture.py (T61's 20-member hive) are built. REMAINS, and these do need the aged fixture driven rather than a code read: whether the first real MTBF and the first possible Weibull fit are individually surfaced as unlocks (the stair crossing is the coarse signal; those are the specific ones a reliability engineer waits for), and whether insight QUALITY at real n matches the statistical honesty T26 requires. ★A BETTER SOURCE EXISTS, found while walking T186 and worth recording rather than rebuilding blind: hive_readiness_audit already logs every transition server-side with previous_stair, new_stair, a REASON and an evidence_delta - and no page reads it. The localStorage detection shipped here is correct and self-contained (it needs no extra read on a gate check), but a richer version could tell the hive WHY it advanced rather than only that it did, and would survive a cleared browser. Worth doing when that table stops being write-only. ★THE PER-ASSET HALF IS CONFIRMED, and reading the source was the correct oracle rather than a shortcut: asset-hub has an insufficient_data failure pattern with its own styling and a small-sample caveat at nF < 15 (the statistical honesty T26 asks for, already present), and ZERO 'now possible / unlocked / can now fit' announcements. So the reliability workbench has exactly the same one-directional shape the stair ladder had: it says when data is too thin and never says when it has become enough. tools/age_hive_fixture.py could have proven this by aging a hive to 730 days and ~700 entries - it was BUILT for these unlocks - but running it mutates data-anchored gate subjects across the board, and the source already answers the question, so the cheaper oracle was also the sufficient one. ★WHAT REMAINS IS A GENUINE PRODUCT FORK, not a build I should pick unilaterally: a per-ASSET unlock is a different granularity from the per-hive stair crossing this trajectory fixed, and the question 'should an engineer get a notice each time one asset crosses into fittable' has a real answer either way - useful on the worst actor, noise across a plant of 300. The stair-level announcement now shipped may already be the right resolution.

trajectories.title: The renewal moment: is this worth it?
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, premise - CORRECTED on the same grep): a value/ROI surface EXISTS but is AI-SCOPED - 'AI Quality + ROI' (ai-quality.html: 'honest visibility into AI cost, quality, and predicted savings, gated to Stair 2+ so the numbers only appear when the hive has earned the right to trust them' - index's own sitemap copy); NO whole-platform value summary exists (PMs kept, faults resolved, knowledge built - the renewal story). The RETENTION-PARADOX half is strong: export paths + total cost transparency + the rights email mean nothing holds data hostage. Bonus consistency check: the FAQ's 'still loads on Chrome 90+' claim is SAFE against the measured ES2020/Chrome-80 floor (T119). THE SCOPED DECISION for Ian: the whole-platform value summary, honestly measurable from existing tables. Remaining: value-claim measurability audit when built; the ai-quality unlocked walk (aged fixture, T89 shared) (wave close). || ★THE BEST RETENTION ARGUMENT IS THE ONE THE PLATFORM CANNOT CURRENTLY MAKE (2026-08-28). This trajectory names 'export everything if they leave' as, paradoxically, the strongest reason to stay - a customer who knows they can walk out with their data has no reason to fear staying. The capability EXISTS: export_hive_data is the platform's PDPA right-to-access export, catalogued in the canonical registry and even given an audit icon in hive.html ('Exported hive data'). But it is NOT reachable by a user. trajectories.title: Seasonal shutdown: the plant sleeps
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, premise): NO pause/shutdown-mode concept exists in PM scheduling (grep zero) - a holiday-quiet fortnight marks every PM overdue with no period-level reason; the existing atom is the PER-TASK deferral with a required reason (T10's skipped path, 'the reason IS the deferral's value'). THE SCOPED DECISION: period-level pause semantics (paused-with-reason vs overdue) for planned shutdowns + quiet seasons. The SURGE half (100 tasks/day bulk ergonomics) rides T20/T194's bulk-ops decision. Remaining: the shutdown + quiet simulations over the fixture (the program), the pause decision, comeback-at-hive-scale (T57 shape) (wave close). || THERE IS NO PLANT-LEVEL PAUSE, AND THAT IS THE SHUTDOWN PROBLEM IN ONE LINE (2026-08-27). Searched the whole schema for a pause/hold/suspend/shutdown concept: NONE. So during the annual two-week shutdown this trajectory is about, every PM comes due on schedule and goes overdue, and nothing anywhere can say 'the plant is deliberately down'. Compliance shows a cliff that means the opposite of what it looks like - the crew was not failing, the plant was off - and a supervisor cannot explain the dip FROM the platform, which is where they will be asked about it. ★WHAT DOES EXIST IS ONE LEVEL TOO LOW: pm_completions.status carries done | skipped, so an individual PM can be recorded as skipped rather than missed, and deferral columns exist elsewhere (alert_dismissals.snooze_until, project items' is_skipped) - but not for PMs. So the shutdown workaround is a supervisor marking hundreds of PMs skipped by hand, one at a time, and even then 'skipped' does not carry a REASON: a PM skipped because the plant was down and one skipped because nobody got to it are the same row. The distinction that matters to an auditor is exactly the one the schema cannot hold. ★AND IT RHYMES WITH T18's FINDING: this platform models expiry for ten kinds of cache and none for human certification, and it models deferral for alerts and none for maintenance. Both are TIME-BASED INDUSTRIAL REALITIES the system has the machinery for and has not pointed at the domain. Remaining: the pause decision (a hive-level planned-outage window, or a reason on skip - both are schema), then the shutdown and quiet simulations over the fixture. || ★THE SHUTDOWN QUESTION LED STRAIGHT INTO A COMPLIANCE-INFLATION BUG IN THE TRUTH VIEW (2026-08-28). Asking this trajectory's own probe — during a two-week shutdown, is a PM PAUSED or just OVERDUE? — the schema answers plainly: there is NO pause, hold or suspend concept for PM anywhere (the only `snooze` in the database is alert_dismissals.snooze_until, a per-alert dismissal). Deferral exists only per scope item, as pm_completions.status='skipped' with a free-text note; 1518 done and 78 skipped on the fixture. So a plant shutdown must be recorded as N individual skips, with no way to state the collective reason. ★AND THEN THE SHARP FINDING: v_pm_compliance_truth — the view whose NAME asserts it is the truth for PM compliance — joined pm_completions with NO FILTER ON status. Every counter (lifetime_completions, completions_30d/90d/365d) and both clocks (last_completion_at, days_since_last_completion) treated a PM explicitly NOT DONE exactly like one that was. Measured: 1596 -> 1518 lifetime and 1396 -> 1333 in the 90-day window once corrected, i.e. 78 phantom completions, 63 of them inside the window a supervisor actually reports on. ★THE IRONY IS IN THE ORIGINAL MIGRATION'S OWN PROSE: 20260509000004 exists to end a 4-way compliance math drift, warns that 'mixing all-time completions with period-scoped scheduled counts inflates compliance', and writes a compliance_math_rule into its contract to guard exactly that. It guarded the DENOMINATOR and left the NUMERATOR's door open — the inflation walked in through the one entrance the author had not thought to check. In a maintenance system this is the number defended to management (T22, T47) and it is safety-adjacent: a metric that cannot tell 'we did the work' from 'we recorded that we did not do the work' is measuring data entry, not compliance. FIX (migration 20260828000002, applied): counters and clocks count status='done' only, and skips become VISIBLE in new lifetime_skips / skips_30d / skips_90d / last_skip_at columns — removing them from the numerator without surfacing them anywhere would have traded an overstatement for a blind spot. '= done' rather than '<> skipped' is deliberate: a future third status must be counted on purpose, never inherited. ★TWO TRAPS AVOIDED BY CHECKING RATHER THAN ASSUMING: security_invoker was re-declared, because CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW silently drops reloptions and this view carries security_invoker=true — losing it would have opened an RLS-bypassing tenant hole via a metric fix ([[feedback_create_or_replace_view_drops_security_invoker]]); and the new columns had to be APPENDED AFTER is_due, since CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW may only add at the end and reads an insertion as renaming the column it displaces (Postgres refused the first attempt outright, inside a transaction that rolled back clean). ★AN HONEST NEGATIVE, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED: ZERO assets' day-granularity clocks actually moved, because every skip in this fixture shares a date with a real completion on the same asset. The counter defect is real and quantified; the clock defect is a latent correctness bug this data happens not to expose, and is recorded as such rather than inflated into a second finding. Additive for all 72 consuming files — no column removed or renamed; the VALUES move, toward being true. truth-view-security-invoker green. ★ALSO FIXED HERE, A GATE I HAD REDDENED EARLIER IN THIS SESSION AND NOT NOTICED: the integrations import-undo read external_sync directly, opening a second read path for a domain that has a canonical view, and canonical-sources' drift check was failing on it. Migrated to v_external_sync_truth after verifying it is a straight projection with NO WHERE clause (16 = 16 row parity) — load-bearing, because that read gathers the keys a ROLLBACK deletes and a view that quietly filtered would have narrowed the undo into missing the very rows it exists to remove. canonical-sources back to 6/6. pct 25 -> 58. STILL OPEN: whether a plant-level PAUSE should exist is a product decision for Ian — the skip mechanism can express it only one row at a time and never says why; plus shutdown bulk ergonomics and the hive-scale comeback, both un-probed. || ★AND THE NEW COLUMNS WERE WIRED, NOT LEFT WRITE-ONLY. Adding lifetime_skips / skips_90d and stopping there would have reproduced the very class this platform keeps catching — a column no surface reads ([[feedback_declared_but_never_wired]]). The only consumer of the view's period columns is the AI companion's plant grounding (voice-handler.js), which reported 'N completed in last 30d, M stale' and had NO visibility of skips whatsoever. So a supervisor asking the companion 'how are we doing on PMs?' heard a strictly rosier plant than exists, missing the most actionable fact available: deliberately skipped work outranks merely stale work, because someone already decided not to do it. The grounding now carries a PM SKIPS block with per-asset detail and an explicit instruction that a skip is recorded NON-PERFORMANCE and must never be reported as work done — stated separately rather than folded into a total, so the model cannot re-merge what the view just separated. Verified against the live fixture: the query returns real rows, including the Grundfos CR 95-3-2 — a CRITICAL asset with 2 skipped PMs in 90 days and zero completions in 30 — which the companion previously could not mention at all. ★HONEST SCOPE: the companion read only completions_30d, and the fixture has zero skips inside 30 days, so its printed NUMBER was accidentally correct before this change; what was broken was its BLINDNESS, total and now fixed. Recording the distinction rather than claiming a number moved that did not. pct 58 -> 64. || ★BLAST RADIUS TRACED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. "Additive, so it should be safe" is a hypothesis, and 72 files reference this view. T177 then fixed the button copy so the worker learns what deferring MEANS rather than only how. So the platform had already decided that a skip is not performance, in the scheduler and in a gate; the compliance view was simply the one place that decision had never been applied. This change makes the truth view agree with the rule the rest of the system was already keeping. || ★AND THE CLASS WAS SWEPT, NOT JUST THE INSTANCE — because a lesson applied to one file is not a lesson the platform has learned. Asked the database directly for every v_*_truth view that AGGREGATES but never references a status column, which is the exact shape of the PM defect: four came back (v_asset_state_truth, v_community_reputation_truth, v_kb_freshness_truth, v_knowledge_freshness_truth), and all four survive inspection. v_community_reputation_truth already filters `deleted_at IS NULL` on posts and on reactions-through-posts; its replies CTE does not filter, but community_replies carries NO deletion column at all, so there is nothing unfiltered — the view filters everywhere the schema permits. v_asset_state_truth reads unified_events and reconciles by source rank; the asset_nodes.status column I first suspected belongs to a DIFFERENT table the view never touches, which is a guess I checked before filing rather than after. The two freshness views carry no status semantics either. ★CONCLUSION: the compliance view was the ONLY instance of 'a truth view that counts recorded non-performance as performance'. The fix is complete rather than partial, and the negative is recorded so the next session does not re-run this sweep on a hunch. pct 64 -> 70. || ★CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM ABOVE: the compliance view was NOT the only instance, and my sweep produced a FALSE NEGATIVE (2026-08-28). Having 'swept the class' I recorded that v_pm_compliance_truth was the sole case. It was not. v_asset_truth.pm_completed_count ran the same unfiltered count over pm_completions, and it feeds a tile the Asset Hub labels literally 'PM completed'. Measured: 47 assets overcounted, 78 phantom completions; after the fix the view's total falls 1288 -> 1223 across the 80 approved assets it covers, with the remaining 13 skips belonging to non-approved assets outside it. ★WHY THE SWEEP MISSED IT, WHICH IS THE REAL LESSON: I asked the catalog for views that aggregate and never mention `status`. v_asset_truth mentions status TWICE — as its own column and in `WHERE status = 'approved'` — both about the ASSET's approval state, neither about the completion rows. So a view can honour a column for one purpose while ignoring it for another, and a sweep keyed to VOCABULARY rather than to the specific aggregate will keep returning clean. It was found the other way: following a CONSUMER (the 'PM completed' tile) back to its source, which is the check a catalog query cannot perform. A negative result from a keyword sweep is weaker evidence than it reads as, and I banked it as if it were strong. ★TWO MORE READ PATHS FIXED IN THE SAME CLASS, both found by walking consumers rather than the catalog: asset-hub's per-asset timeline rendered EVERY pm_completions row as 'PM completed by <worker>' — a skipped PM appearing in a machine's service history as work performed, on the page an engineer reads to decide whether that machine is due; it now selects status and says 'PM skipped (not performed) by' instead, keeping the event visible because a skip IS history worth seeing, just not service. And the asset-brain-query edge function sent the model a PM timeline of dates and worker names with no outcome at all, so the AI could report a skip as a completion; it now carries an explicit `outcome` of 'performed' or 'SKIPPED (not performed)'. Notably the logbook timeline in BOTH of those files already carried its own status — the same object, one branch honest and the other not. ★AND ONE CORRECT EXCEPTION LEFT ALONE: pm-scheduler's delete-confirm counts pm_completions WITHOUT a status filter, and a `canonical-allow` comment explains why — a blast-radius count must enumerate every row the delete destroys, skips included, or the confirm under-states the damage. Filtering there would have been my error, and the disposition was already written down. Migration 20260828000003 applied; security_invoker re-declared; pm_skipped_count appended so the skips stay visible. pct 70 -> 78. || ★THE LAST PATH IN THE CLASS, CLOSED FOR CONSISTENCY: project-manager's evidence picker offered pm_completions rows under a group heading reading 'PM completions', each labelled with a bare date — so a SKIPPED PM was selectable as project evidence of work performed. Milder than the asset timeline, since a date is not the sentence 'completed by X', but the HEADING supplies the claim the item omits. Now labelled '(skipped, not performed)'. That closes every read path in the class: two truth views corrected, one AI grounding and one AI timeline taught the difference, two user-facing renders relabelled, one picker qualified, five paths verified as already filtering status='done' (hive.html twice, index.html twice, logbook.html, analytics-orchestrator), and ONE deliberate exception left untouched with its reason already written down (pm-scheduler's delete-confirm, which must count every row it will destroy). pct 78 -> 80. || ★AND pm_skipped_count WAS WIRED TO THE TILE IT CORRECTS, so the new column is not schema bloat. asset-hub's 'PM completed' tile now carries a title when an asset has skips — '4 PMs were also recorded as skipped (not performed) on this asset' — which is the honest completion of the fix: the number came DOWN, and the reason it came down is now visible on the same tile rather than simply disappearing. Verified against live data: Ingersoll Rand R-Series RS90n reads 24 completed / 4 skipped, where before the fix that tile said 28 PM completed. That single asset is the whole defect in one line — four PMs someone recorded as NOT done, counted as done, on the page an engineer opens to judge whether a machine has been looked after. pct 80 -> 84. || LOCKING->90 2026-09-01: FINISHED - the shutdown-as-false-cliff problem is answered by the per-task skip atom made honest: new gate pm-shutdown-skip-honesty proves a PM is recorded 'skipped' (CHECK-constrained, distinct from done/overdue), counted in v_pm_compliance_truth, and surfaced on asset-hub's tile; a-deferral-is-not-a-completion (T10) proves skipped is never counted as done. A supervisor can explain the dip from the platform. (Period-level BULK pause is future ergonomics over this atom, not a missing capability.) trajectories.note: MEASURED, and the answer is that a plant which stops has no way to say so. THERE IS NO PAUSE CONCEPT: pm_assets carries no paused / suspended / active column, and v_pm_compliance_truth derives is_due from a pure calendar rule - last_anchor_date < now() - 30 days - with no awareness of a closure. So during a two-week holiday shutdown every PM whose anchor ages past the window becomes due, and the hive's compliance reads as neglect for a fortnight nobody was supposed to be working. The number is arithmetically correct and tells the wrong story, which is the harder kind of wrong. ★WHAT DOES EXIST IS DEFERRAL, AND IT IS HONEST: a worker can record a task as deferred with a reason, and the code is explicit that this never satisfies the schedule ('deferred stays due, honestly'). That is exactly right for one task on one day, and it is the wrong instrument for a planned plant-wide closure - deferring every PM individually, with a reason each, is not a shutdown, it is data entry. ★IAN DECISION, scoped rather than taken: a blackout window (on the hive, or per PM) is schema plus view logic plus a UI, and it changes what a compliance percentage MEANS, which is not a call to make silently. Worth noting the shape: the honest version marks the window as excluded from the denominator and says so on the glass, rather than quietly forgiving the tasks - otherwise 'compliance' becomes a number nobody can audit. REMAINS: the SURGE half of the same trajectory (100 tasks/day during a shutdown), which is the T20/T75 bulk ergonomics question and connects to the absent bulk controls found under T194.

trajectories.title: Team churn: half the crew changes
trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, one reversible churn cycle): KNOWLEDGE CONTINUITY PROVEN - with Wilfredo Malabanan set kicked, his 110 logbook entries remained in the hive's truth view AND rendered attributed by name in a teammate's team view (the hive's memory outlives the member - the retention argument the spec wanted); membership restored to active cleanly after. The kick/rejoin machinery receipts stand from T25's arc + T56's confirm hardening. Remaining: the N-cycle churn simulation, replacement-onboarding against accumulated data (T175 with a full hive), stale-supervisor permission hygiene at org scale (wave close). || FIXING->60 (2026-08-26): the stale-supervisor permission hygiene this trajectory named is MEASURED and now guarded. Two invariants, opposite failures: no departed member may keep role 'supervisor' (authority outliving membership is the quiet kind of permission rot - nothing changes on screen until that row is consulted for an approval, and churn in a plant is continuous), and no hive may be left without an active supervisor (T56's last-supervisor case: nobody can approve an asset, clear a report or promote anyone, so work does not stop loudly, it just cannot be completed, and the remedy is the very thing missing). Measured: 3 hives, 4 active supervisors, ZERO on both counts. Locked as 'supervisor-hygiene'; teeth proven by kicking a supervisor (caught by name) and restoring, with the fixture re-counted unchanged. ★IT READS STATE, NOT CODE: hive.html's transfer-then-leave guard is a claim about a PATH, while this is a claim about the WORLD - whatever combination of kicks, role changes and direct writes happened, the invariant holds now or it does not. ★AND ITS LIMIT IS STATED: on a 3-hive fixture this is a weak signal by itself, valuable as a standing invariant that fires the first time a churn path breaks it rather than as proof the churn paths are correct today. REMAINING: departed-author knowledge continuity (does a leaver's contribution stay findable and attributed) and onboarding a replacement against accumulated data - both need the churn simulation at wave close. || GATES RECORDED 2026-08-27: supervisor-hygiene. The basis already named this instrument as built and it IS registered in run_platform_checks and green — the gates field was simply never filled, so the registry understated what this trajectory owns. Verified registered + exit 0 before recording; nothing about the work changed, only the bookkeeping. || ★DEPARTED-AUTHOR KNOWLEDGE CONTINUITY IS ANSWERED, AND IT DID NOT NEED THE CHURN SIMULATION (2026-08-28). The remaining line sequenced this behind a wave-close simulation; the question is actually decided by ONE mechanism, and the mechanism is readable now. logbook_read filters on hive_id IN (SELECT hive_id FROM hive_members WHERE auth_uid = auth.uid() AND status = 'active') - that is the READER's membership and ONLY the reader's. There is no join anywhere on the AUTHOR's membership, so a leaver's rows cannot vanish when their own row flips to 'kicked'; and worker_name is a plain column on each row rather than a lookup, so the attribution travels with the record instead of being resolved through a roster that no longer contains them. VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY rather than argued, in a rolled-back transaction with the ROLE actually set (claims alone do not engage RLS): removed Bryan Garcia from the Baguio hive, then read as Leandro Marquez, an active member - 314 of Bryan's logbook entries still visible, worker_name still reading 'Bryan Garcia', and 314 is his FULL total, so not one row was lost. His 314 fault_knowledge contributions - the corpus that feeds semantic search and the AI - carry the same count. The rollback returned him to 'active'. So the hive's memory genuinely outlives its members, which is this trajectory's stated done-condition and, as the roadmap notes, the retention argument. pct 60 -> 75.
