trajectories.basis: WALKED->25 (2026-08-25, live receipts from THIS session): cold-start reality measured - shift-brain's first generation ran ~90s (multi-lane cold start) vs ~6s warm, with the T76 fix making the wait safe (both buttons locked); fallback_engaged families label stored copies (amc_briefings fallback, analytics 'Saved snapshot, computed 1h ago' seen under offline cold-start in T44's walk); the T27 CPM/EVM silent-absence fix is the per-fn isolation receipt; whAiError distinguishes unreachable vs rate-limit (the shift-brain 429 lesson). Remaining: the per-fn outage injection MATRIX (which surfaces go quiet - each labeled), cold-vs-down distinguishability probes (PP patience calibration) (wave close). || FIXING->60 (2026-08-26): per-fn outage isolation probed by forcing ONE edge function (project-progress) to 503 while the database stayed up - and it found a live defect of the worst kind. ★THE FALLBACK ANSWERED CONFIDENTLY AND WRONGLY: clientRollup returned critical_path: { item_ids: [], total_days: 0, slack_per_item: {} }, and renderCpm()'s PJ8 guard (`if (!cp)` -> 'The critical path could not be computed right now') never fired, because AN EMPTY OBJECT IS TRUTHY. A shutdown project whose real schedule is '12d, 7 of 7 items on the critical path' rendered as 'CRITICAL PATH 0d - 0 of 7 items on critical path' with a full Gantt beneath - telling a supervisor planning a plant outage that NOTHING is critical for a project where EVERYTHING is. Not a blank, not an error: an inversion presented as fact. Fixed with critical_path: null so the existing honest message speaks (every consumer already used optional chaining). ★THE SIBLING PATTERN AGAIN: the EVM half of that same fallback HAD received its marker (evm_reason: 'unavailable', with a comment about 'two notices, two truth conditions') and the CPM half was left behind. Verified live in BOTH directions - engine up renders the real 12d schedule, engine down admits it cannot compute - and resurrection-proven against the pre-fix empty object, which reproduces '0d 0 of 7'. Locked as 'edge-down-admits-it'. REMAINING: the cold-start-vs-down distinction (a 4s first invoke is not an outage) and the edge-down page inventory across the other functions (wave close). || CLASS SWEPT (same day): rather than stop at the one instance, swept every 'could not be computed' branch on the platform for the same shape - a deliberate absence-branch that an empty-but-truthy fallback can never trigger. 11 such guards exist; ZERO are defeated after the fix, so the class is extinct rather than the single case being patched. Locked as 'absence-guard-reachable'. ★A BROAD SWEEP WOULD HAVE BEEN 33 FALSE FINDINGS: parts: [], rows: [], work: [] are correct ways to say 'none'. The defect needs BOTH halves - a consumer that distinguishes uncomputed from empty, and a producer that collapses the distinction. ★AND THE DETECTOR FAILED ITS OWN RESURRECTION TEST FIRST: its producer pattern could not match a value containing nested braces, and the real defect contained slack_per_item: {}, so it reported 0 with the bug PRESENT. A detector that cannot find the bug it was written for is worse than none - fixed to allow one nesting level and proven to go 1 -> 0 across the fix. || GATES RECORDED 2026-08-27: absence-guard-reachable, edge-down-admits-it. The basis already named this instrument as built and it IS registered in run_platform_checks and green — the gates field was simply never filled, so the registry understated what this trajectory owns. Verified registered + exit 0 before recording; nothing about the work changed, only the bookkeeping. || THE COLD-VS-DOWN DISTINCTION IS BUILT, AND THE DEFECT WAS ON THE TRUST SURFACE ITSELF (2026-08-28). Chasing 'a 4s first invoke is not an outage' I surveyed every fetchWithTimeout budget on the platform against utils.js's default of 30s - which is documented as matching the edge cold-start allowance - looking for a caller impatient enough to turn a cold start into a failure. status.html was that caller, and it is the worst possible page for this bug: it probes ten functions' /health on an 8s budget, and its own comment classified 'TIMEOUT' as 'a genuine outage'. The page whose entire job is telling people whether the platform is up was publishing a healthy-but-cold function as DOWN, in red. ★MEASURED BOTH SIDES with one function hung and one genuinely 503: BEFORE '8/10 probed surfaces healthy (80%) - 2 DOWN', the cold card reading 'DOWN - HTTP 0 - 8018 ms - AbortError: signal is aborted without reason'. AFTER '8/9 probed surfaces healthy (89%) - 1 DOWN - 1 did not answer in time (not counted either way)', the cold card reading 'no answer in 8s (may be cold-starting)'. THREE defects in that one line: an outage asserted that nobody observed, a raw internal abort string on a user-facing trust page, and an availability percentage whose denominator counted a surface the probe never actually read. The new 'timeout' state is amber and leaves BOTH the healthy numerator and the DOWN count - a probe that timed out answers neither question, and folding it into either would be the page asserting something it did not see. ★A CORRECTION I NEARLY GOT WRONG: I expected the utils.js null-on-timeout contract to cause a null dereference at res.json(), the class three callers were already fixed for - but status.html is self-contained and defines its OWN wrapper that RETHROWS the AbortError, so no such bug exists here. Reading the local definition rather than assuming the shared one is what kept that out of the record. Locked as gate status-cold-is-not-down, 9 assertions, which deliberately asserts ALL THREE states in one run: the cheapest way to make 'no false DOWN' true is to stop saying DOWN at all, so a real 503 must still read DOWN and a healthy fn still healthy. REMAINING: the edge-down page inventory across the other functions (wave close). || STATUS -> locking/88 (2026-08-28). THREE INSTRUMENT ERRORS came first, each accusing the platform of a defect it did not have: a derived name is not an identity (two anonymous <a> elements both read 'a', so every page looked like a keyboard trap and 47/67 controls looked unreachable); checkVisibility() by DEFAULT ignores visibility:hidden and opacity, and does not care that a sheet is parked off-page by a transform, so the nav-hub and companion controls looked skipped when the browser was correctly keeping them out of the tab order; and an input type=date holds focus across its own day/month/year segments. Built because axe cannot answer two of these three lenses - it cannot press Tab, and it cannot know whether an aria-live region existed BEFORE the message that needed announcing (a region inserted with its own text is never spoken). THREE INSTRUMENT ERRORS came first, each accusing the platform of a defect it did not have: a derived name is not an identity (two anonymous <a> elements both read 'a', so every page looked like a keyboard trap and 47/67 controls looked unreachable); checkVisibility() by DEFAULT ignores visibility:hidden and opacity, and does not care that a sheet is parked off-page by a transform, so the nav-hub and companion controls looked skipped when the browser was correctly keeping them out of the tab order; and an input type=date holds focus across its own day/month/year segments. ONE REAL FINDING, FIXED: asset-hub, shift-brain, achievements and marketplace-seller had NO navigation landmark at all - the hub panel is role=dialog, which is correct for a modal but is not a landmark - so nav-hub.js now marks its persistent wrapper role=navigation with a translated label, one edit covering every page that loads it.

THREE INSTRUMENT ERRORS came first, each accusing the platform of a defect it did not have: a derived name is not an identity (two anonymous <a> elements both read 'a', so every page looked like a keyboard trap and 47/67 controls looked unreachable); checkVisibility() by DEFAULT ignores visibility:hidden and opacity, and does not care that a sheet is parked off-page by a transform, so the nav-hub and companion controls looked skipped when the browser was correctly keeping them out of the tab order; and an input type=date holds focus across its own day/month/year segments. ONE REAL FINDING, FIXED: asset-hub, shift-brain, achievements and marketplace-seller had NO navigation landmark at all - the hub panel is role=dialog, which is correct for a modal but is not a landmark - so nav-hub.js now marks its persistent wrapper role=navigation with a translated label, one edit covering every page that loads it.

R1 FOUND AND FIXED: registration existed and NOTHING watched what happened next - a new worker reached waiting, sat there, and took over on the person's next navigation, so the shell changed under someone mid-task and a half-filled form went with it, with no way for them to know a deploy had happened. nav-hub.js now announces it with a dismissible notice, and stays silent on a FIRST install, which has nothing to interrupt. R2 CLEAN: 1006/1006 columns selected by the daily pages exist in the live schema, so no screen is running ahead of its migration - the shape that shows an error where a number belongs and reads to a person exactly like 'no data'. R3 REPORTED, not failed: 3/4 committing surfaces keep an in-progress draft across a reload; the miss is logbook's SEARCH box, which is not a draft. One calibration: a forward-only proximity window called correct code silent, because the notice function is defined ABOVE the listener that calls it - the detector now reads the registration block in either order.

trajectories.title: You cannot tell which version you are on when you report that something broke - hive
trajectories.basis: [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-06 via tools/prove_release_visibility.mjs (gate release-visibility), the first lens of the LAYER-UX wave to be closed. THE LENS WAS TRUE: measured before the fix, NOT ONE page on the platform carried a build or version identifier a person could find and quote, so every report arrived as 'it broke on my screen' with no way to know whether that screen was even running the code that had been fixed - which makes every cannot-reproduce ambiguous between a real defect and a stale client. FIXED: utils.js gains whBuildVersion(), reachable on all 15 daily pages, and status.html - the page a person is on when something is wrong - shows it with the tooltip 'Quote this when you report a problem'. The version is the one the BROWSER is serving, read from the service-worker shell cache, not a build-time constant: the constant says what SHOULD be deployed and says it identically to someone three deploys behind, while the cache says what this person is actually looking at, and the two disagree exactly when it matters. Verified live with all three in agreement - the page shows 'app v310', the browser holds workhive-shell-v310, and sw.js declares workhive-shell-v310. One calibration: a fresh context has no shell, so a cold check can only exercise the honest-unknown fallback; the gate primes the shell by opening the app once, the way any real visit does, before it asks.

trajectories.title: The error you hit leaves no trace anyone can find afterwards - hive
trajectories.basis: [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-06 via tools/prove_failure_traceable.mjs (gate failure-traceable), LAYER-UX §LX: all four Error-Tracking lenses in one walk, with every Supabase read aborted from the first byte - what 'the network went away' looks like from a chair. 15/15 pages now say more than a bare 'something went wrong' and hand the person something QUOTABLE. THE GAP WAS REAL AND UNIFORM: before the fix not ONE page gave a handle on which failure - no time, no version, no code - so a report arrived as 'it broke earlier' and could be matched to no record. FIXED in utils.js's shared notice, the same one-install-at-the-transport lever the retry used: it now carries the moment and the shell version. A browser-side failure has no server trace id by definition, because the transport is the thing that broke, so the honest handle is what the client can state for itself, and both halves are matchable against the logs by hand. SCOPE STATED, not graded: with the transport severed the error reporter cannot post either, so client_errors and wh_traces do not move during this walk - the record that would describe the failure is lost with it, and that is named rather than counted as a pass. One calibration: the detector could not see a clock time (ref 10:42:07 is three two-digit groups, and the pattern demanded three digits together), so it reported pages carrying a perfectly good reference as having nothing to quote.

THE GAP WAS REAL AND UNIFORM: before the fix not ONE page gave a handle on which failure - no time, no version, no code - so a report arrived as 'it broke earlier' and could be matched to no record. FIXED in utils.js's shared notice, the same one-install-at-the-transport lever the retry used: it now carries the moment and the shell version. A browser-side failure has no server trace id by definition, because the transport is the thing that broke, so the honest handle is what the client can state for itself, and both halves are matchable against the logs by hand. SCOPE STATED, not graded: with the transport severed the error reporter cannot post either, so client_errors and wh_traces do not move during this walk - the record that would describe the failure is lost with it, and that is named rather than counted as a pass. One calibration: the detector could not see a clock time (ref 10:42:07 is three two-digit groups, and the pattern demanded three digits together), so it reported pages carrying a perfectly good reference as having nothing to quote.

trajectories.title: As the hive grows past twenty people, this page gets slower and never says so - logbook
trajectories.basis: [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-06 via tools/prove_growth_honesty.mjs (gate growth-honesty), LAYER-UX §LX Load-Balancing & Scaling, asked as what a person NOTICES as the hive grows rather than as a benchmark. TEN UNBOUNDED LIST READS FOUND AND FIXED - inventory, community, marketplace x2, asset-hub x2, dayplanner, pm-scheduler and alert-hub x2 all read a table with no limit or range, which is fine at 92 rows and is the page hanging with nothing said at ten times that; one of them even carried a comment promising a .limit(500) nobody had ever added. All are now bounded and the walk reads 175/175. G2: 5/5 load-more controls actually render more when pressed - a cap with a dead button is worse than a cap, because the person can see there is more and cannot reach it. G3: pm_assets carries updated_at, so a stale write is detectable rather than silently winning. THREE INSTRUMENT CALIBRATIONS, each a false accusation first: a builder chain ends at its SEMICOLON and is often assembled across statements, so logbook's read looked unbounded while carrying its limit four lines further down past a blank line; a write's .select() is a RETURNING clause and not a list, so an UPDATE by primary key was reported as an unbounded read over 3,820 rows; and a container id of 'feed' is not matched by [id$="-feed"], which made the row counter blind and a working load-more read as dead.

TEN UNBOUNDED LIST READS FOUND AND FIXED - inventory, community, marketplace x2, asset-hub x2, dayplanner, pm-scheduler and alert-hub x2 all read a table with no limit or range, which is fine at 92 rows and is the page hanging with nothing said at ten times that; one of them even carried a comment promising a .limit(500) nobody had ever added. All are now bounded and the walk reads 175/175. G2: 5/5 load-more controls actually render more when pressed - a cap with a dead button is worse than a cap, because the person can see there is more and cannot reach it. G3: pm_assets carries updated_at, so a stale write is detectable rather than silently winning. THREE INSTRUMENT CALIBRATIONS, each a false accusation first: a builder chain ends at its SEMICOLON and is often assembled across statements, so logbook's read looked unbounded while carrying its limit four lines further down past a blank line; a write's .select() is a RETURNING clause and not a list, so an UPDATE by primary key was reported as an unbounded read over 3,820 rows; and a container id of 'feed' is not matched by [id$="-feed"], which made the row counter blind and a working load-more read as dead.

trajectories.title: A feature that works locally is dead in production because the origin sends no header for it - index
trajectories.basis: [2026-09-05] pct -> 60. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-06 against https://workhiveph.com via tools/prove_hosting_reality.mjs, LAYER-UX §LX Hosting lenses H1 and H4, and BOTH FAIL IN PRODUCTION TODAY. H1: 0 of 5 security headers are served - no Content-Security-Policy, no X-Frame-Options, no nosniff, no Referrer-Policy, no Permissions-Policy - because the repo shipped a Cloudflare _headers file and a netlify.toml to a VERCEL host, which reads neither, so any shipped feature depending on one of them is dead and nothing local could ever have told us. H4: /wh-ga4.js comes back 'public, max-age=0, must-revalidate', so it is re-downloaded on every visit, a bill a person pays in data on a Philippine mobile plan. FIX BUILT LOCALLY, NOT YET DEPLOYED: vercel.json is generated from _headers so the two cannot drift, and now also caches js/css for an hour with revalidation - they cannot be immutable because filenames here are not content-hashed, and the service worker re-primes the shell on a version bump so a short browser cache cannot hide a release. These rows stay at fixing because only Ian's deploy can make the claim true. · [2026-09-05] pct -> 90. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 against the LOCAL SUBSTITUTE for the Vercel edge: tools/serve_vercel_headers.py applies vercel.json's own header rules the way Vercel matches them (path-to-regexp sources, every matching rule in order, later keys win) and tools/prove_deploy_headers.py walks this row's page and assets over it - CSP, Permissions-Policy microphone=(self) camera=(self), HTML max-age=0 must-revalidate, scripts/styles max-age=3600, images a year immutable, sw.js no-store: 39/39 after one config fix the walk itself found (the /sw.js no-store rule sat BEFORE the generic js/css rule, so the service worker would have shipped cached for an hour; moved last). This proves the contract the deploy carries; locking, not locked: production is Ian's deploy, which is the lock. Gate deploy-headers-local registered (runs in --fast).

trajectories.title: The platform must refuse an ex-employee whose session is still alive after they were removed from the hive - hive
trajectories.story: walked as the hostile persona through PostgREST, never as the owner connection
trajectories.basis: [2026-09-05] pct -> 100. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_hostile_personas.mjs (gate hostile-personas), 7/7 contracts held, every one walked AS the hostile person through PostgREST on their own token - never the owner connection, which can read every row and so can never prove a refusal, and never a marketplace admin, whose bypass produced seven false leaks once before. A member removed from the hive while holding a live token reads 0 of the 5 rows they could see a moment earlier and a write returns 403 (H1). A stranger reading the listings table directly is answered 401, and the public view answers them 200 with 3 rows and 29 columns carrying no contact and no moderation note (H2). A seller reviewing their own listing or rewriting their own rating_count gets 403 both ways (H3). A supervisor who is not an admin aiming a bulk PATCH at another hive changes 0 rows (H4). An anonymous write forging a real hive id is refused 401 with the policy named (H5). A worker with zero inquiries on a listing opening a dispute against its seller is refused 403 (H6). A plain worker pulling the hive export is refused 403 with the sentence 'PDPA right-to-access requires active supervisor role' (H7). TWO REAL HOLES FOUND AND FIXED LOCALLY, both awaiting Ian's prod deploy: migration 20260907000004 - SELECT * on marketplace_listings gave a stranger seller_contact and the moderation notes, columns no page shows, harvestable at one request per 26 columns; the marketplace and seller-profile pages now read v_marketplace_listings_public (same column names minus the private ones, published-or-own, read-only - the schema's default privileges had granted anon INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on the new definer view, an auto-updatable write path around RLS, revoked in the same migration) and anon lost SELECT on the base table; a stranger still gets 3,146 characters of marketplace. Migration 20260907000003 - mkt_disp_insert checked only that the opener was who they said they were, so anyone with an account could dispute any listing; it now requires an inquiry or an order the opener is party to. ONE FINDING WAS A STOPPED CONTAINER: the export returned 503 'name resolution failed' because two log-shipping containers had been OOM-killed nine hours earlier and the edge runtime resolves them by name - the move this platform already knows; restarted, and the refusal read 403 with a sentence.

trajectories.basis: [2026-09-05] pct -> 100. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-07 via tools/prove_hostile_personas.mjs (gate hostile-personas), 7/7 contracts held, every one walked AS the hostile person through PostgREST on their own token - never the owner connection, which can read every row and so can never prove a refusal, and never a marketplace admin, whose bypass produced seven false leaks once before. A member removed from the hive while holding a live token reads 0 of the 5 rows they could see a moment earlier and a write returns 403 (H1). A stranger reading the listings table directly is answered 401, and the public view answers them 200 with 3 rows and 29 columns carrying no contact and no moderation note (H2). A seller reviewing their own listing or rewriting their own rating_count gets 403 both ways (H3). A supervisor who is not an admin aiming a bulk PATCH at another hive changes 0 rows (H4). An anonymous write forging a real hive id is refused 401 with the policy named (H5). A worker with zero inquiries on a listing opening a dispute against its seller is refused 403 (H6). A plain worker pulling the hive export is refused 403 with the sentence 'PDPA right-to-access requires active supervisor role' (H7). TWO REAL HOLES FOUND AND FIXED LOCALLY, both awaiting Ian's prod deploy: migration 20260907000004 - SELECT * on marketplace_listings gave a stranger seller_contact and the moderation notes, columns no page shows, harvestable at one request per 26 columns; the marketplace and seller-profile pages now read v_marketplace_listings_public (same column names minus the private ones, published-or-own, read-only - the schema's default privileges had granted anon INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on the new definer view, an auto-updatable write path around RLS, revoked in the same migration) and anon lost SELECT on the base table; a stranger still gets 3,146 characters of marketplace. Migration 20260907000003 - mkt_disp_insert checked only that the opener was who they said they were, so anyone with an account could dispute any listing; it now requires an inquiry or an order the opener is party to. ONE FINDING WAS A STOPPED CONTAINER: the export returned 503 'name resolution failed' because two log-shipping containers had been OOM-killed nine hours earlier and the edge runtime resolves them by name - the move this platform already knows; restarted, and the refusal read 403 with a sentence.

trajectories.basis: [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE via tools/prove_full_journeys.mjs and REPRODUCED on 2026-09-10 (it failed the same way in the batch running now), so this is a genuine finding rather than a stale receipt. J11 is the solo technician's story - one person keeping their own machines - and its FIRST hop dies: index.html -> asset-hub.html with own=0 AND hub=0. ESTABLISHED, from the step evidence of one session: the person is signed in and identified (Jun Salvador, signInWall false, effect read - the one-person operator's own records exist) and holds NO hive (hive='', role=''); index.html shows hub=0 while asset-hub.html and logbook.html in the SAME session both show hub=2, so the nav renders for this person on app pages and not on the landing page; and index.html carries no static link to asset-hub at all (13 mentions, every one inside a script). NOT ESTABLISHED, and deliberately not guessed: WHY the hub is absent there. nav-hub.js is loaded by index.html (a plain script tag at :2759), its init() runs unconditionally with no landing-page exclusion, and buildWidget() is not hive-gated - so the tidy explanations do not survive reading the code. The next probe is a live one: open index.html as a hive-less signed-in person and read whether the widget builds, because that is a browser question and the browser is walking another archetype. What the finding already says without the cause: a signed-in solo owner standing on the landing page has neither the nav nor a link to the surface where their own machines live, which is the first step of the journey this platform wrote for them. pct -> 25. · [2026-09-05] CORRECTION to the note above, which overstated the scope - measured across every receipt rather than read off one row. I wrote that a signed-in solo owner on the landing page has no nav; the population says something narrower and more useful. Of 304 index.html hops on record, hub=1 in 259 and hub=2 in 41; hub=0 in FOUR, and those four are exactly TWO rows - W37 and W38, each visiting index twice - both the solo-persona cells of J11 tier A, both rendering thin (chars 612/616 against a median of 1276, controls 16). Eighteen OTHER hive-less index visits DID get the hub, so it is not universal to people without a hive, and W37 reproduced with the same signature in the batch running now, so it is not a random flake either. What that leaves is specific: on this cast, index.html comes up thin and without its nav, and the story's first hop (index -> asset-hub) has no route because index carries no static asset-hub link either (13 mentions, all inside scripts). Still NOT established: the cause. index.html loads nav-hub.js from a plain tag at :2759, init() runs unconditionally with no landing-page exclusion, buildWidget() is not hive-gated, and index.html contains no reference to wh-hub that could hide or remove it - so every tidy explanation has now been checked and none survives. The next probe is live and narrow: open index.html as this cast and read whether #wh-hub is built, and whether the thin render (612 chars) means the page had not finished when it was measured. pct -> 25. · [2026-09-05] CAUSE NARROWED BY ELIMINATION, all of it static so the live probe is one question rather than five. Ruled OUT, each by reading the code rather than guessing: (1) a landing-page exclusion - init() runs unconditionally and buildWidget() has no early return; (2) a hive gate - the only  in nav-hub.js sits inside the community-badge fetch, not the mount; (3) suppression by the page - index.html contains no reference to wh-hub, so nothing hides or removes the widget, and it loads nav-hub.js from a plain tag at :2759; (4) a MODE filter, which was the best suspect and is refuted arithmetically - getMode()'s staleness guard needs  truthy and a hive-less person has wh_hive_role='' so a stored mode is never re-derived, BUT Asset Hub is listed in supervisor+engineer+field and the fourth mode is 'all', so it is visible in EVERY mode and no mode can hide it. What is left standing is PAGE STATE: index.html measured 612/616 chars against a median of 1276 across 304 index hops, with 16 controls, on exactly the two rows that show hub=0 - a thin render, not a filtered nav. trajectories.story: the small plant that pays in pesos through a phone and needs the platform's arithmetic to match the bank's
trajectories.basis: [2026-09-05] pct -> 60. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-09 through the playwright + postgres MCPs as Jericho Bonifacio (worker AND a non-admin marketplace seller, Manila Electronics Assembly) — the J28 credit story across marketplace.html -> marketplace-seller.html -> hive.html -> audit-log.html in one signed-in context. The journey's own first leg was performed through the PLATFORM'S OWN function, not a seeded row: claim_starter_grant() returned {granted:true, amount:500}, and that 500 then SHOWED on his seller dashboard as 'PHP500 total' and was still readable as him at the last hop. All four pages arrived as themselves; the hive held at every step; no skeletons, no visible errors. THE LAST HOP IS A CORRECT REFUSAL, not a failure: audit-log.html tells a worker 'Supervisors only - the audit log is visible to hive supervisors so they can review approval, rejection and member-management decisions', and RLS agrees (0 rows readable as him). So the receipt leg of this story belongs to a supervisor cast; the credit leg is proven for a worker. ORACLE CORRECTED IN THE SAME PASS: the J28 chain counted credit_treasury and service_credit_ledger GLOBALLY - 1 and 7 through the owner connection, 0 and 0 as a real person - because credit_treasury is the platform's own float with no hive at all and the ledger is scoped by policy to account_id = auth.uid(). A global count is a claim about nobody; the chain now counts THIS walker's own consumer entries through the same join the policy uses. · [2026-09-05] ITS RED IS STALE, recorded so nobody re-diagnoses a fixed chain. The receipt says 'the chain is empty in this hive - the missing link is credit_treasury', and the chain that produced that reading was corrected on 2026-09-09: credit_treasury is the PLATFORM's own float - a SINGLETON, CHECK id = 1, with no hive column at all - so counting it per-hive asked a hive question of a platform table, and a worker seeing none of it is the product working rather than a gap. The J28 chain now counts only this buyer's own service_credit_ledger rows, through the same join the RLS policy uses, which is the only version of 'credits are held and spent' a journey can prove. Dates settle it: this row's receipt is 2026-09-08 15:08, the prover carrying the corrected chain is 2026-09-10. What is owed is a re-walk on the current chain, not an investigation - and J28 is in the batch now running. pct -> 60.

trajectories.title: The same day, degraded: the journey re-walked on a bad network, with a dependency down, and through a release - the breakdown to close-out of Manila Electronics Assembly
trajectories.story: the ordinary day that has to survive the conditions a Philippine plant actually has; walked on a 3G connection that keeps dropping

journey.vertical: the breakdown to close-out of Manila Electronics Assembly

trajectories.basis: [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE via tools/prove_full_journeys.mjs on the offline-3g condition, and triaged 2026-09-10 as ONE cluster rather than five separate mysteries. Every open offline-3g row fails the same way - a same-origin script did not arrive at the 1-in-12 abort this condition applies - and the symptom only differs by WHICH file lost its turn: W3579 and W3627 report 'getDb() called before @supabase/supabase-js loaded' (the client), W3122 reports 'window.getDb is not a function' (utils.js, which defines it), and W3512/W3599/W3654/W3700 report a step not arriving as itself or a hop with no way onward (the page or nav-hub.js). Eleven open rows, one mechanism. THE STRUCTURE IS BUILT: browser-floor.js now asks once more for a dropped same-origin script - from the CAPTURE phase, since a resource error does not bubble - carrying integrity and crossorigin across, at most once per tag, with the replacement marked before insertion so a dropping line cannot become a request loop; and sw.js answers app navigations network-first with a kept copy. Unit-verified in tools/test_browser_floor_retry.mjs (16 cases, both directions, mutation-tested four ways) and the arming order audited across all 35 pages that load a shell script. THESE ROWS ARE NOT CLOSED ON THAT: a unit test proves the retry fires, only a walk proves the person got their page, and the re-walk is a browser job. tools/prove_full_journeys.mjs gained --condition this turn so it can be one scoped run over all 20 offline-3g rows instead of re-walking J1+J14+J17+J4+J16 entire to reach five. Status corrected from specced where a real receipt already existed. pct -> 25. · [2026-09-05] WALKED THROUGH THE MCPs AS THE PERSON, NOT THROUGH THE LIBRARY (Ian, 2026-09-10: 'we should always use MCPs for walks'; roadmap SS-LW.1 rule 4 - batch with the library, WALK with the MCP, because each step's snapshot decides the next). chrome-devtools MCP, viewport 390x844x3 mobile+touch, networkConditions 'Slow 3G', signed in through the platform's OWN door. trajectories.title: The supervisor's week: the day plan, the handover, the approvals, the moderation, the numbers - Manila Electronics Assembly · on a 3G connection that keeps dropping
trajectories.story: the person accountable for other people's work, whose week is five surfaces and one story; the same story on a 3G connection that keeps dropping
trajectories.basis: [2026-09-05] Walked live twice under the offline-3g overlay for Manila Electronics Assembly and NOT banked, with the reason traced rather than guessed. Run 1: 5/6 arrived, shift-brain.html did not land. Run 2 (fresh browser): 5/6 arrived, shift-brain landed fine at 4,027 chars and ph-intelligence.html did not land instead. THE FAILING STEP MOVED, which is the whole answer - a specific broken page does not rotate. Read the overlay's own code: offline-3g deliberately DROPS roughly one request in twelve (route.abort('connectionfailed') on every 12th), and its comment says why - 'slow, and it DROPS, which is what makes a page's retry and its empty-vs-failed distinction worth anything'. So when the dropped request happens to be a page's main NAVIGATION, that page cannot arrive, and which page draws the short straw changes run to run. Confirmed the pages themselves are fine: shift-brain.html serves in 0.004s directly. NOT a product defect on this evidence, and NOT banked green either. One honest nuance worth recording rather than asserting: each walk runs in a FRESH browser context, so no service worker is installed yet and a dropped navigation has no cached shell to fall back to - a returning person with the SW active would have offline-fallback.html. That makes this cell a stricter test than the situation it models, which is worth knowing before anyone reads a failure here as a broken page. pct -> 25. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-10 on the offline-3g condition, and NOT banked green - the walk found something real and the fix this turn made does not close it. The condition delays every request and ABORTS about one in twelve, which is the point of it. W3521 (J25, Lucena): logbook.html never arrived at all - landed empty, no own links, no hub - and a later hop lost its nav with it. W3559 (J9, Manila): dayplanner showed the browser-floor canary ('a file it needs did not arrive') and shift-brain lost the hub, while the pages on either side of it kept theirs, which is the signature of scripts dropping rather than a nav gap. ROOT, and it is structural: SHELL_FILES precaches exactly two html pages and the cache-on-visit path was scoped to /learn/ and /tools/, so logbook.html (404KB, the surface a technician opens most) was in the cache by NO route. sw.js now answers app-page navigations network-first and keeps a copy, and validate_sw_offline L1 asks whether a page is recoverable rather than whether it is precached. WHY THESE TWO ROWS STAY OPEN ANYWAY: both walks run a FRESH context, so each was a first visit with nothing cached to fall back on, and a cold first visit whose own navigation is the dropped request cannot be recovered on the client. The repair closes the RETURNING visit - the common case on a plant floor - and these rows are the cold case, which needs either a retry on the navigation or a lighter first paint. Recorded rather than re-greened, because a load artifact, a fixture gap and a product defect are three different dispositions and this one is a product limit that is now named. pct -> 25. · [2026-09-05] STRUCTURE BUILT 2026-09-10 for the defect these three rows measured, and it is verified without a browser because the browser could not have answered it any faster. All three failed on the offline-3g condition, which delays every request and ABORTS about one in twelve; between them they show BOTH halves of one mechanism. The client half: W3559 and W3618 hit browser-floor.js's own banner ('a file it needs did not arrive'), which fires only for supabase-js - so that was the dropped request, and the banner treated ONE drop as the end of the story, telling a person on a plant floor to reload the whole page to recover a single request. The nav half: W3521 (hive -> skillmatrix) and W3618 (pm-scheduler -> analytics) reported hub=0, no nav at all, while the hops on either side kept theirs - nav-hub.js losing its turn with nothing watching it. browser-floor.js now asks once more before warning, and separately catches ANY dropped same-origin script from the CAPTURE phase (a resource error does not bubble). Same discipline both paths: same src, integrity and crossorigin carried across (a retry that drops SRI is a downgrade dressed as resilience), same-origin only, at most one retry with the replacement marked BEFORE insertion so a dropping line cannot become a request loop. trajectories.basis: [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-10 and FAILED TWICE, which is why it is recorded rather than dismissed. This is the offline-3g cell of J4 (audit season, Ramos Jeepney Line, phone-390): the walk emulates a real Philippine plant connection - slow, and it DROPS roughly one request in twelve. The prover recognised the complaints as load-shaped and re-asked in a fresh browser on its own; the second ask failed the same way, and reproducibility is what separates a defect from a load artifact on this program. WHAT IT SHOWS: 7 of the 8 pages in the chain rendered under that same lossy connection - logbook 1,087 chars, audit-log 2,002, report-sender 1,927 and 1,941, analytics-report 531, project-manager 1,566, project-report 1,082. hive.html rendered NOTHING measurable at all, and 2 steps showed the person an error. So it is not that the condition breaks every page; it is that it breaks THIS one. WHAT I COULD NOT SETTLE WITHOUT A BROWSER, stated so the next reader does not repeat it: the static signal is weak. hive.html has no `whQueryTimeout` on its reads - but neither do logbook, audit-log, report-sender, project-manager or alert-hub, and all of those rendered. Only marketplace.html has adopted it (3 sites). The plausible mechanism is arithmetic rather than a missing guard: hive.html is the platform's largest board and makes the most reads, so at a 1-in-12 drop rate it is the likeliest page to lose one - which makes the real question not WHETHER a read drops but whether the page then says so or just shows nothing. The walk says nothing. NEXT (needs the browser, sequenced behind the walk chain): open hive.html alone under the same emulation and watch what it does with a dropped read - a legible 'couldn't load' with a retry is the product working, an empty board or a permanent skeleton is the defect, and that distinction is invisible to every static gate (see the stuck-skeleton lesson). Held at walked; a claim measured and not holding is not banked. pct -> 25. · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE via tools/prove_full_journeys.mjs on the offline-3g condition, and triaged 2026-09-10 as ONE cluster rather than five separate mysteries. Every open offline-3g row fails the same way - a same-origin script did not arrive at the 1-in-12 abort this condition applies - and the symptom only differs by WHICH file lost its turn: W3579 and W3627 report 'getDb() called before @supabase/supabase-js loaded' (the client), W3122 reports 'window.getDb is not a function' (utils.js, which defines it), and W3512/W3599/W3654/W3700 report a step not arriving as itself or a hop with no way onward (the page or nav-hub.js). Eleven open rows, one mechanism. THE STRUCTURE IS BUILT: browser-floor.js now asks once more for a dropped same-origin script - from the CAPTURE phase, since a resource error does not bubble - carrying integrity and crossorigin across, at most once per tag, with the replacement marked before insertion so a dropping line cannot become a request loop; and sw.js answers app navigations network-first with a kept copy. Unit-verified in tools/test_browser_floor_retry.mjs (16 cases, both directions, mutation-tested four ways) and the arming order audited across all 35 pages that load a shell script. THESE ROWS ARE NOT CLOSED ON THAT: a unit test proves the retry fires, only a walk proves the person got their page, and the re-walk is a browser job. tools/prove_full_journeys.mjs gained --condition this turn so it can be one scoped run over all 20 offline-3g rows instead of re-walking J1+J14+J17+J4+J16 entire to reach five. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-09 through the playwright MCP, on the surface that actually calculates rather than the one that advertises it. tools/storm-drain-calculator/index.html is an SEO page with NO calculator inputs (its only two inputs belong to the feedback widget), so the I claim cannot be settled there; it names DPWH Blue Book / Rational Method and hands the reader on with 'Open the interactive Storm Drain Calculator', href /engineering-design.html?calc=storm-drain-stormwater. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-09 through invoke + postgres, driven step by step, and it found a SERIOUS defect that is now fixed. Built the fixture the contract needs: an enabled integration_config given an HMAC secret, and a request signed the way the function documents - HMAC-SHA256 over '<timestamp>.<rawBody>', hex, in X-WorkHive-Signature / X-WorkHive-Timestamp. For a CMMS integration that is the worst shape available: the sending system is told the order landed, never retries, and the plant's completed work vanishes. TWO FIXES: the upsert result is now checked and a failure answers 502 with a sentence the sender can act on ('Nothing was changed, so it is safe to send it again') plus the operator's detail; and an unmapped status is CLAMPED to a legal value - the same lesson integrations.html already learned on its import path and this webhook path never got - keeping what the sender said in sync_payload.status_raw. Re-walked: ok:true now means a row exists, status Closed, status_raw TECO, machine CONV-02. trajectories.story: supabase/functions/login: walked by invoke and by PostgREST as the caller's own persona, never as the owner connection
trajectories.basis: [2026-09-05] Walked live through invoke as the caller with the prober's own credentials, never the owner connection. THE SHAPE READER CANNOT ANSWER THIS ONE, AND THAT IS THE TRUE VERDICT RATHER THAN A GAP: login's success path is 'return json(200, gotrueBody)' - a pass-through of GoTrue's own session object - and its helper is an arrow assignment 'const json = (code, body) => new Response(JSON.stringify(body))' taking the body SECOND. There is no object literal anywhere declaring the success shape, so responseKeysFromVariable (added this session for voice-report-intent) correctly finds nothing here, exactly as it correctly finds nothing for project-orchestrator's Promise<Record<string, unknown>>. Manufacturing a key list for either would invent a contract the function never wrote. So this row is earned on the EFFECT instead, which is what the F lens actually asks for: does it complete its documented job. IT DOES, proven in three steps. (1) Invoked with the plain member's credentials it returned 200 carrying access_token, refresh_token, token_type, expires_in, expires_at, user and weak_password - the real GoTrue session its own comment promises. (2) The issued token RESOLVES ITS OWN USER: GET /auth/v1/user with that bearer returns wilfredomalabanan@auth.workhiveph.com, id 5e036469 - so the credential is genuine, not an envelope that merely looks right. (3) THE DECISIVE ONE, because a token that authenticates nothing would still pass step 2: the same PostgREST read of v_logbook_truth returns 0 rows with the anon key and 5 rows with the issued token. The function's documented job is to turn credentials into a session that can actually read this person's data, and the difference between 0 and 5 on identical requests is that job being done. No probe writes to reverse - a sign-in mints a session, it does not persist a row. The lockout risk this file's own header describes was respected: the prober's known-good credentials were used once, never guessed. pct -> 100.

(recording the number the withdrawal above returns this row to, so the field and the basis agree - the registry gate holds every pct to the last one its basis states) · [2026-09-05] Walked live, and the walk surfaced a real unhandled-error defect. notify-push had been answering 500 'Something went wrong on our side' to the prober; the edge log named the cause: '(body.auth_uids ?? []).filter is not a function'. THE CLASS: ?? guards ABSENCE, not TYPE. The body is annotated 'auth_uids?: string[]' but a TypeScript annotation is erased at runtime and req.json() returns whatever the caller actually sent, so auth_uids: "abc" sailed straight past ?? [] and threw inside .filter. Three costs, all real: the caller was told the PLATFORM broke when their request was malformed; they were told nothing about which field to fix; and it was logged at error level with code unhandled_error, so an integrator's typo became our alert noise. provider_ids one line below had the same hole and a nastier shape - a bare STRING has a truthy .length, so it passed 'if (body.provider_ids && body.provider_ids.length)' and went into .in("id", ...) as a non-list. Both fields are now checked with Array.isArray and answer 400 naming the field. PROVEN LIVE on all three paths: auth_uids: "not-a-list" -> 400 invalid_field 'auth_uids must be an array of ids.'; provider_ids: "nope" -> 400 'provider_ids must be an array of ids.'; and the well-formed request -> 200 {ok:true, data:{sent:0, pruned:0, failed:0, targets:0, note:'no target uids'}} - its documented envelope shape, honestly reporting zero targets rather than claiming a delivery. Then re-walked through the prover: ok, 200 in its own declared shape (ok, error, data), 55 callers name it, asked with the service key because this function names a machine as its caller; its refusal row is banked separately and only ever as a plain member. Zero rows persisted (targets 0, nothing sent), so there was nothing to reverse. One instrument note recorded on the way: restarting a container behind Kong gives it a NEW IP and Kong's upstream targets it by its original NAME, so 'name resolution failed' is a stale-DNS symptom, not a dead function - fixed by giving the replacement container the original name as a network alias. The function edit is local only - deploying it is Ian's gate. pct -> 100.

FIRST, THE DEFECT: the prober reported 'answered 400 ""' - a 400 with no words at all. Reading the source, TWO of this function's five 400 paths returned { inserted, skipped_dup, rejected, errors } with NO top-level error key, while the other three return { error: ... }. So the same endpoint answers the same status code in two different body shapes, and a plant bridge reading .error - the shape this function itself uses three times - got undefined and had nothing to show the operator. A whole rejected batch looked like a silent failure. The more confusing of the two is the hive-scope reject, where the readings are WELL FORMED and still refused because their assets belong to another hive: without a summary line that reads as 'our integration is broken' rather than 'this bridge is pointed at the wrong hive'. FIXED both, keeping the per-row errors[] exactly as it was (it is the better detail) and adding the summary a caller can display. PROVEN LIVE after restarting the edge runtime - the first invocation returned the OLD shape because the runtime was serving a cached build, the deno-cache trap this project has hit before: the all-invalid path now says 'No reading passed validation: all 1 were rejected. See errors[] for the reason on each row.' and the hive-mismatch path names the hive. THEN THE CLAIM ITSELF: posted one reading for a real asset in Wilfredo Malabanan's own hive (Amada HFE 80-25, vibration_mms 7.77777 at 2026-09-09T03:33:33.333Z - a sentinel chosen so the reversal could be exact). The function answered { inserted: 1, skipped_dup: 0, rejected: 0, anomalies: 0, errors: [] } and psql confirms it persisted EXACTLY that: one row, right asset_id, right parameter, right value, right timestamp - what it says it persisted is what is there, no more and no less. Probe write reversed immediately (DELETE 1 by id) and audited: 0 rows remain matching either the sentinel value or the sentinel timestamp. The function edit is local only - deploying it is Ian's gate. pct -> 100.

(recording the number the withdrawal above returns this row to, so the field and the basis agree - the registry gate holds every pct to the last one its basis states) · [2026-09-05] WALKED LIVE 2026-09-10 against the running function, and deliberately NOT with the contract prover. This function's documented job is to RESET A MEMBER'S PASSWORD, and every journey walk on this platform signs in as a seeded member with 'test1234' - so proving it against any real member would have broken the cast the rest of the program depends on. The probe would have damaged the instrument. Instead a throwaway member was built the way the platform builds one and deleted afterwards. SETUP CORRECTION WORTH KEEPING: the first attempt created an auth user plus a hive_members row and got a truthful 404, 'No such active member in this hive.' The function looks its target up through v_worker_truth, not hive_members - a view driven by worker_profiles (LEFT JOIN hive_members) whose worker_name is wp.display_name - so an account and a membership are not yet a person it can find. The 404 was about an incomplete fixture, not the product. THE CONTRACT, asked as Oscar Ramos, a real supervisor of the target's hive: 200 with {ok, worker_name, temp_password, message} - its own declared shape. The persisted effect is checked three ways rather than read off the reply: the stored password hash MOVED ($2a$10$mQ3Agg0gNpT/i -> $2a$10$k9SQNsiNyzL13); the temp_password it handed back ACTUALLY SIGNS THE MEMBER IN, so the reply is not a story; and one hive_audit_log row was written, carrying actor, target_name and target_id (a first reading called that row anonymous - the query had simply not selected those columns). REVERSED AND AUDITED: probe auth users 0, hive_members 0, worker_profiles 0, rows in v_worker_truth 0, and the audit row this run produced deleted, leaving 0 for that actor. Nothing an existing walk can see was touched at any point. pct -> 100.

That lens asks whether a member of hive A, using their own token, gets hive B's data back, and answers it with a sentinel lifted from B. THIS FUNCTION HAS NO HIVE: grep hive_id in tts-speak and there is nothing; voice-transcribe touches a hive's asset TAGS only to prime the decoder and never returns them. So the prover's honest n/a - 'answers both hives the same way' - was the correct BEHAVIOUR being reported as an unanswered question, and no provider key would ever have changed it. THE ENTITLEMENT CONTROL THESE FUNCTIONS ACTUALLY HAVE is the one their source is written around: they spend a paid provider, so access is metered PER IDENTITY (ai_user_rate_limits, 30/hour, 100/day). Measured by the control's SIDE EFFECT rather than by how the reply looked - the correction that made this necessary is that an anonymous call reaching the provider was first read as unmetered, when the meter had run and left a row keyed ip:172.18.0.1. SEPARATION: two ordinary members of different hives each got their OWN bucket keyed by auth uid (89814ccc -1->1, 91e0d1eb ->1), standing alongside a distinct ip: bucket for the anonymous path - so one person's spending cannot consume another's allowance. REFUSAL, proven as a differential with ONE thing changed: Ben Ocampo put at the 30/hour cap asked tts-speak and was refused 429 "AI call limit reached. Try again in about 60 minutes." - a sentence a person can act on, carrying a real retry time - while Bryan Garcia, asking in the SAME moment, was NOT refused (502 from the absent Azure key, i.e. he reached the dependency). A cap that stopped everybody would be an outage and one that stopped nobody would be decoration; this stopped exactly the person whose allowance was spent. Also hardened at the spend site: an unidentifiable caller (no session AND no x-forwarded-for) is now refused rather than waved through, and answered 401 'Sign in to use this' instead of the rate-limiter's 'limit reached, try again in an hour', which would have been false twice over. Stated honestly: that branch is defence in depth, NOT a demonstrated hole - Kong supplies the header on every local request exactly as Supabase's gateway does, so I could not reach it. Probe setup (one bucket row) reversed; audit shows 0 rows. pct -> 100.

trajectories.basis: [2026-09-05] skill-content.js is loaded by exactly one page (skillmatrix.html) and is the single declaration of SKILL_CONTENT[discipline][level]; there is no second copy of the lesson or exam data in the tree, so the U claim - the same thing on every page that carries it - is true by construction on a roster of one. The walk's finding is about WHAT it says rather than consistency: the new shared-component-i18n gate flagged it as a shared file writing user-facing English with no translator call, and unlike the five components fixed alongside it, this one is NOT chrome. It is a 670-line training CORPUS - lesson bodies and ten exam questions per level per discipline. Wrapping those in _t() would make the gate green while every lesson stayed English, so it carries an explicit 'i18n-shared-allow:' marker naming the real disposition instead: a bilingual training corpus is a content-authoring program needing a translator who knows the trade vocabulary, not a wrapper. The exemption is printed in the gate's own output with its reason on every run, so the backlog stays visible rather than disappearing into a green tick. · [2026-09-05] Re-walked with playwright at three renderings, which is as close as this subject can come to the instrument's literal ask and is the honest way to close it. The ledger wants 'three HOST PAGES: phone, desktop, wall display' - but skill-content.js has exactly ONE host, skillmatrix.html, confirmed in the live DOM (scripts matching skill-content: 1). A roster of one cannot be walked across three hosts, so the question was answered in its spirit: the one host rendered at all three viewports, with the display calibrated first (devicePixelRatio 0.667 here, so a requested 260/853/1280 is what yields a true 390/1280/1920 - asking for 390 directly would have measured a 585px tablet and called it a phone). AT ALL THREE the shared corpus says the same thing: its five declared disciplines - Mechanical, Electrical, Instrumentation, Facilities Management, Production Lines - are all present at 390x845, 1280x800 and 1920x1080, and documentElement.scrollWidth sits 6px UNDER the viewport at every size, so nothing is pushed off-screen at the narrow end or stranded at the wide one. The U claim holds by construction on the data side too: skill-content.js is the single declaration of SKILL_CONTENT[discipline][level] and there is no second copy of the lesson or exam text anywhere in the tree, so there is no competing source that could drift. Also reached honestly: the first attempt bounced to index.html?signin=1&return=skillmatrix.html, which is the identity gate doing its job - a session was minted for the plain member to get in, and removed afterwards (sb- keys 0). pct -> 100.

trajectories.story: browser-floor.js: walked on three host pages (phone, desktop, wall display), because shared chrome is graded once and styled before paint
trajectories.basis: [2026-09-05] pct -> 60. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-09 through the playwright MCP, and the notice was made to PAINT rather than inferred from the source. browser-floor.js guards the platform's ES2020 floor by eval-ing optional chaining; on a modern engine it correctly renders NOTHING, so the message can never be read by simply loading a page. Fetched the component's own source, replaced ONLY its capability eval with a throw - the exact path an ES2019 browser takes - and ran it, so what was read is the component's real output rather than a mock. It painted, byte-identical on integrations.html and logbook.html: 'This browser is too old to run WorkHive (it needs a 2020-or-newer browser engine). Please update Chrome / Android System WebView from the Play Store, or open WorkHive in an updated browser.' followed by the Filipino half, 'Masyadong luma ang browser na ito para sa WorkHive - i-update ang Chrome o ang Android System WebView.' - which matters because the person most likely to meet this floor is on an old Android WebView. COVERAGE, counted not assumed: 41 of the 42 root pages load it; the ONE exception is offline-fallback.html, and that is correct by design - the page shown when nothing else loads must render with no dependencies. NO page carries a competing copy of the message (grep for the string across every root page returns only the shared file), so there is nothing that could drift out of step with it.

trajectories.story: session-timeout.js: walked on three host pages (phone, desktop, wall display), because shared chrome is graded once and styled before paint
trajectories.basis: [2026-09-05] session-timeout.js is ONE file loaded by 33 pages, with no competing copy anywhere in the tree, so the U claim holds by construction: every page that carries it shows the same idle prompt and the same cross-tab hive-switch notice. Walking WHAT it says on all 33 turned up the defect. Its own header opens 'On a shared Filipino plant tablet, worker A finishes their shift and worker B picks up the same device' - and it was the one interruption on that tablet that spoke only English. Not outside the contract either: utils.js:414 whLocaleFloor installs window._t(en, fil) platform-wide as a locale FLOOR precisely so shared chrome can translate without owning a dictionary, and nav-hub.js:1877 already took it for the update notice. session-timeout.js simply never joined - the fix-that-reached-one-path shape again. Now the idle heading, the idle sentence, both buttons, the cross-tab notice, its two hive fallbacks and the Reload button all route through a call-time _t lookup (call-time, not bind-time: a page with its own engine defines _t later in the body and this modal paints minutes after load). Second defect in the same sentence: it hardcoded 'idle for 15 minutes' while IDLE_LIMIT_MS is overridable, so under the Playwright override the sentence was simply false; it now reads the threshold, floored at 1 minute. Verified: node --check clean; every DOM-text write in the file (3) now goes through the translator; no oracle asserts on the copy (prove_shared_components.mjs checks #wh-idle-overlay and whClearIdentity, not words). sw.js v339 to v340 - it is a SHELL_FILES entry, determined by parsing the list rather than from memory, so an installed PWA would otherwise keep the English-only prompt.

trajectories.basis: [2026-09-05] Walked live in the browser as the returner this lens describes, and the claim is answered by the page's retirement rather than by a resume affordance - which is the honest reading, not a dodge. Someone coming back to marketplace-admin.html after weeks is in exactly the situation where a stale bookmark hurts most: the work they remember doing here has MOVED. What they now get is the retirement notice, visible and not a dead end: '📊 Marketplace Admin has moved. Listing / seller / dispute VOLUMES are now live Grafana panels; approve / verify / resolve ACTIONS moved to the Platform Actions page (Grafana also alerts you when a queue has items).' Two working onward links - the Founder Ops dashboard and Platform Actions - so the answer to 'show me where I left off' is a sentence naming BOTH halves of where the work went and a route to each. Telling a returner where their task lives now is more use than restoring a filter on a console that no longer does the job. Measured: retirement notice visible, 2 links, deadEnd false. THIS ROW ALSO DEPENDED ON A FIX MADE EARLIER THIS TURN: until then the page ran its entire moderation load behind that invisible overlay - the draft-listings query, five HEAD count probes, the sellers count, the platform-admins check - so a returner silently paid for a console they could not see. That work now stops at the top of boot, while the page_view is deliberately kept, because an arrival here is the signal that the old link is still in circulation. pct -> 100.

Deliberately narrow: it never guesses which pages OUGHT to have concurrency control, only holds a page to the intention it declared by loading the file. That is the same conclusion my own 'filters' work reached, written down in the page before I got there. THE ROOT OF ALL THREE WRONG READINGS, named once: this gate was counting a NAME when the thing that matters is a PROPERTY. A page that compares a stamp before overwriting HAS optimistic concurrency, whatever it calls it. INLINE_GUARD_RE now counts .eq('updated_at', ...) alongside the three helper names, the selftest pins the inline shape, and the ceiling is 2. THE FINDING THAT SURVIVES, and it is a real one on the money path: marketplace.html's settle - the client confirming payment and releasing - filtered on id ALONE. Proven in psql end to end: with a seeded completed request and its payment row, an unguarded confirm succeeded, then a REPEAT confirm succeeded too and overwrote settled_at from :53.827 to :55.047 - a second release rewriting when the money was released. The database trigger guard_settle_requires_payment does NOT cover this, and reading it says why: it fires only when old.status IS DISTINCT FROM 'settled', so it guards ENTRY into settled, never a repeat of it. FIXED by guarding the transition rather than a timestamp, which is the honest guard for a state machine: .eq('status', 'completed') - the first confirm matches, every repeat matches zero rows (proven: 0 rows). That also gives the zero-rows branch a single meaning, so it stops saying 'refresh and try again' (the one thing that cannot change the outcome) and now says the job is no longer waiting for payment, in both languages, and reloads. All probe rows reversed: probe_requests_left=0, probe_payments_left=0. pct -> 25. · [2026-09-05] marketplace-admin.html FIXED, so the ratchet falls 2 -> 1 and only marketplace.html's remaining writes are unguarded. Its moderation action (approve / reject / unpublish) filtered on id alone, and the page did not even SELECT updated_at, so it had no stamp to guard with. Two costs, and the second is the one that matters. Two moderators on the same listing: the second silently replaced the first's decision AND overwrote moderated_by, so the listing's own record of who decided became whoever wrote last. And the seller editing mid-review: the moderator approves what they read, and the write lands on content they never saw - which is how a listing whose photo or price changed underneath the review goes live with an approval attached to it. PROVEN in psql with a valid fixture, after a first attempt was confounded by a DIFFERENT server-side guard (guard_listing_meets_minimum refuses publishing under PHP500, which errored on the unguarded case and would have made the comparison meaningless - re-run at price 1500 so both arms were testing the same thing). Unguarded: the seller edits after the moderator loads, the approve still succeeds, and the listing ends 'WALKPROBE seller changed it | published | by Admin A' - published content nobody reviewed, carrying a reviewer's name. Guarded on the version the decision was about: 0 rows, listing stays draft, moderated_by nobody. FIX: updated_at added to the queue's select, the write guarded with .eq('updated_at', _stamp) only when a stamp is present (so a row loaded before this column existed still moderates rather than becoming unmoderatable), and the zero-rows branch tells the moderator the listing changed since they opened it, re-enables the buttons and reloads the queue. It reloads with loadListings(listing.status) rather than bare: that function REQUIRES a status, and calling it bare would have reloaded a queue for status undefined and emptied the moderator's screen - a bug I nearly introduced with the fix. All probe rows reversed: probe_listings_left=0. pct -> 25. · [2026-09-05] CLOSED. All four pages that load oc-helper.js now guard their state-changing writes, and the ratchet sits at 0. The two real defects this row uncovered are fixed and each was PROVEN in psql before and after. marketplace.html settle: filtered on id alone, so a repeat confirm re-settled an already-settled job and moved settled_at from :53.827 to :55.047 - and the database trigger guard_settle_requires_payment does NOT cover it, because it fires only when old.status IS DISTINCT FROM 'settled', guarding ENTRY into settled and never a repeat. Now .eq('status','completed'): first confirm matches, repeat matches 0 rows. marketplace.html client-cancel: its zero-rows message already said 'it may have moved on' but nothing made that TRUE - a cancel could land on work a provider had already started. Now .in('status', SVC_OPEN.slice(0,5)), the exact states the button is rendered for, deliberately excluding in_progress. Proven both ways: refused from in_progress (0 rows, work continues), still succeeds from accepted (1 row). marketplace-admin.html moderation: filtered on id alone AND the queue did not even select updated_at, so there was no stamp to guard with. Proven: with a seller editing after the moderator loaded the row, the unguarded approve published content nobody reviewed - 'WALKPROBE seller changed it | published | by Admin A'; guarded on the version the decision was about, 0 rows and the listing stays in the queue. That first proof attempt was confounded by a different trigger (guard_listing_meets_minimum, price >= PHP500) and was re-run at a valid price so both arms tested the same thing. It now counts all three shapes, because a gate that recognises one blessed spelling measures conformity to itself rather than adoption - and its failure mode is manufacturing work on code that is already correct. trajectories.title: The platform must bound what this page can consume, and say so when it has - achievements
trajectories.story: layer RL had no row on this page when wave 3 was seeded
trajectories.basis: [2026-09-05] pct -> 60. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-08 via tools/prove_lifecycle_cells.mjs - AR on achievements.html: walked; the refusal itself is proven by the rate-limit lens · [2026-09-05] Re-walked with postgres-mcp plus a live browser check, the instruments this lens needs, and the page's own weekly-XP tile was the one place the claim failed. achievements.html carries 6 row caps; three are marked cap-ok with real reasoning, and the 7-day XP read at .limit(1000) was not - and it is the one that matters, because it is an AGGREGATE SOURCE. A cap on a list is a short list; a cap on a sum is a WRONG NUMBER, silently. The page already knew this: the comment directly above that query explains the dedicated window query exists precisely because deriving the week from the 30-row activity list undercounted a busy worker. The same shape was then reintroduced at 1000 with nothing watching whether the cap was reached. MEASURED before judging: the worst worker-week in the data today is 221 events against the 1000 cap, so it is not being hit now - which is why the fix is NOT to raise the limit (that only moves the cliff) but to make a hit VISIBLE, which is literally what this lens asks: bound what the page consumes, AND say so when the bound has bitten. Rows-returned == the limit is the one observable signal, so _weekXPCapped records it and the tile stops asserting a total it cannot stand behind. PROVEN LIVE, both directions, on the real page. Normal: '+780' / '780 XP from logbook, PM and community work this week' - byte-identical to before, since the flag is false on every ordinary load. Then seeded 1005 XP rows for the signed-in worker (Leandro Marquez, 1085 in his 7-day window) and reloaded: '+1700' / 'At least 1700 XP this week - you logged so much that this count stopped short of all of it'. Before this change that same load would have shown a confident, short total with nothing to distinguish it from a true one. Probe rows reversed by their sentinel source_action (DELETE 1005, probe_rows_left=0, table back to its original 2090) and the page re-checked afterwards: '+780' and the original sentence, exactly as before the probe. pct -> 100.

trajectories.basis: [2026-09-05] pct -> 60. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-08 via tools/prove_lifecycle_cells.mjs - AR on analytics-report.html: walked; the refusal itself is proven by the rate-limit lens · [2026-09-05] Re-walked and THE CLAIM HOLDS, though the bound lives on the SERVER rather than in the page - which is why a client-side .limit() census read this page as unbounded and was looking in the wrong place. analytics-report.html makes exactly ONE client read (v_hives_truth, a single row); everything else is a POST to analytics-orchestrator, forwarding the user's session JWT rather than the anon key so the hive-membership check passes. So the question 'what can this page consume' is answered in that function, and it is answered well. BOUND: eight capped reads, most through dynLimit(periodDays, maxPerDay, hardCap=5000), which SCALES the cap with the requested window instead of freezing one number - its own header states the rule, 'any metric aggregating >200 rows needs a limit that accounts for growth, not a hardcoded cap', and the reason, 'Prevents silent data truncation as the hive grows'. Two caps carry their history in the code (200 -> 1000 for calcs, 300 -> 2000 for parts, each with the sentence explaining what real hive outgrew it). AND THE ARCHITECTURE AVOIDS THE TRAP THAT CAUGHT achievements.html ENTIRELY: every reliability metric - MTBF, MTTR, OEE, downtime pareto, failure frequency, repeat failures, PM compliance - comes from a Postgres RPC computing over ALL matching rows, not from summing a capped client list. That is the correct shape for an aggregate, and it is exactly the fix the weekly-XP tile needed. The capped .select() reads bound descriptive LISTS, so a hit shortens a list rather than falsifying a number. RESIDUAL, recorded rather than hidden: the function returns no explicit truncation flag, so if a hive ever exceeded dynLimit's 5000 hard cap within a period, the affected list would be short with nothing saying so. That is a weaker version of the 'say so' half than status.html achieves - but it cannot silently corrupt a metric here, because the metrics do not come from those lists. pct -> 100.

WALKED LIVE 2026-09-08 via tools/prove_lifecycle_cells.mjs - AR on founder-console.html: walked; the refusal itself is proven by the rate-limit lens · [2026-09-05] Re-walked live with the browser's network log, and the prover's own verdict is what pointed here: prove_consumption_bound graded both pages n/a because they are 'retired behind the overlay - content not shown to anyone'. That is true about the CONTENT and it is exactly why the consumption question mattered more, not less: A RETIRED PAGE THAT STILL LOADS IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE PAGE ON THE PLATFORM, because nobody will ever see the cost. Both retirements are markup only - a fixed overlay at z-index 100000, with the original scripts deliberately left intact so the ~35 static validators that scan these files keep passing - which preserved the boot sequences too. MEASURED, not inferred. founder-console.html ran its full refreshAll behind the overlay: 14 database requests including analytics_events limit=50000, ai_cost_log limit=20000, v_marketplace_listings_truth limit=5000, ai_cost_log limit=5000, v_hive_readiness_truth limit=2000 and five founder_* RPCs - up to ~77,000 rows fetched to render a screen whose entire content is 'The Founder Console has moved to Grafana'. marketplace-admin.html ran its whole moderation load: the draft-listings query, five HEAD count probes, the sellers count and the platform-admins check. FIXED by returning at the top of each boot before any read, testing for the overlay itself rather than a flag - so the documented reversal stays honest: deleting the overlay to un-retire restores the load with it. RE-MEASURED: founder-console 14 DB requests -> 0 of its own (the single remaining v_hives_truth read is shared nav chrome), marketplace-admin's marketplace and admin queries all gone. The overlay still renders in full - 'The Founder Console has moved to Grafana' with both onward links to the Grafana dashboard and Platform Actions - so a visitor loses nothing. ONE THING DELIBERATELY KEPT: the page_view. My first cut silenced founder-console's logPageView along with the work, which would have retired the EVIDENCE too - an arrival here is the signal that the old link is still in circulation and that the pointer to Grafana is doing its job. marketplace-admin logs its view outside its boot block and kept it by construction, so founder-console now logs one as well (with retired: true) and the two pages agree instead of one quietly under-reporting. pct -> 100.

trajectories.basis: [2026-09-05] pct -> 60. WALKED LIVE 2026-09-08 via tools/prove_lifecycle_cells.mjs - AR on marketplace-admin.html: walked; the refusal itself is proven by the rate-limit lens · [2026-09-05] Re-walked live with the browser's network log, and the prover's own verdict is what pointed here: prove_consumption_bound graded both pages n/a because they are 'retired behind the overlay - content not shown to anyone'. That is true about the CONTENT and it is exactly why the consumption question mattered more, not less: A RETIRED PAGE THAT STILL LOADS IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE PAGE ON THE PLATFORM, because nobody will ever see the cost. Both retirements are markup only - a fixed overlay at z-index 100000, with the original scripts deliberately left intact so the ~35 static validators that scan these files keep passing - which preserved the boot sequences too. MEASURED, not inferred. founder-console.html ran its full refreshAll behind the overlay: 14 database requests including analytics_events limit=50000, ai_cost_log limit=20000, v_marketplace_listings_truth limit=5000, ai_cost_log limit=5000, v_hive_readiness_truth limit=2000 and five founder_* RPCs - up to ~77,000 rows fetched to render a screen whose entire content is 'The Founder Console has moved to Grafana'. marketplace-admin.html ran its whole moderation load: the draft-listings query, five HEAD count probes, the sellers count and the platform-admins check. FIXED by returning at the top of each boot before any read, testing for the overlay itself rather than a flag - so the documented reversal stays honest: deleting the overlay to un-retire restores the load with it. RE-MEASURED: founder-console 14 DB requests -> 0 of its own (the single remaining v_hives_truth read is shared nav chrome), marketplace-admin's marketplace and admin queries all gone. The overlay still renders in full - 'The Founder Console has moved to Grafana' with both onward links to the Grafana dashboard and Platform Actions - so a visitor loses nothing. ONE THING DELIBERATELY KEPT: the page_view. My first cut silenced founder-console's logPageView along with the work, which would have retired the EVIDENCE too - an arrival here is the signal that the old link is still in circulation and that the pointer to Grafana is doing its job. marketplace-admin logs its view outside its boot block and kept it by construction, so founder-console now logs one as well (with retired: true) and the two pages agree instead of one quietly under-reporting. pct -> 100.

THE PAGE MOSTLY EARNS IT ALREADY, and its own history is why: a comment above the headline rating records that the stars used to be recomputed from a list 'capped at .limit(20), so it was a partial average presented as the rating', fixed by reading the canonical rating_avg column instead. Its reviews list discloses CONDITIONALLY - ' most recent reviews' exactly when the cap is reached, a plain count otherwise, which is the right shape. Its listings cap of 60 is unreachable: measured, the busiest seller holds 3. THE ONE THAT WAS NOT: the response-time average read v_marketplace_inquiries_truth with .limit(50) and NO .order() AT ALL - the only capped read on the page without one, while every sibling carries .order(...).order('id') and the MR4 note that a sort is not total on its own. Two consequences past the cap: the average would be computed from an ARBITRARY 50 rather than a meaningful 50, and a DIFFERENT arbitrary 50 on the next refresh, so a number presented as a fact about a seller would move on reload. Measured today the busiest seller has 2 replied inquiries, so nothing is wrong on screen right now - this is a latent defect fixed before it bit, not a live one. FIXED: .order('replied_at', desc).order('id') so the 50 are the most recent 50 and the answer is repeatable, and _replyCapped records a cap hit so the stat can state its own scope. PROVEN LIVE on Bryan Garcia (one of the three sellers with replies): '236h', titled 'Average over all 2 of this seller's replies' - and it would read 'Average over this seller's 50 most recent replies, not all of them' past the cap. The figure itself is unchanged and still shown; what changed is that it now says what it covers. Found via the new summed_caps() detector in prove_consumption_bound, which pointed at this page for a neighbouring read - the detector named the wrong table and still put me on the right page, which is what an advisory signal is for. pct -> 100.

I made the chip async and awaited db.auth.getSession() inside it - but 'db' is assigned ~900 lines BELOW that call, so the await threw, my own .catch swallowed it, and the chip silently kept its BUILD-TIME markup text for EVERYONE, signed in or not. That is precisely the failure the note above this function already warns about ('a fix that ships and never executes') and the getDb-exists-before-it-works trap. Caught it by reading the live chip rather than trusting the edit. That ordering is deliberate: the chip may under-promise for a moment and can never over-promise. RE-PROVEN BOTH WAYS on the live page. The last two rows were closed through the MCPs, not the library, after Ian's correction mid-turn ('we should always use MCPs for walks'). SS-LW.1 rule 4 is explicit - batch with the library, WALK with the MCP - and every journey that day had been driven by prove_full_journeys.mjs. THE HABIT HAD A STRUCTURAL CAUSE: live_walk_manifest read exactly one receipt namespace, the one the script writes, so a journey walked correctly by hand through the MCP could never be banked and a row whose scripted receipt was red stayed red however carefully it was re-walked. tools/record_mcp_walk.py writes the MCP namespace, the ledger takes the newest across both, and every receipt carries its instrument so a reader can tell a walk a person drove from one a script drove (gate mcp-walk-receipts, 6 cases: no steps, unknown instrument, a thin step, a lost identity and an --unproven walk are each refused or reddened). WHAT THE MCP WALKS SAW THAT THE SCRIPT CANNOT: the person's door is a USERNAME wall at index.html?signin=1&return=<page>, which the script never meets because it signs in through the auth API with an email; a step the script read as 69 characters IS that wall, so the script had lost its session, and the same step renders 3,754 characters walked as the person on Slow 3G; and audit-log telling a worker 'Supervisors only' with routes home is a legible entitlement state, not the dead hop a char-count reading scores it as. AND A FIXTURE GAP NO SCRIPTED PASS WOULD HAVE SHOWN: Baguio Textile Mills was the only one of six hives whose single supervisor sat in marketplace_platform_admins, so 109 supervisor-half claims rested on nobody - an admin may answer a route question and never an entitlement one.
